conflict: ◆ The pace gap between steady advancement and trial-and-error
◆ Earth's tolerance clashes with Li Fire's impatience
advice: First use Before Completion's discernment of things and placement to clarify the boundaries of your goals, then borrow the Army's capacity for holding the people to establish execution discipline. Let Fire not overstep its bounds, and Earth not seal everything shut.

one_liner: Resonant and devoted, wave upon wave of water naturally forms a deep pool.
analysis: Both hexagrams are Bi (Holding Together), and both belong to Water. Water’s virtue lies in moistening below and aiding what is low. The judgment's 'primal, enduring, steadfast' stresses sincerity as the foundation; the Image's 'build states, bond with lords' reveals a cooperative pattern. When two such hexagrams overlap, the waters converge into a 'compounded closeness' effect—amplifying the pull toward following what is good, yet also, because both are identical, inviting the trap of path dependence. The warning against the 'latecomer's misfortune' becomes a test of two tracks moving in tandem: if both hold to steady integrity, the earth beneath receives twin streams and nourishes all; if they dally and hesitate, water pools into stagnant hollows and breeds inward friction. This bond needs dynamic balance to break the deadlock of sameness.
resonance: ★ The inclusiveness of twin waters in mutual support
★ A field of trust in sympathetic resonance
conflict: ◆ An innovation blind spot caused by convergent decisions
◆ The risk of lagging when rhythms are too synchronized
advice: Each month, set a 'Dissent Day' and take turns inviting a third-party perspective, keeping closeness without losing your edge.

one_liner: Like wind guiding water into form, virtue descends as silent rain
analysis: The hexagram Holding Together shows water and earth in harmony, signifying closeness and cohesion; the Taming Power of the Small shows wind and heaven in motion, signifying the cultivation of cultural virtue. Water's gentle moisture meets wind's permeating influence, creating a dynamic nourishment: Holding Together's 'establishing the myriad states' requires the patient accumulation of the Taming Power of the Small's 'adorning virtue,' while the Taming Power of the Small's 'dense clouds, no rain' needs the inclusiveness of Holding Together's 'approaching the feudal lords' to break the impasse. Together they are like wind driving water vapor to rise into clouds—early on, the rhythm mismatch between swift wind and slow water must be overcome, but once cultural virtue infuses the bonds of closeness, the clouds before rain become sweet dew that nourishes all, achieving a dual harvest of spiritual resonance and practical collaboration.
resonance: ★ Drawing close to build momentum and unite hearts
★ Accumulating virtue, turning it to silent rain that nourishes
conflict: ◆ Wind swift, water slow—rhythms out of sync
◆ Clouds gather but no rain falls—expectations fall short
advice: Hold a monthly cultural gathering, using poetry, calligraphy, qin music, and painting as vessels to release tension, letting Holding Together's inclusiveness receive the Taming Power of the Small's depth.

one_liner: Water clings around the heavenly path; holding to rites, we guard one heart.
analysis: Bi is the water of gentle nurturing, ruling nearness and attachment; Lu is the image of heaven, firm and vital, prizing ceremonial order. When water blends with earth, tolerance gathers hearts; when heaven and lake overlap, rules define the boundaries. Their meeting forms a pattern of outer roundness and inner squareness: Bi's warmth needs Lu's prudence to anchor direction, while Lu's severity needs Bi's moisture to soften rigidity. As the Image says, to establish the ten thousand states, the feudal lords must hold together (Bi); to settle the people's will, the high and low must be distinguished (Lu). It is like a river that follows its channel—ever flowing, yet never losing its course.
resonance: ★ Water graces the heavenly stairway, giving rise to a Kindred bond.
★ Drawing near through rites brings forth the square and the circle.
conflict: ◆ When the yielding meets the unyielding, guard against friction.
◆ In gathering hearts, take care not to lose the sense of measure.
advice: In group collaboration, define clear role boundaries. Let Bi's inclusivity listen to Lu's rule-based suggestions.

one_liner: Water gathers, earth carries, birthing close bonds; Heaven and Earth intermingle, forging a path of Peace; huddling for warmth is no match for paving the road together.
analysis: Hexagram Holding Together (Bi), with water and earth merging, focuses on drawing near and choosing the good; Hexagram Peace (Tai), with earth and heaven in communion, focuses on free exchange between above and below. Water is soft and yielding, needing earth to give it form—as Bi emphasizes serving the right person; the energies of earth and heaven interact and give rise to all things, echoing Tai's 'the small goes, the great comes.' When these two hexagrams meet, they create a dynamic balance: Bi's cohesive power provides a stable base for Tai's circulation, while Tai's open expansiveness in turn helps Bi break free from overly exclusive attachment. But Bi's warning that 'the latecomer suffers misfortune' cautions that hesitation can cost one the first move, and Tai's command to 'complete and assist' requires actively harmonizing resources. If one side becomes too dependent or the other pushes for shortcuts, the rhythm will be thrown off.
resonance: ★ Kinship builds strength, gathering what was scattered
★ Free exchange between above and below, living and flourishing together
conflict: ◆ Hesitating to choose the good vs. rushing with the current
◆ Huddling in mutual dependence vs. breaking through on one's own
advice: Each month, together set the dual goal of 'Closeness and Flow': deepen the core bond while opening to cross-boundary resource exchange.

one_liner: Treading the same earth, yet walking yin-yang paths
analysis: The Bi hexagram (Water over Earth) merges water and earth, governing kinship and cohesion; the Pi hexagram (Heaven over Earth) keeps heaven and earth apart, governing blockage and self-preservation. Both share the lower trigram Kun (Earth), which lays a pragmatic foundation, but the opposing natures of their upper trigrams—Water and Heaven—create tension: Bi actively connects through its moist, nourishing nature, while Pi retreats into self-protection with its clear, unbending stance. The open pattern of the hexagram text, “establishing the myriad states and befriending the feudal lords,” is mirrored in reverse by Pi’s retrenchment strategy, “curbing virtue to escape hardship.” The image text’s “water over the earth” permeability meets the barrier of “heaven and earth not joining.” This structure makes the relationship one of “externally open, internally blocked,” and calls for finding a channel for Water–Heaven energy to transform within the shared stability of Kun earth.
resonance: ★ Building a grounded foundation together
★ Upholding shared bottom-line principles
conflict: ◆ Active connection vs. passive defense
◆ Emotional flow vs. rational detachment
advice: Set a monthly “wall-breaking dialogue day,” replacing abstract ideological debates with concrete collaboration.

one_liner: When down-to-earth water meets a light-chasing sky, they turn the warmth of everyday life into starlight.
analysis: In Bi (Holding Together), water and earth merge, using gentle compliance to gather the grassroots; in Tong Ren (Fellowship with Men), heaven and fire shine together, using strength and clarity to lead ideals. Water's virtue nourishes all things silently; it chooses well and attaches to what is good, turning dispersion into cohesion. Heaven's virtue is lofty and broad; it distinguishes kinds and things, seeking common ground while respecting differences. When the two intersect, water's inclusiveness softens heaven's edge, and heaven's clarity guides water's course—forming a cycle of 'earth supporting heaven, heaven illuminating water.' Yet water can easily become entangled in human feelings, and heaven can drift into vague idealism. One must remain clear-eyed in intimacy and respect differences while seeking commonality.
resonance: ★ A centripetal force of softness and strength complementing each other
★ Resonance of closeness and shared purpose
conflict: ◆ The rhythm gap between pragmatic inclusiveness and idealism
◆ Misalignment between grassroots bonding and high-level vision
advice: Set aside half a day each month to discuss concrete goals and realistic paths. Use Bi's listening to ease Tong Ren's impatience, and Tong Ren's vision to broaden Bi's boundaries.

one_liner: Drawing close gathers force, meeting the light uplifts good; water over earth stirs waves, fire under heaven lights the way.
analysis: The Holding Together hexagram, with water over earth, mutually nourishes — drawing hearts together through gentle compliance. The Great Possession hexagram, with fire over heaven, shines in concert — gathering resources widely through radiant integrity. Water's downward moistening and fire's upward blazing create a dynamic balance: Holding Together's 'choose the good and follow it' provides a solid foundation for Great Possession, while Great Possession's 'restrain evil and exalt good' gives direction to Holding Together. Their intersection is like rivers converging at the sea, reflecting the morning sun — the power of closeness is magnified by radiance, and the harvest is more abundant because of the unity beneath it. Yet beware: Holding Together can drift into over-reliance and lose self-determination, or Great Possession can become so fiercely bright that it harms harmony. Let water's tolerance temper fire's intensity.
resonance: ★ Resonance of gathering through closeness and uplifting good through radiance
★ The same frequency of choosing the good and following Heaven's benevolent decree
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war between gentle reliance and firm, bright principle
◆ The balance between networks of personal feeling and orders of impartial justice
advice: Build transparent cooperative structures — sustain your network with Holding Together's inclusiveness, and use Great Possession's criteria to select core partners.

relationship_name: Tenderness and Humility in Mutual Support
one_liner: Water flows close to the earth; the mountain stands with hidden humility. One leans in actively, the other receives with quiet grace.
analysis: Holding Together is Water over Earth, with affinity and unity at its core, stressing the centripetal force of choosing what is good and following it. Modesty has a mountain within the Earth, taking humble restraint and balance as its path, focusing on the harmonizing power of reducing the excessive to benefit the deficient. When the two meet, the fluidity of Holding Together can activate the steady depth of Modesty, while Modesty's inclusiveness can dissolve the risk of Holding Together's over-attachment. Water and Earth mirror each other in a dynamic nourishment, yet one must heed the potential rhythm mismatch between Holding Together's eager closeness and Modesty's retiring stance. By nature, water is soft and earth is rich; in the Image texts, the expansion of 'establishing the ten thousand states' and the restraint of 'weighing things and distributing evenly' are two sides of the same whole, constituting a symbiotic structure of outward reach and inward reticence.
resonance: ★ The centripetal force of water and earth in mutual embrace
★ The all-embracing inclusiveness of humble bearing
conflict: ◆ The rhythm gap between eager closeness and reserved retreat
◆ The hidden peril of imbalance between over-dependence and over-yielding
advice: Establish a regular feedback loop. The Bi partner should temper any tendency to over-seek closeness, while the Qian partner should show their boundaries when appropriate. Let 'close without familiarity, humble without servility' be the guiding principle of the relationship.

one_liner: Same root, different branches; water and thunder dance together, drawing hearts into one.
analysis: The Bi hexagram [Holding Together] blends water and earth, grounding itself in gentle compliance and closeness; the Yu hexagram [Enthusiasm] stirs thunder over earth, building momentum through harmony and spirited action. Both share Earth as the lower trigram, laying a foundation of stable cooperation, while the upper trigrams — Water and Thunder — create a subtle tension: Water's inclusiveness moistens Thunder's vigor, and Thunder's rousing energy awakens Water's stillness. In the judgments, Bi emphasizes the centripetal power of 'following what is good,' and Yu speaks of the impetus of 'founding vassals and mobilizing armies.' Together, this pairing must infuse closeness with a sense of purpose and keep an enterprising rhythm within harmony. The Image texts — 'establishing ten thousand states and uniting the vassals' and 'making music and honoring virtue' — echo each other, revealing that this relationship needs institutions to consolidate consensus and culture to nourish vitality. But beware: if Water becomes too soft, direction is lost; if Thunder grows too restless, harmony shatters.
resonance: ★ Shared Foundation, Mutual Flourishing
★ Water and Thunder in Harmony
conflict: ◆ Thunder Rushes, Water Lingers
◆ Overindulgence in Joy Breeds Complacency
advice: Set stage-by-stage goals together each month; use the Bi hexagram's 'closeness' to build bonds of trust, and Yu's 'moving with the times' to seize the right moments for action. Avoid falling into unprincipled agreement or blind optimism.

one_liner: You pave the road, I build the bridge—we go with the flow instead of butting heads.
analysis: Holding Together lays a foundation for closeness through the inclusiveness of water gathering on the earth's surface; Following echoes the shifting currents of the times with the flexibility of a lake storing thunder. Both contain the core of 'choosing what is good and abiding by it,' but Holding Together emphasizes actively building a web of relationships (establishing states and drawing near the feudal lords), while Following focuses on dynamically adjusting the rhythm of survival (retiring to rest at nightfall). The meeting of water and lake creates a symbiotic system of permeation and support: Holding Together provides the emotional adhesive, Following supplies the lubricant for adaptation. When the centripetal force of Holding Together meets the fluidity of Following, a collaborative model of 'stability amid change' arises—but beware: if Holding Together becomes too dependent, Following may lose its initiative; if Following shifts course too frequently, it can erode the trust that anchors Holding Together.
resonance: ★ Resonance in choosing the good
★ Synergizing with the flow
conflict: ◆ Tempo differences
◆ The tug-of-war between proactive and passive
advice: Set a fixed communication day each month to calibrate your rhythm; the Holding Together partner should give the Following partner room to flex in decision-making.

one_liner: First be each other's shelter, then the relationship's cleanser — true love isn't afraid of a deep cleanse.
analysis: The Bi hexagram, 'Water over Earth,' governs closeness and cohesion; the Gu hexagram, 'Wind under Mountain,' governs clearing away decay and disorder. Their intersection is like using the tender force of Bi to build a foundation of trust, then using Gu's sharp vigor to sweep away hidden ailments. Bi's line 'the latecomer meets misfortune' warns against hesitation; Gu's text 'before the first day, after the third day' emphasizes preparation. When water and earth meet mountain and wind, a chemical reaction forms: first rally hearts, then clear out chronic ills. Bi provides safety, preventing Gu's radical healing from triggering a collapse; Gu breaks the old to establish the new, preventing Bi's excessive closeness from degenerating into cliquishness. The two balance motion and stillness, keeping clarity within intimacy and deepening the bond through rectification.
resonance: ★ Frequency alignment: both seek a long-term, stable, healthy ecosystem
★ Complementary pace: one builds the stage and gathers people, the other clears obstacles and defuses mines
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythm: one wants to bond warmly and stabilize at once, the other insists on coldly settling old accounts
◆ Handling the balance: too much clinging becomes whitewashing, too much rectification hurts the relationship's foundation
advice: Agree on a monthly 'clear-wind tea talk.' Begin with Bi's inclusiveness to affirm each other's efforts, then use Gu's orderly method to list what needs changing. Follow the 'before and after the first day' rhythm of preparation and implement step by step, turning radical healing into a ritual of mutual upgrading.

one_liner: One knows how to huddle close for warmth, the other knows how to hold up a lantern and lead the way — together, they create a healing space of mutual devotion.
analysis: The Bi hexagram — Water over Earth — governs closeness and attachment; its gentle water seeks common resonance by moistening all below. The Lin hexagram — Earth above Lake — governs teaching and deliberation; its thick earth looks down from above, emphasizing long-term guidance. Water and soil merge into a field where the lower nourishes and the upper supports: Bi's 'primordial, enduring, steadfastness' provides lasting cohesion, while Lin's 'inexhaustible teaching and reflection' supplies the framework for growth. But Bi's warning that 'the one who comes late meets misfortune' pushes for timely alignment, and Lin's warning of 'misfortune in the eighth month' cautions that fullness inevitably declines. When the two meet, beware of missing the moment, and even more, avoid overdependence that drains vitality. Only by meeting Bi's clinging with Lin's inclusiveness can one-way pursuit become symbiosis.
resonance: ★ Natural trust when gentle water meets deep earth
★ A kindred resonance between choosing what is good and teaching without end
conflict: ◆ The timing mismatch between the fear of being late and the anxiety of peaking
◆ The tug-of-war at the boundary between a leading stance and a dependent heart
advice: Set aside regular judgment-free listening time; let Approach pause its lecturing to hold Holding Together's emotional needs, and dissolve blind following with clear goal planning.

one_liner: Bonding calls for clear eyes; observing calls for a heart that draws near.
analysis: Holding Together (Bǐ) blends water with earth, centering on closeness and unity, and stresses the centripetal force of choosing the good to follow. Contemplation (Guān) moves wind across the earth, focusing on insight and instruction, and values the discerning power of surveying the land and observing the people. Their shared lower trigram, Earth, lays a pragmatic foundation for both. The flow of water and the spread of wind create a unique interplay: Holding Together's closeness needs Contemplation's clear guidance to avoid clinging blindly; Contemplation's observation needs Holding Together's warmth to take root, preventing it from hardening into detachment. Together, they are like water nourishing all things without contention and wind shaping the intangible while reaching everywhere—in common soil, they cultivate a symbiosis that honors both connection and discernment.
resonance: ★ Same Roots, Symbiotic Growth
★ Wind Nourishes, Waters Merge
conflict: ◆ Water Overflows, Wind Scatters
◆ Over-Observation Drives Kinship Apart
advice: Each month, set one practical goal together. Test your observations through concrete action, and avoid drifting apart through empty talk.

one_liner: Intimacy with boundaries, warmth hidden within rules.
analysis: The Bi hexagram—Water over Earth—governs closeness and unity. Its Judgement says, 'The restless come at last,' emphasizing the gathering of people through gentleness and choosing what is good. The Shi He hexagram—Fire over Thunder—governs the clarity of punishment and the setting of laws. Its Judgement says, 'It furthers one to use the law,' emphasizing biting through obstructions and establishing order. The all-embracing nature of water and the bright intensity of fire meet here, creating a unique field in which feeling and law sustain each other. Bi provides the adhesive for the relationship, softening Shi He's strictness with the moistening grace of water on earth. Shi He, in turn, draws clear bottom lines, keeping Bi's closeness from slipping into unprincipled indulgence. Their intersection is like governance: the benevolence that draws near to the people and the authority that clarifies punishments must carry equal weight. Set rules in intimacy; hide warmth in just severity.
resonance: ★ Complementary softness and strength, with feeling and law in mutual cultivation
★ Intimacy with boundaries, rules with warmth
conflict: ◆ Bi's emphasis on human sentiment can easily cross lines; Shi He's emphasis on principle can appear cold
◆ Excessive closeness breeds dependence; overly severe punishment damages harmony
advice: When disagreement arises, first use Bi's listening and acceptance to create an emotional bond; then apply Shi He's clear rules to define responsibilities. Reach the heart before you appeal to reason.

one_liner: One values inner unity; the other, outer polish. They're perfectly in step yet often bicker over tempo.
analysis: Pi (Holding Together) is waterlike in nature: fluid, clinging, and emphasizing the cohesive power of choosing the good to follow. Bi (Grace) is mountainlike in nature: stable, adorned, and pursuing a civilized, measured expression. Together they are like a stream winding around a mountain, with fire upon the mountain casting its glow on the water. Pi's 'uniting with the princes' needs Bi's 'clarifying the many affairs of government' to give it form; Bi's 'not daring to settle lawsuits' needs Pi's 'the restless come from all directions' to give it real trust. Yet when water spreads too far, it erodes the mountain; when fire grows too hot, it boils the water. An excess of togetherness loses proportion; an excess of ornament hides the genuine. The task is to stay clear-sighted within closeness and to keep the core safe within adornment.
resonance: ★ Soft and firm interweave to form a vista.
★ Cultivating inner and outer alike in search of harmony.
conflict: ◆ Closeness pace vs. embellishment patience
◆ Penetrating substance vs. hardening form
advice: Set aside half a day each month for deep dialogue—use the honesty of Pi (Holding Together) to calibrate the glamour of Bi (Grace), and let the mountain fire light the direction of the water.

one_liner: Same root, different branches; stick together to guard against decay.
analysis: The Hexagram of Holding Together blends Water over Earth, gaining good fortune through closeness and unity, like water flowing to nourish the land. The Hexagram of Splitting Apart stacks Mountain over Earth, halting decline by thickening the foundation and securing the home, like rocks stabilizing the base. Both share the lower trigram Kun (The Receptive), embodying the quality of inclusiveness and support, but the upper trigrams—Kan (The Abysmal) Water and Gen (Keeping Still) Mountain—create a dynamic tension between motion and stillness. The fluidity of Holding Together can activate the rigidity of Splitting Apart, while the depth of Splitting Apart anchors the superficiality of Holding Together. When water meets the mountain's foundation, the power of closeness transforms into a barrier against collapse; when the mountain supports the water's force, the threat of decline becomes an opportunity for deep accumulation and eventual breakthrough. This pair of hexagrams reveals: those who share the same root must use movement to temper stillness and stillness to nourish movement, so as to find balance between closeness and preservation.
resonance: ★ Shared Foundation
★ Closeness Resists Decline
conflict: ◆ The Pull Between Movement and Stillness
◆ The Conflict Between Dependence and Isolation
advice: Each month, jointly advance one foundational project: the partner embodying Holding Together takes the lead in connecting resources, while the partner embodying Splitting Apart focuses on steady execution. Review regularly to prevent decline.

relationship_name: Moistening and Returning with One Heart
one_liner: When you huddle together for warmth, don't forget to leave a charging dock for your original aspiration.
analysis: In Holding Together, water flows over the earth and gathers strength through closeness; in Return, thunder lies dormant in the earth and revives life through cycling. Water and earth nourish each other, yet they differ in movement and stillness: Holding Together reaches outward to forge alliances, while Return stores energy inward, waiting to break through the soil. When the two meet, water's inclusiveness softens earth's fixedness, and earth's steadiness anchors water's flow. The Judgment's words 'the restless come' and 'on the seventh day comes return' strike a strange resonance — when a group draws together out of disquiet, Return's cyclical law reminds us that true unity must pass through settling and renewal. The Image's open posture of 'drawing near the feudal lords' and the contracting wisdom of 'closing the passes' are like in-breath and out-breath — a measured rhythm of tension and release.
resonance: ★ Water moistens the earth's veins; closeness nourishes the root of renewal.
★ Cycles spin and return; within collaboration hides a rhythm of rebirth.
conflict: ◆ Water seeks speed while thunder waits its hour — a mismatch of timing.
◆ Closing the passes to nurse stillness versus reaching out to all the lords — a tug between withdrawal and embrace.
advice: Set a monthly dual rhythm of 'collaborate and contemplate': in the first half, push cooperation forward; in the second half, each person reviews and recharges. Let Return's cycle discipline Holding Together's bonds.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Intimacy and Truth
one_liner: Intimacy wins true hearts; authenticity gathers a fated bond.
analysis: The Hexagram Bi (Holding Together) blends water over earth, drawing people near through gentle compliance. The Hexagram Wu Wang (Innocence) has thunder rolling beneath heaven, following the Dao of Heaven with uprightness and truth. Their meeting is like earth receiving water from above: closeness must root in sincerity, and truth must allow for tolerance. Bi's warning that 'the one who comes too late meets misfortune' reminds us that hesitation opens fissures. Wu Wang's caution that 'incorrect persistence brings calamity' emphasizes staying true to the right path. Together they form a dynamic balance—water's moistening softens heaven's rigor, while heaven's clarity directs water's course. Closeness need not become blind conformity, nor truth become aloof isolation. Only then can one realize the grand pattern of 'uniting all nations' and the vital energy that 'nourishes all things.'
resonance: ★ The centripetal pull of choosing the good and following it
★ A clear mind that stays upright without compromise
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war between gentle dependence and upright independence
◆ The dissonance between the rhythm of closeness and the timing of Heaven
advice: When drawing close, examine your motives with sincerity. When acting, align your direction with the Dao of Heaven. Do not let personal feelings replace principle.

one_liner: Drawing close like water gathers momentum; storing virtue like a mountain steadies the foundation; together, they achieve.
analysis: The Bi hexagram (Holding Together), Water over Earth, emphasizes proactive connection and attaching to what is good; the Daxu hexagram (The Taming Power of the Great), Mountain over Heaven, focuses on deep accumulation of virtue and far-sighted strategy. Water is soft and moist, able to penetrate the cracks of mountain rock; the mountain, steady and solid, can nurture the vitality of water sources. Together they form a symbiotic structure of 'expanding an external network of people, while internally building a storehouse of strength.' The saying in Bi, 'the late-comer meets with misfortune,' warns that hesitation misses opportunities; in Daxu, 'advantageous to cross the great river' requires stored energy to break through. The combination reveals a dynamic balance: gathering resources through closeness, and setting direction through accumulated virtue. Where the images merge, it is like a river winding around a mountain — borrowing the mountain's mass to store force, while the watercourse expands the terrain.
resonance: ★ Drawing close like water naturally gathers a network of people.
★ Storing virtue like a mountain settles a far-reaching vision.
conflict: ◆ Over-attachment can blur the core of decision-making.
◆ Closed-door cultivation of virtue struggles to respond to external changes.
advice: Each month, jointly draft a 'Connection Checklist' and a 'Cultivation Plan' — use Bi's movement to expand your social circle, and Daxu's stillness to consolidate core strength.

relationship_name: Mutual Arising of Stream and Peak
one_liner: Reach outward, nourish within; movement and stillness move in step.
analysis: The Holding Together hexagram, with its water virtue, governs closeness and intermingling; the Nourishment hexagram, with its mountain nature, emphasizes cultivation and holding to the center. Water spreads across the earth into a web, symbolizing the openness of human connection; thunder hides below the mountain and accumulates momentum, echoing the stabilizing power of inner restraint. When the two meet, they form a tension field of 'expand outward, guard within': the 'restless come' of Holding Together drives relationships to break out of their circles, while the 'careful speech and moderate eating' of Nourishment anchors the boundaries of energy. Water meeting the mountain divides its flow and stores strength; the mountain receiving water becomes moist and sprouts growth — just like the yin-yang interlocking of social networks and personal cultivation, preventing both over-dependence and self-consuming isolation.
resonance: ★ The same frequency of outward networking and inward cultivation
★ The complementary pairing of bonding for mutual gain and self-cultivation in quiet discipline
conflict: ◆ The rhythm mismatch between rapid wide-net connecting and slow deep nurturing
◆ The value clash between flowing with circumstance and holding fast to boundaries
advice: Each month, alternate leadership between 'outward-expanding social days' and 'inward-reflection retreat days'; use the connective power of Holding Together to activate the nourishing field of Nourishment, and use the moderating power of Nourishment to filter out the superfluous socializing of Holding Together.

one_liner: Together, as steady as a rock; alone, bold enough to break convention.
analysis: The Bi hexagram (Holding Together), with its image of water over earth, speaks of closeness and unity, emphasizing the inclusiveness of following what is good. The Da Guo hexagram (Preponderance of the Great), with its image of the lake flooding the tree, embodies independence without fear and the boldness to break the mold. When the two meet, it is like still water encountering a rushing current: the cohesion of Bi provides a foundation for Da Guo's surpassing, while Da Guo's enterprising spirit injects the momentum to break through impasses. Yet the nature of water and lake conceals tension: Bi's warning that "the latecomer brings misfortune" cautions that over-dependence may drag down Da Guo's "ridgepole bending" momentum, while Da Guo's solitary advance can easily disrupt the cooperative ecosystem of Bi's "establishing the myriad states." Only by tempering the hardness of the lake with the softness of water can one reveal the symbiotic wisdom of "attachment without entrapment, independence without isolation."
resonance: ★ Stillness and Motion Complement: The Rhythmic Resonance of Inclusiveness and Breakthrough
★ Foundation and Edge: A Stable Framework Uplifts Extraordinary Endeavors
conflict: ◆ Seeking Stability and Playing It Safe vs. Winning Through Risk: A Mismatch in Decision-Making Tempo
◆ Excessive Reliance vs. Deep Lone Forays: A Tug-of-War Over Boundaries
advice: Establish "anchor-point collaboration": before major actions, use the consensus of Bi to align direction; during execution, grant Da Guo its independent space; and periodically recalibrate the ratio of intimacy and autonomy.

one_liner: In the same perilous current, unity alone can split the waves.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together) shows water over earth; it governs closeness and choosing the worthy. Kan (The Abysmal) shows water flowing double; it governs cultivating virtue amid danger. Both share the upper trigram Water, inheriting a common 'crossing the rapids' nature — but Bi’s lower trigram is Earth, favoring stable bonds, while Kan’s lower trigram is Water, emphasizing dynamic breakthrough. Their guiding texts — “primordial divination, sublime and eternal constancy” and “the abyss rehearsed, holding sincerity” — weave together into a symbiosis where trust is the anchor and affinity is the boat: Bi’s discernment in selecting companions gives direction to Kan’s repeated perils, while Kan’s disciplined practice instills resilience into Bi’s unity. Yet when the current runs too strong, hidden undercurrents arise — beware that the hesitation of “the latecomer suffers misfortune” does not collide with the lone stubbornness of “the heart’s clarity prevails.”
resonance: ★ United in Adversity
★ Integrity as the Foundation
conflict: ◆ Clash of Steady and Swift
◆ Undercurrents Breeding Distrust
advice: When disagreements arise, negotiate openly in the spirit of Bi’s 'allying with the feudal lords,' and use Kan’s 'repeated practice and teaching' to regularly recalibrate the baseline of trust.

relationship_name: Water and Fire Nourish Each Other
one_liner: With your gentle water you bear my bright flame; with my light I guide you into closeness.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together), with water over earth, symbolizes affinity and solidarity; Li (The Clinging), with fire and brightness, represents attachment and radiance. Water is gentle and inclusive, able to bear the intensity of Li's fire without being extinguished; fire is bright and guiding, keeping Bi's affinity from lapsing into blind following. The image texts 'Build many states, be close to the feudal lords' and 'Following brightness, shine in all four directions' echo each other, and their union forms a structured collaborative network: Bi provides cohesion and adaptability, while Li injects sustained drive and clear vision. Water and fire, though different in nature, interact not by overcoming but by generating each other. Gentle water tempers fire's restlessness; bright fire warms water's cold. In dynamic balance, they realize a symbiotic relationship of 'affinity has its way, radiance never dies.'
resonance: ★ Gentle water carries fire, radiance shines without end
★ Affinity is principled, light shines in all directions
conflict: ◆ Water prevails and fire dies, light and dark fall out of balance
◆ Closeness becomes excess, and the light is blocked
advice: Periodically use Li's clear goals to recalibrate Bi's collaborative direction, avoiding overdependence or draining your enthusiasm.

one_liner: When rational solidarity meets intuitive attraction, even a slow simmer can stew up a match made in heaven.
analysis: The Holding Together hexagram has water over the earth, signifying choosing the good and drawing close to it, valuing order and long-term commitment, and cautioning against hesitation and lagging behind. The Influence hexagram has a lake on the mountain, signifying spontaneous resonance, valuing emotional attunement and open-hearted receptivity. Water and lake spring from the same source, yet in relationship they present a collision between rational alliance and intuitive heart-throb. Bi's warning that 'those who arrive late will meet harm' calls for clear and decisive commitment; Xian's virtue of 'emptying oneself to receive others' leans toward natural, unforced expression. If the sturdy framework of Bi can be transformed into an emotional vessel for Xian, structure can nourish intuition, and sincerity can cement the covenant. Water and earth nurture each other; lake and water flow freely together. The resulting bond is outwardly stable and inwardly sensitive, growing deeper with time.
resonance: ★ The steadfast sense of choosing the good and acting on it
★ The inclusive power of welcoming with an open heart
conflict: ◆ Pacing mismatch: Bi's urgent commitment clashes with Xian's go-with-the-flow testing
◆ Framework constraint: Bi's rule-driven orientation squelches Xian's spontaneous expression
advice: Establish regular emotional alignment and carve out deliberate alone time. Use Bi's covenant spirit to clarify relationship boundaries, and let Xian's quiet emptiness keep emotions flowing—never use obligation to hijack intuition.

one_liner: Follow water to gather momentum and shape the field; borrow thunder to hold the heart and break the impasse.
analysis: The Hexagram Bi (Holding Together), through the mingling of water and earth, symbolizes affinity and unity, emphasizing the fluid wisdom of choosing the good and following it. The Hexagram Heng (Duration), through the close interplay of thunder and wind, reveals the steadfast power of enduring constancy. Water's gentle moisture resolves thunder's intensity, while thunder's kinetic energy activates water's stillness. Their interplay creates a dynamic balance: Bi's 'uniting the many states and drawing near the feudal lords' requires the grounding support of Heng's 'standing firm without changing direction,' and Heng's endurance relies on Bi's ability to gather people by going with the flow. The chemistry of soil-and-water nourishment and thunder-and-wind agitation is like a river meeting a canyon—it needs both inclusive meandering and purposeful rushing forward.
resonance: ★ The centripetal force that pools momentum into a deep well
★ The fixed star that breaks the deadlock and lays the foundation
conflict: ◆ Shifting with the current vs. holding fast without moving
◆ Affinity networks vs. independent principles
advice: Each month, draw up a 'change and constancy' list: the Bi side takes the lead in adjusting collaborative methods, the Heng side guards the core rules, and execute water-like flexible plans with thunder-like decisiveness.

relationship_name: The Balance of Gathering and Parting
one_liner: Close, you huddle for warmth; apart, you each walk your own path.
analysis: Water over Earth (Bi, Holding Together) coalesces all things through moisture, while Heaven over Mountain (Dun, Retreat) sets limits through lofty distance. The inclusiveness of Bi (the image of 'water over earth') and the detachment of Dun ('heaven above the mountain') form a dynamic balance: when the waters overflow, the mountain provides an anchor against dispersal; when the mountain grows too steep, the water softens its edges to keep it from isolation. The hexagram texts — 'Those who are not at peace come' and 'keeping distant from petty people' — reveal the core tension: drawing near requires choosing what is good to follow, while retreating calls for clear-sighted resolve. The Image text's 'building ten thousand kingdoms' symbolizes active connection, while its 'without aversion yet with dignity' symbolizes restrained distance — together they compose a rhythm of closeness and release that feels effortless.
resonance: ★ Choose the good and befriend them
★ Know when to step back
conflict: ◆ Over-clinging
◆ Deliberate distance
advice: When drawing close, keep your personal boundaries clear; when stepping back, keep a channel of kind communication open.

one_liner: Soft water gathers power to meet strong thunder; courteous closeness alone completes the design.
analysis: In Holding Together, water rests upon the earth, drawing people's hearts together through gentle compliance and close attachment; its Judgment stresses following what is good. In The Power of the Great, thunder moves across the heavens, establishing authority through firm vigor and ritual propriety; its Image clearly states that no step is taken beyond propriety. When the two meet, the tolerance of soft water requires the standard of strong thunder to define boundaries, while the might of strong thunder requires the moistening of soft water to dissolve rash advance. The warning in Holding Together—'Whoever comes late meets misfortune'—serves as a caution that those who attach themselves tardily miss the moment, and this precisely calls for The Power of the Great's decisive steadfastness as expressed in 'perseverance furthers.' Conversely, if The Power of the Great's fierce hardness lacks the harmonic attachment of Holding Together, it easily becomes an army of one. The crossing of these differing hexagrams yields a unique tension—'binding closeness with ritual, transforming hardness with closeness'—like a river confronting thunder: it must be channeled and also revered.
resonance: ★ Attachment with propriety builds a shared foundation
★ Soft and firm in mutual aid, action and rest observe due measure
conflict: ◆ Water's force overflows, boundaries easily lost
◆ Impulsive thunder disdains all indirection
advice: Let propriety and law serve as the framework for intimacy, and periodically recalibrate resolute decisions with a soft, unhurried stance.

one_liner: You are rooted, steady as the earth; I rise, radiant as the dawn. United, we flourish; divided, we wound each other.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together) — water over earth — gathers momentum through gentle affinity and closeness; Jin (Progress) — fire over earth — breaks through deadlock with radiant initiative. Their lower trigrams are both Kun (the Receptive) earth, forming a stable foundation of trust. But the upper trigrams, water and fire, create dynamic tension: Bi's 'restless ones come at last' needs Jin's 'the light rises above the earth' to dissolve hesitation with clear direction; Jin's 'three audiences in a day' needs Bi's 'close to the feudal lords' to temper its edge with acceptance. When water and earth nourish each other, Bi's cohesive power paves the way for Jin's pioneering, and Jin's radiant virtue feeds back into Bi's standard of choosing the good. If water and fire lose their balance, Bi's clinging can turn into Jin's exhaustion, and Jin's impatience can scorch Bi's warmth.
resonance: ★ Rooted and Co-growing (The lower Kun-earth of both hexagrams builds a shared foundation of trust)
★ Mutual Illumination (Jin's radiant virtue lights up Bi's discerning eye for the good)
conflict: ◆ Water and Fire Clash (A frequency mismatch between the pace of advancement and the need for closeness)
◆ Interplay of Light and Dark (The tension between Jin's outward brilliance and Bi's inward conservatism)
advice: Each month, set a shared 'rooting plan' and 'breakthrough goal.' Use Bi's listening to settle Jin's impulse, and Jin's clarity to give direction to Bi's inclination to attach.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Dark and Light
one_liner: Water gathers on the earth, drawing together for warmth — a symbiosis that hides its edge.
analysis: The Hexagram of Holding Together (Bi) — water over earth — speaks to closeness, unity, and mutual reliance. The Hexagram of Darkening of the Light (Mingyi) — earth over fire — speaks to sheathing one's brilliance and biding one's time. Water flows only because the earth bears it, just as Bi gathers and connects; fire lies buried beneath the earth yet still holds its spark, teaching the wisdom of keeping one's integrity through hardship. When these two hexagrams meet, a graceful chemistry forms: the open, inclusive nature of Bi softens the solitary, guarded quality of Mingyi, while the patience and depth of Mingyi give Bi's striving for connection a deeper root. But when the elements of water, fire, and earth interweave, too much clinging may crowd out the independent space Mingyi needs, and Mingyi's strategic concealment may in turn erode the transparent trust that Bi depends on.
resonance: ★ A foundational resonance between a supportive, clinging spirit and a persevering, self-contained resolve.
★ A rhythmic fit between the bearing quality of water-and-earth and the mutual arising of clarity and shadow.
conflict: ◆ Friction at the boundary between the need for open unity and the wish to keep a hidden edge.
◆ A tension between yielding, solid gentleness and the smothered restlessness of a bright fire.
advice: In partnership, build trust on the candid openness of Holding Together, and use the reticence of Darkening of the Light to leave each other room to settle and breathe.

one_liner: Outwardly, forge kindred bonds; inwardly, hold to the family way. When strength and grace entwine, your own pattern takes shape.
analysis: The Bi hexagram (Holding Together) shows water and earth merging to teach the art of belonging; the Family hexagram shows wind and fire generating each other to reveal the order of the household. Water is gentle and gathers easily; wind is free-flowing and transforms all it touches. Their meeting creates a living balance of 'reaching outward, guarding within.' The open design of Bi — 'binding the many states and uniting the feudal lords' — needs the steady core of Family — 'words with substance, deeds with constancy' — to stay on course. And the Family's principle of right living, through Bi's gift of choosing the good, learns to expand beyond its own walls. Water and soil nourish the growing of all things; wind and fire light up the hidden depths. This pairing builds a bridge between the world of people and the values of home, so that belonging never becomes hollow, and family rules never become brittle.
resonance: ★ Water nourishes, wind spreads — affinity flowers into love.
★ Household upright, words constant — order takes firm root.
conflict: ◆ When water floods and wind races, inner and outer fall into disarray.
◆ Clinging too tightly makes house rules hard to uphold.
advice: Hold a monthly 'Household and Community Council Day,' using the hexagrams' guidance to balance outer connections with inner discipline.

one_liner: Water gathers, fire disperses; even in unity, difference gives rise to destiny.
analysis: The Bi hexagram, water over earth, governs closeness and unity, like water gathering on the ground to nourish all things. The Kui hexagram, fire over lake, governs divergence and coexistence, like fire blazing upward while the lake moistens below. Water's gentleness embraces fire's intensity; fire's brightness illumines water's darkness. Their interplay creates a dynamic balance: Bi's impulse to unite softens Kui's tendency toward estrangement, while Kui's independent awareness prevents Bi from sinking into blind conformity. In the judgments, Bi warns that "those who come later meet misfortune," cautioning against forced unanimity; Kui's "small matters bring good fortune" suggests seeking subtle harmony within difference. The Images—"enfeoffing the myriad states and uniting the princes" and "commonality within difference"—further reveal that macroscopic unity rests on microscopic tolerance.
resonance: ★ Water and lake intermingle; tolerance turns difference into sacred bond
★ Fire's light shines on water; divergence reveals essential truth
conflict: ◆ Fire and water clash; closeness meets the obstacle of independence
◆ Earth and lake misaligned; unity gives rise to conflicting directions
advice: Hold a monthly 'Divergent Views Tea Gathering': first share a pot of tea to establish Bi's closeness, then take turns voicing differing viewpoints to practice Kui's divergence—using ritual to solidify a rhythm of seeking common ground while honoring difference.

one_liner: Drinking from the same river — one builds dikes and channels, the other cuts through mountains and opens roads.
analysis: The outer trigrams of both hexagrams are Kan (The Abysmal), water, symbolizing shared fluidity and a common sense of crisis, but the inner trigrams—Kun (The Receptive), earth, and Gen (Keeping Still), mountain—create a subtle tension. In Bi (Holding Together), 'water over earth' embraces all things with gentleness, emphasizing closeness and cohesion; in Jian (Obstruction), 'water over the mountain' meets obstacles and detours, focusing on inner reflection and breaking through. Water virtue splits here: Bi dissolves danger through moistening, while Jian gathers strength by stillness, awaiting its time. When the two meet, Bi's instinct to connect can soften Jian's solitary aloofness, while Jian's prudence can anchor Bi's indiscriminate sociability. Beware Bi's over-compromise diluting principles, and Jian's excessive inwardness causing missed opportunities.
resonance: ★ Shared radar for crisis
★ Survival wisdom of yielding to conquer
conflict: ◆ Seeking closeness through accommodation vs. Standing guard in self-reliance
◆ Going with the flow vs. Cultivating the heart against the current
advice: Set aside a 'Water Mirror Day' each month: let Bi lead open dialogue to gather resources, then let Jian lead closed-door review to recalibrate direction—use ritual alternation to balance outward expansion and inner guarding.

one_liner: You set the stage, I break the ice — kindred understanding tears down every wall.
analysis: Holding Together is like water seeping into the earth, drawing people close through affinity; Deliverance is like thunder splitting the clouds, shattering deadlocks with its shock. Their convergence forms a unique magnetic field—'still waters run deep, melting the hardest ice.' The inclusiveness of Holding Together provides the soil for Deliverance's pardon, while Deliverance's explosive energy feeds back into Holding Together's unity. But water tends to be enduring while thunder strikes suddenly, and their rhythms can easily fall out of step. One must anchor the impetuous wisdom of 'early fortune' with the steadfastness of 'primordial constancy,' and only then can lasting harmony emerge through forgiveness and grace.
resonance: ★ Affinity and absolution share a common root.
★ Flexibility provides the foundation for breakthrough.
conflict: ◆ Steady pace vs. sharp edge of change.
◆ Gentle reserve vs. restless expenditure.
advice: On the first and fifteenth of each lunar month, share a cup of clear tea, review backlogged matters, and let the long-lasting moisture of Holding Together dissolve the sudden eruptions of Deliverance.

one_liner: You gather hearts; I refine my own. One outward, one inward—together a complete whole.
analysis: Hexagram Holding Together is like water upon the earth, rooted in closeness and unity, emphasizing the choice of what is good and the cultivation of wide-ranging connections. Hexagram Decrease resembles a marsh below the mountain, centered on diminishing and refining virtue, advocating the suppression of anger and desire and the settling of the self inward. Water's nature flows and nourishes all things; the mountain's nature is steady and sheathes its edge. Where the two intersect, a dynamic balance emerges between 'outward expansion and connection' and 'inward cultivation and restraint.' The openness and inclusiveness of Holding Together can dissolve Decrease's tendency toward excessive self-examination, while Decrease's rational restraint can temper Holding Together's over-dependence. Together they form a unique complementarity between the management of relationships and the discipline of self-cultivation.
resonance: ★ Building a Foundation of Trust Together
★ Cultivating Inner and Outer Balance Together
conflict: ◆ The Rhythm Gap Between Flow and Stasis
◆ Boundary Friction Between Clinging and Restraint
advice: Each month, set aside a 'Connection Day' and a 'Retreat Day,' alternating between group interaction and solitary reflection.

one_liner: You hold the fort while I blaze new trails — better than just keeping each other warm, we level up and take on the world together.
analysis: Holding Together belongs to Water; water over the earth signifies closeness and unity, with a centripetal force built on sincerity. Increase belongs to Wind; wind and thunder in motion signify gain and progress, carrying the energy to break patterns and iterate. When these two meet, it is like still waters running deep against a fierce wind and sturdy grass: Holding Together's 'renewed inquiries and eternal steadfastness' provides a stable groundwork of trust that tempers Increase's impulsive 'favorable for crossing the great water'; Increase's 'moving toward the good' injects evolutionary vitality into Holding Together, dissolving the stagnation and rigidity of 'the latecomer's misfortune.' Water and earth nourish wood, wind assists water's momentum. This bond achieves a balance between 'upholding integrity and close harmony' and 'dynamic growth.' It is a growth-oriented pairing that can both huddle for warmth and level up together.
resonance: ★ Values that resonate: choosing the good and following it
★ A shared drive to evolve by moving toward what is good
conflict: ◆ The pace gap between Holding Together's preference for stability and fear of change, and Increase's decisive swiftness
◆ The tug-of-war between the tendency to rely and cling, and the need to break through independently
advice: Hold a monthly 'Wind and Thunder Review' session, using Holding Together's open-hearted listening to digest differences, then turn Increase's 'correcting mistakes and moving toward good' into a shared micro-habit checklist to follow together.

relationship_name: The Balance of Gentleness and Resolution
one_liner: Soft, clinging water meets decisive lake-heaven—one weaves a web, the other breaks the deadlock.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together) uses the merging of Water and Earth to illustrate the way of attachment, emphasizing the enduring cohesion of 'the original divination, primordial constancy.' Guai (Breakthrough) uses Lake over Heaven to symbolize the power of decision, advocating the bold action of 'proclaiming in the royal court.' The two share a watery origin but take vastly different forms: Bi seeps through like an undercurrent to build a network of trust, while Guai pours down like a torrent to clear away entrenched problems. When the inclusiveness of closeness meets the sharpness of decisiveness, a chemical reaction occurs: 'softness gathers strength, hardness breaks the deadlock.' In their images, the gradual strategy of 'establishing the myriad states and embracing the feudal lords' interweaves with the thunderous measure of 'dispensing benefits to those below.' This is like taming water, which requires both dredging and dike-building—through dynamic balance, the transition from 'the latecomer meets misfortune' to 'favorable for having somewhere to go' is achieved.
resonance: ★ The Complementary dynamic of closeness and decisiveness
★ The balance of dispensing benefits and unity
conflict: ◆ Differences in rhythm (slow vs. fast)
◆ Differences in approach (gentle compliance vs. firm decisiveness)
advice: When making decisions, first gather consensus with the sincerity of Bi, then act decisively with the clarity of Guai. Avoid indecision or forcing your views on others.

one_liner: A stable base meets shifting winds; together they birth new opportunities.
analysis: The Bi hexagram is like water gathering on the earth, ruling over closeness and cohesion; the Gou hexagram is like wind roaming the heavens, ruling over unexpected encounters. When water gains the help of wind, it circulates without stagnation; when wind receives water's support, its mandate takes root. Yet Bi emphasizes the steady guard of 'the original divination, eternal perseverance,' while Gou reveals the restless advance of 'the strong woman, do not take her.' When the two intersect, there is often a 'clash of stillness and motion': Bi's deep cultivation needs Gou to break the deadlock, and Gou's adaptability needs Bi as its anchor. Water and earth by nature repel each other, but when wind strokes the water's surface, ripples arise in mutual reflection—precisely the symbiosis of the preserver and the breaker of patterns.
resonance: ★ Closeness and Cohesion
★ Wind Roaming the Four Directions
conflict: ◆ Soft Water Prone to Stagnation
◆ Swift Wind Prone to Dispersion
advice: Use Bi's solid foundation to absorb Gou's new openings; when encountering change, steady yourself before acting, and avoid reckless advances that exhaust your existing resources.

one_liner: One root, divergent streams—every gathering and parting completes the pattern.
analysis: The Hexagram of Holding Together (Bi) blends water and earth, emphasizing closeness and attachment; the Hexagram of Gathering Together (Cui) stacks lake over earth, emphasizing convergence. Both have Kun earth as their lower trigram, laying a foundation of stable interdependence. The flow of water and the accumulation of the lake create a dynamic balance: Bi's 'drawing close to the feudal lords' open inclusiveness and Cui's 'guarding against the unexpected' cautious restraint are two sides of the same coin. When Kan water nourishes Dui lake, guard against excessive attachment dissolving boundaries; when Dui lake contains Kan water, beware of excessive wariness blocking communion. United by a shared vision of 'gathering,' they anchor themselves in the virtue of earth, forming a symbiotic structure that is yielding outside yet resilient within.
resonance: ★ Cohesion co-created by water and earth
★ The dialectical unity of closeness and caution
conflict: ◆ Different rhythms of flow: Holding Together actively draws near vs. Gathering Together slowly filters
◆ Ideological tension: boundary-less closeness vs. structured gathering
advice: Set a monthly 'boundary-calibration day' to test the depth of closeness and the threshold of caution through concrete matters.

one_liner: First find your people and draw strength together, then build up your reserves and climb step by step.
analysis: Holding Together (Bi) is 'water over the earth,' signifying closeness and unity. Its Judgment warns that 'those who come late will meet misfortune,' stressing the importance of following the right people and seizing the moment. Pushing Upward (Sheng) is 'wood growing in the earth,' signifying the accumulation of small gains into great heights. Its Image speaks of 'going along with virtue,' and its Judgment encourages 'advancing southward brings good fortune,' focusing on steady ascent. Both share the foundation of Kun (the Receptive, Earth). Bi's water can nourish Sheng's wood, turning a horizontal network of relationships into a vertical ladder of growth. Bi's 'cultivating good connections everywhere' provides the resources and shelter for Sheng's 'quiet accumulation and sudden emergence'; conversely, Sheng's 'accumulating the small to reach the high' repays Bi, keeping it from becoming mere opportunistic clinging. The intermingling of water and earth creates a unique chemistry: 'nourish the foundation with people, rise with steadiness'—valuing present connections while planning for the long term.
resonance: ★ Cast a wide net of goodwill to lay a shared foundation
★ Accumulate deeply, burst forth, and ascend together
conflict: ◆ Seizing the first opportunity can easily look impatient
◆ Steady, deep cultivation may be criticized as sluggish
advice: Adopt a 'three advances, one pause' strategy: after every three social connections you make, force a full week of internal reflection and skill consolidation. Let Bi's outward openness draw people in, while Sheng's deep tending solidifies your roots.

one_liner: When closeness meets a bottleneck, one heart breaks the deadlock; water and marsh sustain each other — perseverance is the prize.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together) is Water over Earth, like streams soaking the soil, urging unity and wise choices. Kun (Oppression) is Lake over Water, drained dry, whose image says that in difficulty one must stay true to one's purpose even at the cost of self. Two different hexagrams converge: water and lake, distinct in nature yet mutually nourishing. Bi's closeness injects cohesion into a desperate situation; Kun's tenacity prevents Bi from turning into blind conformity. Yet the saying 'truthful words are not believed' warns that communication easily creates rifts — only sincerity can shatter the deadlock. The two are like parched land blessed with timely rain; moisture takes time. What matters is mutual trust and shared endurance, using softness to overcome hardness and dissolve the depletion of resources.
resonance: ★ Closeness and mutual aid, braving storms together
★ Hardship tempers the will, goals strike the same chord
conflict: ◆ Words fall short, trust becomes fragile
◆ The tug between collective dependence and standing firm alone
advice: Set aside one 'judgment-free dialogue day' each month: let Bi's broad-mindedness listen to Kun's persistence, replace empty talk with concrete actions, and steadily accumulate trust.

one_liner: Waters of a common root nourish silently, yet undercurrents entwine.
analysis: In Holding Together, water rests upon earth, with clinging and gathering at its core; in The Well, water rests upon wood, with enduring nourishment as its path. Both share the upper trigram Water, with its flowing, all-embracing nature, but their lower trigrams differ — Earth and Wind. Holding Together, like a reservoir in the soil, emphasizes human bonds; The Well, like wind threading through timber, seeks steady outflow. The hexagram texts — 'divine again, supreme constancy' and 'the town may change, but the well does not' — create a tension: Holding Together calls for the flexibility to gather only with the worthy, while The Well upholds the stability of 'nothing lost, nothing gained.' The Image commentaries — 'the king establishes myriad states and draws the feudal lords near' and 'the noble one comforts the people and encourages mutual aid' — show that both value communal cohesion, yet Holding Together excels in horizontal connection, while The Well is rooted in vertical depth. When water and earth clash, dependency and stubbornness collide; when wind stirs the water, a lasting ecology of mutual support can emerge.
resonance: ★ Waters from the same source, building a nourishing foundation together
★ Clinging and mutual aid, both seeking communal thriving
conflict: ◆ Wind seeks change vs. Earth upholds routine — rhythms can easily misalign
◆ Water overflows into clinging vs. The Well's rigidity — boundaries can blur
advice: Regularly use the spirit of The Well's nourishment to calibrate the density of Holding Together's attachment, letting the flexibility of Wind channel away the stagnation of Earth.

one_liner: Steady water holds the base, blazing fire opens the new—a duet of kinship and transformation.
analysis: Holding Together uses the mingling of water and earth to symbolize clinging and cohesion, emphasizing the building of trust networks through gentle compliance. Revolution uses the clash of lake and fire to symbolize breaking the old and establishing the new, requiring ripe timing before change is set in motion. When the two intersect, water's inclusiveness gives fire a safe space to experiment and learn, while fire's innovative force injects evolutionary energy into water's unity. In the hexagram texts, "Those who are restless come to join" and "On your own day, you will be believed" subtly echo each other: the cohesive power of Holding Together can dissolve the turbulence of early reform, while the breakthrough energy of Revolution can shatter the comfort-zone stalemate that Holding Together may create. Yet beware: if the water becomes too strong, it can extinguish the flame; if the fire burns too fiercely, it evaporates the moisture. The key lies in striking the balance between "being close without clinging" and "changing without impatience."
resonance: ★ Building the foundation for change through gentle cohesion
★ Acting in due time turns resistance into driving force
conflict: ◆ The rhythm clash between preserving stability and breaking barriers
◆ The pain of innovation meets the consensus of closeness
advice: Establish a "change sandbox" mechanism: carve out a test space in your core relationship circle, and use small iterative steps to validate new approaches—this preserves overall stability while activating creative energy.

one_liner: You're in charge of rallying people and building the platform; I'm in charge of stoking the fire and setting the rules. In sync, we're a top-tier match for pulling off major feats.
analysis: The Bi hexagram, 'water over earth,' is of the water element and emphasizes the cohesion of 'drawing close to the feudal lords' and choosing what is excellent, providing a deep foundation of human connections. The Ding hexagram, 'fire over wood,' is of the fire element and focuses on 'steadying one's position and solidifying one's mandate' — breaking the old to establish the new. The interplay of Water and Earth gives the relationship a powerful centripetal force, while the Cauldron of Fire and Wind injects explosive energy for transformation. When the two meet, it is as if the gentle nourishment of Bi feeds the blazing fire of Ding, using wide-ranging connections to fuel a groundbreaking enterprise; in return, Ding's 'great good fortune and success' nourishes Bi, elevating loose personal ties into a stable alliance. One brings people together; the other refines them — emotional grounding and rule-based breakthroughs interlock perfectly.
resonance: ★ Emotional grounding and breaking through in enterprise
★ Flexible cohesion and firm rule-setting
conflict: ◆ Excessive clinging can lead to a loss of independent judgment
◆ Hasty innovation can scatter human harmony
advice: When forming a partnership, first use Bi's patience to weave a strong network of trust, then follow Ding's rhythm to establish clear rules and boundaries. Never force reform before human bonds are secure; proceed step by step, 'uniting hearts first, setting rules later.'

relationship_name: Water and Thunder in Mutual Aid
one_liner: Soft water tames the fierce thunder; truth emerges in closeness.
analysis: Holding Together (Bi) shows water over earth, gathering hearts through gentle fidelity; Arousing (Zhen) shows thunder in repeated motion, urging self-reflection through forceful vigilance. The virtue of water nourishes downward and can contain the thunder's restlessness; the virtue of thunder rises up and can awaken the water's stillness. Their intersection creates a unique field of 'stillness storing movement, movement preserving stability': Bi's choosing what is good provides the bedrock of trust for Zhen, and Zhen's fearlessness in crisis injects the edge to break impasses into Bi. Yet water that is too soft may indulge the thunder's recklessness, and thunder too hasty may scatter the water's coalescence — a dynamic balance must be sought between closeness and awe.
resonance: ★ Soft water embraces, soothing the restless thunder's agitation
★ Thunder strikes through deadlock, igniting the will to unite
conflict: ◆ The long-flowing water meets the thunder's haste, rhythms easily fall out of sync
◆ Trust-based closeness meets sudden upheaval, security is often tested
advice: When decisions diverge, let the Bi (Holding Together) side first build consensus through listening, then the Zhen (Arousing) side advance with a three-step probing method — avoiding 'violent thunder breaking the water' or 'stagnant water drowning the thunder.'

relationship_name: Flow and Stillness in Mutual Aid
one_liner: Water winds around the mountain without overstepping; devotion and knowing when to stop suit each other well.
analysis: In the Holding Together hexagram, water is the moving nature: its image of “water over earth” speaks to the way of bonding and gathering, emphasizing the initiative to follow what is good. In the Keeping Still hexagram, mountain is the resting nature: its image of “mountain on mountain” reveals the power of restraint—knowing when to stop and stay in place. When these two intersect, a unique field takes shape: stillness hidden within movement, and boundaries within union. The warm affinity of Holding Together needs the boundary-sense of Keeping Still to anchor its direction and avoid the blind flocking that brings the “latecomer's misfortune.” The resting wisdom of Keeping Still needs the flowing energy of Holding Together to break the deadlock and dissolve the rigidity of “thinking beyond one's position.” When water and earth spur each other, the force of affinity, meeting mountain stone, turns into a nourishing trickle; the still posture, meeting the water's momentum, gives birth to moist vitality. This is like the dynamic balance achieved in the collision between the inclusiveness of “founding the myriad states” and the sobriety of “not letting thoughts go beyond one's position,” as recorded in the Images of the two hexagrams.
resonance: ★ Motion and stillness balance and bring nourishment
★ Closeness with measure keeps to one's own place
conflict: ◆ Flow blocked by obstacles grows stagnant and rough
◆ Excessive closeness turns into a fetter
advice: At work, establish a “three-step closeness method”: on first contact, seep in like water and explore the boundaries; in deep engagement, stand like a mountain to clarify roles and responsibilities; when reviewing, recede like the tide to leave room.

relationship_name: Water Nourishes, Wood Takes Its Course
one_liner: You huddle close in a hurry; he advances step by step. Slow burn meets fast friend, and it turns out to last the longest.
analysis: Water-over-Earth, Holding Together (Bi), takes its image from water on the ground: water moistens and flows downward, signifying rapid bonding and following what is good. Wind-over-Mountain, Development (Jian), takes its image from a tree on the mountain: wood grows and expands, signifying gradual progress and the nurturing of virtue to refine customs. Bi, like water, is inclusive, able to break down walls and connect quickly — but it carries a hidden timing anxiety, the 'latecomer meets misfortune.' Jian, like a tree taking root, sets the rhythm with the ritual propriety of 'the maiden's marriage brings good fortune,' and so it tempers Bi's haste. Together they balance speed and slowness, merging warmth with order. Bi provides emotional glue; Jian provides long-term grounding. Avoiding blind clinging or excessive delay, the two can forge a deep bond that is intimate yet properly measured.
resonance: ★ Water and earth merge, breaking the ice quickly
★ Mountain and wood take root, accumulating steadily
conflict: ◆ Rhythms out of sync: Bi is hasty, Jian is slow
◆ Boundaries blurred: intimacy loses its order
advice: The Bi side should give the other ample time to observe; the Jian side should take the initiative to show goodwill at key moments. Replace surprise intimacy with regular small gatherings, allowing the relationship to warm up naturally at a steady rhythm.

relationship_name: Water and Thunder: The Nourishing Bond
one_liner: Your steady, long-flowing security lets me sheathe my thunder-clap edge; only by keeping the rhythm can we slow-simmer passion into a lifetime.
analysis: The Hexagram Holding Together (Water over Earth) counsels 'renewed inquiry, supreme and lasting constancy,' seeking enduring stability through gentle attachment. The Marrying Maiden (Thunder over Lake) is imaged as 'thunder over the lake,' signaling emotional eruption that tends toward 'action brings misfortune, nothing is favorable.' Water's forbearance meets thunder's restlessness: at first this looks like a clash of steadiness and haste, but hidden beneath is a chemistry of 'moistening in silence, thunderclap by the lake.' Holding Together teaches us to choose the good and follow it, warning against 'the latecomer's misfortune'; The Marrying Maiden reminds us to 'know the end and its flaws,' cautioning against blind advance. When the two interact, water's stillness must dissolve thunder's volatility, and thunder's vitality must rouse water's inertia. Only by staying clear-eyed in attachment and reserving an escape route within passion can we turn conflict into symbiosis.
resonance: ★ The companionship of a long, steady stream
★ The instant heart-stirring rapport
conflict: ◆ Misaligned tempo: the craving for stability vs. impulse
◆ Over-idealization that ignores hidden hazards
advice: Set a 'three-day cooling-off period' for sudden passions, while using Holding Together's covenant spirit to clarify mutual boundaries and buffer the Marrying Maiden's emotional impulses.

one_liner: United you face the lightning — cooperation is fast, precise, and steady.
analysis: The Holding Together hexagram is like water gathering on the earth, with affinity and unity at its core; it emphasizes following the good and gently embracing all things. The Abundance hexagram is like thunder and fire blazing together, symbolizing greatness and clarity; it advocates decisive insight, resolute action, and holding to the center and what is right. When these two intersect, water's tolerance and nourishment moisten thunder's firm movement, while thunder's swiftness activates water's sluggishness. The warning in Holding Together — 'the latecomer meets with misfortune' — cautions that hesitation breeds change, and Abundance's call to 'act at high noon' urges timely effort. So you must infuse decisiveness into affinity and keep clarity within unity. The gentle yielding of water-over-earth affinity complements the firm judgment of thunder-over-fire, turning indecisiveness into efficiency — but take care lest excessive accommodation weakens your principles, or overly forceful decisions wound harmony.
resonance: ★ Build a shared foundation and stride toward abundance together.
★ Gentle tolerance meets clear judgment; act with moderation.
conflict: ◆ Holding Together favors slow deliberation; Abundance demands quick decisions.
◆ Water's long course tends to stagnate; thunder-fire's rush tends to flare up.
advice: After setting a shared goal, define clear decision points. Use inclusiveness to collect input, and execute key steps with decisive speed. Avoid endless discussion or going it alone.

one_liner: Water gathers in deep pools, fire lights the way; in union there is radiance, in separation solitude.
analysis: Bi (Holding Together) mingles water and earth, governing closeness and cohesion; Lü (The Wanderer) stacks mountain and fire, layering brightness for cautious far travel. Water's nature descends to nourish all things; fire's nature ascends to illuminate lost paths. Their intersection creates a dynamic balance: Bi's inclusiveness provides an emotional anchor for Lü's wandering, while Lü's prudence sets rational boundaries for Bi's cohesion. Yet if water is excessive, it quenches fire's brightness; if fire is too fierce, it evaporates water's nourishment. One must seek the middle way between the openness of 'drawing near to feudal lords' and the restraint of 'discerning and cautious punishment.'
resonance: ★ Building a Foundation of Trust
★ The Wisdom of Keen Perception
conflict: ◆ Over-tolerance vs. Rash Haste
◆ Free-Flowing vs. Rule-Bound
advice: Establish a regular review process to calibrate Bi's direction of cohesion with Lü's prudence.

one_liner: Water builds the stage with its power to bond; wind carries the orders with its power to penetrate. Together you are a divine pair for 'soft breakthrough.'
analysis: The hexagram 'Holding Together' (Bi) — 'water over the earth' — governs kinship and unity, stressing the value of choosing what is good and securing a stable foundation. The hexagram 'The Gentle' (Xun) — 'entering through the wind' — governs gentle, repeated commands, skilled at penetrating execution and flexible adaptation. When the two join, water's embrace gives the wind soil in which to root, and the wind's agility gives water a living flow. The centripetal pull of 'Holding Together' — 'the restless arrive in droves' — calls for the decisive 'repeated commands and carrying out of affairs' of 'The Gentle' to set the tone. In turn, 'The Gentle''s modest successes in local breakthroughs are magnified by 'Holding Together''s vision of 'uniting the feudal lords.' Without wind, water stagnates; without water, wind dissipates. United, they are like decrees that ride the wind and become rain, people's hearts gathering because of the momentum — a profound Kindred harmony of inner and outer strength.
resonance: ★ Gaining strength through kinship, moistening all things silently
★ Penetrating with the wind, every order enforced and every prohibition honored
conflict: ◆ Too much water makes things stagnant — over-reliance creeps in
◆ Too much wind makes things scatter — resolve drains away
advice: First build trust with sincerity as your foundation; then move forward step by step with gentle perseverance. Don't try to dominate with commands or bind others by emotions alone.

relationship_name: Mutual Sustenance of Moisture and Joy
one_liner: Water comes alive when it meets the lake; people grow close when they meet joy.
analysis: The Bi hexagram—water within the earth—governs closeness and cohesion, emphasizing the centripetal pull of attaching to the good. The Dui hexagram—two lakes stacked—governs harmony and free exchange, focusing on the infectious power of resonant words. When the two meet, it is like a hidden underground spring feeding a bright lake: Bi's calm inclusiveness provides a foundation for Dui's delight, and Dui's agile responsiveness in turn awakens Bi's latent vitality. Yet if the water swells too strongly, it easily overflows the lake's banks. One must temper the drifting excess of 'the joined lakes' with the steadfast discipline of 'initial divination, supreme and lasting perseverance,' so that closeness does not lose its clarity and communication does not remain merely superficial.
resonance: ★ Closeness gives rise to nourishment
★ Joyful words melt the hardest ice
conflict: ◆ Over-dependence stalls the flow
◆ Excessive joy stirs restlessness and loses the root
advice: Each month, choose an auspicious day to work together on one shared matter, using Bi's focus to settle Dui's exuberance and Dui's feedback to correct Bi's fixation.

one_liner: Able to part and reunite, intimate yet at ease.
analysis: The hexagram Bi (Holding Together) is water over earth, signifying closeness; the hexagram Huan (Dispersion) is wind over water, signifying separation. Both are images of flowing movement. The Image of Bi — 'Water over the earth' — emphasizes cohesion and centripetal pull, while Huan's 'Wind over the water' reveals an outward-spreading tendency. In the judgment texts, Bi values the bond of 'drawing near the princes,' while Huan uses 'establishing the ancestral temple' to rein in dissipation — forming a dialectic of 'gathering and dispersing as complements.' Water's downward moistening meets wind's upward surge, exactly like the tug-of-war between intimacy and freedom in relationships: clinging too closely creates constraint, while scattering entirely loses ground. When the two intersect, wind borrows the water's momentum to create ripples of beauty, and water moves with the wind to show its inclusive nature — balance must be found within the motion.
resonance: ★ Mutual fulfillment through flow
★ Dynamic equilibrium between gathering and scattering
conflict: ◆ When the wind rages, the water scatters and cannot gather
◆ Too much dispersion makes closeness impossible to sustain
