Bo is in charge of subtraction, stripping away the flashy, tottering outer shells; Yi is in charge of addition, recharging the core life-force through careful speech and moderate eating. When they come together, it's like a tree going through winter: first it sheds its dead leaves to protect the trunk, then quietly sends nutrients to the roots. It doesn't chase outside excitement — only inner solidity and staying power.
resonance: ★ Stop-loss and endurance: Bo teaches you to cut out the draining items in time, and Yi follows up by turning the saved energy into self-nourishment — a perfect closed loop.

★ Kindred rhythm of rooting inward: both hexagrams hit the brakes and avoid making a fuss; one steadies the base to prevent collapse, the other guards the intake to prevent waste — their tempo is perfectly aligned.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Bo is in a defensive contraction phase and doesn't even want to step out the door, while Yi hides a spring-thunder vitality and wants to actively regulate — one is inclined to lie flat, the other to stir things up.

◆ Different focus: Bo values the solidity of the external environment and foundation; Yi focuses on the moderation of personal food and speech. When trouble comes, one fears the house caving in, the other worries about running out of grain.
advice: When setting rules, bind the bottom line of 'thicken the base and settle the home' together with the daily practice of 'watch words and eat lightly' — don't split your survival strategy and your wellness plan into two separate sheets.

relationship_name: A Steady Base for a Dangerous Crossing
one_liner: Your job is to lay the foundation solid; mine is to brace the roof beam when it's about to come down.
analysis: The Bo hexagram is like a steadfast old stone—its teaching is 'Not favorable to undertake anything.' When storms come, its first instinct is to pull back, defend, and compact the ground beneath. Da Guo, by contrast, is the roof beam bending under enormous weight, shouting 'It furthers to undertake something'—even as the whole structure crumbles, it insists on cutting its own path forward. When these two meet, at first glance it looks like slamming the brakes and flooring the gas at the same time. But look closer, and they are deeply complementary: without Bo's patient bottom-line of 'securing the home by thickening the foundation,' Da Guo's lone courage easily becomes a rootless duckweed. Conversely, without Da Guo's bold 'stand alone and be unafraid' breakthrough energy in times of crisis, Bo's caution just stews into stagnant water. This is not about one converting the other—it's how the chassis and the engine mesh: one holds the line, the other tears open the way out of a dead end.
resonance: ★ Underwriting and Breaking Through: Bo's steady-handed defense gives Da Guo's adventures the most solid backing, keeping the cost of trial and error extremely low.
★ Still Waters Converging with Raging Waves: one habitually gathers energy inward and stores it; the other dares to release pressure outward and break encirclement—together they form a perfect loop.
conflict: ◆ The Tension Between Consolidation and Daring: Bo finds Da Guo restless and risk-addicted; Da Guo finds Bo too timid to move.
◆ The Rhythm Mismatch Between Retreat and Head-On Confrontation: when a crisis hits, one wants to pull back and recover, the other insists on charging straight in—this can drain each other.
advice: Before any major decision, let Bo first draw up a clear list of safety bottom lines; then Da Guo can go all out above those lines. Don't drag each other down by insisting on your own paces.

one_liner: You lay the foundation in the valley; I wade through the rapids. Put us together and we cross every hurdle with steady feet.
analysis: Bo (Splitting Apart) is like an old mountain that weathers yet keeps deep roots. In decline it pulls in its edge and pours all its strength into building a thick foundation for the home. Kan (The Abysmal) is an undercurrent that blazes a path through mountains, repeatedly honed by danger through the sustaining power of a steadfast heart. When the two meet, Bo's retreat provides the safety net for Kan's advance, and Kan's flow breaks the deadlock of Bo's stagnant waters. Bo fears blind attacks; Kan's steady momentum turns each obstacle into a stepping stone. Kan easily exhausts itself in whirlpools; Bo's mountain-like steadiness re-anchors its center. This isn't a thunderclap collision—it's groundwater seeping through rock. One silently supports from beneath; the other quietly permeates. The mountain gains a spring, and the water gains its banks.
resonance: ★ Steady in danger with a safety net: Bo's thick base and secure home gives Kan an emotional buffer, so even the toughest battles don't spiral off track.

★ Inward rooting and heart-cultivation: Kan's constant virtue and Bo's gathering-and-grounding both point to sinking deep—one trains resolve in motion, one stores vitality in stillness. Their spirits resonate.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched pace: Bo favors restraint when movement is unwise; Kan stresses action to break through. When trouble appears, one hits the brake, the other floors the gas.
◆ Different damage-control: Bo retreats and yields to preserve vitality; Kan learns by repeated trial and error. Over time, they may argue over whether to keep pushing.
advice: When conflict arises, let the Mountain personality draw the safe boundary first, then let the Water personality experiment in small steps within it. Replace blind charging with regular reviews.

one_liner: One lays the groundwork in a low valley, the other shines a spotlight in the open—together they keep life solid and bright.
analysis: Bo is “the mountain resting on the earth”—its art lies in yielding, settling, and making the root go deep. At such a time, forcing ahead only strips the mountain thinner. Li, by contrast, is “brightness rising twice,” like a fire that refuses to die out, born to pour light and heat outward. The two meet with mismatched rhythms: one calls out, “It is not favorable to undertake anything,” urging restraint, while the other longs to “perpetuate brightness and illuminate the four quarters,” wishing to light up the whole scene. Yet this dissonance is exactly what makes them complementary. However bright Li's fire, without thick earth to bear it, it is only a phantom; however massive Bo's mountain, without Li's light upon it, it sinks into dead stillness. Bo's “thickening the base to secure the dwelling” gives Li the steadiest foundation, while Li's “tamed cow” gentleness knows how to shine a warm, gentle light through the waning season—to keep the other quiet company through the bitter winter. One sheathes the blade, one renews the brilliance; neither grabs the spotlight, yet together they simmer into warmth.
resonance: ★ Rooting in the shadows, blooming in the light: Bo's accumulated depth feeds Li's unfolding, and Li's radiance pours hope back into Bo's low season.
★ Soft resilience guards the deep root: Li's patient, enduring “tamed cow” nature is exactly what can soothe Bo's fretful anxiety as decline sets in.
conflict: ◆ Rush and stillness pull against each other: Li's fire wants to light up the situation immediately, but Bo is in its “not favorable to undertake anything” hibernation—forcing action only fritters away energy.
◆ Brilliance and falling darkness rub together: Li's glare can sting Bo's sensitivity, while Bo's over-contraction leaves Li feeling its ardor doused with cold water.
advice: The Li side should neither rush the pace nor pour on too much warmth; first help the Bo side make the foundation steady. The Bo side, likewise, should stop throwing cold water—try using Li's light to spot the hidden reefs ahead, then take one slow step at a time.

one_liner: One is busy shoring up the walls and guarding the roots, the other opens the heart's door to let the water in. A slow burn meets a soulful heart—and somehow, it's the most solid thing of all.
analysis: The Bo hexagram [Splitting Apart] counsels 'not favorable to set out'—like autumn harvest and winter storage, pulling all strength into the foundation and making the home secure. The Xian hexagram [Influence], by contrast, shows 'a lake on the mountain,' with the essence of an open, valley-like mind and mutual resonance. When these two meet, it isn't dry wood catching flame; it's a deep-dug well meeting a living spring. Bo's restraint and guardianship give Xian's sensitive emotions the most stable chassis, keeping feelings from flooding. Xian's openness and acceptance can melt the loneliness and guardedness Bo carries in its decline. When the mountain is below, it can carry the lake; when the mountain is above, one must beware of erosion. The essence of this relationship is letting Bo's steady power support Xian's fluid agility—as the pair tests each other, the roots slowly sink deep, and love naturally finds its way.
resonance: ★ Rooted Meets Living Water: Bo's power to thicken the base and secure the home perfectly catches Xian's delicate, dew-like subtlety, keeping love from floating on the surface.
★ Open Valley Receives the Sinking Mountain: The Xian gentleman's receptive humility gently dissolves the tension and defense that Bo shows during its waning season.
conflict: ◆ Retreat Collides with Openness: Bo's instinct to shrink into self-protection can make Xian feel the other is too closed off and never offers a stepping stone.
◆ Sensitive Meets Obtuse: Xian craves high-frequency emotional resonance, while Bo tends to bury things and slowly digest them—so their rhythms often fall out of sync.
advice: Don't rush into demanding immediate feedback. Give the other the security of a 'thick foundation' first; once the ground is steady, the lake water will naturally rise.

one_liner: Bo (Splitting Apart) pumps the brakes and builds the foundation; Heng (Duration) sets the cruise control for the long haul.
analysis: The Bo hexagram is 'the mountain resting on the earth'—rocks weather and crumble, teaching us to recognize a period of decline and not barge through headfirst. Instead, we must 'strengthen what lies below and secure the dwelling' to fortify our base. The Heng hexagram is 'thunder and wind in accord'—thunder crashes, wind races, yet the rhythm stays steady. It's all about locking onto a goal and stubbornly seeing it through. When these two hexagrams come together, it's like pairing a seasoned foreman with a long-distance running coach. Bo's 'unfavorable to undertake anything' isn't telling you to give up; it's a reminder to pull back your battle lines when resources run dry. Heng's 'standing firm without changing direction' supplies the sense of purpose, showing you how to keep applying yourself once you've taken root. Mountain nature is still and heavy; thunder nature is active and unceasing. Between the pull-back and the push-forward, you master the art of hunkering down and hanging tough. Spend enough time together, and you'll notice that Bo's caution reins in Heng's impatience, while Heng's steady resolve lifts Bo's slump. A good life is built slowly, not stormed into.
resonance: ★ Don't make reckless moves during the rooting phase: Bo's 'unfavorable to undertake anything' applies the brakes to Heng's long-distance charge, reminding you to repair your foundation when resources run low and avoid blind depletion.

★ Stick to your convictions without easing up: Heng's 'standing firm without changing direction' neutralizes Bo's passive retreat, showing people in decline that holding the line is itself a form of long-termism.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythms can drain energy: Heng is used to pushing forward with thunderous speed, while Bo keeps pointing at hidden dangers and calling for a halt. One thinks the other is too slow, the other too hasty, leading to tug-of-war over timing.

◆ Different ways of handling crisis: Bo tends to tighten up and cut losses when things start to crumble, while Heng trusts that sticking to principle will see it through—facing sudden upheaval, their strategies may end up going in completely opposite directions.
advice: When you hit a fork in the road, first let Bo assess the risks and set the stop-loss line, then let Heng break down the long-term execution plan within the safe zone. Don't let emotions take the place of planning.

relationship_name: Mutual Fulfillment in Retreat and Hold
one_liner: Retreat when it's time — only with a stable base can you go far.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is like an old tree with deeply coiled roots, quietly strengthening its foundation during decline; the Retreat hexagram is like a lone crane stretching its wings, gliding away when the wind turns wrong. The mountain is steady by nature yet prone to sinking into mire; Heaven is lofty by nature yet neglects to take root. When the two meet, Splitting Apart's 'securing the home by thickening the base' gives Retreat the confidence to 'keep the petty at a distance,' while Retreat's wisdom of stepping away helps Splitting Apart avoid wasteful exertion. Like an old craftsman repairing a dangerous house — he first backs off to a safe distance to observe the structure, one of them ramming earth and driving piles, the other clearing the view from above. In crisis, they forge a rhythm for survival: 'retreat without falling apart, hold without stiffening.'
resonance: ★ Only with a solid foundation can you dare to retreat: Splitting Apart teaches you to consolidate the base, Retreat reminds you to disengage at the right time — both stress thorough preparation before pulling back.

★ Keep your distance from petty quarrels to stay clear-minded: Retreat advises against tangling with small-minded people, and Splitting Apart keeps you lucid amid decline — a shared wisdom of not recklessly fighting what you cannot change.
conflict: ◆ Defending the base vs. saving yourself by leaving: Splitting Apart says reinforce in place, Retreat says get away from danger — your actions may pull in opposite directions.
◆ Timing the retreat is hard to sync: Splitting Apart waits for the decline to run its course, Retreat stresses early withdrawal at the first sign — different rhythms can cause disagreements.
advice: Reserve three days each month for solitary review. List Splitting Apart's 'reinforcement actions' as a checklist, and when you see Retreat's warning signs, act on the top three items first.

one_liner: One teaches you to sink into a horse stance and lay a solid foundation; the other stands up and flexes. Together, they work with both steadiness and raw force.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is a mountain resting on the earth—when all things wither, it teaches you not to run around but to quietly compact your foundation. The Power of the Great is thunder splitting through the sky—when yang energy is at its peak, it teaches you to observe the rules and charge forward. These two hexagrams together aren't about one overpowering the other; they're a precise coordination of "throttle and brake." Without Splitting Apart's 'thick base and settled home' to underpin it, the Power of the Great's fierce, unbridled energy can easily turn into a runaway horse that smashes its head bloody. Without the Power of the Great's 'do not step on the improper' to break the impasse, Splitting Apart's contracting energy will just stew until it stiffens, then rot in place. Their chemical reaction lies in 'know where to stop, and only then can you move.' Splitting Apart is responsible for pressing down on restlessness and storing resources in the dark; the Power of the Great is responsible for spotting the right moment and hurling out all the accumulated force in one go. One manages the chassis, the other manages the output. Anyone who understands their rhythm will save themselves ten years of detours.
resonance: ★ Perfect interlocking of foundation and momentum: Splitting Apart's 'thick base and settled home' gives the Power of the Great's thunderous movement a solid launching point, so the drive never degenerates into aimless thrashing.

★ Kindred in restraint: The Power of the Great insists on 'not stepping on the improper,' while Splitting Apart advises against rushing into action—both know how to apply the brakes at critical moments and act with a sense of measure.
conflict: ◆ A mismatch of rhythm can cause tempers to flare: Splitting Apart is used to slow simmering and steady building, while the Power of the Great, once its thunderous nature kicks in, wants results immediately—each finds the other too slow or too reckless.

◆ A tug-of-war over the flow of energy: one keeps subtracting to sheathe its edge, the other keeps adding to release tension—in daily communication, they easily end up wrestling over holding back versus letting go.
advice: Before any major decision, follow Splitting Apart's rule: stay silent for three days and sort out your cards. Then borrow the Power of the Great's momentum and move with lightning force. Whatever you do, don't try to think and act at the same time or the two energies will battle each other.

one_liner: One steadies the ground so it doesn't collapse; the other casts light to illuminate the entire field.
analysis: The Bo hexagram (Splitting Apart) is a mountain resting on the earth; it speaks of a defensive stance during decline and decay, emphasizing "reinforce the base and secure the home"—making the foundation solid and protecting the lower layers. The Jin hexagram (Progress) is brightness emerging above the earth; it is the image of the sun rising and advancing into light, stressing "manifest one's own bright virtue." Both share the lower trigram Kun (The Receptive), so their roots are the same, but their directions are opposite: Bo contracts downward and fears movement; Jin radiates upward and dares to charge. Bo is like a seasoned defender of a city who knows to shore up the walls when the wind blows strong; Jin is like the light at dawn, eager to show its talents and achievements to the world. Together, Bo provides a base for Jin, and Jin breaks the deadlock for Bo. If Bo doesn't let go, it can smother Jin's light; if Jin doesn't restrain itself, it will accelerate the erosion of Bo's foundation. The chemistry between these two hexagrams is the push-and-pull—and the mutual fulfillment—of "holding" and "advancing" on the same patch of earth.
resonance: ★ Shared Earthly Roots, Movement with Foundation: Both lower trigrams are Kun (The Receptive); Bo's solid base and Jin's emergence into light are rooted in the same soil. Their fundamental logic is aligned—each understands where the other comes from.

★ Steadfast Support Advances Ambition: The stable home that Bo provides gives Jin a secure rear base for its "triple reception in a day" (its rapid ascent). Without a thick foundation, even the brightest light can flicker out all too soon.
conflict: ◆ Restraint Suppresses Expansion: Bo's conservative tendency—"it is not favorable to go anywhere"—can mistake Jin's enterprising fervor to "manifest its bright virtue" for recklessness and slam on the brakes.

◆ Brightness Scorches Steadiness: Jin's eagerness to push achievements onto the stage can accelerate the depletion of Bo's already fragile foundation, making Bo feel its bedrock is being hollowed out and its sense of security is draining away.
advice: Before Jin charges ahead, it should ask Bo whether the foundation is steady; before Bo tries to hold Jin back, it should help Jin lay the necessary resources in place.

one_liner: The darker the world grows, the less you should rush about. You tamp the foundation, I hide my last card—hold steady and you'll outlast the dark.
analysis: The Splitting hexagram is like a landslide, warning you not to charge outward but to turn back and firm up the ground beneath you. Darkening of the Light, on the other hand, buries the torch in the soil, teaching you to play dull before outsiders while keeping a bright flame within. When these two hexagrams meet, they are the ultimate survival pair for chaotic times. Splitting supplies a physical defense strategy—cutting away showy branches and pulling resources down to the roots. Darkening provides a spiritual cushion—refusing to compete for surface brilliance and folding its edge inward. One subtracts in the material world to secure the home; the other subtracts in the mind to hide the blade. As the outer environment slides downhill, this duo forms an extraordinarily anti-fragile shield: no blind expansion, no head-on collision. Through a thick base and a lucid core, they gather strength in silence. Others collapse from wear and tear; you root deeper while dormant.
resonance: ★ Retreat and Recharge: Both Splitting's 'thicken the base to secure the home' and Darkening's 'use obscurity to brighten' affirm the survival wisdom of contracting defenses and rooting inward during low valleys.
★ Pragmatic Concealment: Both refuse surface glory—one throws its weight into the foundation, the other hides its light in the chest. A strikingly compatible pair.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Splitting is quick to cut off redundancies and protect the core, while Darkening is used to slow-burning patience and waiting for a window. This can pull you between cutting losses now and enduring further.

◆ Communication Gap: Splitting cares about tangible physical foundations; Darkening leans toward spiritual inner guarding. One demands visible security, the other an unspoken resonance—easy to talk past each other.
advice: When differences arise, don't argue over who's right. Sit down together, take stock of core resources, and slash all wasteful projects that produce no real gains. Also agree to set aside half a day each week for closed-door review with no external output, turning all that outward energy back into sharpening fundamentals.

one_liner: No matter how hard the storms rage outside, don't go stirring up chaos—warm up your own hearth first, and life will naturally become steady.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is like a mountain pressing on the earth, emphasizing that 'it is not advantageous to undertake anything.' In a period of decline, it knows when to hold back and pours all its energy into the groundwork of 'thickening the base and securing the home.' The Family hexagram, on the other hand, is wind and fire feeding each other—it prizes the order of the hearth and the daily practice of 'words with substance and deeds that are consistent.' When these two come together, it's not about spectacular expansion but a Kindred rapport between preserving and tending. Splitting Apart's calm solidity provides a safe harbor for The Family's warm, smoky vitality; The Family's care and steady warmth, in turn, dissolve the heavy drain that Splitting Apart naturally carries. One keeps the foundation solid against outside erosion; the other brings rhythm to everyday life. Together they are the most grounded partners for a low stretch: first hold your ground, then sort out the daily necessities—and the roots will not fail.
resonance: ★ A Kindred Hold on the Bottom Line: Splitting Apart knows not to act blindly in low times, while The Family stays true to words and actions every day. Both share the unsentimental wisdom that a real life needs no empty show.

★ Complementary Warmth from Within: Splitting Apart's dense outer shell keeps outside depletion at bay, shielding the low-burning hearth fire of The Family so that it can be fed continuously and the inner order never breaks.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: The Family likes to put things on the table and follow the rules, while Splitting Apart tends to keep quiet and retreat, feeling that less is more—leaving a warm face pressed against a cold wall.

◆ Emotional Temperature Gap: The Family craves a bright, transparent atmosphere for communication, but the down-phase heaviness of Splitting Apart can make the other person feel suffocated, and over time that breeds silent friction.
advice: When disagreement arises, don't force an immediate answer. Do some concrete chore together first; let action replace debate, and the emotions will naturally settle.

one_liner: One works hard to lay a foundation for stability, the other finds joy in seeking out differences; together they turn daily life into a model of 'unity in diversity.'
analysis: Bo (Splitting Apart) is the mountain pressing down on the earth, energy sinking inward, about thickening the base and securing the home—at such times, the worst thing is to stir things up blindly; you have to set the roots deep. Kui (Opposition) is fire burning upward, water flowing downward—naturally divergent, yet somehow able to find kindred spirits within the differences. Put these two hexagrams together, and Bo's steadiness perfectly catches Kui's scatter. Bo doesn't run outward; it quietly clears the mess and reinforces the foundation. Kui doesn't force consensus either; instead, it picks out amusing little sparks from the disagreements. Bo gives Kui a solid floor, cushioning those seemingly out-of-sync contradictions; Kui opens a window for Bo, reminding it not to cling to the old so tightly that it forgets to enjoy the view. One is like an old house being renovated, the other like a traveler dropping in as a guest—one slow, one quick—yet they manage to simmer their differences into something complementary in the narrow spaces of small good fortune.
resonance: ★ A capable safety net: Bo's thick foundation can firmly catch Kui's scattered energy, so those wild, soaring ideas don't just float away.
★ Difference sparks delight: Kui is naturally drawn to what's different, which happens to break up the stuffy deadlock Bo tends to fall into, adding a breath of freshness to daily life.
conflict: ◆ Off-beat rhythm: Bo is used to holding back and slowly simmering, while Kui keeps probing for change in the fine details—one thinks the other is too slow, the other thinks the one is too dull.
◆ Divergent goals: Bo seeks a secure home and stability, while Kui looks for vitality in small blessings—when major matters arise, they're apt to head in opposite directions.
advice: When disagreements come up, don't rush to make everyone agree. First set out a safe zone: one party holds the line on baseline boundaries and logistics, the other stays flexible and experiments with small moves. Dividing up the duties works better than trying to force everything into a single rope.

one_liner: Stop trying to force things. Our strategy now is simple: keep our feet planted, keep our hearts together, and weather this stretch — the sun will come out.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is 'the mountain rests on the earth,' with the center of gravity below — a reminder that in a period of decline you shouldn't run around; you need to shore up the foundation. The Obstruction hexagram is 'water on the mountain,' with obstacles ahead — it counsels that when faced with a trap, don't fight it directly; instead turn inward, build virtue, and seek steadiness. When these two hexagrams come together, it's practically a 'low-period duo.' Splitting Apart's 'solid base' provides the undercarriage for Obstruction's 'wading through danger,' and Obstruction's 'turning back to oneself' makes up for the mental burnout of Splitting Apart's decline. One prevents the foundation from giving way, the other prevents the road ahead from slipping. Neither advocates reckless advancement; instead, they resonate strongly on the beat of 'stop and look inward.' This match isn't for pioneering, but it's exceptionally good at catching each other in the trough of a downturn and gradually turning chaos into a safe haven.
resonance: ★ Mutual foundation support: The Splitting Apart hexagram emphasizes focusing on the base to secure the household, while the Obstruction hexagram calls for steadiness in danger. Together, the two can back each other up and avoid blind, reckless moves.
★ Aligned inner cultivation: In the face of decline and obstacles, both advocate seeking answers within and sheathing one's edge — a highly consistent spiritual rhythm.
conflict: ◆ Sluggish action: Splitting Apart is unfavorable for taking action, and Obstruction is full of obstacles. Together, they easily sink into a 'thinking but not moving' procrastination swamp.
◆ Emotional buildup: One is anxious watching the foundation sink; the other frets over the muddy road ahead. If they don't clear the air promptly, they'll infect each other with negativity.
advice: When you hit a disagreement, don't rush to decide. Set aside a fixed half-day each week to take stock of your resources together, break big goals into immediately actionable small steps, and then move forward.

relationship_name: Hold the Foundation, Break the Gridlock
one_liner: One keeps the foundation solid and avoids reckless moves; the other waits for the right moment and then releases the tension with a clean break.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is a mountain pressing down on the earth, everything withering, advising that 'it is not favorable to undertake anything,' urging you to first shore up what lies below and secure your home — all about staying patient and riding out the low valley. The Deliverance hexagram is thunder and rain converging, the pent-up frustration finally bursting open, urging prompt action, 'good fortune through early action' — the earlier you move, the smoother it goes. When these two come together, it's 'strategic resolve' colliding with 'tactical breakout.' The steadiness of Splitting Apart provides a safety cushion for Deliverance's explosive energy, so things don't collapse; Deliverance's decisiveness sweeps away Splitting Apart's dullness, preventing the relationship from stagnating into a dead-end decline. They don't resonate on the same frequency; rather, their rhythms are Complementary: Splitting Apart quietly holds the line and repairs cracks during low periods, while Deliverance decisively cuts through tangled knots and travels light the moment a turning point appears. As long as Splitting Apart doesn't procrastinate and Deliverance doesn't rush ahead, this relationship can turn 'endurance' into 'breakthrough' and gather 'scattered' into 'living.'
resonance: ★ Holding the Line and Loosening the Bonds: Splitting Apart's 'shore up below and secure home' provides ample security, giving Deliverance's 'forgive past faults and show mercy' the confidence to act, not fearing old scores, only looking forward.

★ A Kindred Rhythm of Enduring and Breaking: Splitting Apart knows not to stir things up in the low period, and Deliverance knows not to hesitate when the turning point arrives. Together, they have a natural instinct for when to stay still and when to charge.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Splitting Apart feels it's not ready and can't move; Deliverance feels the opportunity is here and waiting will kill it. One wants to dig in and march steadily, the other wants a quick strike — they can easily trip each other up.

◆ Emotional Temperature Gap: Splitting Apart's conservatism can feel lifeless, while Deliverance's bluntness can come off as careless. One is silently digesting pressure, the other wants to turn the page quickly — communication can break down.
advice: When disagreements arise, Splitting Apart shouldn't block the road with 'let's wait a bit longer,' and Deliverance shouldn't pressure with 'hurry up.' Agree on a buffer period of 'observe for three days, then move when you see clearly,' and weave the steadiness of Splitting Apart and the swiftness of Deliverance into a single rope.

one_liner: One tells you to stop and solidify your foundation; the other urges you to travel light and charge ahead. Either way, the mountain in our eyes stands just as steady.
analysis: Both hexagrams share Ken, the Mountain, as their upper trigram — outwardly steady and restrained, yet within they enact two different approaches to the 'subtraction' way of life. Splitting Apart has earth energy floating weakly below; its Judgment says plainly, 'It does not further one to undertake anything,' and its Image emphasizes 'thickening the base and securing the dwelling' — a philosophy of preserving what has been built during passive decline. Decrease, whose lower trigram is Lake water eroding upward, instead advocates 'It furthers one to undertake something,' and through 'curbing anger and suppressing desire' actively subtracts to cultivate virtue. When the two come together, Decrease's disciplined blade can cut through Splitting Apart's anxious self-consumption, while Splitting Apart's practical confidence can catch Decrease's light-packed advance. One clears away stale inventory and cuts off delusions; the other repairs the city wall and steadies the groundwork. Sharing the same still mountain, they form a subtly interlocking gear between 'moving and staying' and 'reducing and guarding.'
resonance: ★ Kindred in Subtraction: Both know that going too far is as bad as not going far enough. One strips away the superficial to preserve the root; the other trims delusions to nourish the spirit. Both instinctively reject blind expansion.

★ Calm-Spirit Resonance: Both have the Mountain of Ken pressing down from above, so they don't easily get worked up. They habitually hold their ground before planning for the long term, with solid emotional foundations.
conflict: ◆ Push-and-Pull: Splitting Apart explicitly says 'not favorable to undertake anything' and advises quiet preservation, while Decrease proclaims 'favorable to undertake something' and urges forward motion. One fears upheaval and collapse; the other resents stagnation and missed chances.

◆ Rhythm Misalignment: Splitting Apart wants to slowly 'thicken the base and secure the home' to mend the roots; Decrease wants to quickly 'curb anger and suppress desire' to clear away burdens. One favors defensive repair; the other favors decisive letting-go and advancement.
advice: When facing a major decision, first use Splitting Apart's pace to take stock of your real resources, then borrow Decrease's blade to cut away unnecessary emotions and steps. Make an action list in this order: stabilize the base first, then subtract.

relationship_name: A Firm Foundation, Riding the Wind
one_liner: You weld the chassis solid; I hoist the sails full. Together, we're just right for big ventures.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is like autumn harvest and winter storage—it values 'not favorable to undertake anything,' and its core is stripping away the superficial and reinforcing the foundation. The Increase hexagram is like spring breeze and rain—it champions 'favorable to cross the great water,' and its core is seizing momentum and iterating quickly. When the two meet, it's exactly the meshing of 'brake' and 'accelerator.' The mountain-over-earth stance of Splitting Apart can hold down the wind-and-thunder restlessness of Increase, preventing blind expansion from leaving the foundation unsteady; while the flowing vitality of Increase can blow away the stagnant decline of Splitting Apart, turning passive defense into a living game. In this relationship, one teaches when to pull back and build strength, the other teaches when to break through and open new paths. Energy completes its loop in the alternating rhythm of 'defense' and 'attack'—never so reckless as to overturn the cart, nor so cautious as to miss the prevailing wind.
resonance: ★ Chassis and sail in lockstep: Splitting Apart's thick-layered foundation secures the home, giving Increase's swift expansion a backing that won't let the floor cave in.
★ Complementary breakthrough and consolidation: Increase's readiness to move toward the good disperses Splitting Apart's stale, declining energy, lifting the whole upward.
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war over pacing: Splitting Apart counsels staying put and avoiding risk, while Increase always wants to set out immediately and experiment across boundaries.
◆ The game of resource allocation: Splitting Apart tends to contract, defend, and count every penny, while Increase leans toward heavy investment and chasing growth in scale.
advice: Set clear 'risk red lines' and 'sprint windows': the Splitting Apart side defines the bottom line and runs stress tests; the Increase side charges freely above the red line. Align your advance-and-retreat rhythm on a fixed monthly basis.

one_liner: One slams the brakes to protect the chassis, the other floors the gas to clear the roadblocks.
analysis: Bo (Splitting Apart) is the mountain pressing down on the earth's skin, yin energy sinking; it emphasizes 'making the foundation thick and the home secure' — like a night watchman whose first instinct in any crisis is to stop losses and protect life, not to make reckless moves. Guai (Breakthrough), by contrast, is a lake-marsh hanging at the edge of the sky, yang energy surging upward; it advocates 'raising the matter in the royal court' and striking decisively — a forceful breaker of deadlocks. These two opposite hexagrams are like the two sides of the same coin: Bo's 'not favorable to undertake anything' collides with Guai's 'favorable to undertake something,' and the tension immediately fills the air. Bo fears Guai's rashness will shatter the family foundation; Guai resents Bo's timidity for missing golden opportunities. But the beauty is this: without Bo's accumulated steadiness as a bedrock, Guai's decisiveness is water without roots; without Guai's swift sword cutting through tangles, Bo's perseverance would only rot in the mud. Put them together, and they complete each other's required course in life: knowing when to endure and when to charge.
resonance: ★ Chassis and Edge: Bo's rock-solid grip on the foundation gives Guai's bold, swinging action a safe landing pad — no fear of flipping over.
★ Sediment and Release: The mountain's weight can catch the lake-sky's downpour; one stores up power, the other clears the channels, so emotions never get stuck inside.
conflict: ◆ Brakes and Throttle: Bo wants everything stable and advises backing off to watch; Guai is impatient to clear the field and break the deadlock. If the rhythm is off, each will accuse the other of being either too slow or too reckless.

◆ Hiding the Blade vs. Drawing the Sword: Bo prefers 'thickening the base and securing the home' — quietly guarding what's his; Guai favors 'raising it in the royal court' — openly dispensing rewards. Their methods diverge like north and south, and friction is easy.
advice: When you hit a disagreement, first have the 'Bo' side list three worst-case bottom lines, then have the 'Guai' side set a breakthrough timeline above those lines. Don't argue attitudes; just sync your watches and act.

one_liner: You weld the foundation solid; I scout the winds outside. With both in place, we won't drift.
analysis: The Bo hexagram (Splitting Apart) is like an ancient mountain eroded by wind and rain, warning that 'it is not favorable to undertake anything.' Its core strategy is to root inwardly and settle securely in rich soil. The Gou hexagram (Coming to Meet) is the drafts that sweep across the world, emphasizing unexpected encounters and commanding the four directions, with energy spreading furiously outward. When the two meet, at first their rhythms seem to clash: Bo wants to pull back into its shell and patch the foundation, while Gou wants to push the doors open and build goodwill everywhere. But deep down, they hold a powerful complementary balance — without Bo's 'strengthening the lower part,' Gou's 'issuing commands' would become rootless duckweed, scattered by the next breeze; without Gou's 'wind under heaven,' Bo's 'mountain resting on earth' could easily fall into stagnant stillness. Bo provides the ballast; Gou provides the fresh wind. One welds the core together, the other tests the waters outside. Over time, Bo learns to use the wind for fresh air, and Gou learns to put down roots. They grow from 'each doing their own thing' to 'once the base is solid, then we move.'
resonance: ★ Wind Over a Foundation: Bo's solid base can catch Gou's sudden inspirations securely, keeping good ideas from floating in midair.
★ Encountering New, Strengthening the Root: The unexpected connections and messages Gou brings can reinvigorate the long-dormant resources in Bo.
conflict: ◆ Static vs. Dynamic Tempo: Bo likes to close the door and take stock; Gou always wants to open up and cast a wide net. Their rhythms easily pull against each other.
◆ Scatter vs. Gather Tug-of-War: Gou's energy naturally spreads outward and probes; Bo's instinct is to shrink inward and defend. Their goals often go in opposite directions.
advice: Alternate 'retreat days' and 'scouting days' by agreement: during each fixed cycle, Bo handles inventory and reinforces the bottom line, while Gou goes out to network and connect with new opportunities, then reports back to Bo for evaluation and implementation.

one_liner: One is shoring up the foundation to keep the house from collapsing; the other is setting out banquet tables and building connections. Both stand on solid ground, but one plays it inward and the other outward.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram has the Mountain pressing down on the Receptive Earth; its Judgment says plainly, “It does not further one to undertake anything,” and the Image emphasizes “thickening the lower levels and securing the home” — a textbook period of contraction and defense. The Gathering Together hexagram has the Lake spreading over the Receptive Earth; its Judgment cries out, “It furthers one to undertake something” and “The king approaches the temple,” and the Image warns “remove the weapons and guard against the unexpected” — an active phase of gathering and expansion. The two hexagrams share the same Earth foundation, both knowing that if the roots are unstable, everything else fails, but their response logic is one of drawing in versus reaching out. Splitting Apart is like closing the door and hoarding grain in deep winter; Gathering Together is like arranging alliances in the spring light. The Receptive Earth can both bear the silence of the Mountain and nurture the flow of the Lake. The “thickening the lower levels” of Splitting Apart underwrites the festivities of Gathering Together, while the “undertaking with purpose” of Gathering Together breaks the deadlock of Splitting Apart's dull days. The two don't try to convince each other — they use the same solid ground to sustain a rhythm of alternating stillness and motion.
resonance: ★ Standing on the Same Solid Ground: Both understand that a towering building depends on an Earth foundation — they don't play at empty gestures and deeply value long-term roots.

★ Staying Vigilant in Peace: Splitting Apart's “thicken the lower levels and secure the home” and Gathering Together's “remove weapons and guard against the unexpected” both come from a strong sense of bottom-line thinking.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch in Advance and Retreat: One says stop fussing and hunker down, the other urges you to seize the moment and build contacts — their paces often clash.
◆ Emotional Channels Out of Sync: Mountain nature is silent and digests inward; Lake nature is outgoing and loves sharing. In communication they tend to find each other too dull or too loud.
advice: Set clear switching points between quiet periods and social days. Let Splitting Apart guard the bottom line and Gathering Together handle outward outreach — with distinct roles, don't cross the line.

one_liner: One is busy laying a foundation and shoring up against collapse; the other is bursting to shoot upward. Once the frame is set, together they can hold up a sky.
analysis: The image of Bo (Splitting Apart) is a mountain resting on the earth; it signifies decay and contraction, advising us to thicken the foundation, secure the home, and avoid reckless action. The image of Sheng (Pushing Upward) is wood growing from the earth; it signifies rising with the current and values accumulating small gains into great accomplishments. Their directions diverge — one descends, one ascends — yet they secretly align with the laws of nature. Bo is the guardian who, during turbulent times, stubbornly secures the bottom line and clears away excess. Sheng is the pioneer who, once set on a direction, breaks out of the earth through a daily cadence of small steps. Bo's caution keeps Sheng from overstepping and toppling; Sheng's vitality dissolves Bo's murky stagnation. The chemistry of this pair is essentially the interlocking of a defensive floor and long-term compounding: without Bo's underpinning, Sheng easily grows into hollow grass; without Sheng's pull, Bo simply turns into a stagnant pool.
resonance: ★ The kindred bond of rooting and branching: Bo's unyielding defense of the baseline gives Sheng stable soil, and Sheng's upward growth feeds the mountain's vitality in return — one guards, one advances, closing the loop.
★ Long-term resolve in unfavorable times: Bo knows not to thrash around when conditions are bad; Sheng believes in small steps adding up. Both trust that surviving the winter brings spring.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms out of step: Bo always wants to clear hidden risks before moving; Sheng thinks adjusting on the go is fine. One seeks stability and slows things down, the other seeks speed and looks reckless.

◆ Internal drain from tug-of-war: Bo's thickening the base and securing the home can harden into overcautiousness, stifling Sheng's upward drive; Sheng's southward campaign can make Bo feel the foundation is being hollowed out.
advice: Before each new plan, let Bo run a risk-and-floor assessment; then have Sheng break the plan into small weekly goals that can be acted on. Replace blind sprints with a solid base and micro-iterations.

one_liner: One holds the line and endures the bitter winter; the other grits their teeth and refuses to quit. Together, they are a gritty pair who can turn a dead end into a path forward.
analysis: In the Bo hexagram (Splitting Apart), the Mountain rests on the Earth; energy flows downward, and its wisdom is to thicken the foundation and steady the household — a classic defensive, conserving type. In the Kun hexagram (Oppression), the Lake has dried up, leaving no external resources, yet it demands total commitment to one's purpose — a lone brave warrior breaking out of adversity. When the two meet, it's like setting up a stage on the ruins: Bo's steadiness can cushion Kun's restlessness, keeping blind stubbornness from tipping into collapse; Kun's tenacity can ignite Bo's dullness, preventing the missed opportunities that come from too much retreat. Bo says, "Don't rush — lay the groundwork first." Kun says, "Even with no water, you have to keep moving." This pairing doesn't need smooth sailing; it's made for impossible situations. In the most desperate, resource-stripped straits, it can use dogged will and solid footing to endure until the tables turn.
resonance: ★ Shared bottom line: Both are in a downward cycle with scarce resources, so they know how to keep their edge sheathed and avoid blind expansion. In the low moments, they can support each other without adding drama.
★ Tenacity in adversity: Bo teaches staying rooted and storing strength; Kun forces a firm resolve. Both believe that if they endure, the sky will clear — their inner cores are in deep resonance.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythms: Bo says "not favorable for action" and advises quiet defense; Kun stresses "devote yourself to your purpose" and wants to forge ahead. One moves, the other stays, so they can easily trip each other up.

◆ Communication barrier: Kun's "words are not believed" means it talks a lot with no one listening, while Bo just keeps its head down building walls and never speaks up. Put them together and they can easily internalize their stress — everything ends up a guessing game.
advice: Set a clear line between defense and break-out: Bo takes charge of counting resources and securing the rear, while Kun takes charge of making a decisive charge when the time is ripe. Don't blur guarding the base with breaking through.

relationship_name: Clearing the Dross, Drawing the Deep
one_liner: You clear the ground with fearless decluttering; I dig the deep well to keep the living water flowing.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is a mountain resting on the earth; its core is 'not favorable to undertake anything.' In a time of decline, you must honestly strengthen the base and secure your home. The Well hexagram is wood above water; it values 'the town may change, but the well does not' — no matter how the outside world shifts, the nourishment underneath never runs dry. When these two hexagrams come together, they are the classic 'clearing the field and sustaining life' duo. Splitting Apart is like a great cleanup, stripping away layer after layer of showy burdens; at this moment, the worst thing is blind flailing, and The Well happens to be there to hold the bottom. Once the glitter is stripped away, the well's channel is not clogged; with the well water flowing, the peeled-away foundation gets the nourishment to revive. One does subtraction and holds the bottom line; the other does addition and supplies living water. In the valleys or transitions of life, they can form the most resilient survival alliance.
resonance: ★ Seeing the true taste after stripping away the shiny surface: once Splitting Apart clears out the outward bluster, the Well's living water can nourish the core without obstruction.

★ A Kindred commitment to holding the bottom line: Splitting Apart stresses the defensive posture of strengthening the base and securing home, while the Well offers the constant support of 'the town changes, but the well does not' — both trust in stability above all.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm of action: Splitting Apart explicitly says it is not favorable to undertake anything and advocates quiet defense, while the Well encourages the frequent coming and going around the well — one is still, one is moving, and they can easily trip each other up.

◆ Divergent views on resources: during decline, Splitting Apart tends to contract and cut losses, while the Well is used to sharing generously — friction easily arises over spending or investing energy.
advice: In a low period, don't rush outward. The Splitting Apart side should first clear internal clutter to make space; then the Well side can deliver resources in measured, need-based portions — no blind dumping.

one_liner: One focuses on shoring up the foundation against collapse; the other is eager to strike a match and change the skin. Get the rhythm right and it's a dangerous-building renovation; get it wrong and it's an instant blaze.
analysis: Bo (Splitting Apart) is like a steady guardian of the city walls. The mountain resting on the earth hints that the foundation is shifting, and at this time "it is not favorable to undertake anything"—the only move is to silently thicken the soil and stabilize the base. Ge (Revolution), by contrast, is the impatient breaker of deadlocks. Lake and fire press against each other, holding back a surge of energy to "regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons" and start over from scratch. When these two meet, Bo's steadiness just happens to catch Ge's danger, and Ge's breakthrough precisely cuts through Bo's stagnation. Without Bo's accumulated depth, Ge's transformation is a castle in the air; without Ge's fresh blood, Bo's persistence will only drag into a dead end. The whole essence of this relationship lies in "hitting the beat"—Bo holds the line and secures the base, Ge lights the fire and clears the way. Once they make it through the trust-building period, even rotten wood can be remade into a fresh beam.
resonance: ★ Complementary Foundation and Spark: Bo's "thickening the base to secure the home" gives Ge's "regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons" a safe buffer zone for trial and error, letting bold reforms avoid veering off course.

★ Strong Consensus on Timing: Both hexagram texts carry the wisdom of "waiting." Bo knows when to advance or retreat; Ge trusts its own day. Both understand that a good meal is worth waiting for, and when it's time to act, they strike without hesitation.
conflict: ◆ Clashing Paces: The Bo side is still patiently checking for hidden hazards and reinforcing the ground, while the Ge side is already eager to light the fire and burn away old rules. Each finds the other either too slow or too rash.

◆ Emotional Release on Different Frequencies: The mountain is silent and pressure-bearing; the lake-fire is outward and scorching. When trouble hits, one habitually bottles things up and suffers internally, while the other flips the table without warning. Communication easily breaks down.
advice: Before pushing for reform, the Ge side must leave a buffer period for the Bo side to take full stock of the situation. After the other side lights the fire, the Bo side shouldn't rush to douse it with cold water—first draw a clear bottom line, then let go.

relationship_name: Where the Stopping and the Still Embrace
one_liner: One quietly lays the foundation in the middle of a mess, the other simply draws the curtain at the boundary — both know exactly when to call it quits.
analysis: Splitting Apart is a mountainside eroding and peeling away, a reminder not to grit your teeth and push through — hurry up and thicken the soil beneath your home, mend the foundation. Keeping Still is two mountains stacked together, stressing the art of knowing your limits and guarding your boundaries, never letting your thoughts stray even half a step past the line. When you two come together, it feels like a perfectly coordinated strategic retreat. The heavy sense of decline in Splitting Apart is caught by the steady resolve of Keeping Still, and the cool detachment of Keeping Still is softened by Splitting Apart's down-to-earth pragmatism. Neither of you likes to stir up needless trouble; you both know to hit pause when the situation is cloudy or your energy is running on empty. Splitting Apart patches the drafty walls, Keeping Still keeps the outside noise shut out. This relationship doesn't chase soaring victory — instead, it has each other's back in the low valleys, turning non-interference into a higher form of survival wisdom.
resonance: ★ A Kindred Sense of Cutting Losses: Splitting Apart knows that forcing things brings nothing, Keeping Still knows when enough is enough — the two of you click perfectly on when to pull back.

★ Inward Grounding: Splitting Apart emphasizes thickening the foundation below, Keeping Still says don't let your thoughts leave their place — both of you pull energy inward rather than clinging outward, and your security comes from inner sedimentation.
conflict: ◆ Energy Sinks Too Deep: Splitting Apart already has an air of decline, and Keeping Still is pure stillness — together, you can easily fall into a stagnant deadlock where neither wants to make the first move.

◆ Boundaries Too Cold: Keeping Still's 'does not see the person' carries an inborn aloofness, and Splitting Apart's 'not favorable to undertake journeys' leans conservative — when emotions run high, you tend to build walls on both sides and lack warm exchange.
advice: When you hit a sticking point, agree to take turns leading: one bows their head to solidly lay the foundation, the other lifts it to draw the stop-loss line — don't let two pockets of quiet fester into inner friction.

one_liner: One clears away the wreckage, the other fires up the stove and cooks something new.
analysis: Hexagram Splitting Apart is the patience of 'subtraction' — rocks and stones crumble and return to the earth, teaching us not to thrash about in the low valley but to first compact the foundation. Hexagram The Cauldron is the boldness of 'addition' — wood feeds fire to transform raw ingredients, forging scattered resources into a new order. Put these two together and you have a perfect relay from 'clearing the field' to 'starting the game.' Splitting Apart's 'It does not further to undertake anything' is not about giving up; it's about making room. The Cauldron's 'Take up a correct position and consolidate destiny' is not busywork; it's finding the right heat. Without Splitting Apart sweeping away old accounts and settling the groundwork, The Cauldron's fire can easily burn into a hollow flame. Without The Cauldron raising the energy for renewal, Splitting Apart's thick base just becomes stagnant water. One still, one moving; one drawing in, one letting out — you turn the 'period of ruin' into an 'upgrade pack.'
resonance: ★ Endure the cold bench, and you'll get to serve the hot pot: Splitting Apart teaches you to hold steady and build the foundation; only then does The Cauldron have wood to burn and rice to cook. The stillness of the low times fuels the turnaround.

★ Once the mess is swept clean, new rules can take hold: Splitting Apart strips away the hollow shells layer by layer, and The Cauldron takes over the clean counter — placing the new plan steadily over the fire to simmer into flavor.
conflict: ◆ Those who fear the cold find the fire too hot; those who fear the fire find the ground too cold. Splitting Apart is used to drawing in and defending; when it meets The Cauldron's bold innovation, it feels the steps are too big and the roots are torn. The Cauldron, in turn, finds Splitting Apart too slow, mistaking caution for procrastination.

◆ If you rush to the feast before settling old accounts, the new dishes come out half-cooked: if Splitting Apart hasn't dug out the rotten roots, and The Cauldron is already adding fuel and seasoning, you'll end up boiling the hidden hazards into a mush — the busier you are, the messier it gets.
advice: Don't rush The Cauldron to produce results during Splitting Apart's cleanup phase. Spend the first two or three months clearing old accounts and emotional baggage, then light the fire together and test the dishes.

relationship_name: When Splitting Ends, Gradual Growth Begins
one_liner: First firm up the foundation, then slowly climb the slope—no one rushes the other.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram (Bo) is the image of a mountain slowly weathered and stripped away—a reminder that in times of decline, you must pull back, protect your core, and anchor your roots. The Development hexagram (Jian) is the image of wind moving through trees on the mountainside, teaching that everything grows in its own season, step by step. When these two hexagrams come together, it's like the rebuilding period after a great reshuffle. Bo is the force of subtraction: it trims away hollow branches, cuts the false growth, and tells you to face reality without thrashing around. Jian is the force of addition: it puts down roots and sprouts steadily on the solid foundation, one deliberate step at a time. Their chemistry doesn't come from instant sparks—it lives in the rhythm of breaking down first, then building up. Bo's stillness can temper Jian's restlessness; Jian's patience can dissolve Bo's gloom. Spend enough time together, and you'll understand that life isn't about charging uphill every day. Sometimes you need to step back and tamp down the muddy ground, so that later a great tree can take root and stand tall.
resonance: ★ Rooting without rushing: both agree that slow equals steady. Bo holds the line and doesn't charge ahead; Jian moves with the seasons and doesn't skip stages—their working rhythms naturally align.

★ Honoring simplicity to nurture true energy: Bo's 'steadying the base and securing the home' and Jian's 'dwelling among the worthy and cultivating good customs' both value inner substance. No flashy tricks—just the patient discipline of pushing a pawn forward one square a day.
conflict: ◆ Retreat meets ascent: Bo leans toward contraction and defense, feeling it isn't time to act; Jian wants to keep climbing the stairs—so they can get tangled over when to make a move.

◆ Heaviness drags on lightness: Bo's background is somber and conservative, always calculating risk first; Jian's wind-and-wood nature pushes forward with gentle warmth, and finds the other too slow—they easily step on each other's rhythm.
advice: When disagreement arises, don't rush to settle the grand direction. Together, take two weeks to inventory the most basic financial accounts and emotional bottom lines. After that, strictly follow a rhythm of advancing only one step per week.

relationship_name: Mountain and Thunder in Mutual Support
one_liner: One lays the foundation, the other takes on all comers.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is like mountain rock slowly weathering, reminding one to temper their sharp edges and consolidate their foundations; the Arousing hexagram is like spring thunder splitting the gloom, forcing one to face crises head-on and be reborn through breakthrough. When the two meet, it is like an old farmer reinforcing his granary before the thunderstorm season—Splitting Apart's 'thickening the base and securing the home' provides a cushioning layer for the Arousing's 'fear and trembling, self-reflection', while the Arousing's upheaval in turn pushes Splitting Apart to stop passive retreat. This combination does not chase quick success, but instead forges resilience to risk through repeated cycles of crisis and consolidation, fitting scenarios that require long-term vision yet are often hit by sudden turbulence.
resonance: ★ Solidly hold the line: Splitting Apart's thick-base-and-secure-home provides a physical and psychological buffer against the Arousing's sudden shocks.
★ Mutually awakened in crisis: The Arousing's thunder splits open Splitting Apart's inertia of decline, rousing its dormant power of repair.
conflict: ◆ Rhythmic mismatch: Splitting Apart's cautious waiting often slows the Arousing's lightning-fast decision cycle.
◆ Energy counteraction: The Arousing's urge to break through can easily shatter the fragile balance Splitting Apart has painstakingly maintained.
advice: Reserve one day each month for a stress test: use the Arousing's crisis simulation to test whether Splitting Apart's foundations are truly solid.

one_liner: One won't move for fear of falling into a pit; the other gets carried away and charges ahead. Put together, one pulls the brake and the other steps on the gas — just right.
analysis: The Bo hexagram is a mountain resting on the earth, centered on stability. It is not favorable for bold advances; everything must first be built on solid ground. The Gui Mei hexagram is thunder moving over the lake: emotions surge and momentum is at full throttle, but the judgment plainly warns that undertaking brings misfortune — a reminder not to be swept away by passion. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like an old house meeting a fresh renovation: Gui Mei's thunder-lake fire can break through Bo's stifling deadlock and bring vivid emotion and connection; while Bo's thick foundation and secure home give Gui Mei's impulse a safety net, teaching it to last long and recognize flaws — if you want something enduring, you must see the weaknesses and lay a solid foundation. One handles the gas pedal, the other repairs the chassis; their rhythms may seem out of sync, but in fact they are perfectly Complementary.
resonance: ★ One builds the foundation, the other explores new roads: Bo's practicality gives Gui Mei's romanticism a landing space, so feelings or collaborations don't float in midair.
★ Their crisis awareness is highly aligned: Bo fears peeling and decline; Gui Mei knows how to endure and spot decay. Both know to prepare for rain, so they can weather storms together.
conflict: ◆ Severely mismatched pace: Gui Mei finds Bo too slow, always applying the brakes; Bo finds Gui Mei too reckless, ignoring the consequences. Daily life can explode into fights over speed.

◆ The tug-of-war between defense and openness: Bo is used to layering on defenses, while Gui Mei wants to bare it all in one go. This probing between closing the door and breaking it down can easily backfire.
advice: Before any major decision, let Gui Mei turn their passion into a plan, then have Bo check through a risk list item by item. Only after both sign off should you take action.

one_liner: You own the spotlight at high noon; I’ll quietly tamp the earth at the mountain’s foot.
analysis: The Splitting Apart hexagram is like a mountain resting on the earth, emphasizing “it does not further one to undertake anything,” with energy turning inward and the core demand being “strengthen the base and secure the home” — the more the outer layer peels away, the more tenaciously one guards the foundation. The Abundance hexagram, by contrast, is thunder and lightning, fire and boiling oil, pointing directly to “fit to be at high noon,” meaning to seize the moment of peak brilliance and act with thunderous decisiveness and clear judgment. When these two hexagrams come together, it is a “preserve-the-gains” faction colliding with a “sprint” faction. The steadiness of Splitting Apart can catch the impatience of Abundance, preventing the radiance from growing so strong that it burns through the root; the thunderous momentum of Abundance can split open the oppressiveness of Splitting Apart, illuminating the corners where decay is quietly spreading. They do not need to be forcibly synchronized; instead, in the dislocation of “you charge forward, I cover the gap,” they complete a relay of energy as flourishing and decline alternate.
resonance: ★ Steadying the board: Splitting Apart’s “strengthen the base and secure the home” provides a safety cushion for Abundance’s aggressive expansion, preventing thunder-fire from becoming so intense that it turns back and consumes itself.
★ Breaking through to reveal truth: Abundance’s thunderous light can instantly see through Splitting Apart’s hidden crises, leaving the first signs of decline nowhere to hide.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm: Abundance values riding the momentum at high noon, while Splitting Apart insists that it does not further one to undertake anything and advocates quiet waiting — their action tempos will easily pull against each other.

◆ Internal energy drain: Splitting Apart’s contraction and defense can make Abundance feel hamstrung, while Abundance’s high-profile sorties accelerate the peeling and attrition of Splitting Apart’s foundations.
advice: Schedule the “charging period” and “maintenance period” separately: when Abundance is at the helm, go ahead and make bold decisions; when Splitting Apart is at the helm, resolutely step on the brakes and count the family assets — never issue cross commands.

relationship_name: Anchor the Base, Explore the Far
one_liner: You weld the foundation solid; I scout the road ahead — together we cure every kind of aimless thrashing.
analysis: The Bo hexagram is a mountain pressing down on the earth, energy sinking deep underground. Its wisdom is: when things are in decline, don't run around recklessly — thicken the base and you'll find stability. The Lü hexagram is fire burning on a mountain, carrying a wakeful clarity for feeling through unfamiliar territory: small steps, but bright eyes. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like an old foundation meeting a new guide. Bo's 'not favorable to undertake anything' reins in Lü's restlessness, reminding you not to rush out to expand territory before securing the home front. Lü's 'clarity and caution' opens a window in Bo's heaviness, letting those who hold the line know that even as the old order chips away, they can carry a spark and walk outward. One governs stillness and guarding within; the other governs movement and observing without. The energies don't clash — they mesh: Bo offers security, Lü offers direction. As long as they don't fight each other, one manages the chassis, the other reads the wind, and life gains resilience in the rhythm of contraction and exploration.
resonance: ★ With a solid base, you dare to step out: Bo's conserving mindset of thickening the foundation and settling the home gives exactly the ground beneath Lü's fire-on-the-mountain wandering. Together, they naturally know to secure the home first, then set out.

★ Caution laced with cleverness: Lü's philosophy of clarity and prudence clicks perfectly with Bo's restraint of 'not favorable to undertake anything.' Neither likes to gamble on luck — both habitually leave a retreat route before taking a step.
conflict: ◆ The base-keeper finds the pathfinder too restless: Bo thinks that when the situation is decaying, you should hunker down and stay safe, while Lü keeps wanting to venture out by the glimmer of light — so they can easily argue over every move.

◆ The drifting feeling dilutes belonging: Lü is used to packing up and leaving anytime, while Bo is fixated on rootedness and settling down. One feels home is too heavy; the other feels the heart is too adrift.
advice: When disagreements come up, first make a risk-baseline checklist together — write down the worst outcomes each of you can accept. Then the base-keeper uses the list to manage the home front, and the pathfinder uses it to plan the journey. Don't let emotions ram into each other.

one_liner: You weld the chassis shut; I drill through the cracks.
analysis: Splitting Apart is like a solitary mountain that has weathered storms; its Judgment plainly says, 'It does not further one to undertake anything,' and its core is to withdraw inward and firm up the foundation. The Gentle, by contrast, is the wind that slips through every opening, and it advocates, 'It furthers one to have somewhere to go' — relying on adapting to the moment, soft outside and firm within. When the two meet, it looks at first like a tug between stillness and movement, but in truth it is the complement of a chassis and a probe. If the mountain is not thick, the wind scatters as it passes; if the wind is not soft, it snaps on meeting the mountain. The decline phase of Splitting Apart most needs the Gentle's penetrating power to clear out old stagnation, and if the Gentle's renewing orders and carrying out affairs lacks the steadying support of Splitting Apart's 'thickening what is below and securing the dwelling,' it will easily drift wherever the current carries it. The beauty of this relationship: one side is responsible for compacting the foundation before the storm, and the other is responsible for tearing open a way out of deadlock through flexible means. As long as the mountain leaves a slit, the wind can pass through the hall; as long as the wind knows how to swirl with the terrain, the mountain can also renew itself through subtle change.
resonance: ★ Flexible dredging: The Gentle wind's smooth, penetrating nature can precisely thread into the mountain's flaking cracks, helping Splitting Apart clear away stale habits and avoid rigidly guarding itself into a stalemate.

★ Steady base, lifted wind: Splitting Apart's thickening the foundation and securing the dwelling provides a safety net for the Gentle wind's wide-ranging explorations, keeping its renewing orders and carrying out affairs from becoming rootless and erratic.
conflict: ◆ Rhythmic mismatch: Splitting Apart wants to hold still and preserve safety, while the Gentle wants to ride the momentum forward — one still, one moving, they can easily get tangled up in back-and-forth indecision.

◆ Opposing energy currents: Splitting Apart withdraws inward to prevent loss, while the Gentle radiates outward to break through — their different directions easily ignite arguments over whether to guard or charge.
advice: When disagreements arise, let Splitting Apart first draw the inviolable safety line, then let the Gentle explore and experiment freely within that boundary — set the frame, then roam, instead of clashing head-on.

one_liner: You quietly lay the foundation while I round up the crowd; once the footing is solid, the gathering really heats up.
analysis: The Bo hexagram shows a mountain resting on the earth. Its energy turns inward, advising against reckless advancement during a period of decline — instead, thicken the roots for stability. The Dui hexagram shows lakes mirroring each other in joy, two waters converging. Its energy opens outward, nourishing delight through communication and sharing. When these two meet, it's like a steadfast rock encountering flowing water. Bo's power to hold can check Dui's tendency to scatter, keeping social life from becoming idle burnout. Dui's joy can melt Bo's inertia, turning quiet persistence into warm companionship. One knows how to repair walls in the valley; the other knows how to stir waves in calm waters. There's no need to force the same rhythm — the one who holds the line and the one who breaks new ground are made for each other, blending practical grit with easygoing grace as a remedy for everyday life.
resonance: ★ Steady support and agile breakthrough: Bo's pragmatism can hold Dui's emotional waves steady, and Dui's brightness can quickly illuminate Bo's valleys.

★ Complementary stillness and openness: one excels at drawing boundaries and keeping calm in chaos, the other uses light conversation to break through deadlocks — both have security and expressiveness to spare.
conflict: ◆ Clashing rhythms: Bo prefers to retreat and protect, avoiding stirs; Dui loves outward expansion and frequent gatherings — they can easily dismiss each other as too dull or too flighty.
◆ Different wavelengths: Dui wants immediate feedback and emotional echo; Bo holds back until fully thoughtful — over time, awkward silences or restless friction arise.
advice: Reserve a half-day quiet zone each week: turn off phones, cook or walk together silently — letting Dui practice settling and Bo practice laughing easily.

one_liner: One clings to the base for fear of a cave-in; the other roams the world rallying the troops. Together they squeeze scattered sand into a brick.
analysis: The Splitting Apart (Bo) hexagram is like a stubborn rock that is weathering away yet holds its line, devoted to 'thickening the base and securing the home.' When danger comes, it shrinks back into its shell to mend the groundwork. The Dispersion (Huan) hexagram, by contrast, is a draft sweeping across the water — it advocates 'wind moving over the water' and excels at blowing scattered grains of sand together into a temple of shared faith. When these two meet, the first impression is a clash between the 'keep-the-status-quo' school and the 'break-the-gridlock' school, but beneath it lies hidden design. Bo's steadiness can catch Huan's flightiness, giving that aimless drift an anchor; Huan's agility can blow away Bo's gloom, turning the stubborn old compound into a spiritual rallying point where wandering hearts come home. Bo fears scattering; Huan is scattering itself — yet at the extreme of dispersion, it needs Bo's 'thickening the base' as the net underneath. The two, one contracting and one expanding, elevate physical defense into spiritual cohesion.
resonance: ★ Building a Spiritual Fortress Together: Bo repairs the physical foundation, Huan raises a shrine of faith — both are seeking a home for the wandering soul.

★ Partners in Breaking Through Adversity: Bo's 'not favorable to undertake anything' is a timely stop-loss; Huan's 'favorable to cross the great river' is seizing the tide to break out. One still, one moving, they just manage to dodge the worst.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: When trouble arrives, Bo is used to holding troops and fixing internal affairs, while Huan rushes to spread outward and build networks. One finds the other too sluggish, the other finds the first too rash.

◆ The Tug Between Control and Letting Go: Bo clings tightly to the core, afraid of losing resources, while Huan advocates going with the flow, dispersing and reorganizing. In key decisions, they often rub against each other over whether to 'hold on tight' or 'let go.'
advice: When you hit a disagreement, first have the Bo party take stock of bottom lines and resources, marking out a safe zone. Then let the Huan party reach out with a clear framework. Don't blindly expand before you know what you have.

one_liner: One holds the brake to keep the chassis steady, the other paints the lane to set the tempo—together, it's 'no need for drama to make the long haul.'
analysis: Bó (Splitting Apart) is like a mountain resting on the earth—it is about withdrawing and holding firm, not blindly charging ahead when energy is waning, but rooting downward and enriching the foundation. Jié (Limitation) is like a lake storing water—its core lies in measure and boundaries, channeling flow through clear limits. When these two meet, Bó provides the solid vessel Jié requires; without a stable mountain, water merely floods or dries up. Jié, in turn, gives Bó a sustainable operating mechanism, making 'thickening the base and securing the home' not a rigid defense but a disciplined way of storing energy. Bó's 'unfavorable to undertake anything' meets Jié's 'bitter limitation cannot be persevered in,' and together they form a dynamic balance: knowing when to pull back, and also how to stay flexible within the rules. This pairing is not suited for wild, sweeping sprints, but it excels at system upgrades in low valleys—gathering scattered resources and replacing consumption with restraint.
resonance: ★ A solid foundation makes rules easy to establish: Bó's 'thickening the base and securing the home' gives the relationship a risk-resistant bedrock, so Jié's structures never become castles in the air. Both partners share the underlying logic of steadying before moving.

★ Knowing how to leave space keeps the relationship from draining itself: Jié's sense of measure, paired with Bó's 'not favorable to undertake anything,' means the two naturally reject over-demanding and emotional overdraft. Giving each other room is exactly what makes it last.
conflict: ◆ Over-conservatism can miss the moment to break through: Bó tends toward lying flat and defending, and if Jié only watches the rules without reading the situation, the two together can turn caution into rigidity—drawing a prison around themselves just when a breakthrough is needed.

◆ Misjudging the measure can create suppression: Bó needs wide-open space to recuperate, while Jié habitually manages the pace with rules and frames. If restraint becomes too severe and turns into bitter limitation, what was meant to secure the home becomes a psychological burden.
advice: Once a month, set aside time for 'clearing old accounts + confirming bottom lines.' Cut out energy-draining trivialities, keep only three core rules, and allow each other to run naturally on your own breathing rhythm the rest of the time.

relationship_name: Steadfast Trust on a Shaky Foundation
one_liner: While you tamp down the foundation in the trough, I hand you my true heart at the wind's edge — one keeps the floor steady, the other keeps the warmth alive.
analysis: Bo is like autumn mountains shedding their leaves, with energy turning inward, seeking only the self-preservation of 'strengthening the base and settling the home.' Zhong Fu, by contrast, is like a clear breeze over the marsh, advocating the lenience of 'deliberating lawsuits and deferring executions' and the sincerity of 'trust reaching even pigs and fish.' When these two hexagrams meet, it is a collision between a realistic defensive line and the flow of emotion. Bo's caution backstops Zhong Fu's gullibility, preventing true-heartedness from being worn down by reality; Zhong Fu's transparency and fluidity blow away Bo's gloomy rigidity, keeping a declining phase from spiraling into a dead end. This is not blind optimism — it is about still using supple trust to mend the cracks after clearly seeing the predicament of 'not favorable to undertake anything.'
