analysis: Wu Wang (Innocence) is like a thunderbolt from heaven, insisting that right is right and wrong is wrong, with no tolerance for anything slipshod. Huan (Dispersion) is like wind moving over water, expert at dispersing and dissolving deadlocked situations. When these two hexagrams meet, it's really 'iron rules' meeting a 'flexible touch.' Innocence's directness can wound; Dispersion's following-the-current guidance buffers the edge. Conversely, if Dispersion only seeks to dissolve and pacify, it can lose its backbone — Innocence's 'uprightness' is its anchor. In this pairing, one keeps the big direction from veering off course, the other slowly unravels emotional and interpersonal knots. It's not about one changing the other; it's a hard bone wrapped in soft fascia, able to go further together.
resonance: ★ Breaking Through and Anchoring the Heart: Innocence's bottom-line principles plant an anchor in scattered situations, giving flowing energy a place to return to.
★ Going with the Flow: Dispersion's dissolving power paves the way along Innocence's frankness, so honest words don't land like a sledgehammer.
conflict: ◆ Looseness Hits an Iron Wall: Dispersion tends to resolve indirectly, but Innocence only sees right and wrong, easily feeling the other is dodging responsibility.
◆ Rigidity Shatters Gentleness: Innocence's 'not favorable to undertake anything' can be a blunt cut, while Dispersion needs breathing room and transitions; head-on clashes only hurt both.
advice: When disagreements arise, the principle-upholding side should pause for three seconds before rushing to conclusions, and the situation-dissolving side shouldn't just circle around the issue — state the core need directly, and engage with 'honest words plus a soft landing.'

one_liner: Lead with a true heart, back it with rules—not reckless, not rigid.
analysis: Wu Wang (Innocence) carries the directness of heaven-thunder, acting entirely from the heart without detours. Jie (Limitation) is like water stored above the lake—naturally knowing how to set boundaries and control pace. The chemistry of this pair lies in knowing when to tighten and loosen: Innocence's purity can dissolve Limitation's rigidity, avoiding the bitter austerity of clinging to dogma. Meanwhile, Limitation's measure can rein in Innocence's impulsiveness, keeping harmony with the time from becoming blind haste. Together, it's like a wild horse fitted with a good saddle—not struggling, not indulging, but placing natural enthusiasm into a sustainable vessel, and life grows more ordered the longer you go.
resonance: ★ Setting limits with the flow: Innocence honors responding to heaven and time, while Limitation excels at framing natural momentum, so honest words don't become a wounding blade.

★ Leaving space without crossing lines: The drive of heaven-thunder paired with the tolerance of lake-water—the two know to brake proactively when passion runs high, giving the relationship room to breathe.
conflict: ◆ Rules snag intuition: Innocence hates being boxed in; once Limitation's rules become too rigid, it makes that natural sincerity feel stifled and miserable.
◆ Restraint turns ascetic: When Limitation over-tightens, it slides into nitpicking details, and then Innocence's free-spiritedness may feel the other is deliberately picking fights.
advice: Before setting any rule, carve out a twenty percent flexible space; before acting on impulse, take three minutes to calculate the real costs. Write the bottom line together with a margin for change.

one_liner: One's job is to rip off the masks; the other's is to keep the real heart warm. As a team, their whole approach to life is 'truth told softly.'
analysis: Innocence (Wu Wang) is like a thunderclap rolling across the sky—it's all about the 'original face,' with no room for dilution, and the slightest deviation invites disaster. Inner Truth (Zhong Fu) is the breeze skimming the lake—it relies on 'heart-to-heart empathy,' capable of moving even pigs and fish with sincerity. When these two hexagrams pair up, it's the hard rules of heaven colliding with the soft empathy of the human world. Innocence draws the bottom line and absolutely tolerates no falsehood; Inner Truth provides a buffer zone, translating blunt reality into truths that can actually be heard. Without Innocence's 'rightness,' Inner Truth easily becomes an unprincipled pushover; without Inner Truth's 'gentleness,' Innocence's directness easily becomes a cold arrow that wounds. Together, one hard and one soft, they simmer 'absolute truth' into 'trustworthy authenticity.'
resonance: ★ Bottom-line support: Innocence's 'error brings calamity' draws a red line for the relationship, while Inner Truth's 'deliberate over judgments and defer executions' leaves room within that line—both know the other never plays it false.
★ Soft wind transforms thunder: Inner Truth's wind over the lake wraps Innocence's bluntness in understanding, so hard truths don't shatter trust but instead take root and grow.
conflict: ◆ An iron face struggles to make room for feeling: Innocence insists on 'following heaven and the times, allowing no deviation,' and when it meets Inner Truth's compassionate 'lightening sentences and deferring death,' it tends to see the other as muddying the waters and lacking principles.

◆ A soft heart hits a hard nail: Inner Truth habitually uses empathy to seep in slowly, but Innocence's thunderous temper simply can't wait; when provoked, it mistakes Inner Truth's patience for dawdling, and communication cuts out altogether.
advice: When disagreements arise, the Innocence side should shut up for three seconds and swallow the judgment; the Inner Truth side should stop beating around the bush with chicken-soup wisdom, lay out specific needs directly, and align using a 'just the facts, no labels' approach.

relationship_name: Guard the True, Heed the Small
one_liner: One avoids pointless hustle, the other avoids overreaching—they make an exceptionally solid team.
analysis: Innocence is like a thunderbolt from a clear sky—it tears through illusion and points straight to what is real, emphasizing going with the flow and not acting on impulse. Preponderance of the Small is like muffled thunder rolling through the mountains, reminding us that small matters may be fine-tuned while large affairs call for restraint. When these two come together, the first sets the ground rule of “do not cross the line,” and the second supplies the flexibility of “adjust as needed.” In a startup, for example, Innocence keeps direction true to the path, while Preponderance of the Small allows modest improvements in sales pitch and operational details. But Innocence’s demand for absolute authenticity can collide with Preponderance of the Small’s “small overstepping”: when Preponderance of the Small wants to use a clever tactic to break a deadlock, Innocence will question whether the original heart has been lost. This relationship is like an old master training an apprentice—the master holds to the rules, the apprentice tries his hand at clever tricks. Once they find their rhythm, they can carve out a work of art that has both backbone and spirit.
resonance: ★ Integrity without compromise: both Innocence’s “wrongness brings harm” and Preponderance of the Small’s “overdoing humility” reject flashiness, favoring solid, down-to-earth action.
★ A keen sense of proportion: Preponderance of the Small’s caution in “preferring below to above” and Innocence’s restraint in “no advantage in moving ahead” form a natural risk filter.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched pacing: Innocence waits on the natural turn of time, while Preponderance of the Small wants to test the waters with small moves—one looks dilatory, the other rash.

◆ Differing perceptions of measure: Innocence strives for absolute purity, Preponderance of the Small accepts the gray zone of “excess is no better than deficiency”—tension arises over tight control versus room to maneuver.
advice: When key decisions loom, let Innocence draw the red line—what is absolutely off-limits—and let Preponderance of the Small map the operating zone within it—where details can be flexible. Review and adjust the boundaries every month.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Sincerity and Caution
one_liner: One fears veering off course, the other fears capsizing; together they make a steady crossing.
analysis: The Hexagram of Innocence (Wu Wang) is like a sudden thunderclap in a clear sky—it insists on acting without pretense and moving in accord with the times. The Hexagram of After Completion (Ji Ji) resembles boiling water over a fire—it warns that hidden changes lurk after success. When these two collide, it is like a doer paired with an early-warning system: the pure momentum of Innocence drives things to fruition, while After Completion's crisis awareness weaves a safety net. The straightforwardness of Heaven-Thunder meets the meticulousness of Water-Fire, often pulling between 'should we charge ahead or hold back?' But if you anchor direction with the rectitude of Innocence and prune excess with the caution of After Completion, you can walk a virtuous cycle of 'not arrogant in success, not timid in facing danger.'
resonance: ★ Sincerity as the foundation + attention to detail: Wu Wang keeps it real, Ji Ji zeroes in on loopholes—together you have boldness and fewer missteps.
★ Seize the moment + keep a fallback: Heaven-Thunder seizes the timing, Water-Fire prepares the retreat—you can advance and defend in changing circumstances.
conflict: ◆ Straightforwardness collides with overcaution: Wu Wang finds Ji Ji paranoid; Ji Ji finds Wu Wang too reckless.
◆ The tug between purity of purpose and risk anxiety: Wu Wang wants to push through in one go, Ji Ji always wants to stop mid-way for checks.
advice: Before major decisions, the Wu Wang side should proactively share risk plans; the Ji Ji side should turn worries into concrete checklists rather than vague warnings.

one_liner: You just keep walking forward from the heart; I'll hold the magnifying glass and slowly untangle the knots. Don't rush into the river—first feel for the stones.
analysis: Wu Wang (Innocence) is all about 'no pretense, no reckless moves'—like a clean crack of thunder splitting through empty posturing. Wei Ji (Before Completion), by contrast, is 'the task not yet done, fire and water turning away from each other,' a reminder not to let your guard down near the finish line. When these two hexagrams meet, one breaks through with authenticity, the other closes with prudence. Wu Wang's bluntness may make Wei Ji seem too impetuous, but Wei Ji's exacting worry is precisely what can catch the latent risk hidden in Wu Wang's 'if not correct, misfortune.' Together, they're like an old hand taking a novice on a night drive: Wu Wang keeps the wheel steady and on course, while Wei Ji keeps an eye on the dashboard for hidden problems. No games, no rushing—once the 'true' is planted firmly, the tangled mess will naturally straighten itself out.
resonance: ★ Thunder and Fire mirroring each other: Wu Wang's pure intuition can cut straight through Wei Ji's indecision, while Wei Ji's step-by-step approach can catch the blind spots Wu Wang might step over.

★ Timing and discernment: Both deeply disdain blind conformity—one moves with the seasons without reckless action, the other reads the situation before making a move. The rhythm differs, but the underlying logic is remarkably in sync.
conflict: ◆ Out-of-step pacing: Wu Wang thinks Wei Ji overthinks and misses opportunities; Wei Ji finds Wu Wang too idealistic, blind to the hidden reefs in reality.

◆ Wet tail: Wei Ji's over-analysis wears down the crisp decisiveness of Wu Wang's 'thunder moves across the world.' The draining cycle of repeated testing makes Wu Wang feel everything is bogged down in mud.
advice: Divide the work clearly: Wu Wang sets the overall direction and bottom lines; Wei Ji handles breaking down the steps and managing risks. Before acting, ask 'Does this align with our true heart?' then ask 'Are the details complete?'

one_liner: Both of you are quiet accumulators, and together you top off the reservoir to the brim.
analysis: The two Gen (Mountain) trigrams pressing over Qian (Heaven) are essentially drawing outward momentum back inward. When you meet, you don't need small talk to understand that grounded confidence of "save it up first and act later." In the hexagram image, "Heaven within the Mountain" has always been about openness and sedimentation. When two Great Accumulations meet, it's like two underground reservoirs connecting—knowledge, experience, and patience irrigate each other and grow ever deeper. But when accumulation goes to the extreme, it turns into hoarding. Both of you are too used to waiting for the wind, and you may miss the exact second it rises. Fortunately, the hexagram text says, "It is auspicious not to eat at home," meaning once the store is full, you must go out and use it. The biggest danger to your relationship is being all talk and no action. You need to turn the substance inside you into real, tangible synergy to avoid the deadlock of two mountains guarding each other.
resonance: ★ Kindred Sedimentation: Both of you know how to tuck your brilliance into daily life, not rushing to perform, yet able to hold each other up in quiet support.
★ Spiritual Resonance: You both believe in "studying the words and deeds of those who came before," so discussions about historical lessons or long-term visions click instantly without effort.
conflict: ◆ Slow Tempo: You both tend to "store first, release later," so when issues arise, you often wait for the other to move, and neither wants to break the deadlock first.
◆ Overthick Boundaries: Overlapping mountains can easily fence each other in, and excessive caution can leave the relationship short on fresh, lively warmth.
advice: Agree to pick one long-brewing matter each month and jointly see it through to completion, so the reservoir doesn't become a stagnant pond.

one_liner: On the surface both stay steady, but underneath one is holding back a big move while the other is simply catching their breath — together, life feels remarkably solid.
analysis: Both are crowned by the Mountain (Keeping Still), so they naturally know when to pause and never show their hand too soon. The Taming Power of the Great is like a think tank, storing the experience of those who came before and the energy of heaven and earth, aiming to cross great rivers one day; Nourishment is like a meticulous actuary, attending to daily needs and measured words, valuing a long, steady stream. When they meet, one offers long-term strategic reserve, the other manages the present rhythm of body and mind. This is not a flash of passion but a long-term partnership: you accumulate grounding, I cultivate vitality — however fierce the outside storm, inside there is order.
resonance: ★ Both practice the art of restraint: their upper trigrams share the Mountain (Keeping Still), so they instinctively know when enough is enough and don't reveal their cards, creating a calm, unhurried security between them.

★ A long-termist resonance: The Taming Power of the Great gathers insight and breadth, Nourishment sustains the body and discretion; both believe in building depth before striking, turning ordinary days into a slow-burn momentum.
conflict: ◆ The tug between vision and daily life: The Taming Power of the Great is always ready to venture outward for something big, while Nourishment is anchored to the day's meals and measured words — each may see the other as reckless or overly frugal.

◆ A rhythm mismatch in releasing energy: Qian metal below wants to break ground and store power, Zhen wood below wants to grow with the moment; one focuses on strategic reserves, the other on immediate replenishment, so decisions can become two separate calculations.
advice: Hold a monthly reconciliation: the Taming Power of the Great side sketches six-month goals, while the Nourishment side reviews daily expenses and energy allocation. Break the grand vision into executable weekly plans, keeping ideals from floating or draining you.

one_liner: Quietly amassing strength, but ready to flip the table when it counts.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a steady mountain, valuing 'broad knowledge of past words and deeds.' It quietly accumulates experience, cultivates connections, and refines inner strength, never making a move until the timing is right. The Preponderance of the Great, by contrast, is lake water flooding over trees—even under the pressure of a 'bending ridgepole,' it charges ahead, trusting in 'independence and fearlessness,' and deliberately picks the toughest bones to gnaw. When these two collide, it's like a reservoir meeting a floodgate. The deep reserves of Great Taming can underpin the reckless impulses of Great Exceeding, providing a safety net for breakthrough moves. And Great Exceeding's decisiveness and boundary-breaking nature ignites the energy Great Taming has been storing for years, pushing it out of its comfort zone to cross great rivers. One thickens the foundation, the other smashes through the ceiling—together they're a winning hand.
resonance: ★ Foundation and Breakthrough: The deep experience Great Taming has amassed can steadily catch the loss of control when Great Exceeding's 'ridgepole bends,' giving even radical risk-taking a safe exit.

★ Breaking Out in Tune: Great Taming's 'not eating at home' and Great Exceeding's 'it furthers one to have somewhere to go' both urge venturing outward—together, neither is content to rest on their laurels.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Great Taming prefers a steady, gradual build, while Great Exceeding always finds the pace too slow and easily sees the other as stalling and missing the window of opportunity.

◆ Resource Philosophy Clash: Great Taming values long-term savings and nipping problems in the bud; Great Exceeding is willing to bet big or even overdraw to produce results—often sparking complaints about pointless thrashing.
advice: Before any major decision, let Great Taming spend three days running risk simulations and mapping out a stop-loss line; then hand full executive authority to Great Exceeding to execute the breakthrough. Never make the call at an emotional peak.

one_liner: One goes deep to build reserves; the other wades through water to break a path.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is about 'a mountain within heaven'—pressing sharpness into a steady base, gaining confidence through 'learning much from what came before.' The Abysmal, by contrast, is 'water flowing on and on'—born to tumble through rapids, relying on 'the heart's constancy' to find a way through. When these two energies meet, it's like a deep mountain reservoir facing a surging underground river. The Taming Power's 'stillness' can contain the Abysmal's 'danger,' keeping momentum from being blindly spent; the Abysmal's 'flow' can vitalize the Taming Power's 'reserves,' preventing hidden strength from turning into dead water. One provides strategic depth, the other handles tactical breakthroughs. As long as the Taming Power doesn't use dogma to dam up the water, and the Abysmal doesn't use impatience to drain the mountain, they can find the exact rhythm between storing power and breaking through.
resonance: ★ Stability in the midst of danger: the profound grounding of the Taming Power catches the Abysmal's pitching through storm-waves, giving every risk a safe retreat.
★ Stored flow becomes momentum: the Abysmal's ceaseless movement gives the Taming Power's static accumulation an outlet, putting all its saved strength to the sharpest use.
conflict: ◆ Blocking and colliding: if the Taming Power over-fortifies or moralizes, it will suffocate the Abysmal like a dam holding back water—stirring up an undercurrent of rebellion.
◆ Consumption and anxiety: if the Abysmal only charges ahead without looking back, it will squander the Taming Power's hard-stored resources like running water, sparking a crisis of trust.
advice: The Taming Power simply lays out the logistics and safety net, then lets the Abysmal charge forward; every time the Abysmal hits a wall and returns, the Taming Power only offers tea and reviews what happened—never raking up old stories or forcing a stop.

one_liner: You quietly build the nest egg; I make things happen beautifully.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is the quiet, steady force of 'tucking the sky into a mountain'—deeply reserved, slowly accumulating. The Clinging (Li) is the continuous glow of 'two fires layered,' spreading its influence in all directions. When these two hexagrams come together, they complete each other's blind spots: without the foundation of Great Taming, Li's fire can burn into a wisp of hollow smoke—pretty to look at but not warm enough to touch; without Li's expression, Great Taming's treasures become invisible dead stock. The mountain builds a solid hearth for the fire, giving the light lasting endurance; the fire casts a spotlight on the mountain, revealing all the wisdom and depth stored inside. One works on fundamentals backstage, the other brings the stage to life. Put together, it is 'having substance and daring to show it—and showing it for the long run.'
resonance: ★ Fuel for the hearth: The steady foundation of Great Taming supplies Li's fire with an endless flow of fuel, so the light is not a brief flash of false heat but a warm glow that keeps burning.

★ Stored scriptures, mirrored world: When the 'words and deeds of old' saved in Great Taming meet Li's 'continuous brightness illuminating the four directions,' learning is no longer dust on the bookshelf but living wisdom that can awaken others.
conflict: ◆ A quiet jar meets a burst of light: Great Taming prefers to simmer slowly and ponder again and again, while Li is in a hurry to reveal every thought. When their rhythms are off, they tend to blame each other as 'too slow' or 'too restless.'

◆ Protective closeness vs. full exposure: Great Taming wants to keep good things tucked away for further nurturing, while Li feels 'if it's gold, it should be hung out to shine.' This makes it easy to pull in opposite directions about when to reveal the bottom card and how much reserve to keep.
advice: Create a rhythm of 'store energy, then shine': Great Taming stays backstage accumulating substance and setting boundaries, while Li handles frontstage timing and presentation. Neither should cross over into the other's work.

one_liner: A composed soul with real substance meets an open-hearted receiver—together, it's a sincere and long-lasting bond.
analysis: Great Taming is 'Heaven within the Mountain'—like a deep well quietly storing life experience, it prizes steady accumulation and slow release. Influence is 'Lake on the Mountain'—like living water, it prizes an open heart. When the two come together, Great Taming's steadiness gives Influence's sensitivity a solid foundation, while Influence's agility brings Great Taming's stored reserves to life. Great Taming wants to output value, and Influence can take it all in and feed emotional warmth back. One brews experience into wine; the other savors the lingering finish. Without Influence, Great Taming risks becoming a self-admiring library; without Great Taming, Influence's resonance easily stops at a taste.
resonance: ★ A library meets its kindred spirit: Great Taming's historical wisdom precisely fills the cognitive gaps that appear when Influence opens itself with an empty heart—minds resonate on the same frequency.
★ A deep well meets a living spring: Great Taming's rich reserves give Influence's intuitive receptivity a stable base, keeping emotional exchanges grounded and vivid.
conflict: ◆ Slow burn meets instant access: Great Taming habitually mulls things over and stores up energy, often missing the best window for the immediate emotional response Influence craves.
◆ Guarding boundaries meets going with the flow: Great Taming's adherence to principle and restraint can sometimes cold-shoulder Influence's unguarded overtures, making it seem unromantic.
advice: Great Taming, don't wait until everything is perfect to respond—when Influence shares, respond with emotional warmth first. Influence, don't rush for promises—give Great Taming space to digest and settle, and replace high-frequency questioning with steady, long-lasting companionship.

one_liner: One quietly stockpiles the family nest egg, the other sticks to their principles—together they make a partnership tough enough to weather anything.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great, like a mountain holding the sky, is about sedimentation and stored energy; its Image reminds us to learn from history and cultivate virtue. Duration, like thunder and wind stirring each other, is about endurance and fixed direction; its Image states that one must have an unshakable standard to stand firm. When the two come together, it is like a reservoir paired with a diversion canal: the Taming Power stores the living water of wisdom, and Duration provides the stable channel for release. The mountain's solidity can anchor the restlessness of thunder and wind, while the dynamism of thunder can enliven the mountain's heaviness. In practical life, this pairing is made for long-term projects—the broad accumulation of the Taming Power feeds Duration's steadfastness, and Duration's focused commitment keeps that accumulation from becoming a castle in the air. But beware: the Taming Power's 'wide learning' may dilute Duration's 'immutability,' while Duration's rigidity may fetter the Taming Power's flexibility.
resonance: ★ Amassed power meets the long game: the Taming Power's stored energy gives Duration its staying power, and Duration's steadiness ensures the accumulation is not wasted.
★ Aligned goals: both value long-term worth—one stocks the grain, the other paves the road; together they can go far.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm: the Taming Power wants to explore new directions, while Duration demands sticking to the original plan.
◆ Flexibility vs. rigidity: the Taming Power adjusts when circumstances change, but Duration's 'unchanging course' can seem inflexible.
advice: Set a monthly 'review day': the Taming Power lists new gains, Duration checks whether the original intention has drifted—replace rigid persistence with dynamic calibration.

relationship_name: Mutual Growth of Accumulation and Retreat
one_liner: One builds the nest egg; the other leaves room to breathe—together they avoid internal friction.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great belongs to the Mountain, and its art is drawing Heaven's energy inward, nourishing virtue and talent through wide knowledge of past words and deeds. Retreat belongs to Heaven; no matter how high the mountain, it cannot stop Heaven's movement. It teaches that when there is a mountain under Heaven, one keeps petty people at a distance—not with animosity but with dignity—and makes a graceful exit when circumstances turn. When the two hexagrams meet, their rhythms are complementary. The Taming Power's reserve gives Retreat the capital for falling back; Retreat's withdrawal gives the Taming Power space to digest and settle. One habitually accumulates energy in depth; the other innately needs breathing room. Once they grasp each other's pace, they won't mistake saving for controlling, nor stepping back for escaping; instead, through the interchange of advance and retreat, they can cultivate a thicker, richer bond.
resonance: ★ The Art of Leaving Space: The experiences the Taming Power gathers need Retreat's yielding to digest; giving each other breathing room actually makes the bond sturdier.
★ Clear Boundaries: Retreat's dignified withdrawal—keeping distance without hatred—protects the Taming Power's confidence to develop outward, so neither ever holds the other hostage.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: The Taming Power always wants to stockpile a little more security, while Retreat feels the urge to pull back as soon as the atmosphere tightens—easily becoming a chase-and-run pattern.
◆ Misread as Indifference: Taking the Taming Power's reserve as coldness, or Retreat's boundaries as not caring—without communication, both end up sulking separately.
advice: Establish clear periods for accumulation and windows for ventilation. When you want to conserve energy, say so in advance; when you need to withdraw, give a definite return date. Don't test each other's limits with silent treatment.

one_liner: Same engine — one revs in neutral, the other floors it in fifth gear.
analysis: Both have Qian (The Creative) as their lower trigram, and deep down they harbor powerful drive and ambition. For The Taming Power of the Great (Hexagram 26), the upper trigram is Mountain, emphasizing learning from the words and deeds of the past — like a reservoir, it stores energy inward, building up before releasing. For The Power of the Great (Hexagram 34), the upper trigram is Thunder, emphasizing strength and vigor — like lightning, it discharges outward, splitting everything in its path. When the two come together, one tends to find the other too slow, and the other too reckless. But precisely because their core is the same, Great Taming's long-term foresight can give Great Power's rashness a navigation system, and Great Power's swift decisiveness can push Great Taming to cash in on its accumulated capital. It's not about one changing the other; it's a relay race between storing energy and breaking through.
resonance: ★ Same frequency of purpose: Both share the lower Qian trigram, so each knows deep down the other is determined to get things done — you understand each other's ambition without words.

★ Shared observance of rules: Great Taming values accumulating virtue and nurturing talent; Great Power adheres to 'Do not tread on what is not proper.' One sets internal boundaries, the other draws external lines — neither deals in empty talk.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythm: Great Taming is used to inventorying resources before acting, finding Great Power too impetuous; Great Power is used to breaking through first and optimizing later, finding Great Taming too slow and missing chances.
◆ Energy temperature difference: Great Taming's energy is inward and reserved, always leaving room in speech; Great Power's energy is explosive and outward, blunt and trigger-happy.
advice: When disagreements arise, let Great Taming plot the route and inventory resources, and let Great Power step on the gas and clear obstacles. Divide the work clearly and don't cross lines to micromanage.

one_liner: One builds the foundation, the other charges ahead — in sync, steady progress.
analysis: Great Accumulation is like deep mountains hiding jade, emphasizing the settling of learning and virtue; Progress is like the dawn sun, valuing the display of talent and action. The mountain is steady, the fire is fierce; the thick accumulation of Great Accumulation provides the foundation for Progress's bursting forth, and Progress's clarity opens a window for Great Accumulation's quiet cultivation. When the two meet, it is like an old master craftsman encountering a cutting-edge designer: one polishes inner skill without rushing to show it, the other flashes sharpness and dares to try. But if the mountain presses down and smothers the fire, or the fire burns the mountain's trees, it becomes a stalemate — if Great Accumulation is overly conservative it will slow Progress's pace, and if Progress blindly rushes ahead it may deplete Great Accumulation's reserves.
resonance: ★ Complementary rhythm of storing energy and shining: Great Accumulation settles depth, Progress lights the way ahead — one lays the foundation, the other builds the tower.
★ A kindred unity of knowledge and action: Great Accumulation's scholarship meets Progress's drive, and knowledge takes root and blooms.
conflict: ◆ Differences in pace can cause friction: the mountain seeks stability, the fire is impatient for progress; mismatched steps drain energy.
◆ The tug-of-war between caution and risk: Great Accumulation prioritizes risk avoidance, Progress charges ahead — decisions often diverge.
advice: Hold a monthly 'Reserve & Radiance Dialogue': Great Accumulation lists its reserves, Progress reports its advances, calibrating resources and rhythm in both directions.

one_liner: One is frantically building up a big move, the other advises you not to show your cards yet—together they embody "steady, precise, and ruthless."
analysis: Da Chu (The Taming Power of the Great) presses heaven into the mountain's belly, emphasizing deep accumulation and explosive release, biding its time. Ming Yi (Darkening of the Light) buries light beneath the earth, teaching one to sheathe brilliance in adversity and cultivate clarity through obscurity. This pairing is like a strategist meeting a sleeper agent: Da Chu calculates "favorable for crossing the great river," amassing capital for a big move; Ming Yi reminds to "persevere through hardship," keeping one's wits close when the times are unclear. Their chemistry lies in a fundamental consensus on pacing—both understand restraint, but one gathers strength to strike, the other hides to survive. Da Chu's "accumulating virtue" can compensate for Ming Yi's gloom, and Ming Yi's "use of obscurity" can temper Da Chu's impulsiveness—partners suited for long-term positioning and crossing the dark night together.
resonance: ★ Both understand the art of "holding back the ultimate move": Da Chu hoards the essence of heaven and earth in the mountain, Ming Yi hides an unquenchable inner flame underground—neither rushes for temporary glory; they believe in long-termism.

★ Clear-headed partners in adversity: Da Chu builds confidence by "learning from the words and deeds of the past," while Ming Yi preserves strength by "using obscurity to gain clarity"—both can hold steady in downturns without making reckless moves.
conflict: ◆ Their pacing never quite syncs up: Da Chu feels the provisions are ready and it's time to charge and break through, while Ming Yi feels the environment is too dangerous and they must remain hidden—one wants to pull off something big, the other just wants to stay alive.

◆ The tug-of-war between self-expression and self-concealment: Da Chu is used to cultivating talent openly and waiting for the right price, while Ming Yi deliberately plays dumb and shows weakness—over time, each may find the other too flamboyant or too repressed.
advice: When disagreement arises, don't rush to persuade the other. Da Chu takes charge of calculating resources and making contingency plans, while Ming Yi evaluates environmental risks and sets safety boundaries. Coordinate in the order of "Ming Yi probes first, Da Chu strikes later."

one_liner: You're building up big skills to venture outward, while I keep a small flame and simmer our days into a fragrant life.
analysis: Great Taming is like mountains holding heaven within—its bones carry the adventurous spirit of “it is favorable to seek sustenance elsewhere,” skilled at long-term planning and gathering momentum, eyes always on the great river in the distance. The Family, by contrast, is like wind feeding fire—valuing words with substance and deeds with constancy, turning life into an orderly, steady stream. When these two hexagrams come together, it's a grand vision meeting everyday life. If Great Taming's ambition lacks the hearth-smoke grounding of The Family, it floats in midair; if The Family's stability lacks Great Taming's farsighted guidance, it gets mired in trivia. One pushes outward to build reserves, the other tends inward to steady the heart—each supports the other, so the journey is both steady and far-reaching.
resonance: ★ The rapport of stored power and steady warmth: Great Taming's slow-burn breakthrough needs The Family's day-by-day rhythm to carry it, or the momentum runs out.
★ The meshing of vision and groundedness: The Family's discipline of matching words to deeds can break Great Taming's grand plan to cross great rivers into executable steps.
conflict: ◆ Grand narrative collides with daily necessities: Great Taming always talks strategy and long-term vision, while The Family cares more about immediate expenses and household rules. When frequencies clash, mutual contempt creeps in.

◆ The pull between venturing outward and guarding within: Great Taming believes in “not eating at home” and loves running out to find opportunities, while The Family favors “the maiden's constancy” and wants more time spent building the home front. Out-of-step paces breed distance.
advice: Break Great Taming's long-term goals into small family projects you can review each month, and advance them on The Family's rhythm of constancy. That gives you room to roam while letting every step leave an echo.

one_liner: One hunkers down charging a big move; the other loves to differ. Their squabbling ends up blazing a wider trail.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a storehouse tucked deep between heaven and earth: it values deep accumulation and slow release, packing in experience until the moment ripens to cross the great river. Opposition, meanwhile, is fire leaping upward and lake water seeping downward—naturally contrarian, yet it manages to strike sparks within the shared and the different. When these two come together, the Taming Power's steadiness can underwrite Opposition's leaping energy, keeping differences from dissolving into sand; and Opposition's nitpicking can puncture the Taming Power's tendency to build in isolation, forcing it to drag its hoarded substance into the light. The contrarian crackle of Fire and Lake meets the encompassing patience of Mountain and Heaven—not a contest of dominance, but using difference as a whetstone. The Taming Power solidifies the groundwork; Opposition makes trial runs at each fork. When the scope of 'not eating at home' meets the flexibility of 'small things bring good fortune,' they turn a cold bench into a hot one and hammer differences into a working game.
resonance: ★ Thick Base Catching Sparks: The Mountain-Heaven depths of the Taming Power steadily catch the leaping, divergent inspiration of Opposition, keeping creativity from floating in mid-air without a place to land.
★ Nitpicking Refines Gold: Opposition's built-in 'spot the difference' radar precisely filters out the Taming Power's hoarded redundancy, leaving only the substance that can truly land.
conflict: ◆ Slow Simmer Meets Quick Flame: The Taming Power favors long-term dormancy and refinement, finding Opposition too fussy over trifles; Opposition, in turn, finds the other rigid—stopping before the bloom, withering too soon.

◆ Deep Pool Splits the Light: The Taming Power wants to gather all energy into one point; Opposition prefers to scatter in every direction. When allocating resources, they often clash over whether to concentrate or spread.
advice: Once a month, schedule a session for picking things apart. The Taming Power brings its accumulated plans; Opposition's only job is to raise counterpoints. After the argument, immediately pick one smallest goal and execute it.

one_liner: You stockpile the skills, I wade through the detours — together we play the long game of rough first, steady later.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great has Heaven within the Mountain, and its key word is 'accumulate': quietly storing up insight and inner strength without rushing to show it. Obstruction has Water on the Mountain, and its key word is 'endure': when the road turns treacherous, you don't crash through — you turn inward and refine the heart. When these two meet, it's like a sturdy granary facing a muddy mountain path. The steady calm of the Great Taming can hold the anxious energy of Obstruction, giving it plenty of security. Obstruction's caution, in turn, reminds the Great Taming not to charge ahead blindly. The Great Taming says 'crossing the great river' needs the right moment; Obstruction says 'turning back to cultivate virtue' is exactly the phase of building power. Together, they're not a blaze of dry wood but the deep reserves of the Great Taming transformed into Obstruction's breakthrough confidence. One stockpiles the supplies, the other sets the rhythm — the harder it gets, the more their mutual support becomes the unspoken foundation.
resonance: ★ Backup Confidence: The Great Taming's deep reserves can absorb Obstruction's emotional drain in adversity, giving anxiety a place to rest.

★ Heart-Sharpening at the Pit: Obstruction's inward virtue-cultivation and the Great Taming's own accumulation are on the same frequency — both see inner reflection as the first move toward a breakthrough.
conflict: ◆ Pacing Mismatch: The Great Taming is used to quietly building momentum and waiting for an opening, while Obstruction tends to spiral into self-doubt over immediate barriers — one thinks it's too slow, the other thinks it's too blocked.

◆ Action Disagreement: The Great Taming sets its sights on the long-term strategy of crossing the great river, while Obstruction leans toward the risk-averse 'southwest' retreat, making them clash over advance and retreat.
advice: Set a small-step review ritual: the Great Taming breaks big goals into weekly tasks, Obstruction writes a quick reflection after each one, and concrete progress replaces mutual second-guessing.

one_liner: One saves up the nerve; the other flips the table and sweeps the board clean when it's time.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a silent mountain of support, taking in all the energies of heaven and earth and slowly digesting them. Its game is holding in the big move and investing for the long haul. Deliverance, by contrast, arrives like a sudden thunderstorm — after the rain clears, every score is settled. It's the master of cutting through the mess with one clean stroke. When these two team up, one is stuffing things in with all his might, the other is pouring them out in a rush. The rhythm may look mismatched, but it actually makes for a perfect loop: the experience and confidence the Taming Power has banked supply the ammunition for Deliverance's bold breakthrough; and Deliverance's swift strike helps the Taming Power one-tap delete its hoarded tensions and baggage. There's nothing phony here — one manages the stockpile, the other manages the flow. Together, they live by the motto: 'Root deep in calm times; don't burn energy on infighting when trouble comes.'
resonance: ★ A Kindred Rhythm of Charge and Release: The Taming Power's long-term accumulation hands Deliverance the confidence to break through quickly, and Deliverance's decisiveness gives the Taming Power's depth a stage to perform on.

★ Experience Dislodges Deadlocks: The Taming Power chews on precedents; Deliverance is fluent in dropping the old baggage. Together, they turn a dead knot into a stepping stone — no twisting into cul-de-sacs.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms Don't Sync: The Taming Power likes to weigh and marinate; Deliverance calls that dawdling and wants to pry the lid off and get to business. They may brand each other 'too rigid' and 'too hasty.'

◆ Hoarding vs. Letting Go: The Taming Power hates to trash old ledgers and old rules; Deliverance insists that once a page is turned, it's turned. When old accounts resurface, one wants to excavate; the other wants to shred them outright.
advice: When a difference shows up, the Taming Power should draw up two or three backup plans for Deliverance, and Deliverance can run with the quickest one. No nagging about pace along the way.

one_liner: One is busy storing up inner strength, the other actively throws off burdens; partnering in life, they're all about spiritual minimalism.
analysis: Both hexagrams have Gen (Keeping Still) Mountain at the top, so the underlying tone is steady and inward. Da Xu (The Taming Power of the Great) is a mountain belly hiding an entire sky — it focuses on hoarding experience, resources, and confidence, never drawing its sword lightly. Sun (Decrease) is a marsh scooped out beneath the mountain — it actively cuts away excess desires and emotions, seeking a clean, refreshing clarity. When the two meet, it's like an old craftsman with an apprentice: Da Xu keeps stuffing real skills into the toolbox, afraid there won't be enough; Sun keeps decluttering the toolbox on a regular basis, afraid it will get too heavy and crush the bearer. Da Xu's 'broad knowing' needs Sun's 'blocking desires' to purify it, or it turns into an information-hoarding habit; Sun's 'doing subtraction' needs Da Xu's 'deep accumulation' to give it a floor, or it ends up with nothing but a hollow core. The two resonate on the path of self-cultivation — one manages expansion, the other manages economy — and together they balance the energy budget of life with perfect clarity.
resonance: ★ Inward rooting: both understand the wisdom of 'stopping' — they don't blindly seek externally, but pull their energy back and polish the core.
★ Spiritual minimalism: they naturally reject flashiness and waste, valuing solid accumulation and clear breathing space instead.
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war between hoarding and discarding: Da Xu always wants to prepare extra paths for fear of not having enough, while Sun finds the clutter oppressive and wants to clear it all — disagreements arise over what stays and what goes.
◆ Emotional temperature gap: Da Xu tends to press worries deep under the mountain and chew on them slowly, while Sun prefers to slash through knots quickly, sometimes coming across as unfeeling.
advice: Set aside a half-day 'energy audit' each week: Da Xu lists the materials or thoughts accumulated recently, Sun picks out only the three most useless items and discards them directly, then the rest are sorted and filed — this preserves confidence without draining energy.

one_liner: One quietly builds the war chest, the other sprints to find the opening; together they’re steady enough to stand firm and quick enough to take off.
analysis: The Great Taming’s 'Heaven within the Mountain' is about storing energy inward; Increase’s 'Wind and Thunder intertwined' is about breaking outward. Both hexagram texts proclaim 'It furthers one to cross the great water,' which shows they share the same goal but take very different paths: the Great Taming builds reservoirs and trains troops, practicing the long-term discipline of auspicious 'not eating at home' (i.e., serving the world); Increase opens the floodgates and rides the wind, specializing in the fast iteration of 'when you see good, move toward it.' Without the Great Taming’s support, Increase tends to scatter into aimless fussing; without Increase’s circulation, the Great Taming tends to stagnate into dead water. At the core, this pairing is a 'battery with an amplifier'—one manages supplies, the other leads the charge, turning stored capital into tangible new growth.
resonance: ★ Wind Borrows the Mountain’s Strength: The Great Taming’s deep foundation gives Increase’s action a solid base, so every move has genuine weight rather than mere bluster.

★ Moving Toward the Good to Patch the Gaps: Increase’s agility in 'moving toward what is good' exactly fills the Great Taming’s blind spot of self-isolation, keeping the pair in a constant state of evolution.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Mismatch: The Great Taming prefers slow simmering and striking after thorough accumulation, while Increase is all about lightning-fast action; early on, they may resent each other over the speed.

◆ Resource Drain: The Great Taming leans toward hiding good things away for slow digestion, whereas Increase insists on circulating and sharing them; different habits of distribution easily cause friction.
advice: Set a clear rhythm for 'storing' and 'releasing': in the early phase, listen to the Great Taming and do the groundwork; once the launch is on, let Increase take the full lead for trial, error, and iteration. Don’t grab the steering wheel at the same stage.

one_liner: One quietly builds their strength, the other calls the shots and settles things—both are tough as nails underneath.
analysis: The lower trigram in both is Qian, the Creative (Heaven), showing that deep down both carry an unyielding strength and drive—only their outward rhythms are complete opposites. The Taming Power of the Great is like a mountain enclosing heaven: it habitually pulls its edge inward, values accumulation, and cultivates virtue, like an immovable storehouse. Breakthrough is like a lake suspended over heaven: it follows the rule that when full, it overflows—cutting through decisively when the time is right. Together, the Taming Power's steadiness can catch Breakthrough's impatience and prevent rash decisions; Breakthrough's incisiveness can puncture the Taming Power's over-caution and force accumulated reserves into tangible results. This isn't about one remaking the other—it's a relay between 'storing grain' and 'opening the granary.' The shared Qian-metal core lets them understand each other's ambition, except the Taming Power waits for the wind, while Breakthrough makes the wind.
resonance: ★ A shared core of strength: with Qian Heaven below, both are stubborn and ambitious at heart; they don't need many words to grasp each other's devotion to a goal.

★ Seamless link between stockpiling and unleashing: the Taming Power's deep reserves perfectly feed Breakthrough's need for decisive action—one supplies the ammunition, the other pulls the trigger, so the coordination is extremely smooth.
conflict: ◆ Clashing rhythms are pure torture: the Taming Power always thinks the time isn't right and wants to wait; Breakthrough finds it too slow and wants to flip the table. One wants stability, the other speed—everyday communication easily sparks anger.

◆ Different emotional outlets: the Taming Power tends to internalize and digest pressure, while Breakthrough prefers to vent and break through directly. In conflicts, one stews in silent hurt, the other speaks too sharply and wounds.
advice: The Taming Power should learn to hand over decision-making at key moments, and Breakthrough should ask the Taming Power, 'Is our grain sufficient?' before making the final call—make a point of aligning the timelines of 'saving' and 'spending.'

one_liner: One is busy charging up a killer move, the other is all about surprise strikes—put them together and their hidden hand turns into a royal flush.
analysis: Dà Xù (The Taming Power of the Great) is like an old warehouse deep in the mountains, built on the principle of heaven stored within the mountain—it prefers to build up plenty of substance before acting. Gòu (Coming to Meet) is like a swift wind sweeping through the hall, focused on spreading across the world and seizing unexpected encounters, adept at catching the prevailing trend. When these two meet, Dà Xù finds Gòu too flighty, and Gòu finds Dà Xù too stifling. But curiously, Gòu's chance encounters are exactly the breakthrough opportunity that lets Dà Xù 'favorably cross the great river,' while Dà Xù's accumulated virtue provides a solid foundation for Gòu's 'proclaiming mandates to the four quarters.' One builds inner strength; the other creates outward momentum. Slow craft meets rapid fire, striking a rhythm that is steady first, then explosive.
resonance: ★ Deep pool receives living water: Dà Xù's profound foundation perfectly catches the fresh connections and sudden opportunities Gòu brings, ensuring no good chance slips away.
★ Warehouse linked to broadcast: Dà Xù's quietly gathered real talent is carried to all directions by Gòu's reach, fully realizing the ambition of 'not eating at home.'
conflict: ◆ Tortoise speed collides with the vanguard: Dà Xù is used to advancing step by step and weighing every move, while Gòu likes to strike while the iron is hot and act on instinct—their execution rhythms tend to trip each other up.

◆ Holding the line meets breaking the mold: Dà Xù instinctively guards against unpredictable, overpowering forces, while Gòu loves to break conventions and embrace variables—they often clash over risk control.
advice: Don't force each other's pace. Let Dà Xù first dig deep into the resources Gòu brings, and once the foundation is solid, let Gòu step out to generate momentum. Set a clear handoff point between the charging phase and the launching phase.

one_liner: One practices inner mastery in the deep mountains; the other sets up a stage on level ground. Put them together and you've got a killer combo.
analysis: Great Taming is 'Heaven within the Mountain': the dynamic force of Heaven is hidden inside the solid mountain, perfect for biding one's time and storing up power. Gathering Together is 'Lake upon the Earth': water vapor spreads and gathers people together, all about rallying companions and integrating resources. When the two meet, it's like a warehouse manager running into an event planner. Great Taming doesn't rush to show its face; it first fills its saddlebags with experience and virtue. Gathering Together, on the other hand, is expert at stringing scattered pearls into a necklace, creating a buzz and setting the rules. Great Taming's 'favorable to cross the great river' needs Gathering Together's 'favorable to see the great person' to build bridges and pave roads. And if Gathering Together's bustle lacks the foundation of Great Taming's depth, it can easily become a flash in the pan. One sends roots deep, the other spreads leaves wide — together they complete the whole cycle of growth.
resonance: ★ Stored strength finds its stage: the genuine abilities Great Taming has accumulated can be displayed on the platform of Gathering Together's gatherings, so one's talents don't go to waste.

★ Gather without dispersing: the liveliness of Gathering Together needs Great Taming's rules and cultural depth to anchor the crowd, so that people don't scatter in a hurry and instead genuine bonds can settle and form.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Great Taming is used to slow, careful work and closed-door practice, while Gathering Together always wants to strike while the iron is hot and start a meetup right away. One thinks the other is too sluggish; the other thinks the one is too impatient.

◆ Defensive clash: The image of Gathering Together emphasizes 'removing weapons and guarding against the unexpected,' so it has a built-in radar for outsiders. Great Taming stresses the accumulation of virtue and sets a high threshold for trust. In the initial phase, the two tend to probe each other and find it hard to open their hearts.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for a closed-door meeting. Great Taming brings only the practical lessons gained recently; Gathering Together turns those ideas into an action checklist. Use concrete projects to replace meaningless socializing.

one_liner: You thicken the foundation at home; I ride the momentum and grow upward. This combo is all about steady, sure-footed progress — no flailing around.
analysis: Great Accumulation (The Taming Power of the Great) is mountain-like: it compresses heaven-earth vision and the wisdom of the ancients into the belly — an art of "concealing" and "stockpiling." Pushing Upward is like a seedling threading out of the soil: in no rush to flower, it simply follows the earth's qi inch by inch — an art of "flowing" and "growing." Brought together, the pairing is "strategic reserve" colliding with "steady execution." Great Accumulation never hurries to cash in; first it lets virtue, contacts, and skill amass until they spill over. Pushing Upward never blindly sprints; it leans on the confidence you've supplied and goes to see the great person and head south as scheduled. The mountain anchors the earth; the earth feeds oxygen to the wood. One welds the foundation sealed, the other maxes out the height. Without Great Accumulation's deep squat, Pushing Upward tends to drift; without Pushing Upward's breaking ground, Great Accumulation risks becoming stagnant water. One still, one moving, the two turn "deep reserves, slow release" into a tangible everyday rhythm.
resonance: ★ Mutual confidence: The knowledge and networks Great Accumulation has stashed give Pushing Upward a steady supply of nourishment for every step — unhurried, unruffled, rising.
★ Same frequency: One refuses to fuss and simply accumulates; the other doesn't covet speed and values going with the flow. Both like to let things happen in their own time.
conflict: ◆ Dragging rhythm: Great Accumulation always wants to wait until every piece is in place; Pushing Upward, though slow, is itching to break ground — so "let's wait a little longer" can make you miss the window.

◆ Misaligned expression: Great Accumulation tends to bottle up thoughts and feelings to digest alone; Pushing Upward needs clear direction and positive feedback. Over time, you'll start second-guessing each other.
advice: Hold a fixed monthly "cards-on-the-table" session: Great Accumulation proactively shows the hard-won assets and contacts it has gathered, while Pushing Upward reports recent progress. Don't let your Kindred rapport turn into a silent gourd.

one_liner: One quietly builds up reserves, the other stubbornly endures in a drought-stricken field. Together: stop grinding yourself down — I have provisions here.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a granary stocked with dried provisions and ancient texts, habitually drawing energy inward, believing in building depth before breaking through. Oppression is like a well that's run dry — cramped and arid outside, yet burning with a fire of determination to fulfill its purpose. When these two come together, it's not about one saving the other; it's a prepper colliding with a stubborn diehard. The Taming Power of the Great's steadiness can underwrite Oppression's anxiety, teaching it not to rush to prove itself during the stifling period when words aren't believed, but to steady its stance with past wisdom and actions. Oppression's desperate circumstances, in turn, force the Taming Power of the Great to take the stored grain out of the warehouse for real use, preventing accumulated resources from becoming stagnant water. One gathers, one releases; one stores, one spends — together they transform the slow ordeal into true resilience.
resonance: ★ With grain in the cellar, the heart is unruffled: The Taming Power of the Great's deep reserves give Oppression a tangible fallback and resources, turning stubborn endurance into principled perseverance.

★ Desperate times force out real ability: Oppression's barren conditions compel the Taming Power of the Great to put its knowledge and experience to the test, avoiding empty talk and ivory-tower thinking.
conflict: ◆ Actions speak louder than words: Oppression's frustration of words not being believed clashes with the Taming Power of the Great's preference for quiet accumulation, leading to mutual blank stares in communication, each feeling the other doesn't understand them.

◆ Tempo always clashes: The Taming Power of the Great is used to slowly stewing over past wisdom and precedents, while Oppression urgently seeks to break the deadlock at once. One finds the other too sluggish; the other finds the first too rash.
advice: The Taming Power of the Great should regularly lay out its knowledge and resources for Oppression to use; Oppression should directly ask for support when hitting a wall, rather than waiting until everything dries up to think of the other.

one_liner: One quietly stockpiles a grand move; the other simmers a nourishing broth day in, day out. Living together as partners, a slow, steady flow is what truly sustains.
analysis: Great Accumulation is the deep diver of 'Heaven within the Mountain' — it gathers insight, virtue, and resources inward, waiting until full before daring to 'cross the great river.' The Well, by contrast, is the distributor of 'Wood above Water,' offering the everyday nourishment of 'the town may change, but the well never moves.' When these two hexagrams come together, it is 'strategic reserves' colliding with 'civic infrastructure.' Great Accumulation provides an inexhaustible source of confidence; the Well provides a delivery rhythm that never fails. Without the depth of Great Accumulation, the Well runs dry; without the Well's circulation, Great Accumulation's storehouse of wisdom rots inside. The only real hurdle is that Great Accumulation always wants to hold out for a dazzling big move, while the Well obsesses over details, afraid a 'broken jug' will spoil everything. When the tempo is off, each can think the other is either too flighty or too rigid. But push through that stage, and you reach a genuine depth that releases slowly and nourishes without fanfare.
resonance: ★ A closed loop of accumulation and application: Great Accumulation quietly stores up substance without showing off, while the Well turns experience into everyday usable broth, making knowledge truly nourishing.

★ A kindred long-termism: neither trusts quick fixes. Great Accumulation's 'perseverance furthers' and the Well's 'no loss, no gain' both respect staying in your role and simmering slowly — no short-sighted, desperate shortcuts.
conflict: ◆ Grand ambition collides with daily minutiae: Great Accumulation keeps an eye on 'crossing the great river' with a big move, while the Well keeps an eye on the rope and bucket, afraid a 'broken jug' will ruin the rules. When the rhythm is rushed, each starts blaming the other.

◆ Hoarding mindset meets constant drawdown: the more Great Accumulation stores, the safer it feels; the Well, however, is living water being drawn out. When Great Accumulation feels 'all outflow, no inflow,' it easily feels drained and has an emotional flare-up.
advice: Set clear 'closed-door reserve periods' and 'external delivery periods' — for example, spend three days in focused accumulation without handling trivial matters, then use four days to break the results into reusable modules and deliver them. Don't let preparation become procrastination, and don't treat sharing as depletion.

one_liner: One quietly amasses a family fortune, the other reads the heat and flips the old table — together they’re cooking up something big.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is “Heaven within the Mountain” — as if the boundless energy and the wisdom of the ancients were all squeezed into one mountain, it prizes deep accumulation before release. The Reforming is “Fire in the Lake”: when water and fire clash, great change is inevitable, so it prizes spotting the right moment and decisively breaking with the old to create the new. Put these two together and you’ve got an ammunition depot meeting an igniter. If the Taming Power of the Great never encounters the Reforming, it risks becoming a scholar full of grand theories who never dares to move; if the Reforming has no deep reserves to support it, it’s just flailing. When they work together, the Taming Power of the Great provides the rock-solid foundation for change, and the Reforming brings stagnant water back to life. One masters conservatively building momentum; the other masters shattering deadlocks and opening fresh tracks. The chemical reaction is: in ordinary times, endure the solitude and feverishly bank experience; when the critical hour arrives, dare to flip the table and switch lanes.
resonance: ★ Storing Energy, Biding the Moment: The Taming Power of the Great’s deep reserves give change the fearlessness to risk mistakes, while the Reforming’s decisive action turns hoarded resources into true flow.

★ Knowing the Past, Illuminating the Present: The Taming Power of the Great loves to study the old masters, the Reforming is skilled at seizing the now — put them together and they spin aged wisdom into bold new tricks.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Mismatch: The Taming Power of the Great is used to slowly building up resources and dreads charging ahead; the Reforming thinks the other is dragging its feet and wants to overhaul the rules in a single blazing stroke. They quickly get on each other’s nerves.

◆ Ideological Friction: The Taming Power of the Great treats old rules and old experience as treasures to be enshrined; the Reforming sees anything old as a stumbling block to be tossed immediately. When these values collide, sparks fly.
advice: Set a “reserve-building period” and a “trial-and-error day.” Let the Taming Power of the Great handle resource inventories in daily life, and let the Reforming choose fixed checkpoints to run small pilot projects. Don’t wait until you’ve saved up your fortune to make a move, and don’t move rashly until you’ve emptied the family store.

one_liner: You quietly amass the family fortune; I light the fire and cook up innovation. Together, we're a winning hand.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is a mountain, centered on 'concealing' and 'storing' — pressing experience and energy deep into the heart without haste. The Cauldron is fire, centered on 'forging' and 'establishing' — turning raw ingredients into cooked meals and flipping old rules into iron laws. When these two hexagrams meet, it's a 'resource bank' colliding with a 'transformation furnace.' The steadiness of the Great Tamer can restrain the Cauldron's impatience, while the Cauldron's drive can convert the Tamer's hoarded knowledge into concrete achievement. One is a night watchman, the other a head chef; together they can simmer long-brewed depths into dazzling, lively flavor — but you must endure the dull early phase of stocking up without yet producing.
resonance: ★ True gold is simmered over a slow fire: the Great Tamer's long-term accumulation is exactly what the Cauldron needs for a gentle, thorough stew — no haste, no half-raw half-cooked results, and a solid foundation before turning the table.
★ Experience meets action: every hard bone the Tamer has gnawed and every old book it has read is forged by the Cauldron into workable new rules — nothing wasted.
conflict: ◆ Hoarding too long breeds mold: the Tamer is used to cradling things and mulling them over endlessly, while the Cauldron is eager to light the fire and get going. When the rhythm slips, one is called sluggish, the other reckless.

◆ Differing control of the heat: the Cauldron champions bold, sweeping renovation, while the Tamer prefers steady, sure steps and reverence for the old ways. When reform goes too far, one fears a scorched pot, the other complains the fire is too mild.
advice: Set clear charging periods and furnace-opening dates. The Tamer only needs to deliver resources on schedule; the Cauldron must strictly follow milestones for trial and implementation. Anchor the rhythm to a calendar so no energy idles in empty spinning.

one_liner: You quietly build the nest egg; I blow open new horizons with a single shout.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a mountain. Its essence lies in 'storing' and 'nourishing'—silently stockpiling experience and resources, never in a hurry to make a display. The Arousing is like thunder. Its core is 'motion' and 'waking'—breaking through stagnation with sudden shock. When these two come together, it is a reservoir meeting a fuse. The Taming Power's steady composure can catch the Arousing's rashness, giving its explosion a solid base. The Arousing's edge can cut through the Taming Power's caution, forcing the hoarded resources to truly flow. At ordinary times, the Taming Power grinds the blade slowly; the Arousing, the moment a wind blows, charges with that blade. The oracle 'not eating at home' combined with 'startling a hundred miles' says that this pair's greatest fear is marking time. They must turn the ink in their stomachs into the mud under their feet, and prove themselves in the wind and waves.
resonance: ★ Power-up and breakthrough on the same frequency: the Taming Power's deep reserves give the Arousing's decisive strikes a solid foundation; together, they can always win the hard battles.

★ Unflappable in crisis, each other's trump card: the Arousing's nose for danger instantly activates the Taming Power's stockpile, while the Taming Power's foresight keeps the Arousing's burst from going off the rails.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch drains energy: the Taming Power is used to slow, meticulous work, while the Arousing prefers to cut the knot with a swift sword. The slow-fast clash makes each side feel the other is holding them back.

◆ Conservation and aggression collide: the Taming Power wants to keep resources tight to avoid risk, but the Arousing believes nothing ventured, nothing gained. When it comes to money or decisions, they'll argue over playing safe or charging ahead.
advice: When a disagreement arises, the Taming Power should first list the resource inventory and the bottom-line risk, then the Arousing can pick the boldest move within those bounds. Draw the safety line first, then step on the gas.

one_liner: One is frantically amassing capital for a big play; the other is constantly tugging your sleeve, saying take the win and stay in line. Together, they bring ambition safely down to earth.
analysis: In Da Xu (The Taming Power of the Great), Qian (The Creative) surges inside the mountain's belly, its head full of learning from past words and deeds, ready to cross the great river. Gen (Keeping Still) presses down with its doubled mountain, knowing only the peace of not thinking beyond its place. Because both upper trigrams are Gen (Mountain), the two share an instant, boundary-aware kinship — yet their inner temperatures are vastly different. Da Xu is a dormant volcano, storing the Creative's drive under thick soil; Gen is a stern boundary stone, using stillness to filter out any thought that crosses the line. In daily life, Da Xu hoards resources and plots breakthroughs; Gen applies the brakes, draws red lines, and pulls wandering ideas back to the ground. They seem to be one moving and one still, but in truth they are each other's foundation. Without Da Xu's deep reserve, Gen's stopping turns into stagnant water; without Gen's knowing when to stop, Da Xu's river-crossing can easily derail and capsize. When they join forces, fervent ambition is poured into a mold of discipline and slowly simmered into solid confidence.
resonance: ★ Kindred Boundary Sense: Both upper trigrams are Gen (Mountain), so both naturally agree that everything has a limit, rarely cross the line, and find boundary-setting communication effortless.

★ Deep-Accumulation Resonance: Da Xu's storing of virtue and nurturing the worthy, along with Gen's 'not thinking out of place,' both value rooting inward, shun superficial excitement, and can boost each other in focused depth.
conflict: ◆ Kinetic Friction: Da Xu's lower Qian (The Creative) always wants to charge outward and do big things, while Gen's doubled mountain habitually stays put. One is urgent to break through, the other just wants to hold the line — rhythms often mismatch.

◆ Vision Tug-of-War: Da Xu champions 'not eating at home brings good fortune' — going out into the world to apply oneself; Gen stresses 'not thinking beyond one's position' and keeping to one's own role. They easily battle over whether to expand into new fields.
advice: In times of disagreement, Da Xu shouldn't rush ahead with all guns blazing — give Gen three days to sit quietly and reflect. And Gen shouldn't just keep setting limits — try helping Da Xu break big goals into small weekly action lists, using the rhythm of stopping to lay stairs for the stored-up energy.

one_liner: One quietly builds toward a masterstroke, the other takes the stairs one at a time. Together, they're a low-risk, high-certainty long-game pairing.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great packs the vast cosmos into a mountain, prizing deep accumulation over quick returns; Development grows like a tree along the mountain's contours, all about taking things in order and never rushing ahead. When these two hexagrams meet, it's a master of inner depth encountering a master of rhythm. The Taming Power's 'not eating at home' urges it to charge outward, but when energy is too full, it easily becomes reckless. Development's 'the maiden's marriage brings good fortune' exactly hits the brakes, reminding that everything must follow procedure and read the timing. As the wind threads through the mountains, it gradually blows the knowledge and grounded confidence the Taming Power has stored up into visible results. They don't bet on overnight riches, only on blooming step by step—a classic 'go deep first, then go long' partnership.
resonance: ★ Rooted in Each Other: The Taming Power's accumulation of virtue gives Development's dwelling-in-worthy-virtue a firm core, so gradual progress never ends up idling—it is an expedition well supplied.

★ Same Rhythm: Both reject eagerness and reckless advance—one advocates building strength before braving danger, the other insists on following ritual and procedure. They naturally understand each other's steadiness.
conflict: ◆ Pace Mismatch: After the Taming Power has fully accumulated, it often has a burst of impulse to cross the great river, but Development's gradual instinct keeps applying the brakes. At critical points, they can easily get stuck in tug-of-war and internal attrition.

◆ Path Divergence: The Taming Power loves broad strategic knowledge-building; Development obsesses over daily processes and details. In the early stages, they may dismiss each other as too flighty or too nitpicky.
advice: Set a 'small-step delivery' milestone every month. Break the Taming Power's grand reservoirs into concrete tasks that Development can handle one bite at a time, replacing emotional friction with a progress bar.

one_liner: One slowly amasses capital in the storehouse; the other wants to sign the marriage certificate the moment they lock eyes.
analysis: Da Xu (The Great Accumulation) values "Heaven within the Mountain" — pulling in sharp edges and accumulating learning, storing depth until there is enough substance to "cross the great river." Gui Mei (The Marrying Maiden), on the other hand, is "Thunder over the Lake" — emotion surges and drowns out the warning that "advancing brings misfortune." When these two meet, Da Xu is a seasoned helmsman, always wanting to chart escape routes and tally the books first; Gui Mei is a messenger with a live spark, ready to leap into the game no matter how high the waves. Da Xu's "stored virtue" can catch Gui Mei when she's brash; Gui Mei's vitality can push Da Xu to stop circling inside old experience. If neither bends, Da Xu finds the other too frivolous, while Gui Mei sees the other as stiflingly cautious. But when the clear eye of "knowing the end and its pitfalls" is blended into the patient habit of "learning the words and deeds of the past," impulse stews down into a long, steady flame, and they become a duo that is both grounded and electric.
resonance: ★ Steady Base, Soothing Waves: Da Xu's profound depth catches Gui Mei's emotional surges and gives her a solid, grounded security.
★ Breaking the Stalemate: Gui Mei's direct, head-on strikes shatter Da Xu's over-cautious gridlock and push the relationship into real momentum.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Rhythm: Da Xu likes to stockpile resources before acting; Gui Mei lives in the moment — each winds up finding the other too slow or too reckless.
◆ Bottom-Line Tug-of-War: Gui Mei can get swept away by feeling and ignore long-term risks, while Da Xu over-weighs the pros and cons until he looks cold and calculating.
advice: Da Xu: when Gui Mei is high on emotion, don't rush to throw cold water — walk three steps with her first. Gui Mei: before making a decision, treat Da Xu's "pitfall checklist" as a memo and put a safety latch on your impulse.

one_liner: Quietly builds strength in ordinary times, and at the crucial moment strikes without hesitation.
analysis: Great Accumulation settles learning and virtue like a mountain, while Abundance bursts forth with action and insight like thunder and lightning. The former, through the metaphor of 'a mountain within heaven,' reminds us to build deep before releasing; the latter, through the image of 'thunder and lightning arriving together,' emphasizes moving with the times. When steady accumulation meets decisive execution, a symbiotic rhythm of 'nurture first, then release' emerges: the caution of Great Accumulation lays the foundation for Abundance's initiative, and Abundance's sharpness breaks through the conservative impasse that Great Accumulation can fall into. But note: if virtue is hoarded too long without expression, it becomes building a cart with the door closed; if Abundance is pursued too hastily without preparation, it is like thunder striking without roots. The key to blending these two lies in grasping the breathing rhythm between 'storing' and 'releasing.'
resonance: ★ Accumulate deeply and act brilliantly: Great Accumulation's reserve provides fuel for Abundance's radiance, and Abundance's clarity gives direction to Great Accumulation's growth.

★ Virtue and decisiveness nourish each other: the inclusive nurturing of talent in Great Accumulation and the upright judgment in Abundance together form a framework where knowledge and action are one.
conflict: ◆ Storing without releasing, missing the moment: Great Accumulation's excessive caution can suppress the bold initiative that Abundance requires.

◆ Overly harsh discernment wounds the root: if Abundance's dispensing of justice and punishment loses its measure, it can destroy the carefully cultivated ecosystem of virtue that Great Accumulation has nurtured.
advice: Set a 'recharge day' each month to review your accumulations, and schedule a 'breakthrough day' each quarter to push key decisions forward — let cyclical rhythm harmonize stillness and action.

one_liner: One banks a reserve, the other roams the rivers and lakes; their bond is steady with a touch of wanderlust.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a mountain holding the image of heaven — it values profound accumulation, measured release, and moral cultivation. The Wanderer is like fire moving along a mountain ridge — it emphasizes dynamic exploration, clear discernment, and prudent judgment. When the two meet, the mountain gives the fire fuel and foundation, while the fire illuminates the mountain's path and breaks through stagnation. The Great Taming's 'good fortune in not eating at home' subtly hints at a tendency to send stored resources outward, which echoes the Wanderer's 'small success' and its spirit of far-flung travel. But fire is prone to scattering, and mountain is prone to solidifying: if the Great Taming hoards without transforming, or the Wanderer charges forward blindly, resources can be misaligned. True harmony lies in letting the mountain steady the fire's restlessness and the fire shatter the mountain's stuffiness — forming a virtuous cycle of storing and releasing energy.
resonance: ★ A relay of cultivation and pioneering: the wisdom and experience accumulated by the Great Taming can become a compass for the Wanderer's adventures, keeping it from costly trial and error.
★ A mutual testament of virtue and discernment: the Great Taming studies the lessons of history, the Wanderer reads the reality of the present; together they give decisions both depth and edge.
conflict: ◆ A mismatch of rhythm breeds friction: the Great Taming favors slow, deep cultivation, while the Wanderer prefers rapid iteration; divergent tempos can spark anxiety and tug-of-war.

◆ Friction between securing and breaking ground: the Great Taming tends to consolidate gains, the Wanderer longs to push past comfort zones; different notions of boundaries can create a tug-of-war over decisions.
