advice: Create a 'store–act' cycle: use the Great Taming's planning power to set resource-reserve milestones, and the Wanderer's execution drive to define exploration windows; review monthly to recalibrate the ratio of saving to spending.

one_liner: One quietly builds up the nest egg; the other seizes every chance to get things done.
analysis: Great Taming (Da Xu) is 'Heaven within the mountain' — energy gathers inward, prizing settling, stored virtue, and nurturing the worthy, without rushing to show immediate results. The Gentle (Xun) is 'entering with the wind' — energy seeps outward, prizing flexibility, following the trend, and executing decrees. Their meeting is not a collision of force but a solid foundation matched with a clever hand. Great Taming's composure gives the Gentle an unhurried confidence; the Gentle's penetrating power can take the learning and resources Great Taming has accumulated and deliver them precisely into practice. Great Taming's 'not eating at home brings good fortune' hints at stepping out to fulfill ambitions, and the Gentle happens to excel at paving roads and bridging gaps. But if Great Taming becomes too sink-heavy, it becomes stagnant water; if the Gentle becomes too floaty, it turns superficial. The beauty of this pair is a complementarity of depth and breadth — like an old tree root meeting a draft in the hall: the root goes deep, the wind blows through, so their work has both staying power and nimble vitality.
resonance: ★ Foundation and pathway interlock: Great Taming's thick sediment gives the Gentle's flexible maneuvering a stable platform that won't flip — no matter how the wind blows, a solid base won't be carried off.
★ A relay of learning and execution: the wisdom Great Taming has gathered from past words and deeds is exactly what the Gentle's fine hand at carrying out orders can turn into tangible results.
conflict: ◆ Restlessness from syncopated rhythms: Great Taming is used to slowly cooking and waiting for the right moment, while the Gentle wants to ride the trend and push forward fast — one thinks the other is too slow, the other thinks the first is too rash.

◆ The rub of stubbornness and whimsy: Great Taming sticks to its reasoned truth and won't easily change course, while the Gentle habitually turns with the wind. Long-term, each may see the other as lacking conviction or being too rigid.
advice: Great Taming fixes the broad direction, then lets the Gentle run trial-and-error adjustments freely. At key junctures, the Gentle must circle back to align the underlying logic with Great Taming, lest the two head off on separate paths.

one_liner: One quietly piles up savings, the other makes friends with an open heart. Put them together and you get a two-course combo of inner depth and outward charisma.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a mountain concealing jade, valuing inward restraint and stored energy. The Joyous hexagram resembles a lake rippling with light, skilled in outward expression and harmonious exchange. The mountain's steady presence can anchor the lake's flightiness, while the lake's fluidity can soften the mountain's rigidity. When the deep reserves of the Taming Power of the Great meet the open communication of The Joyous, it's like a master craftsman meeting a fresh curator: the former distills experience into substance, the latter gives that substance wings. This combination doesn't win through instant sparks, but through a cycle of settling, transforming, and giving back that creates lasting value—ideal for situations that require both patient buildup and bold outward presentation.
resonance: ★ Wisdom and accumulation meet the desire to share: the deep reserves of the Taming Power of the Great provide material for The Joyous's teaching, and The Joyous's exchange lets that wisdom flow
★ Kindred harmony between inner restraint and outer expression: the steady mountain gathers its power, the lively lake delights the heart—movement and stillness form a naturally Complementary pair
conflict: ◆ Tempo mismatch: the Taming Power values long-term accumulation, The Joyous craves immediate feedback—one may find the other too slow, the other too frantic
◆ Depth of expression: the Taming Power leans toward subtle, understated communication; The Joyous prefers direct, cheerful banter—easy to talk past each other
advice: Once a month, hold a 'deep-talk tea gathering.' The Taming Power partner comes with three core points prepared; The Joyous partner breaks the ice with light topics. Then, through Q&A, turn the raw substance into stories worth spreading.

one_liner: One piles up substance until it overflows, the other spreads that energy to the world — together they run a lavish banquet that never loses.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is about storing and nurturing — like tucking an entire sky into a mountain. It doesn't rush to show off, only hones its inner craft and stockpiles provisions. Dispersion, on the other hand, is about opening and spreading: wind running over water, undoing every obstruction and clog, breathing life back into people and resources. Together they form an energy loop of stillness and motion. The Taming Power fears becoming stagnant water; Dispersion fears drifting like duckweed. But both hexagram texts share 'It furthers one to cross the great water,' meaning they both have the guts to take on big stages. The Taming Power gives Dispersion a real ammunition depot; Dispersion helps the Taming Power broadcast all its stored virtue into actual influence. They don't fight each other — they hand off the baton.
resonance: ★ A Kindred Vow to Cross the Great Water: Both hexagram texts harbor a will to cross the river. When life's big tests arrive, one relies on a solid foundation to endure, the other on clever maneuvering to turn danger aside — yet their road to a breakthrough is strikingly the same.

★ Building a Shared Spiritual Totem: The Taming Power emphasizes accumulating virtue and cultivating inner strength; Dispersion emphasizes establishing temples and rallying hearts. Both value inner faith and the transmission of values, allowing them to resonate on the same spiritual frequency.
conflict: ◆ A Tug-of-War of Misaligned Tempos: The Taming Power is used to slow cooking — accumulating first, releasing later. Dispersion prefers to go with the flow and show its cards immediately. Early on, they're likely to clash endlessly over whether to wait for the right moment or strike while the iron is hot.

◆ Disagreement over Where Energy Goes: The Taming Power wants to use good steel on the blade — focused, concentrated force. Dispersion leans toward sharing the rain evenly and connecting widely. When allocating resources, one finds the other too scattered, the other finds the first too stingy.
advice: The Taming Power shouldn't keep its cards hidden forever — every so often, hand one or two solid pieces to Dispersion to test the waters. And Dispersion shouldn't cast a net everywhere — first plant the seeds the Taming Power gives you and let them take root before branching out. Together, set a steady rhythm: bank one batch, release one wave.

one_liner: One is all about building up reserves, the other is the dedicated brake-tapper — together, they run a steady ship.
analysis: Great Accumulation is like a grand strategist, storing Heaven within the Mountain, biding its strength to amass resources and cultivate a broader vision, always aiming for something big. Limitation, meanwhile, is the actuary and discipline committee, holding water over the Lake, attentive to measure and boundaries, fearful of resources overflowing or running dry. Put them together, and you get ambition meeting the measuring stick. Great Accumulation handles expansion and deep accumulation; Limitation sets the rules and paces the rhythm. Without Limitation's constraint, Accumulation easily reaches for the stars; without Accumulation's substance, Limitation becomes mere rigidity. The steadiness of the Mountain and the flow of the Lake calibrate each other, turning 'storing deeply and releasing slowly' into sustainable long-termism.
resonance: ★ Same frequency of goals: both value long-term planning; Accumulation builds hard power, Limitation curbs unnecessary waste — together they make steady, long-term progress.
★ Complementary frameworks: Accumulation focuses on inner substance, Limitation on outer rules; a solid core plus a sturdy frame means doing things with clear structure.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm tug-of-war: Accumulation likes to wait for the big move, while Limitation wants to draw red lines and control the pace immediately — they can clash between 'hold on' and 'wrap it up.'
◆ Difference in scale: Accumulation thinks big and hates being stingy; Limitation fears overreach and tightens the belt — the push and pull can back each other into a corner.
advice: Let Accumulation take the lead on strategy and resource expansion, while Limitation sets budgets and key milestones. Reconcile 'investment and retention' once a month, and use Limitation's yardstick as a safety valve for Accumulation's ambition — don't treat the rules as shackles.

one_liner: One quietly builds a fortune, the other wears their heart on their sleeve to befriend others. Put them together and you get a dependable duo with both substance and style.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is 'Heaven within the mountain'—a bottomless treasure vault that prizes slow, steady accumulation and solitary self-cultivation. Inner Truth is 'Wind over the lake'—ripples spreading across the water, all about moving people with sincerity and holding nothing back. When the two meet, the Great Taming's 'not eating at home' needs Inner Truth's 'sincerity reaches pigs and fish' to connect with the outside world. Without the Great Taming's depth, Inner Truth's candor easily becomes empty talk; without Inner Truth's transparency, the Great Taming's accumulation turns into dusty archives. Both hexagram texts mention 'crossing the great water', which means once they join forces, one paves the way with hard power, the other breaks the ice with soft power, together they can steadily weather life's biggest storms.
resonance: ★ Substance underpins sincerity: the Great Taming's deep reserves keep Inner Truth's frankness from feeling shallow; every promise is backed by real capability.
★ Sincerity activates the storehouse: Inner Truth's wind-like penetration blows the wisdom hidden in the Great Taming's mountain out into reality, keeping knowledge from going moldy.
conflict: ◆ Closedness meets openness: the Great Taming prefers to hide first and reveal later, probing slowly; Inner Truth likes to speak plainly and from the heart, so their rhythms easily collide.
◆ Doctrine vs. empathy: the Great Taming loves to cite classics and lay down rules; Inner Truth values the warmth of human feeling in the moment—reason and emotion tend to squabble.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for 'no-purpose conversation'. The Great Taming speaks only from lived experience without showing off theory; Inner Truth shares only real feelings without lecturing. Let knowledge land and let emotions be met.

one_liner: You make sure the granary is full; I double-knot my laces before we leave.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is like a granary in a valley that holds an entire sky—it champions the outward break of 'good fortune in not eating at home' and the groundwork to 'cross the great water.' The Preponderance of the Small, on the other hand, is a low boom of thunder skimming the ridgeline, clinging to the down-to-earth stance of 'better to keep below than rise above.' Both rest on the shared stability of Ken, the Mountain, yet they move in entirely different rhythms: one herds energy inward, stockpiling momentum; the other bows its head, wringing out every last detail. The Great finds the Small too narrow, all hedged with restrictions; the Small finds the Great too ungrounded, too light on its feet. But when the frequencies match, the Great's grand blueprint becomes the Small's working drawing, and the Small's 'exceeding in frugality' becomes the perfect net for the Great's resource burn. This pairing wins not on passion but on a rock-solid chassis and pixel-perfect alignment of granularity—a doer-type couple that can slow-cook a long-term goal into real, concrete results.
resonance: ★ Same Frequency, Quiet Steadiness: Both hexagrams carry the mountain's groundwork, so when trouble comes, they naturally settle first and then move—neither is drawn to grandstanding.
★ Complementary Success: The Taming Power of the Great's grand vision must be paved by the Preponderance of the Small's humility and restraint—solid process beats empty reputation.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: The Great keeps its eyes on the long-term payoff of 'crossing the great water,' while the Small insists on doing only the sure and small things now—so at the start they often pull in opposite directions over who goes first.

◆ Perspective Split: The Great prizes the explosive potential of deeply stacked resources; the Small obsesses over the cost-efficiency of every tiny loss—they can easily end up arguing about whether a small detail even matters.
advice: Break the Great's macro goals into a micro-task list the Small can stomach. Each week, only check progress, don't debate direction. Run the smallest closed loop all the way through before adding more investment.

one_liner: You build the foundation deeper; I make sure the ending is clean. One stockpiles grain for winter, the other watches the stove so nothing burns.
analysis: Great Taming is 'Heaven within the Mountain' — like an invisible reservoir that doesn't rush to show off, only quietly stores resources and nurtures vision. After Completion is 'Water over Fire' — like a hearty dish fresh off the stove, the heat is just right but you have to keep watching so it doesn't burn. When these two come together, it's the 'foundation digger' meeting the 'quality control specialist.' Great Taming's slow rhythm provides a cushion for After Completion's tension, while After Completion's crisis awareness pushes Great Taming not to just hoard without delivering. But if Great Taming only charges outward, it can disrupt After Completion's careful rhythm of 'thinking ahead to prevent trouble'; and if After Completion keeps muttering about 'final disorder,' it will find Great Taming too lukewarm. The two need to learn how to weave long-term thinking into daily upkeep — only then can they both accomplish things and keep the whole situation stable.
resonance: ★ Long-Term and Short-Term Interlocking: Great Taming handles long-term buildup, After Completion focuses on the current finishing touches — they connect seamlessly across time, making their collaboration especially steady.

★ Substance and Flexibility Complementing: After Completion's preventive awareness activates Great Taming's reserves, and Great Taming's deep resources dissolve the anxiety After Completion feels after success.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Mismatch: Great Taming is used to slow, steady accumulation; After Completion wants immediate results — when moving a project forward, one thinks the other is too slow, the other too hasty.
◆ Perspective Tug-of-War: After Completion is always watching details out of fear of chaos, while Great Taming cares more about the big picture — during reviews, they tend to talk past each other.
advice: When disagreements arise, Great Taming should first offer a clear 'milestone schedule' to reassure After Completion; After Completion should condense its 'risk list' into three core actions. Then align at fixed checkpoints instead of draining each other in a battle of details versus big picture.

one_liner: One keeps the arsenal full, the other tests the waters on the front lines.
analysis: The Taming Power of the Great is about 'Heaven within the Mountain'—swallowing insight and virtue deep into the belly like a vast reservoir. It never shows its hand, waiting for the day it can 'cross the great river.' Before Completion, on the other hand, is 'Fire over Water'—the work isn't done yet, and the fox's tail is only just wet. You can neither hurry nor dawdle; it all comes down to 'carefully discriminating things and settling them in their proper places' to find the way. Put these two together, and you have one person stockpiling grain and sharpening knives while the other steps on mines and scouts the road. The Taming Power's steadiness can calm Before Completion's impatience and backstop all those unresolved messes; Before Completion's restless stirring forces The Taming Power to take all that book-learning out for a field test. But if The Taming Power holds in for too long, it turns into a pedant; if Before Completion splashes around without a plan, it ends up in over its head. Both need to see: storing power isn't for show, and trial-and-error isn't flailing. 'Hiding' and 'doing' have to click into the same rhythm.
resonance: ★ Backstop and Breakthrough: The Taming Power's deep reserves can catch Before Completion's clumsy trial-and-error without a flinch, turning every 'wetting of its tail' into solid XP instead of a crash-and-burn.

★ Discernment and Placement: Before Completion's meticulous 'careful discrimination of things and settling them in their places' helps The Taming Power file away its hoarded 'words and deeds of the past,' so all that knowledge doesn't become dead inventory collecting dust.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Mismatch: The Taming Power is used to building momentum slowly—'favorable to eat elsewhere, not at home'—while Before Completion is always goaded by 'the little fox almost across the ford.' One finds the other too slow; the other finds the first too reckless.

◆ Disconnect Between Inner and Outer: The Taming Power's 'accumulated virtue' leans toward inner depth; Before Completion's 'not yet completed' urgently needs external feedback. If communication falters, you get empty talk from the study colliding with real combat in the mud.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for 'review + trial run': the Taming Power side picks one hard-won experience from the bottom of the box, and the Before Completion side runs it as a small, minimum-viable test. Use the real results to align your understanding—don't work in separate silos.

one_liner: Two people who know how to nourish themselves come together — even the silence has a sweet aftertaste, and arguing feels like a waste of breath.
analysis: Two Mountain-over-Thunder hexagrams stacked together carry the art of self-nourishment to its peak. Neither of you runs on outside excitement; you recharge best in solitude. In the image of 'thunder beneath the mountain,' stillness and movement merge into a kindred rhythm of daily life: you know why I speak little, and I understand why you're a picky eater. This same frequency makes the relationship feel effortless — like two thermoses clinking, just the right temperature. But 'guard your words' stacked on 'guard your words' can trap all your feelings inside, turning your days into an ascetic's discipline. True nourishment isn't about building a cart behind closed doors; sometimes thunder must break through the soil, and you need to voice what's in your heart so the vital 'qi' can truly flow.
resonance: ★ Synced daily rhythms: You both weave rhythm into your routines, naturally aligning meal and sleep times without a word.
★ Kindred boundaries: You both know the measure of guarded speech, never casually crossing lines to pry, leaving each other plenty of space to process.
conflict: ◆ Emotional drain: Both of you are wired to swallow words and process alone, so friction easily turns into a cold war — no one wants to offer the first step out.
◆ Life runs bland: Overdoing restraint and self-control can make the partnership watery, missing the lively spark of everyday living.
advice: Make one day a month a 'break-the-rules day.' Go out for a bold, heavy-flavored meal or catch a lively show, and use that outgoing energy to let loose everything you've been holding in.

one_liner: One pinches every penny to build a solid nest egg, the other takes on the hardest battles and carries the load. Put them together, and the foundation stays solid while the roof gets thrown wide open.
analysis: The hexagram Yi (the Corners of the Mouth, Providing Nourishment) is like thunder tucked beneath a mountain: it is all about long, steady streams, careful speech, and eating with restraint — storing energy bit by bit into the very bone. Da Guo (the Preponderance of the Great), on the other hand, is like lake water flooding over the forest; when a crisis demands an extraordinary move, it would rather let the main beam bend than fail to break through alone. These two opposite hexagrams, when they come together, don't cancel out; they create a precise meshing of stored force and eruption. Yi's restraint gives Da Guo a safety net, preventing blind forward charges from gutting the roots. Da Guo's audacity yanks Yi out of an over-cautious comfort zone, daring to open a new path just when it matters. In their relationship, one tends the daily ground and the other overturns the table when the game is stuck. Energy withdraws and releases, and the two of them knead steadiness and boldness into one complete survival strategy.
resonance: ★ Holding the line, breaking the deadlock: Yi's steady, step-by-step approach can rein in Da Guo's reckless rushes, while Da Guo's decisiveness helps Yi snap out of the daily rut.

★ Nourishing the root, crossing the ridge: one focuses inward to root and store energy, the other dares to split open obstacles outward, fusing into a complete rhythm of deep accumulation and sudden release.
conflict: ◆ A mismatch of rhythm: Yi likes to play it safe, plan first and then act, while Da Guo likes to act first and talk later, seeking victory through risk — in daily decisions, they can easily get on each other's nerves.
◆ A temperature gap: Yi craves peace and moderation and finds the other overheating; Da Guo carries high-voltage pressure and finds the other too reserved, not forthright enough.
advice: Set clear lines between daily stewardship and critical breakthroughs: let Yi take the lead on small matters to keep the rhythm, let Da Guo make the calls on big matters and shoulder the risk, and in ordinary times keep your decision-making out of each other's way.

one_liner: The mountain builds your foundation, the water breaks the impasse — one banks the strength, the other storms the barrier.
analysis: Hexagram 27 (Nourishment) is like a sage seated high on a mountain peak, attending to 'prudent speech and moderate meals,' drawing energy inward to polish and refine it. Hexagram 29 (The Abysmal) is like a surging undercurrent that never rests, forging its tenacity through repeated trials in treacherous shoals. The quiet stillness of Mountain-Thunder becomes a reservoir for Kan's water. When Kan encounters grave danger, the discipline Yi cultivates prevents reckless expenditure; and the fluidity of Kan's waters dissolves the rigid defensiveness Yi might sink into. Their meeting is not one of mutual remodeling, but like a connoisseur of aged tea paired with strong liquor: each settles and matures in its own time, yet in times of crisis the mountain steadies the ground while the water opens a path — together they forge a wisdom of 'using stillness to master motion, and tenacity to crack stalemates.'
resonance: ★ A natural team of stored strength and peril-breaking: Yi's frugal speech and measured diet accumulate inner capital, exactly offsetting the resources Kan consumes when storming through obstacles.
★ The chemistry of steadiness dissolving danger: Kan's 'heart that prevails' needs the composed temperament Yi cultivates as its ballast.
conflict: ◆ Friction from mismatched rhythms: Yi likes slow, fine-grained nurture and may find Kan's risky breakthroughs too hasty.
◆ The tug between conservation and breakthrough: Yi's defensive mindset can make it miss the windows of opportunity Kan creates.
advice: When Kan hits danger, first take stock of reserves the Yi way; when Yi faces a decision, borrow Kan's thinking to keep a route open for adaptation.

one_liner: You take care of quietly building the reserve, I take care of shining bright outside — it's hard for a life like this not to become prosperous.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is like a still mountain harboring thunder — it values the inward accumulation of 'guarding words and moderating appetite.' The Li hexagram is like a double fire shining on itself — it pursues the outward radiance of 'renewing brightness in all directions.' Their encounter is essentially the meshing of 'storing energy' and 'releasing energy.' Without Yi's restraint, Li's blaze can easily burn out; without Li's pull, Yi's solidity can sink into dull self-isolation. The mountain provides the fire with an endless supply of fuel and steadiness; the fire gives the mountain warmth and visibility. This pairing doesn't rely on fleeting passion — it's like a slow simmer on an old stove: one tends the heat and the base ingredients, the other manages the aroma and the moment it's served. As long as you keep the rhythm of 'nourishing' and 'illuminating,' you can turn inner cultivation into outward influence — achieving each other without draining each other.
resonance: ★ Low heat brings out true flavor: Yi's restraint supplies stable fuel for Li's flame, so passion doesn't turn into a flash in the pan but flows as a steady stream of light between you.

★ A still mountain supports a bright light: Li's outward expression needs Yi's steadiness as its foundation. With introspective cultivation backing it, talent becomes even more substantial and enduring.
conflict: ◆ A raging fire burns the forest: if Li over-displays and over-spends, it can easily gut the inner resources Yi has carefully stored, turning 'nourishing' into 'depleting.'

◆ Heavy pressure smothers the small flame: if Yi becomes overly cautious, tight-lipped, and self-secluded, it can press down on the spark like thick earth on a flame, leaving Li's desire to express and create nowhere to go.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for 'offline and quiet' time to recharge separately, then come together to reflect and share. Let storing and shining follow a fixed rhythm — don't let one person always be the expressive one and the other always silent.

one_liner: You watch your words to build inner strength; I open my arms to embrace emotions. One still, one moving—just the right fit.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is like a steady mountain, emphasizing careful speech and measured appetite, drawing energy inward to nourish oneself solidly. The Xian hexagram is like a lake on a mountaintop, centered on openness and receptivity, emotionally sensitive, longing for the resonance of mutual reaching out. When the two come together, one quietly builds inner reserves, the other constantly sends out signals. Yi's restraint can catch Xian's sensitivity, keeping emotions from spilling into flood; Xian's liveliness can dissolve Yi's tension, bringing warmth into structure. The steadfastness of Mountain-thunder meets the gentleness of Lake-mountain—not a thunderous collision, but a quiet, long-streaming nourishment. As long as Yi doesn't find Xian too clingy, and Xian doesn't find Yi too wooden, this pair can knead self-cultivation and emotional flow into resilience, and life together grows sweeter over time.
resonance: ★ Complementary Rhythms: Yi's cautious words steady Xian's emotional waves; Xian's open heart hears Yi's unspoken care. One holds back, one lets go—they fall into the same frequency.
★ Mutual Nourishment: Yi focuses on inner cultivation, Xian excels at emotional exchange. Material and spiritual needs connect seamlessly in this relationship, filling each other's life gaps.
conflict: ◆ Boundary Tension: Yi tends to swallow words and digest alone; Xian reads silence as indifference. Different expressive temperatures cause unnecessary internal friction.
◆ Tempo Mismatch: Xian craves high-frequency interaction and immediate response; Yi prefers slow warming and solo recharging. One complains of clinginess, the other of coldness.
advice: Set aside half a day each week purely for talking. Yi should practice sharing small daily details; Xian should learn not to rush in with questions when the other is quiet, replacing emotional guessing with concrete companionship.

one_liner: One floors the gas and races forward; the other knows when to brake and save fuel. Together, they run a household with zero internal friction.
analysis: The Nourishing emphasizes careful speech and moderate eating—a cultivation that draws inward. Duration is about standing firm without changing course—a persistence that expands outward. Thunder beneath the mountain is an inner power that balances motion and stillness; thunder with wind is an outer practice of enduring constancy. The Nourishing provides the charging station for Duration, preventing it from exhausting its resources in blind sprints; Duration installs a navigation system for The Nourishing, keeping over-caution from turning into marking time. The mountain’s steadiness anchors the elusiveness of wind and thunder, while Duration’s resilience brings the fruits of Nourishment down to earth. This is not a fiery collision but a slow, steady supply line. One knows when to stop and digest; the other knows how to keep going long after the meal. Rhythms complement each other; energy closes into a loop.
resonance: ★ A steady stream builds deep reserves: Duration’s sustained drive needs stable supply, and The Nourishing’s restrained accumulation provides exactly that—keeping it from running on empty in the later stretch.
★ Stay on course without drifting: The Nourishing tends to hesitate while self-caring, but Duration’s commitment to constancy anchors the goal and breaks through steadily with momentum.
conflict: ◆ Clashing rhythms drain the heart: The Nourishing habitually pauses to digest and adjust, while Duration wants to finish in one stroke—different paces can trip each other up.

◆ Friction between keeping and breaking through: The Nourishing plays it safe and thinks thrice to avoid mistakes; Duration values long-term execution and may find the other too hesitant to take real action.
advice: Break the long-term plan into stage-based tasks. After every sprint, mandate a two-day silent recovery period—don’t chase deadlines, just recharge—so motion and stillness form a steady rhythm.

one_liner: One recharges by watching their words, the other sidesteps trouble by walking away—both put protecting their own energy before everything else.
analysis: The Corners of the Mouth hexagram (Yi) is like a mountain concealing thunder within: it teaches turning inward, being careful with speech and diet, and channeling all vitality into nurturing the roots. The Retreat hexagram (Dun) is like heaven looming high above a mountain: it teaches pulling outward, leaving draining circles gracefully and firmly, without harshness. Their meeting is the precise lock of a nourishment session with a withdrawal session. Nourishment builds the foundation and hoards energy, teaching us to guard our vital force amid noise; Retreat sets boundaries, reminding us not to fight losing battles. One draws in, the other lets go—both are exalted forms of self-preservation. In interaction, they never cling; they know how to leave breathing room. When storms hit, one lowers the head and sips tea to calm the spirit, the other turns and closes the door to dodge the edge. Even a glance carries the lucid clarity of kindred spirits.
resonance: ★ Same-frequency protection: both deeply loathe hollow socializing, and know how to withdraw their energy to invest in themselves—they will never play along with anyone's act.
★ Kindred space: one stores energy through restraint, the other cuts losses by withdrawing; in company they naturally keep a safe distance—no crossing lines, no clinging.
conflict: ◆ Offbeat rhythms: Nourishment likes to stay put and tend to its own soil; Retreat pulls away at the slightest stir. This can make one feel neglected and the other feel smothered.

◆ Differing conflict styles: when friction arises, Nourishment tends to swallow words and process internally, while Retreat goes straight for physical distance and cold treatment—easily letting small things curdle into overnight grudges.
advice: Set a rule of emotional buffering: when friction occurs, both step back and do your own thing; once the air clears, arrange a light meal and talk it over slowly—don't force an on-the-spot answer.

one_liner: You just floor it and charge ahead; I'll keep watch, hit the brakes, and supply the nourishment.
analysis: The Yi hexagram (Nourishment) is like a steady mountain pinning the thunder beneath it. It teaches to "be careful with words and moderate food and drink" — inward, nourishing, a slow and steady kind of replenishment. The Da Zhuang hexagram (Great Power) is thunder splitting the open sky, yang energy overflowing, blasting outward — yet it warns that "do not tread where propriety does not permit"; even the mighty must follow the rules. When these two meet, it's brake pads encountering a high-displacement engine. Da Zhuang's drive can make Yi feel depleted; Yi's slow tempo can make Da Zhuang feel suffocated. But the beauty lies in their complementarity: Da Zhuang needs Yi's caution and moderation to prevent overdoing it; Yi needs Da Zhuang's vigor and resolve to break free from excessive inward drain. The mountain can calm the thunder's restlessness; the thunder can split the mountain's dullness. One draws in, the other lets go — blending nourishment and strength into a sustainable ferocity.
resonance: ★ The confidence of Complementary action and stillness: Da Zhuang's momentum needs Yi's steadiness as a safety net, keeping it from a blind rush into a fall.
★ Kindred rhythm of storing and releasing: Yi's cautious, measured ways build the physical and mental reserves that Da Zhuang's bursts of power depend on.
conflict: ◆ The restlessness of mismatched rhythm: Yi prefers a slow simmer and deliberate thought; Da Zhuang sees it as dawdling, causing mutual tugging in the process.
◆ Friction over boundaries: Da Zhuang is born to open new ground, while Yi tends to guard its own small plot — easy to clash over who has crossed the line.
advice: Draw clear red lines around your force before cooperating. Da Zhuang leads the charge, but every push must sync progress with Yi; Yi handles logistics, but must never use 'let me think about it' as an endless delay. Lock the pace with a fixed review meeting.

one_liner: You focus on quietly building a solid foundation; I go out and take the world by storm. Together, we turn deep reserves into breakout wins.
analysis: Yi's 'thunder beneath the mountain' is about rooting inward, guarding words and moderating appetite, building a deep foundation. Jin's 'brightness rising over the earth' is the sun at dawn, meant to display one's talents. Put these two together and you get a classic 'reserve energy' vs. 'release' pairing. Yi's restraint gives Jin's drive a safety net, keeping Jin from burning out as hollow fire. Jin's ambitious forward motion gives Yi's quiet cultivation direction, preventing Yi from stewing into stagnant water. Over time, one learns to practice inner strength in silence, the other learns to put their radiance to practical use. Neither clings to the other — rather, 'nourishment' supplies 'progress' with fuel, and 'progress' opens a path for 'nourishment.' Day by day, life grows brighter.
resonance: ★ Deep reserves, swift release: Yi's solid accumulation provides an endless well of confidence for Jin's rapid rise — bold strides aren't the problem, an empty foundation is.
★ Illuminate the path ahead: Jin's bright initiative breaks through Yi's excessive caution, giving inner cultivation a chance to turn into real achievement.
conflict: ◆ Offbeat rhythms: Yi likes a low, slow simmer with careful words and deeds, while Jin wants to strike while the iron is hot and make a bold entrance — they can clash over whether to hurry or hold steady.
◆ Imbalanced drain: if Jin keeps radiating outward but forgets to return for refueling, Yi feels depleted; if Yi clamps down too hard, Jin feels hemmed in at every turn.
advice: Agree on a 'divide and conquer' between action and stillness: Jin handles outward results and expanding territory; Yi focuses on internal review and replenishing resources. Set aside half a day each week for shared quiet review so the momentum doesn't overdraw the foundation.

one_liner: You do the heavy lifting in the dark; I’ll keep supper warm and have your back in every conversation.
analysis: Yi is Mountain, governing stillness and nourishment, emphasizing cautious speech and measured eating—true logistical care. Ming Yi is Earth, governing endurance and concealment; 'the brightness enters the earth' points to its hidden light amid difficult circumstances. When these two hexagrams meet, it is like a fire-seed pressed under thick earth finding a sturdy mountain at its back. Ming Yi burns through itself easily in adversity and urgently needs Yi's quiet, low-key support. Yi does not rush to question; it simply sets down a hot meal and swallows its judgments, giving Ming Yi room to breathe. In return, Ming Yi's resilience—hidden light shining through darkness—lets Yi's care avoid trivial comfort and grow into deeper substance. One governs quiet nourishment, the other governs concealed sharpness; together they are the perfect partners in a dark game: you hide your light and keep your clumsiness, I add fuel and protect the stomach.
resonance: ★ Passing Soup in the Dark: At its lowest, Ming Yi fears empty talk most; Yi's pragmatic, disciplined nourishment precisely provides both emotional and material replenishment.
★ Silent Companionship: Yi's careful speech perfectly meets Ming Yi's need for silence—hidden light in darkness—without probing or judging, giving ample safe distance.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Rhythms: Yi is used to tending body and mind step by step, while Ming Yi often lives in high-pressure stress mode, and may mistake the slow pace for dawdling.
◆ Energy Drain: If Ming Yi's suppressed feelings go unvented for too long, Yi's restraint becomes emotional blockage; careful care can turn into a hostage situation.
advice: Ming Yi, don’t swallow every grievance alone—say clearly what kind of concrete care you need. Yi, don’t just feed; regularly take the other person out into the sun and let the inner fire air out.

one_liner: You watch your words and tend to yourself; I stoke the fire and warm our little home. The days naturally run smooth.
analysis: In Nourishment, 'Thunder beneath the Mountain' is about storing energy inward—speaking with care, eating with measure, earning your own keep, and not leaking energy outward. In The Family, 'Wind issuing from Fire' is about letting the inner warmth naturally spread outward—emphasizing consistency between words and deeds, and order in the household. When these two come together, Nourishment's steadiness calms The Family's petty anxieties, and The Family's hearth-fire melts Nourishment's aloof restraint. One is a cultivator sitting still in the mountains; the other is a cook blowing life into the stove. Nourishment teaches us not to speak carelessly or waste energy; The Family teaches us to ground honest words and actions in daily life. This pairing doesn't rely on fiery passion—it slowly simmers into flavor through the quiet understanding of inner work expressed outward. The longer you stay together, the deeper the substance.
resonance: ★ Same Frequency of Inner Cultivation and Outer Expression: Both Nourishment's self-care and The Family's household management value substance before appearance, with no empty posturing—their energy flows in striking alignment.

★ Prudent Speech and Steadfast Action: Nourishment emphasizes watching your mouth and moderating food; The Family values seeing things through from start to finish. Together, they make a solid, reliable life partnership.
conflict: ◆ Introversion vs. Extroversion: Nourishment tends to draw energy inward, which can come across as quiet and reserved; The Family needs emotional interaction and clear feedback, and may feel neglected over time.
◆ Frugality vs. Hearth-Glow Friction: Nourishment favors a clear mind and a simple diet; The Family prefers lively gatherings and social warmth, leading to clashes over spending and social frequency.
advice: Set aside one day a week as a 'Quiet Meal Day.' Turn off your phones, focus on the food and chores, and after the meal only discuss three small, concrete matters—no rehashing old debts, no airy talk.

relationship_name: Nourish the Authentic, Embrace the Different
one_liner: You keep your mouth in check and your stomach well fed; I poke at the prickles and pick out the differences. Our tongues may clash, but day by day, life together tastes better.
analysis: Nourishment, Mountain over Thunder, teaches turning inward—guarding words, moderating appetite, and seeking a quiet, sustained self-sustenance. Opposition, Fire over Lake, is born with an eye for discord—it scrutinizes, challenges, and believes in the clear-headed friction of agreeing to disagree. Their meeting is a dialogue between a contemplative and a disruptor. Nourishment's steadiness cushions Opposition's restlessness, so sharp differences don't ignite. Opposition's edge pierces the heaviness that comes from too much restraint, reminding Nourishment that self-cultivation isn't self-isolation. They don't try to fit seamlessly; instead, they learn to nourish each other through differences—one provides the anchor of moderation, the other expands the horizon with variety. As long as they hold to the practical bottom line of honest self-nourishment, Opposition's 'small things bring fortune' will take root in the textures of daily life.
resonance: ★ Complementary Rhythms: One slowly simmers and builds the foundation; the other quickly tests and finds new routes—together they make a daily life that's steady, with a dash of surprise.
★ Kindred Core: Both are after the right way to live—Nourishment guards its center by turning inward, Opposition clarifies its edges by turning outward; different paths, same destination.
conflict: ◆ Communication Temperature Gap: Nourishment stays quiet and rarely commits, while Opposition speaks plainly and puts disputes on the table—one side feels attacked, the other feels brushed off.

◆ Energy Tug-of-War: Nourishment wants the calm, restrained life of self-care; Opposition loves the disruptive arena of debate and breakthrough. The center of life keeps braking between stability and change.
advice: Institute a three-second buffer and a Difference Experience Day: pause before speaking so Nourishment's silence doesn't become a cold war and Opposition's bluntness doesn't become an attack. Once a week, take turns leading a crossover activity—let the quiet one try something new, and let the restless one learn to sit still.

one_liner: One slowly stockpiles inner strength, the other looks inward at every hurdle—together they're the cure for all kinds of reckless flailing.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is about thunder under the mountain: pulling energy back in to nourish yourself, watching your words, and keeping your composure. The Jian hexagram is water on the mountain: when outer obstacles block you, you retreat inward to cultivate virtue. When these two come together, it's not a fiery collision but a slow-simmered kindredness. Yi gives Jian the emotional and material grounding to hit walls without falling apart; Jian's peril, in turn, pushes Yi out of its comfort zone, making it realize that frugal eating isn't enough—you must turn within and refine your character to break the deadlock. With the mountain nature as the shared foundation, one tends the inner storehouse, the other surveys the outer terrain, braiding nourishment and passage into one rhythm.
resonance: ★ Kindred rooted inward: Both agree that in any situation, don't rush outward—steady yourself and look within. This unhurried foundation makes it extremely easy for them to vibrate on the same frequency.
★ Safety in a slow rhythm: Yi's restraint and Jian's prudence are a natural fit. Together they don't hustle or push, and in low periods they can always cover each other's backs.
conflict: ◆ Prone to over-conservatism: Yi is used to playing it safe, while Jian tends to retreat when danger appears. Together they may infect each other with a 'wait and see' procrastination, missing the window to break through.

◆ Emotional undercurrents are hard to clear: Yi swallows words to nurture life, Jian stuffs gloom into the heart to cultivate virtue. When real conflict arises, they tend to give each other the cold shoulder, lacking the direct, straight-shooting communication that breaks impasses.
advice: Set aside one fixed meal each week where no business is discussed—just home-cooked food. When a decision gets stuck, take turns using one sentence to name the core worry; don't play guessing games.

one_liner: One teaches you to slowly tend to your stomach and heart; the other urges you to quickly turn the page.
analysis: The Yi hexagram (Nourishment) is as steady as a mountain, valuing careful speech and restrained diet, drawing energy inward, with a focus on self-cultivation and boundaries. The Jie hexagram (Deliverance) is like a thunderstorm, championing forgiveness and leniency, letting pent-up emotions disperse outward, with a focus on breaking through impasses and releasing. When the two meet, it's like putting a safety valve on a pressure cooker: Yi's restraint can catch Jie's impatience, keeping you from hurting yourself in the quest for quick relief; Jie's transparency can loosen Yi's tightness, preventing over-nurturing from turning into internal wear and tear. In life, one builds the foundation day by day, the other clears the silt at key moments—alternating between action and stillness is the long-term plan.
resonance: ★ A Kindred Understanding Between Nurturing the Heart and Letting Go: Yi's moderate eating and Jie's pardon of faults both know the art of forgiving oneself—one uses routine to nourish the body, the other uses tolerance to heal the heart.

★ The Rhythm of Accumulating Force and Breaking Through: the deep stillness of thunder stored beneath the mountain meets the explosive release of thunder and rain in Jie—a perfect match for a life that builds reserves in calm times and acts swiftly when trouble strikes.
conflict: ◆ The Push and Pull Between Stability and Change: Yi is used to regulating step by step, while Jie insists that acting early brings release—one slow, one fast, and they can easily get under each other's skin.

◆ The Friction Between Caution and Directness: Yi asks you to think twice before acting, while Jie values quick, clean communication and leaving the past behind—during conversations, one holds back for fear of misspeaking, the other rushes to say things openly.
advice: When you're stuck, first use Jie's mindset to turn the page and cut your losses quickly, then use Yi's rhythm to reflect and heal slowly. Don't force self-care while emotions are flaring, and don't go making reckless moves when you should be resting.

one_liner: One watches what they eat to nourish the body; the other reigns in their temper to cultivate the heart. Together they make a refreshingly clear-minded minimalist duo.
analysis: Both hexagrams are crowned by the Mountain (Gen), so both people radiate the same composed, self-contained steadiness. Yi (Nourishment) is like a still mountain holding spring thunder within—it values self-sufficiency, careful words, and frugal eating, drawing energy inward. Sun (Decrease) is a mountain with a hidden lake below—it advocates reining in anger, curbing desire, and trimming away glitz, pushing excess wants outward. Thrown together, these two innately understand each other's art of letting go. One is quietly stockpiling vitality; the other is actively subtracting impurities. Their directions seem opposite, yet both are practicing 'less is more.' That said, Yi's thunder moves to sustain life, while Sun's lake delights in release. One wants to grow slowly and fully; the other wants to cut quickly and cleanly. Their tempos will need adjustment. As long as they hold fast to that shared mountain-heart, they can cultivate an exceptionally clear and light relationship.
resonance: ★ Minimalist living: both believe in talking less and stirring less, saving energy for the people and things that truly matter.
★ Strong sense of boundaries: both are as steady as a mountain, rarely overstepping and never chasing drama or pointless commotion.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched tempo: Yi wants to slowly nourish and build up; Sun leans toward quick subtraction and decluttering. Patience runs thin.
◆ Opposite energy flow: one seeks self-generation inward, the other reduces desire outward; each can feel the other is trying too hard.
advice: When disagreements arise, don't rush to remodel each other. First set a rule of one hour of silence; then lay out what each wants to nurture and what each wants to cut, and talk it through before acting.

one_liner: One shared engine — you conserve inward to build the base, while I race outward to seize chances.
analysis: Both hexagrams sit atop the driving impulse of Thunder, but Mountain and Wind direct that energy in two different directions. The Hexagram of Nourishment emphasizes inward focus — prudent speech and measured eating are classic signs of the conservationist, warming up the foundation first. The Hexagram of Increase emphasizes outward release — moving toward the good is classic doer energy, adjusting the steering wheel while running. Two people sharing the Thunder's accelerator: one taps the brake to steady the center of gravity, the other eases off the gas to catch the wind. Nourishment's restraint can catch Increase's impulsiveness; Increase's flexibility can enliven Nourishment's stubbornness. As long as you keep clear lines between stewardship and innovation, this is the most grounded progress-together combination.
resonance: ★ Same-frequency underlying action drive: both carry Thunder's explosive quality; once direction is set, no inner friction — execution rhythm is naturally in sync.

★ Complementary correction systems: one excels at storing energy in silence and dodging pitfalls, the other habitually makes quick turnarounds in practice; combined, they form a perfect error-avoidance guide.
conflict: ◆ Mutually exclusive pacing: Nourishment prefers to chew slowly and swallow carefully for safety; Increase likes to run while looking for efficiency — day-to-day they may resent each other's sluggishness or recklessness.

◆ Boundary-pulling: Mountain governs restraint and draws its own circle, Wind governs flow and loves testing beyond limits. When decisions arise, Nourishment thinks Increase is too flighty; Increase thinks Nourishment is too stuffy.
advice: Clearly divide the duties of 'holding the line' and 'exploring new paths.' The Nourishment side handles finances and risk control; the Increase side handles external breakthroughs and trial-and-error. Set aside one fixed day each month to align books and progress.

one_liner: One quietly accrues the wherewithal, the other flamboyantly unleashes the ultimate move — together they balance the books just right.
analysis: The Nourishment hexagram is like a mountain pressing down on hidden fire: it teaches careful words and frugal desires, pulling energy inward to slowly rebuild strength. The Breakthrough hexagram is a lake that has burst its banks: it calls for openhanded reward and firm decision, pushing momentum outward to clear away obstacles in clean strokes. When these two meet, one is afraid that more words will only invite more mistakes, while the other wishes he had a loudspeaker. One prefers to grow confidence through steady, trickling savings; the other likes to sever tangled knots with one sharp blow. The rhythms may seem out of sync, but there is a hidden secret: without Nourishment’s sedimentation, Breakthrough’s decisiveness becomes water with no source; without Breakthrough’s sharpness, Nourishment’s cultivation merely stews into internal attrition. The pull in and the push out link nurturing with use into a perfect closed circuit.
resonance: ★ Static and dynamic complement each other: Nourishment’s poise wraps around Breakthrough’s impulsiveness, grounding every move in steady earth.
★ Stockpile and strike in unison: Breakthrough’s clean rupture gives Nourishment’s patient stockpile the outlet it craves.
conflict: ◆ Verbal friction: Nourishment guards its words with a triple seal, Breakthrough always speaks its mind — conversations feel like two stations colliding.
◆ Rhythmic mismatch: One slow-simmers to build backbone, the other flash-fries to clear roadblocks — their working tempo always trips over each other.
advice: Set a fixed sequence: first calculate, then decide. Let Nourishment handle early evaluation and risk control, and Breakthrough take the final call and drive it forward. Split cultivation and execution into an assembly line, so they don’t wrestle in the same arena.

one_liner: One cultivates the inner self, the other conquers the outer world—when they come together, they must first match each other's rhythm.
analysis: The Nourishment hexagram is like a deep valley holding a spring, teaching us to settle within, speak with care, and mind our nourishment. The Encounter hexagram is like a long wind sweeping across, urging expansion outward and serendipitous meetings. The mountain's nature is steady and protective; heaven's nature is fluid and boundary-breaking. When the two converge, Nourishment's restraint can temper Encounter's impulsiveness, while Encounter's liveliness can jar Nourishment out of stagnation. But if Nourishment clings too tightly, it can cut off the opportunities Encounter brings; if Encounter spends too freely, it can drain the reserves Nourishment has built. The true fit lies here: let Nourishment's calm steer Encounter's boldness, and let Encounter's disruptive power open new horizons for Nourishment's growth.
resonance: ★ Stored energy meets fresh opportunity: the depth of Nourishment provides the groundwork for Encounter's chance meetings, turning serendipity into lasting sustenance at first contact.

★ Stillness and motion complement each other: thunder rumbling beneath the mountain and wind sweeping across the sky both pulse with life—together they create a growth cycle that connects inner and outer.
conflict: ◆ Preservation meets breakthrough: Nourishment values order and may see Encounter's randomness as an affront, while Encounter's drive for disruption often finds Nourishment's caution a hindrance.
◆ Introversion collides with expansion: a philosophy of restraint—guarded speech and frugal habits—runs up against an instinct to spread far and wide, causing tug-of-war over resources.
advice: Establish a staged alignment system: the Nourishment side sets the ground rules and replenishment plan; the Encounter side takes the lead on external probes and opportunity capture. Then meet monthly over tea to review and fine-tune any rhythm deviations.

relationship_name: Nurturing and Gathering in Mutual Aid
one_liner: You hustle to gather the crowd; I keep time and steady the ship. Together, life feels both lively and grounded.
analysis: Yi (Nourishment) is like mountain thunder lying low—rooting inward, watching words and diet, living with precision and self-discipline. Cui (Gathering Together) is like lake water spreading over the earth—naturally loving to gather people, stocking grain and tools amid the bustle to prepare for the unexpected. When the two meet, it's like a slow-cooking stove meeting a banquet host. Yi's steadiness can anchor Cui's restlessness, keeping the crowd from scattering; Cui's living water can moisten Yi's austere solitude, preventing excessive inner burnout. The only rub: Yi's closed-door cultivation often collides with Cui's open-door hospitality. Their rhythms differ, so they must learn to leave white space in the noise and open the door while alone.
resonance: ★ Still Water Bears the Boat: Cui's liveliness needs Yi's steadiness as a safety net, or the gathering easily crumbles into sand. Together they can keep their measure amid the noise.
★ Gathering Fire Becomes Light: Yi's long-term discipline paired with Cui's charisma can turn one person's quiet cultivation into a great cause for many—energy multiplies quickly.
conflict: ◆ Closed-Door Meets Knock: Yi is used to closing the door for frugal meals and cautious words, but Cui loves opening the door to host gatherings. When boundaries are broken, they tend to drain each other.
◆ Stockpiling vs. Clear Mind: Cui likes to stockpile supplies against mishaps, but Yi feels over-accumulating ruins the true meaning of nurturing. Their daily rhythms and spending habits often clash.
advice: Agree on a rotating schedule for activity and stillness. When Cui hosts, Yi manages the process to prevent chaos; when Yi goes into retreat, Cui shields them from useless socializing. Alternate who leads the rhythm.

relationship_name: Nurture with Care, Rise by Degrees
one_liner: Your job is to keep the foundation steady; mine is to climb with the flow.
analysis: The Nourishment hexagram is like an inward-looking reservoir—thunder hidden beneath the mountain. It teaches us to watch the mouth, gather the heart, and put energy only where it counts. The Pushing Upward hexagram is a seedling breaking through the soil—wood born from the earth—and once it has set its direction, it advances a pawn every day. When these two hexagrams meet, they do not clash with flying sparks; they mesh precisely, like pressing the accelerator before shifting gears. Without Nourishment's moderation and settled depth, Pushing Upward's climbing easily becomes a flare of hollow fire with no staying power. Without Pushing Upward's initiative and openness, Nourishment's careful tending decays into a closed loop of self-isolation. The mountain gives the earth a sturdy foundation; the wood, using the wind, splits open the soil. Together they form a perfect circuit of energy: you make the groundwork thicker, and I make the road longer. This is a long-termist, kindred understanding—one that turns restraint into endurance.
resonance: ★ A gentle stream nourishes the roots: Nourishment's restraint provides Pushing Upward's growth with an endless supply of inner sustenance, avoiding the hollow waste of pulling up sprouts to force growth.

★ One step at a time, rising upward: Pushing Upward's 'small steps make great heights' perfectly receives the energy Nourishment saves by speaking carefully and eating moderately, turning restraint into real ascent.
conflict: ◆ The rhythm can jam: Nourishment is used to stopping for introspection and maintenance, while Pushing Upward is always eager to strike while the iron is hot and press ahead—mismatched paces can drag each other down.

◆ Holding things in too tightly becomes internal friction: when Nourishment suppresses expression and desire too much, Pushing Upward loses its impulsive force for breaking through and becomes dead water that is only stored, never released.
advice: Start an 'energy ledger': when your tank is full, focus on one specific small goal; the moment you feel tired or find yourself wanting to complain, shut up, rest, and eat light—never force it, and never chatter aimlessly.

one_liner: You handle grinding through the valley, I keep the rice bowl steady; together, that's a solid, down-to-earth life.
analysis: Yi is Mountain over Thunder, all about seeking your own sustenance and being careful with words—like a deep well that knows to hold resources close and nourish them slowly. Kun is Lake over Water, but the lake has no water in it, all about words not being believed and pushing through to fulfill your will, like walking on a dry riverbed—the more you explain, the weaker you get. When these two hexagrams come together, it's supply meeting demand. Yi's restraint catches Kun's anxiety dead-on—when nobody believes the Kun person's explanations, Yi simply shuts up and offers real, solid support. And Kun's fierce drive to see its purpose through to the end can push Yi out of its over-cautious comfort zone. The mountain holds down the thunder's restlessness, the lake leaks away the water's emptiness. One cultivates inner strength, the other holds the bottom line—together, they build the steadiest symbiosis just when resources run dry.
resonance: ★ Prudent Words, No Debate: When Kun's words go unheard, Yi's silence and practicality slip right past the futile exchange—action over explanation is exactly the right fit.
★ Solid Nourishment Breaks the Deadlock: Yi's steady, self-sufficient groundwork precisely fills the dried-up lake of Kun's exhaustion, giving the stubborn survivor a safety net.
conflict: ◆ Pacing Mismatch: Yi is used to conserving energy and building strength slowly, while Kun is desperate to burn the boats and push to the bitter end—each may find the other too plodding or too reckless.
◆ Emotional Temperature Difference: In dire straits, Kun craves intense empathy, but Yi tends to stay coolly observant and practical, which can make the struggling one feel stone-cold.
advice: In times of hardship, don't force the other person to declare a stance. The Yi type will simply have the meals ready and the escape route secure—showing up with action beats ten thousand words of reasoning.

one_liner: You focus on getting yourself in order, and I focus on activating resources—together we're a sure-win partnership.
analysis: The Nourishment hexagram is like thunder stored beneath the mountain, emphasizing inward gathering, cautious speech, and moderate eating—a classic self-nourishing personality. The Well hexagram is like water drawn upward through wood, emphasizing outward connection, helping others, and shared benefit—a natural shared energy. When these two hexagrams meet, the essence is the collision of 'individual boundaries' and 'public flow.' Nourishment's restraint can install a valve on the Well's generosity, preventing endless giving from draining one dry. The Well's living water can pry open Nourishment's closure, allowing personal reserves to find an outlet to nourish others. The mountain stays still within; the water flows without. One knows when to stay quiet and conserve; the other excels at when to uncork and share. As long as you hold the bottom line of 'self-sufficiency before helping others,' this relationship can be like a living well—both stable and endlessly vital.
resonance: ★ Nourish without Depletion: Nourishment's restraint and the Well's resourcefulness naturally fit together; giving with a sense of measure lets resources flow steadily without harming each other's vitality.

★ Stillness and Motion in Harmony: The steady accumulation of Mountain-Thunder meets the upward growth of Wood-Water; one lays the foundation, the other expands the horizon—your working rhythm is especially compatible.
conflict: ◆ Boundary Friction: Nourishment tends to turn inward, speaking cautiously and acting prudently, while Well craves outward connection and frequent interaction—one side can easily feel too distant or too intrusive.

◆ Mismatched Consumption: Well pursues continuous, unbroken output, while Nourishment emphasizes precise, on-demand replenishment. If the rhythm isn't aligned, one can overextend and the other can seem overly calculating.
advice: Set fixed 'solo recharge days' and 'shared sharing sessions.' Use a clear rhythm instead of impulsive giving, so neither side feels over-exploited nor neglected.

relationship_name: Mutual Completion of Nurture and Reform
one_liner: You keep the foundation steady and nurture it slowly; I watch for the right moment and flip the table. Together, we're a dream team that repairs and reforms as we go.
analysis: The Nourishment Hexagram is like a steadfast mountain, valuing careful words and moderate consumption, drawing energy inward, and building a solid base through self-discipline and accumulation. The Revolution Hexagram is a fire burning in a marsh, daring to break the old and establish the new when the time is right, moving with decisive force. When these two come together, it's a precise meshing of stability and change. Nourishment's deep reserves provide the provisions for Revolution's breakthroughs, while Revolution's sharp edge can cleave through the conservative stagnation Nourishment might sink into. It's like tending a garden: one digs deep and fertilizes to enrich the soil, the other prunes regularly to keep growth from running wild. Over time, one stops making pointless moves, the other stops stubbornly grinding, and instead they can hold their ground amid change and grow something new out of stability.
resonance: ★ Solid Accumulation Carries Confidence: The resources Nourishment has saved through long-term discipline give Revolution the buffer for trial and error when it makes a sudden pivot, so change doesn't drain the family reserves.

★ Breaking Old to Build New Gets a Second Wind: Revolution's decisive reforms regularly clear out the redundant habits Nourishment has cultivated, keeping self-cultivation from becoming a stagnant, self-enclosed pond.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch Is a Killer: Nourishment prefers to simmer at its own pace, while Revolution wants to light the fire the moment it sees an opening, each side finding the other too slow or too rash.

◆ Boundary Clashes Cause Internal Friction: Nourishment values inward self-preservation, instinctively rejecting Revolution's sweeping, dramatic energy, and is prone to mistaking its partner's breaking of old patterns as reckless mischief.
advice: When disagreements arise, set clear lines first: use Nourishment's discipline for fine-tuning daily routines, wait for Revolution's timing to be ripe before making major decisions, and apply stability and change in separate scenarios rather than muddling them.

one_liner: You hold your tongue and build your depth; I wield the fire and refine true gold.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is like a mountain holding thunder — it teaches drawing inward, speaking carefully, and eating sparingly, filtering out the world's noise and excess desires until only the purest nourishment remains. The Ding hexagram is like wood feeding fire — it teaches refining outward, placing your accumulated foundation over the flames and letting it slow-cook into a clear, grounded destiny. Together, these two hexagrams form a complete system of digestion and transformation. Yi provides a stable base and clean raw materials; Ding supplies steady heat and a clear direction. Without Yi's restraint, Ding's fire burns too fiercely and runs on empty. Without Ding's tempering, Yi's nourishment just settles in the belly and turns to fat. Side by side, they can turn the small stuff of daily life into real currency for career and personal growth — one lays the groundwork, the other delivers the finished piece.
resonance: ★ Slow fire brings out true flavor: Yi's restraint provides clean ingredients for Ding's cooking. Both believe good things cannot be rushed; they must be simmered slowly over time.
★ A stable foundation never wavers: The mountain's stillness holds the fire's leaping motion, giving Ding's ambition for change a place to land — so you can charge ahead without tipping over.
conflict: ◆ Silence breeds frustration: Yi tends to swallow emotions in silence, while Ding urgently needs to pour ideas into the pot and bring them to a boil. When one is fast and the other is slow, frustration builds up internally.
◆ Hard to control the heat: Ding wants to make bold, sweeping changes, while Yi prefers to preserve old rules and nurture slowly. One wants a blazing hot stir-fry; the other wants a gentle slow-cook.
advice: When you hit a rough patch, the Yi side should first write out a list of needs and make bottom lines clear; the Ding side can then adjust the heat accordingly. Don't meet enthusiasm with silence.

one_liner: You both carry thunder in your bones — one uses it to hold steady and nurture, the other to break through and charge.
analysis: Yi is a mountain hiding thunder — it holds that raw surge in, turning it into daily caution in speech, moderation in appetite, and inner nourishment. Zhen is double thunder crashing — it uses fear as a whetstone, staying calm in the fray and growing bolder with every setback. At your core, you both carry the gene for motion; you understand that crisis and vitality coexist, but you deliver power in completely opposite ways. Yi is like fitting an engine with shock absorbers, trusting slow and steady accumulation; Zhen is like flooring the accelerator straight into the storm, forging steadiness through action. In a relationship, Yi can pull on Zhen's reins and teach it to settle impulse into endurance; Zhen can knock on Yi's comfort zone and remind it not to get so caught up in self-care that it forgets to break new ground. One defends, one attacks, and when the thunder at your foundations rumbles, it becomes the secret code only the two of you truly understand.
resonance: ★ Shared instinct for crisis: Deep down, you both know that when thunder sounds, change is inevitable. Your radar for sudden developments is extremely sharp, and without a word, you instantly read each other's tension.

★ Same source of inner drive: Both of you share the lower trigram Zhen, giving you that raw, never-say-die momentum. Once you've set your mind on something, no matter how loud the outside world gets, the engine inside you never stalls.
conflict: ◆ Severe rhythm clash: Yi tends to tap the brakes and nurture slowly, while Zhen always wants to floor the gas and charge. Days are easily spent arguing red-faced over whether to steady up or go all in.

◆ Mismatched communication channels: Yi values cautious speech for safety; Zhen believes in shaking the world with sheer presence. One thinks the other is too repressed; the other thinks the one is too flamboyant.
advice: Set a switch for action and rest: When a sudden crisis hits, let Zhen charge in and break through first; afterward, always follow Yi's pace for a calm review. For everyday planning, let Yi handle the gatekeeping, while Zhen simply executes without crossing lines.

relationship_name: Knowing When to Stop, Nourishing Well
one_liner: Outwardly, both sit there like a great unmoving mountain — but inside, one is busy charging up for the long haul, and the other has just switched into power-saving mode.
analysis: Both have Mountain as their upper trigram, so they naturally share a foundational logic of setting boundaries and practicing restraint. Beneath Yi (Nourishment) lies hidden Thunder, governing intake and growth; beneath Gen (Keeping Still) lies Mountain upon Mountain, governing sedimentation and stopping. The beauty of this relationship lies in how movement and stillness calibrate each other: Gen's absolute stillness can rein in Yi's tendency to overconsume, keeping the quest for knowledge and self-nourishment within proper bounds; Yi's faint thunder stirs Gen with a hint of vitality, preventing it from sinking into desolate stagnation. They don't sustain their bond through fiery collisions but by holding each other up through silent companionship. One learns to pause three seconds before speaking; the other realizes that stillness is not escapism but a way of storing strength. In the end, they find the most comfortable rhythm of coexistence between restraint and release.
resonance: ★ Kindred boundary awareness: Both are used to raising walls to the outside world, not easily opening up and not fond of crowds, so they give each other plenty of breathing room.

★ Understanding the art of leaving space, with no emotional drain: One watches their words to avoid trouble, the other calms their thoughts to cultivate the heart. Together, they don't have to try hard to please; just being quiet in each other's company feels comfortable.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched energy rhythms: Yi's hidden Thunder always wants to absorb something new, while Gen is used to staying perfectly still, so each may find the other too restless or too greedy for more.

◆ Awkward standoffs when trouble hits: One uses restraint to keep balance, the other simply cuts off the signal, so when conflict arises they both fall silent, and nobody takes the first step to bridge the gap.
advice: When a disagreement arises, don't be in a hurry to argue. Sit together quietly for twenty minutes and let the emotions come down from the mountain; then the conversation will sort itself out more smoothly.

one_liner: One builds a solid foundation, the other takes steady steps; together they're a pair slowly simmering a good life.
analysis: Nourishment, like a mountain, guards inner boundaries, honoring 'careful words and temperate eating.' It draws energy inward and focuses on self-nourishment. Development, like wind brushing through trees, follows 'gradual progress' and spreads a long-term rhythm outward. When these two come together, there's no fiery clash—only a precise interlocking of tempo. Nourishment's restraint gives Development's advancement a steady foundation, and Development's patience in turn supports Nourishment's daily practice, keeping groundedness from turning into self-imposed isolation. Like tending a bonsai, Nourishment is the fine art of controlling water and pruning branches; Development is the slow sprouting that responds to the seasons. This pair's greatest taboo is rushing for quick results; the best state is to let days simmer into a compound-interest curve.
resonance: ★ Rhythmic resonance: Both despise over-urging growth, value spending time on solid accumulation, and proceed step by step without craving speed.
★ Solid foundation: One guards the inner baseline of body and mind, the other lays out long-term paths outward; inner cultivation and outer expansion naturally create a virtuous cycle.
conflict: ◆ Slow progress: Both sides are conservative and steady; when facing a juncture that requires a breakthrough or quick experimentation, they tend to watch each other and miss the first opportunity.

◆ Communication gap: The Nourishment hexagram tends to keep things in with careful speech; the Development hexagram prefers to follow procedure and isn't good at giving emotions directly. Over time, this can quietly create hidden obstacles.
advice: Hold a monthly 'progress check-in' to openly discuss the experiences, concerns, and plans each has quietly accumulated. Don't let prudence become internal friction.

one_liner: Build yourself strong first, then receive another person's heart — only then can this love never break.
analysis: The Yi hexagram teaches to 'be careful with words and moderate food and drink' — a slow craft of rooting inward. The Guimei hexagram warns that 'action brings misfortune and no advantage; to know the end, know the defect' — a sharp turn toward outward connection. Mountain pressing down on Thunder is restraint and sedimentation; Thunder striking the Lake is impulse and pursuit. When these two hexagrams meet, it is a 'fear of going hungry' encountering a 'fear of missing one's marriage fate.' Yi's steadiness can hold Guimei's restlessness, but Guimei's thunder may also find the mountain too stifling. The real chemistry lies in this: Guimei reminds Yi not to become an emotional island through self-cultivation alone, while Yi teaches Guimei to see the cards on the table before acting on impulse. The thunder beneath the mountain stays silent unless it must—once it sounds, it becomes lasting nourishment. The thunder over the lake does not rage unless it must—only after raging does it understand the value of a gentle, steady stream. For this relationship to work, you must knead 'self-discipline' and 'entrusting yourself to another' together, neither overdrawing your passion nor neglecting your fate.
resonance: ★ To love, you must first nurture yourself: Yi emphasizes self-sufficiency; Guimei longs for emotional belonging. Only by caring for yourself first do you gain the strength to build a lasting bond.

★ Knowing flaws ensures longevity: Guimei's 'know the defects' and Yi's cautious speech and frugal diet both carry a clear-eyed wisdom. Knowing where the hidden reefs lie keeps love from blind intoxication.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms out of sync: Guimei's thunder wants to settle the title at once; Yi's mountain wants to observe and test first. One finds the other too slow, the other too hasty.

◆ Mismatched communication: Yi habitually closes its mouth, swallowing words in introspection; Guimei easily surges with emotion and speaks bluntly. Their dialogues often feel like talking across different frequencies.
advice: Set a 'cooling-off rule': when you hit a disagreement, each spend the time of one meal alone, digest your emotions, then speak. Don't send Guimei's impulsiveness to crash against Yi's silence.

one_liner: One quietly builds the family fortune behind the scenes; the other wins battles with flair in the spotlight.
analysis: The Yi hexagram speaks of guarding words and moderating food – it is the art of tending life through inward gathering and a slow, steady flow. The Feng hexagram, with thunder and lightning together, is the high-noon hour – an outward burst that rides the momentum and shines. Put the two together, and you have a steady quartermaster meeting a razor-sharp vanguard. Yi, the mountain over thunder, knows restraint and sedimentation; it can hold Feng’s drive without letting it burn out of control. Feng, the thunder over fire, brings brightness and decisiveness that can break through Yi’s tendency to hesitate and overthink. One teaches how to hold in; the other teaches how to let go. Over time, Yi’s patience gives Feng a solid foundation, and Feng’s boldness cracks open new paths for Yi – together they form a survival strategy that can defend and attack.
resonance: ★ Storing Energy, Catching the Wave: Yi's steady foundation can firmly receive the massive energy of Feng's outburst, so no momentum is wasted.
★ Breaking Gridlock, Showing the Way: Feng's thunder-fire decisiveness can instantly cut through the over-caution and inner friction Yi tends to fall into.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Yi likes to chew slowly and nourish gradually, while Feng always feels the heat is too low and wants results right away.
◆ Scale Friction: Yi seeks stability and moderation in everything, and when faced with Feng's bold, sweeping style, it can feel like losing control.
advice: When a key decision comes up, don't rush to decide. First let the Yi person close the door and chew through the risks, then let the Feng person take the plan and charge ahead.

one_liner: One stays home simmering soup to nourish life, the other roams the world scouting the way; together it's: 'you keep us fed, I'll lead the road.'
analysis: The Nourishment hexagram is like a mountain hiding thunder—it values 'stability' and 'nourishment,' drawing energy inward, watching words and steadying the breath, like an old tree coiling its roots in silent reserve. The Wanderer hexagram is like a fire blazing on a mountain peak—it runs on 'movement' and 'perception,' advancing step by step in foreign lands, using the firelight to read the road ahead. When these hexagrams come together, it's not one overpowering the other; it's a kindred link between 'home base' and 'scout.'
