Nourishment supplies the Wanderer with emotional and physical stamina; the Wanderer brings back the outside world's weather for Nourishment. But fire is quick to scatter, and mountains tend to stagnate—one always wants to sink roots and stay put, the other habitually packs a bag. Given time, they may get stuck on the 'stay or go' rhythm. Fortunately, Mountain-Thunder and Mountain-Fire spring from the same line. As long as they blend the self-discipline of 'guarding words and moderating diet' with the clarity of 'discerning insight and cautious action,' they can both eat well and walk well this troubled world.
resonance: ★ Hearth and backpack complement each other: the Nourishment hexagram excels at making daily life substantial, while the Wanderer hexagram is used to traveling light. One stockpiles inner strength, the other opens up new horizons.

★ Reserved speech meets sharp observation: Nourishment teaches less talking and more settling; the Wanderer teaches keeping eyes peeled to the situation. Together, they're the golden combo for 'quietly making big moves.'
conflict: ◆ Homebody vs. road-trip tug-of-war: Nourishment likes to stay in its comfort zone and cultivate slowly; the Wanderer finds staying put boring. One slow, one fast—they can start to get on each other's nerves.

◆ Scattering fire vs. fixed mountain drain: the Wanderer's fire darts upward seeking flexibility; the Nourishment's mountain presses down for stability. When they disagree, it can turn into silent mutual draining.
advice: Set a monthly rule of a 'three-day mini-voyage.' At ordinary times, stay home and cook in peace, then settle stay-or-leave disagreements by 'rotating who takes the lead.'

one_liner: One knows how to hold back and spend sparingly, the other is skilled at going with the wind — together they are a pragmatic pair built to last, like a slow, steady stream.
analysis: For Yi, the 'thunder below the mountain' emphasizes drawing energy inward and self-nourishment; in their approach, they always take stock of the family resources first and keep a tight rein on words and appetite. Xun's 'entering with the wind' is a soft, adaptive power of execution that rides the current and excels at finding a way in through the cracks. When the two come together, it's not a hard collision but a joining of chassis and airflow. Yi handles the braking and leaves room, giving the relationship a foundation that withstands risk; Xun handles reading the wind and offering the ladder, turning conservative plans into workable actions. As long as Yi doesn't seal up like a closed jar and Xun doesn't lose their backbone by drifting with the tide, this combination can slowly season into something fine — 'hold the line, keep the tempo' — the kind that only gets more solid the longer it's lived.
resonance: ★ Rhythmic sync: Yi's restraint leaves a safe buffer period, and Xun's gentleness knows exactly how to slip into the gaps to move things forward — without jumping the beat or dragging their feet.
★ Complementary energy: one turns inward to build vital essence, the other reaches outward to test the wind — together, they're a pragmatic team that saves up capital before finding the way.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned advance and retreat: Yi is used to thinking three times before moving and prefers to stay put, while Xun always wants to follow the wind, testing and adjusting direction at any moment — they're likely to lock horns over 'hold steady or chase change.'

◆ Temperature gap in expression: Yi values guarded speech and avoids causing trouble, while Xun needs high-frequency communication to carry out orders — one finds the other too shut-in, the other finds the first too roundabout.
advice: When problems arise, start by having Yi map out the bottom lines and resource ledger, then let Xun flexibly pave the way; when you disagree, don't rush to argue — give each other half a day of space, and let results replace emotional tugging.

one_liner: One stays quiet to recharge, the other chatters to make friends — together they make a top-tier recharging session.
analysis: Yi is thunder under the mountain, focusing on careful speech and moderation in diet, drawing energy inward for self-cultivation and restraint. Dui is two lakes joined, centered on friends talking and learning, like living water spilling outward, valuing shared resonance and emotional flow. When these two hexagrams meet, it's a dance between contraction and release. Yi gives Dui's liveliness a solid foundation, preventing joy from sliding into flamboyance; Dui opens a window for Yi's quiet practice, keeping inner cultivation from becoming solitary self-appreciation. When they get along well, they relax in front of someone reliable and grow wiser in a relaxed setting; when they don't, Yi finds Dui too loud, and Dui finds Yi too dull. The key is for Dui to know when to leave space and listen, and for Yi to be willing to open up and speak from the heart.
resonance: ★ Energy flow: Yi's inward sinking steadily catches Dui's emotional overflow, while Dui's open sharing provides real-world feedback for Yi's quiet cultivation — they nourish each other.
★ Study and heart-nourishing: Dui thrives on exchange and debate, infusing Yi's self-reflective solitude with fresh insights, turning personal practice into mutual progress.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm: Yi values careful words and restrained desires, habitually watching the scene half a beat behind; Dui loves instant interaction and easily mistakes Yi's silence for coldness or a dampener.
◆ Boundary tug-of-war: Dui seeks emotional resonance and likes to open up without reservation; Yi values inner order, and excessive pouring-out directly disrupts Yi's energetic balance.
advice: Before the gathering, swap hearty meals and boozy chatter for light tea and simple snacks. Let Dui spark topics and warm the room, while Yi curates the real takeaways and wraps it up. End while the energy is highest, leaving plenty of time to recover.

one_liner: Build a solid foundation first, then let your influence spread.
analysis: The hexagram of Nourishment is like a steady mountain storehouse—it values cautious words and measured consumption, storing energy inward. The hexagram of Dispersion is like a long wind drifting across the water—it seeks to break the pattern and spread outward. When these two meet, they form an energy loop of gathering first, then releasing. Without Nourishment's solid groundwork, Dispersion's scattering becomes rootless duckweed, floating for a while and then fading away; without Dispersion's driving force, Nourishment's restraint can easily stagnate into still water, causing internal harm. Their Kindred quality lies here: one makes daily life fuller and more nourishing, the other turns the accumulated good energy into ripples sent outward. Over time, you realize this is not just a Complementary pairing—it stitches personal cultivation and social connection into one fabric, and the longer it lasts, the more momentum it gains.
resonance: ★ Stillness and motion give birth to each other: Nourishment's quiet power provides an inexhaustible source of living water for Dispersion's flow.
★ Cultivating within and without: one polishes the heart-mind internally, the other transmits influence externally—together they form a complete loop of growth.
conflict: ◆ Clashing rhythms of expression: Dispersion's divergent thinking tends to talk too much, running straight into Nourishment's bottom line of cautious speech.

◆ Mismatched pace of gathering and dispersing: Nourishment prefers steady progress and slow accumulation, while Dispersion always wants to break through and spread out—one feels stifled, the other feels dragged along.
advice: When facing an important project or interpersonal friction, first give yourself two days of quiet retreat to build your inner strength, then invite the other person to walk by the water or in an open space, letting the natural flow of air gently scatter the pent-up thoughts.

one_liner: Guard your tongue, draw lines in your heart, and sharing a life together is both nourishing and never overstepping.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is like a mountain, focused on inner nourishment and restraint—emphasizing cautious speech and moderate eating, drawing energy back inward. The Jie hexagram is like water, focused on establishing rules and channeling—stressing measure and regulation, and discussing virtue, building dikes for the flow of energy. When these two hexagrams meet, inner nourishment encounters outer control. Yi provides the depth and richness of life's foundation; Jie provides the scale and rhythm of daily operations. If Jie is too tight, Yi will feel stifled and develop internal wounds; if Yi is too loose, Jie's dike becomes a mere formality. The true chemistry lies in the mutual calibration between "bitter limitation cannot be maintained" and "seeking one's own sustenance": one reminds you not to turn life into asceticism, the other cautions you not to turn nourishment into reckless extravagance. The mountain stands firm, the water flows alive—rules are infused with human warmth, and nurturing both body and mind lands on solid ground.
resonance: ★ Guarded Speech and Measured Limits: Yi reminds you to talk less and listen more; Jie emphasizes rules and proportion. Naturally, the two know how to leave space in conversation—no overstepping, no interrupting.

★ Wise Nourishment: Yi governs inner care, Jie governs outer restraint. One knows what to eat to fortify the body; the other knows how much to eat to avoid harming the stomach. Their life rhythms are naturally in tune.
conflict: ◆ Rigid Rules: If Jie stubbornly clings to rigid frameworks, it can turn Yi's self-reliance into mechanical execution, leaving one feeling suffocated.
◆ Self-Indulgence: If Yi only cares about its own comfort and ignores Jie's measured restraint, over time life becomes lax and unbridled, shattering the original balance.
advice: Set aside half a day each week as a rule-free window for Yi to stretch freely; the rest of the time, follow Jie's rhythm. Define clear bottom lines, but don't choke each other.

one_liner: First nurture yourself to clarity, then meet sincerity with sincerity.
analysis: The Yi hexagram is like a steady mountain, teaching us to root inward and mind what we take in and what we say. Zhongfu (Inner Truth) is like a clear breeze over a lake — open, transparent, trusting without reservation. Together they form a sober arrangement: 'establish yourself first, then trade hearts.' Yi's restraint gives Zhongfu's candor a safety net, so true feelings don't burn out as inner friction. Zhongfu's warmth, in turn, opens a window in Yi's solitary practice, keeping self-nurturing from becoming self-isolation. One makes daily life solid and rhythmic; the other keeps the relationship clean and grounded. The mountain doesn't repel the wind, and the wind doesn't shake the mountain — the energy finds its most comfortable flow between 'holding the line' and 'opening up.'
resonance: ★ Only by nurturing yourself can you truly help others: Yi's self-sufficiency keeps Zhongfu's giving from becoming an exhausting bid for approval — together they learn to fill their own cups before pouring into each other.
★ Transparency dissolves suspicion: Zhongfu's sincerity, trusted even by pigs and fish, breaks through Yi's habitual armor of defense, trading straightforward honesty for enduring reassurance.
conflict: ◆ Restraint collides with overflow: Yi values careful speech and measured consumption; when Zhongfu surges with emotion, everything pours out — and Yi may feel flooded, drained by the other's fullness.

◆ Self-cultivation collides with outward reach: Yi tends to close the door and settle within, while Zhongfu longs to send kindness outward and connect; when rhythms slip, they can feel like they're not on the same channel.
advice: Create a 'heart-buffer period': before Zhongfu pours out its heart, pause for three seconds and ask if you're crossing a line; when the Yi side feels suffocated, take the initiative to share a small piece of daily life — don't let silence stew into estrangement.

one_liner: One stores up the strength, the other hits the brakes—together they live as steady as an ancient tree's roots.
analysis: Yi is thunder hidden beneath the mountain—it teaches you to swallow your energy, speak with care, eat with restraint, and focus on building strength within. Xiao Guo is thunder atop the mountain—it teaches you to leave room in every move, prefer flying low to climbing high, and keep yourself reined in when reaching outward. Together, these two hexagrams are the perfect partners: inner cultivation and outer restraint. One tells you not to waste words or energy, so your foundation grows deep; the other reminds you to take smaller steps and keep your posture low. When challenges arise, Yi steadies the base and plans carefully, while Xiao Guo dodges the sharp edges and picks the safest route. Neither likes grand gestures; they win through steady, long-lasting flow. In terms of energy, one stores, the other restrains—combine them, and you get a classic 'steady progress through balance' duo. As long as they don't overdo the nurturing into isolation, or overdo humility into spinelessness, and keep a good balance between contraction and expansion, this bond will only grow richer and more solid.
resonance: ★ Conserving Strength: They both know to save their energy for what truly matters, never blindly following the crowd and draining themselves.
★ Low-Flying Pragmatism: One emphasizes self-reliance, the other advocates 'down rather than up'—both stay rooted in reality and don't peddle pipe dreams.
conflict: ◆ Over-Restraint: When Yi's careful speech and frugal habits meet Xiao Guo's excessive deference, both tend to bottle things up and communication becomes a game of charades.
◆ Limited Scope: One focuses only on self-sufficiency, the other seeks only to avoid mistakes—when a big breakthrough is needed, they're liable to stumble together.
advice: Set a monthly heart-to-heart session to voice pent-up worries directly. For major decisions, decide in advance who will be the final decision-maker; the other serves as a risk monitor. Don't defer to each other and let the moment slip away.

relationship_name: Nourish the Right, Preserve the Achievement
one_liner: When success comes, don't let it go to your head. Watch your words, steady your spirit, and the good days will keep flowing gently.
analysis: After Completion is water over fire—a matter already brought to great success, yet the judgment warns plainly: 'Good fortune at first, disorder at the end.' It's like a pot of rich soup just finished simmering; if the heat rises even slightly, the bottom burns. Nourishment, on the other hand, is thunder hidden beneath the mountain, valuing 'caution in speech and moderation in eating and drinking'—the craft of a slow, low flame. When these two hexagrams come together, it's a sprint period meeting a recovery period. After Completion's sharp energy and achievements need Nourishment's restraint as a foundation; Nourishment's quiet cultivation finds its footing in After Completion's fullness. Mountain steady, water flowing; thunder hidden, fire bright. One teaches you not to overturn after your accomplishments; the other teaches you to extend your blessings through everyday moderation. This is no thunderous clash but a Kindred bond that slow-simmers the brightest moments into a steady, lasting stream.
resonance: ★ A Kindred vigilance for nipping trouble in the bud: After Completion fears the final unraveling, Nourishment stresses careful words. Both of you are naturally sensitive to risk, habitually keeping an umbrella ready on a sunny day.
★ A nourishing steadiness: one knows how to control the heat so nothing scorches, the other knows how to temper desire and keep life grounded. Everyday time together is like a slow-brewed tonic soup.
conflict: ◆ A tug-of-war over pace: After Completion likes to seize the result in one decisive push; Nourishment prefers to build roots slowly and methodically. One finds the other sluggish, the other finds the first impulsive.

◆ A temperature gap in expressing emotions: After Completion's readiness to anticipate problems can turn into anxious nagging, while Nourishment's careful speech can harden into a cold-war silence. When differences come up, one pours out the bitterness, the other swallows it down.
advice: When anxiety arises, the After Completion side should first write three concrete contingency plans; the Nourishment side should reply with the most peaceful sentence they can find. Trade vigilance and silence for a clear, doable action list.

one_liner: One keeps a tight rein on words and steadies the foundation; the other sees the water clearly and feels the riverbed — no need to rush, and no room for chaos.
analysis: The Yi hexagram (Nourishment) is a mountain enveloping thunder — it is about drawing inward and nurturing, like pressing the brake on life, reminding people to watch their words, moderate their consumption, and conserve strength to take root. The Wei Ji hexagram (Before Completion) is fire floating above water — things are still halfway; fire nature surges upward, water nature flows downward, so it urgently needs to find its proper position and stop thrashing about. When these two hexagrams come together, it is exactly a steadying star meeting a pathfinder. Yi's steadiness can hold down Wei Ji's restlessness, while Wei Ji's sense of incompleteness pushes Yi to step out of its comfort zone. You don't need to rush to bring things to completion; instead, it is better to slow the pace: first use Yi's discipline to build a solid foundation, then use Wei Ji's sharp perception to test the boundaries. This pairing does not chase instant harmony; rather, it is like slow-simmering soup — patience and time turn the unfinished into just right.
resonance: ★ Guarded Words and Sharp Discernment: Yi teaches us to keep quiet and nourish the breath; Wei Ji teaches us to open our eyes and distinguish things — one draws in, the other reaches out, perfectly complementary.
★ Slow Simmer Gets It Done: Neither advocates brute force; one relies on inner nourishment and stored energy, the other on trial and error to find the position — together they advance steadily.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Mismatch: Yi is used to waiting until the timing is ripe before moving, while Wei Ji always fears falling behind and wants to cross the river immediately — they can easily find each other procrastinating.

◆ Clashing Standards: Yi values inner discipline and restraint; Wei Ji values outer adaptability and trial and error. When it comes to concrete matters, one wants to hold the line, the other wants to improvise.
advice: Set aside a fixed half-day each week for offline quiet time. Don't discuss progress; only review your methods. Straighten out Wei Ji's chaos with Yi's discipline before taking action.

one_liner: Two ceiling-carriers together—don't tell each other to lie flat; being each other's load-bearing wall is the most solid move.
analysis: Great Preponderance is, by nature, the hexagram for extraordinary times—it speaks of a ridgepole pressed to the point of bending but still having to hold. When two Great Preponderances collide, it's like two similarly curved load-bearing beams propping each other up. You know all too well that suffocating feeling of 'the lake submerging the wood.' Outsiders see you as stubborn and clannish; only the other person knows that you're actually shouldering lightning for the sake of ordinary life. The Image says: 'Standing alone, without fear; retiring from the world, without regret.' When you two come together, you simply turn 'retiring from the world' into a jointly built safe harbor. Neither of you needs the other to say 'just lighten up'—what you want is to stand shoulder to shoulder and straighten the bent spine of life. This relationship doesn't run on sweet talk; it runs on having each other's back in a crisis. But double the lonely courage can also lock you both in a pressure chamber, so remember occasionally to push open the doors and windows and let some air through.
resonance: ★ Same Lake-Water Frequency: You've both lived through the suffocating period of being submerged by reality, so without a word you understand that clenched-teeth exhaustion of just holding on.
★ Bending Beams, Mutual Support: Under the overwhelming weight of life, you both instinctively chose to bend rather than break, becoming each other's backup pillars.
conflict: ◆ Island Effect: Two people habitually 'retiring from the world without regret' tend to build their own closed-loop world, mistaking genuine outside concern for intrusion.
◆ Excessive Rigidity: Both are used to carrying things alone, so when a disagreement arises, neither wants to be the first to yield, and small matters easily simmer into emotional attrition.
advice: Once a month, completely set aside your load-bearing roles and go do something utterly pointless with no KPIs—let your taut nerves catch some breeze.

one_liner: One's a beam that dares to hold up a falling sky; the other's water that wades through over-the-head floods. Together, they're the go-to cure for any dead end.
analysis: Great Exceeding is 'the lake submerges the tree' — the beams groan under the water's weight, yet are forced to summon a fierce resolve to stand independent and unafraid. The Abysmal is 'water coming again and again' — wave after wave, testing the tenacity of a heart that stays clear and steadfast. When these two hexagrams meet, it's less an idle romance and more a life-and-death partnership forged in crisis. Great Exceeding makes the critical calls — even if the whole structure tilts, it will tough it out. The Abysmal provides the safety net in long, low valleys, steadying the ground with day-after-day practice and repeated teaching. Lake and water share the same source: Great Exceeding charges the water into high-pressure potential, and the Abysmal turns it into a hidden current that can bore through stone. When 'standing alone without fear' meets 'constant practice of virtue,' one breaks the deadlock, the other handles the aftermath. They don't chase surface calm; instead, amid pressure and hidden currents, they grind out a rough-edged kinship: you take the bridge across the cliff, and I'll teach you to breathe in the rapids. This relationship keeps no idle bystanders — only those who are serious count.
resonance: ★ Pressure-Paired Frequency: Both are used to working under high pressure, unafraid of losing control, and can quickly sync their rhythm in a crisis
★ Resilient Complementarity: Great Exceeding's rigid frame pairs with the Abysmal's water-smooth flexibility, taking apart obstacles with a blend of firmness and grace
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Great Exceeding tends to break through in one sustained assault, while the Abysmal prefers to endure drop by drop over time — so they can easily pull against each other on pace
◆ Emotional Drain: Great Exceeding can come off as aloof and headstrong, while the Abysmal tends to sink its feelings to the bottom without communicating — a cold standoff can lock them into gridlock
advice: Before making decisions, sync your watches: the Great Exceeding side sets the direction and steps on the gas; the Abysmal side maps the route and works the brakes. Write down clear rules for when to push and when to steady — don't rely on unspoken guesswork.

one_liner: You bear the crushing weight below; I shine the light and show the way above—this duo is built to crack the toughest nuts.
analysis: The Preponderance of the Great is 'the lake drowns the wood'—water overwhelms timber, bending the ridgepole. Under extreme pressure, people often choose to 'stand alone without fear,' habitually swallowing everything and bearing it in silence. Li, by contrast, is 'the doubling of brightness'—fire stacked on fire, born to radiate light and heat, illuminating all directions, living through attachment and continuity. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like a load-bearing pillar in a dark room encountering a searchlight that never goes out. Great Preponderance's depth and solitary courage can easily become blind spots of self-consuming endurance; Li's clarity and outward energy are precisely what can bring those hidden pressures into the open. Li doesn't take on the weight for Great Preponderance, but it offers a clear perspective and a steady supply of emotional fuel. Great Preponderance, in turn, doesn't borrow Li's shine—its solid load-bearing strength keeps Li's flame from drifting off into empty air. Water and fire seem to oppose each other, but in truth one settles and the other rises, turning 'grim endurance' into 'breaking through'—forging a radiant, practical wisdom under immense pressure.
resonance: ★ Guiding without adding trouble: Li's firelight precisely reveals the load limit of Great Preponderance's beam—no blind commands, just direction, so the one bearing it knows exactly where to channel their strength.

★ Holding the ground without hype: the deep foundation of Great Preponderance's lake-wood can catch Li's outward-spreading impulse, providing solid fuel for the glow, so passion doesn't burn out and scatter.
conflict: ◆ Quiet resentment meets flamboyance: Great Preponderance is used to sinking emotions into a deep pool to digest alone, while Li likes to lay everything out and dissect it openly—making Great Preponderance feel overexposed and irritated.

◆ Quick fire on wet wood: Li pursues clarity and swift action, but Great Preponderance is by nature heavy, wet timber. Forcing a fast tempo to ignite it only produces choking smoke and strains the relationship.
advice: Set a rule: 'Light the lamp before moving the beam.' Li, don't rush to offer advice—first provide emotional support. Great Preponderance, don't tough it out alone—open up about the pressure points and work out solutions together.

one_liner: On the surface, they chat and laugh easily, but one is silently bearing pressure while the other is quietly opening their heart.
analysis: The Great Exceeding is a lake pressing on withered wood: the ridgepole is about to bend, yet it chooses to stand alone and unafraid—this is a lone warrior's courage in an uphill battle. Influence is a mountain holding a gentle lake: it practices emptying itself to receive others, opening the heart to catch every wave of emotion. Because both have the same Lake trigram above them, they warm up quickly in conversation and laughter at first. But on closer acquaintance, their cores prove very different: The Great Exceeding instinctively takes everything onto its shoulders—a doer with thorns; Influence instinctively opens the heart—a feeler with subtlety. This pair is like simmering a soft soup in a pressure cooker: The Great Exceeding's boldness gives Influence the bottom line to break through, and Influence's tenderness untangles The Great Exceeding's knotted nerves. The key is for The Great Exceeding to stop being the lone hero, and for Influence to stop always yielding. When hard endurance is kneaded together with deep receptivity, the too-rigid ridgepole can soak into flexibility, and the empty, floating resonance gains solid substance.
resonance: ★ Laughter opens the ice easily: Sharing the Lake trigram above, once the conversation gets going, they quickly become familiar, and in social settings they naturally generate a warm, effortless rapport.

★ Strength and softness working together can achieve things: The Great Exceeding's breaking-through boldness plus Influence's subtle sensitivity means that when trouble hits, one dares to make the call and the other knows how to back it up.
conflict: ◆ Tough endurance collides with the need for resonance: The Great Exceeding is used to gritting its teeth and carrying on alone, while Influence craves deep emotional exchange—so each can feel the other is either impervious or overly dramatic.

◆ Tension meets a slower tempo: The Great Exceeding pushes for efficient, forward-moving action, while Influence values a kind of open-hearted, gradual response—when rhythms are off, they end up tripping each other.
advice: When pressure builds, The Great Exceeding shouldn't shut the door and work alone—set aside two hours a week just to listen to Influence slowly pour out its heart. And Influence shouldn't only empathize—take the initiative to give The Great Exceeding's decisions one practical, actionable suggestion.

one_liner: One dares to flip the table to smash the impasse; the other holds the line and backstops the fall. Together they're a golden duo—steady, with a hidden edge.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is like lake water surging over a wooden bridge: it teaches courage to break through alone in crises, yet warns that overt rigidity snaps easily. Duration is like thunder and wind reinforcing each other: it stresses answering all changes with constancy and deepening one's roots. Both hexagrams have Wind as the lower trigram, so at their core they understand how to go with the flow and adapt flexibly; but with Lake above one and Thunder above the other, one is always set on overturning the status quo, while the other clings to the old ways. In partnership, The Great Preponderance can split open the deadlock and bring vital life, while Duration can simmer change into a durable norm. The key is not to mistake The Great Preponderance's drive for recklessness, nor Duration's persistence for rigidity—find the rhythm between 'breaking' and 'holding.'
resonance: ★ Roots Share the Wind: Both have Wind below, so each instinctively bends and detours rather than fighting head-on, skilled at using leverage.
★ Heading Out Together: Both hexagram texts urge 'It furthers one to have somewhere to go'—true doers who, once they know the direction, dare to step.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned Rhythms: The Great Preponderance's itch for change can read as impatience, while Duration's emphasis on stability can seem sluggish—when the beats don't match, tension pulls them apart.

◆ Clashing Principles: The Great Preponderance champions 'standing alone without fear' and daring to overturn convention; Duration advocates 'standing firm without changing direction' and clinging to principles. When tough choices arise, dispute is likely.
advice: When a major decision arrives, have The Great Preponderance toss out three aggressive options, then let Duration choose the steadiest to put into practice; review once a month and fine-tune the tempo.

relationship_name: Bearing Pressure, Knowing When to Stop
one_liner: You're the one who fights like hell through the storm, and I'm the one who hits the brakes at the cliff's edge — together we're life's best shock absorber.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is the lake flooding the wood — water covers the treetops, the pressure immense, yet it insists on standing independent and fearless, pushing forward against the bending ridgepole. Retreat is the mountain under heaven — the sky high and the mountain far away; it knows to keep its distance from petty people without hostility, yet with dignity, and to withdraw when the time comes. When these two meet, one is like a pressure cooker that insists on popping its own lid, the other a thermostat that silently turns down the flame. The Great Preponderance's rash courage can easily burn itself dry; Retreat's timely exit is exactly what offers relief. But if Retreat's over-avoidance lacks the tenacity of Great Preponderance, it can easily become an ostrich mentality. When unlike hexagrams meet, it's not about one transforming the other — it's about finding the rhythm between advance and retreat: when the storm hits, Great Preponderance holds the line; before the situation turns chaotic, Retreat has already laid the escape route. The extremity of lake water is diluted by the wide openness of heaven and mountain, giving rise to a clarity that dares to risk everything yet also knows how to stay alive.
resonance: ★ Carry the load without inner friction: Great Preponderance dares to tough it out when faced with a tough pass; Retreat knows when to pull out of a rotten situation. Both believe in taking what can be taken and leaving what can't — never dragging things out.

★ A private spiritual plot: Great Preponderance retreats from the world without gloom; Retreat keeps petty people at a distance with dignity. At their core, both deeply value personal boundaries and never waste energy on meaningless socializing.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm of action: Great Preponderance is used to charging into crises, while Retreat always wants to pull out early to avoid danger. One finds the other too withdrawn; the other finds the one too rash.

◆ Different ways of handling emotions: Great Preponderance tends to go all-in and fight to the finish, while Retreat prefers to cool things down and draw clear lines. When communicating, one is a powder keg, the other an ice cellar.
advice: Each time a decision is needed, Great Preponderance is in charge of assessing the worst consequences it can bear, and Retreat is in charge of drawing the red line for when retreat is mandatory. Both act according to that shared understanding, never acting on impulse or giving in to avoidance.

one_liner: You can bear a thousand-pound burden, and I'll make the thunder crack even louder—together, we handle what nobody else can.
analysis: Great Preponderance is the bearer of pressure in the image of 'Lake over Wood'—like a load-bearing beam soaked through with water, silent on the outside but unyielding within. Great Power is the action-taker of 'Thunder over Heaven'—bursting with energy but equipped with its own brake, and committed to using force only in the right direction. When they come together, one handles the underlying support and resistance, the other expands the territory. Great Preponderance's 'standing alone without fear' provides a safety net for Great Power's headlong charges, while Great Power's firm, vigorous momentum is exactly what splits open the dull impasses that Great Preponderance tends to sink into. Yet both share the word 'Great,' and their energy can easily overload. Without moderation, it becomes stubborn endurance clashing with hard-headed toughness. The key is for Great Preponderance to learn to use leverage to break the deadlock, and for Great Power to understand how to apply and release force with measure. Only then can they achieve success.
resonance: ★ The Complementary dynamic of backing up and charging forward: Great Preponderance keeps the base steady in deep waters without collapsing; Great Power acts with swift thunder in the open to break deadlocks. In headwinds, one holds the fort, the other clears the path.

★ The dovetailing of resilience and rules: Great Power's 'not stepping where propriety forbids' draws a red line for Great Preponderance's unconventional tactics; Great Preponderance's 'withdrawing from the world without regret' catches the emotional backlash when Great Power hits a wall.
conflict: ◆ Energy stacking easily overloads: both are 'great' in scope. Great Preponderance habitually endures to the point of exhausting itself, while Great Power charges without enough braking. Together, they can blow small frictions into hard battles.

◆ Rhythm misalignment breeds discord: Great Preponderance tends to silently absorb pressure and store strength; Great Power is used to moving directly and decisively. One finds the other too dull, the other finds the other too rash—communication often feels out of synch.
advice: When key decisions arise, Great Power should first curb its impulse and let Great Preponderance lay out the pressure points and hidden risks in full. Then Great Preponderance sets an absolute 'no-touch' bottom line for action. Both advance within that line, with no last-minute escalations.

one_liner: You shoulder a thousand-pound load in the shadows; I stride into the spotlight. Together, we turn a deadlock into an open road.
analysis: Great Preponderance is 'the lake that drowns the wood' — water floods the treetops and the structure groans under pressure; its way is to hold fast alone at the extreme, never drifting with the current. Progress is 'light rising over the earth' — the sun breaks through the dawn and climbs ever higher; it asks you to lay your talents bare in the light and let them be recognized. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like a lone workhorse grinding over a plan at midnight, colliding with a pathfinder who strides into the pitch meeting the next morning. The weight and inwardness of Great Preponderance exactly cradle the lightness and visibility of Progress; the brightness and motion of Progress, in turn, shine a way out of the suffocating impasse that Great Preponderance has been shouldering alone. But lake water is cold and yin, and fire is dry and volatile — the tempos easily slip: one swallows everything, the other wants to announce it to the world. If they can wear each other in, Great Preponderance's resilience lays a bulletproof floor beneath Progress's ascent, and Progress's light lifts the lonely armor of 'stand alone, fear nothing' off Great Preponderance's back.
resonance: ★ The Burden-Bearer Meets the Lamp-Lighter: Great Preponderance is used to silently swallowing heavy loads; Progress is born to brighten the darkest corners. One inward, one outward, they dissolve the mental wear-and-tear of stubborn solo endurance.

★ Deadlock-Breaking Partnership: Progress's step-by-step rise needs a solid undercarriage, and Great Preponderance's extreme stress-bearing power when the ridgepole bends is precisely what can carry Progress through its most dangerous upward phase.
conflict: ◆ Out-of-Sync Frequencies: Great Preponderance prefers the cool retreat of 'no vexation in seclusion'; Progress craves the warm embrace of 'three audiences in one day.' One wants to hide and recharge; the other wants to hit the stage and grab the spotlight now.

◆ Aura Clash: Great Preponderance's lake water is dark, damp, and leaden; Progress's fire is dry, scorching, and rising. Keep too much company and one side feels suffocated by gloom, while the other gets written off as frantic and pushy.
advice: When disagreement hits, Great Preponderance, don't just go silent and disappear — leave a visible progress bar on the table. And Progress, don't yank your partner onstage; learn to hand over a warm cup of water from the wings. Turn 'solo hauling' into 'joint venture.'

one_liner: You charge ahead with bold, sweeping moves, and I'll stay in the shadows to back you up and handle whatever needs handling.
analysis: Great Preponderance is the peril of 'the lake flooding over the wood.' The Judgment says plainly, 'the ridgepole bends,' yet still 'it furthers one to undertake something' — the lone courage that moves ahead even when the weight is known. Darkening of the Light, by contrast, is the hidden time of 'brightness entering the earth.' Its Image speaks of 'veiling the light to make it shine' — the art of tucking your edge into the soil and enduring the long night. When these two meet, it's a dialogue between 'high-voltage charge' and 'quiet accumulation.' The lake's overflow needs thick earth to absorb it; otherwise, Great Preponderance's 'excess' becomes blind, stubborn endurance. And Darkening of the Light's 'darkness,' with no one to break the spell, sinks into a stagnant pool. Great Preponderance dares to stand alone under heavy pressure — just the force to cleave an escape route for Darkening of the Light. Darkening of the Light knows how to stay centered and bide its time, and can reach out to catch the ridgepole just before it snaps. It's not about who shines brighter; it's about one who breaks through and one who holds the line.
resonance: ★ Mutually supported in adversity: Great Preponderance holds firm in the storm; Darkening of the Light gathers strength in the valley. Together, no matter how rough the crossing, they wade through.

★ Complementary in motion and stillness: the surging lake needs thick earth to settle and contain it. One breaks the deadlock and opens the way; the other anchors the rear and guards the ground. Their rhythms mesh perfectly.
conflict: ◆ The tug of war between breaking through and hiding one's talent: Great Preponderance always wants to lay things on the table and confront directly, while Darkening of the Light insists the timing is not ripe and one should first lie low. They tend to clash over 'act now or wait.'

◆ The stacking of pressure and internal drain: Great Preponderance can push itself to the edge of the 'bending ridgepole' and still not call a stop. Darkening of the Light habitually swallows its grievances. Neither is willing to show weakness, so hidden wounds can fester.
advice: Set a clear rhythm of 'alternating light and shadow': before Great Preponderance charges, let Darkening of the Light draw the safety lines; Darkening of the Light should also not keep everything inside — lay out the key risks openly, and when it's time to show the blade, don't drag your feet.

one_liner: One takes the thunder and breaks the deadlock outside; the other tends the fire and simmers the porridge at home — just right for building a life together.
analysis: The hexagram of the Preponderance of the Great is an image of "the lake submerging the wood" — an omen of bearing pressure. It calls for standing firm on your own in extraordinary times, daring to be the one who breaks a deadlock, and charging ahead even when "the ridgepole sags." The Family hexagram, by contrast, is a warm image of "wind issuing from fire," valuing order and constancy in the salt-and-oil details of daily life. Put these two together, and you have a sharp knife slipped into a soft cork sheath. The edge and high pressure of the Preponderance of the Great urgently need the Family's hearth-smoke as a safety net, or it will snap; and the Family's steady routine also needs the boundary-breaking boldness of the Preponderance to rip open the dull, repetitive days. These two are not about one reshaping the other; rather, one is responsible for outward expansion, the other for inward steadiness. The Preponderance gives the Family a sense of security and freshness; the Family gives the Preponderance a sheltered harbor for recovery. This combination doesn't chase daily romance, but when the storm arrives, one holds up the umbrella while the other lights the lamp.
resonance: ★ Breaking through with a safety net: The Preponderance of the Great dares to charge forward because it knows someone at home is holding down the fort — no fear of losing it all.
★ Constancy generating new spark: When the Family's rules are injected with a pinch of adventurous spirit from the Preponderance, life won't simmer down into a stagnant pool.
conflict: ◆ Tempo mismatch: The Preponderance of the Great finds the Family too slow; the Family finds the Preponderance too hasty — one gets irritated, the other gets rattled.
◆ Mixed signals: The Preponderance is used to silently toughing it out without complaint, while the Family thrives on daily communication and small feedback — over time, misunderstandings pile up.
advice: When the Preponderance comes home from carrying the load outside, don't put on a sour face. When the Family is within, don't just lecture — give a genuine hug. Swap "words with substance" for "one warm deed."

one_liner: You handle the relentless grind and the heavy lifting; I handle poking holes and breaking deadlocks. We may not look like a match, but we're actually perfect together.
analysis: Great Preponderance is 'the lake submerges the wood' — the ridgepole bends but doesn't break, embodying a solitary courage that stands unafraid and bears pressure. Opposition is 'fire above, lake below' — fire and water turn away from each other, emphasizing the lucid clarity and boundary of 'unite through difference.' When the two meet, the heaviness of Great Preponderance and the aloofness of Opposition at first seem incompatible: Great Preponderance is used to shouldering everything alone, while Opposition instinctively keeps distance and magnifies differences. But it is precisely Opposition's 'small matters bring good fortune' and its seeking of common ground despite differences that can precisely dissolve Great Preponderance's tendency to 'break when too rigid.' Great Preponderance supplies a steadying core like an anchor in the sea; Opposition supplies a perspective that flexibly dismantles problems. When Great Preponderance is pushed to the limit by crushing pressure, Opposition doesn't urge compromise — it helps cut the vast whole into manageable pieces, supporting that solitude with the wisdom of 'harmony without uniformity.' This is not a mushy Complementary bond, but a hardcore partnership of two independent people who can shoulder burdens side by side.
resonance: ★ A safety net within a sense of boundaries: Opposition's 'fire above, lake below' instinctively knows the right measure. It never floods Great Preponderance with excessive emotion, but instead leaves breathing room when the other is stubbornly holding on, silently catching the pressure with the wisdom of 'unite through difference.'

★ Kindred: small moves break the deadlock. Great Preponderance's 'favorable to have somewhere to go' tends to overexert; Opposition's 'small matters bring good fortune' is a reminder to break down grand goals into concrete steps. One takes the skeleton, the other the details — cooperation feels remarkably smooth.
conflict: ◆ Lone courage meets a cool gaze: Great Preponderance, with its 'standing alone without fear,' is used to fighting solo. When it meets Opposition's instinctive aloofness, it easily misreads the other's rational observation as cold indifference, breeding resentment.

◆ Pressure creates misalignment: Great Preponderance pursues the extreme load-bearing of a 'bending ridgepole,' while Opposition leans toward going with the flow and seeking common ground. In a crisis, one wants to brace and fight to the end, the other wants to retreat flexibly — their rhythms easily clash.
advice: Great Preponderance, don't always bear everything silently alone. When you're stuck, take the initiative to break the hard problem into small concrete tasks and pass them over. And Opposition, don't just stand there nitpicking — break the ice with 'I know this isn't easy for you,' then offer solutions that accommodate the differences.

one_liner: You clear the mines and blaze the trail; I cover the rear and patch the gaps. Don't rush blindly—play it steady and win.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is the image of a lake flooding over the treetops: a headlong, no-holds-barred surge. The ridgepole strains but never breaks, and its mandate is to press forward with purpose. Obstruction, in contrast, is water on the mountain—a perilous peak struck by a cold stream, where every step is a struggle, leaving only the turn toward inner discipline and self-cultivation. When the two come together, it's like a contest between accelerator and brake: The Great Preponderance is always ready to floor the pedal and smash through the impasse, while Obstruction instinctively pulls the handbrake to check the road. But here's the wonder: the recklessness of the Great Preponderance is just what splits open the deadlock that Obstruction faces, and Obstruction's inner restraint can catch the Great Preponderance before it rolls the vehicle. Lake and water share the same source—one spills outward to spread momentum, the other cuts deeper to refine its flow. Their collision doesn't cancel out; it becomes a rhythm of daring to go and daring to stop.
resonance: ★ Same Water Vein: Lake and stream share a common source—one spreads across the lowlands to build momentum, the other condenses into a current on the heights. At their core, both understand the deep logic of adapting to circumstances.

★ Thriving in Peril: The Great Preponderance, faced with a bending ridgepole, still dares to advance; Obstruction, faced with a mountain barrier, knows to cultivate virtue. Neither shirks the real difficulty—they differ only in approach: the one hard-driving, the other gentle and yielding.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned Rhythm: The Great Preponderance finds Obstruction too dawdling and wants to flip the table and charge right now; Obstruction finds The Great Preponderance too reckless, terrified that one misstep loses the entire game.

◆ Energy Tug-of-War: The expansionist urge of Lake-over-Wood keeps draining the reservoir of Water-on-the-Mountain. One strains to pour resources outward, the other fights to pull in its edge—this can easily spiral into internal attrition.
advice: When disagreement arises, let The Great Preponderance pause for three minutes so Obstruction can finish the risk assessment; Obstruction should proactively draw a safety line under which The Great Preponderance may experiment. Don't keep wresting between flooring the gas and yanking the handbrake.

one_liner: Grit through it first, then let go — the matter unravels on its own.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is like a load-bearing beam submerged by marsh water, symbolizing someone who grits their teeth and endures under extreme overload; Deliverance, by contrast, is the sky clearing after thunder and rain, advocating the release of attachments and the pardoning of the past. When the two meet, it resembles a person who always toughs it out encountering a friend who knows when to ease up. The Great Preponderance's "standing alone without fear" needs Deliverance's "forgiving faults and pardoning misdeeds" to soften its sharp edges, or it will snap; while Deliverance's open-mindedness, without the Great Preponderance's resilience as its foundation, can drift into shallowness. This pairing works especially well in crisis management — first break the deadlock with the boldness of the Great Preponderance, then handle the aftermath with the wisdom of Deliverance. In everyday life, though, watch for a rhythm mismatch between "being exacting" and "going with the flow."
resonance: ★ Heavy pressure finally finds an exit: the Great Preponderance's burden catches its breath in Deliverance's release.
★ Breaking a deadlock needs room to spare: Deliverance's tolerance can dissolve the Great Preponderance's inclination toward ruthless finality.
conflict: ◆ Dogged persistence meets easygoing grace: the Great Preponderance's stubbornness may be seen by Deliverance's casualness as lacking a deeper understanding.
◆ Letting go meets with intensity: Deliverance's laid-back attitude can trigger the Great Preponderance's anxiety about responsibility.
advice: When you hit an impasse, first hold your ground for three days, then proactively invite the other person to tea and keep the conversation to light, inconsequential topics.

one_liner: One keeps adding weight and carrying the load, the other is busy letting go and clearing the deck; together they land right on the balance point.
analysis: Great Preponderance is the pressurized image of 'the lake drowning the wood'—wood submerged, spine bending, demanding the resolve to 'stand alone without fear' and take on the burden. Decrease, by contrast, is the contracting pattern of 'a mountain over the lake'—mountain pressing on water, teaching one to 'curb anger and cut desire,' slicing away excess wants and emotions in one stroke. When these two hexagrams come together, it’s like a high-revving engine paired with a precision pressure-relief valve. Great Preponderance handles the critical moments—holding firm under pressure and breaking open a path forward—while Decrease works quietly alongside, subtracting, pruning away needless attachments and internal friction. The lake water in these two hexagrams sits above in one and below in the other, creating a perfect bite between outward expansion and inward holding. Without Great Preponderance’s sense of duty, Decrease can easily slip into lofty detachment; without Decrease’s restraint, Great Preponderance will eventually be crushed by its own ambition. Together they don’t pull each other apart—they dynamically calibrate each other’s excesses and shortfalls.
resonance: ★ Same Origin in Lake Water: both hexagrams carry the lake image, showing that at the root they both understand forbearance and sedimentation. One uses surging water to bear pressure, the other uses still water to nurture the heart—so in conversation they catch each other’s emotional weight without effort.

★ Minimalist Rapport: Great Preponderance prizes the crispness of 'it is advantageous to have somewhere to go'; Decrease values the plain simplicity of 'two bowls may be used for sacrifice.' Both detest dragging things out; once the direction is clear, they cut straight to the core.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch in Advance and Retreat: Great Preponderance is used to piling on more in a crisis and toughing it out; Decrease advocates subtracting first thing. One is anxious to charge ahead, the other is stomping the brakes—at key points they’ll argue over whether to go or fall back.

◆ Emotional Handling Clash: Great Preponderance, 'standing alone without fear,' is used to grinding through things alone; Decrease, 'curbing anger and repressing desire,' demands instant suppression of temper. The former finds the latter too cold; the latter finds the former too bottled-up. Small issues can easily harden into silent warfare.
advice: When disputes arise, Great Preponderance shouldn’t rush to push back—split off some of the burden so Decrease can do its subtraction. And Decrease shouldn’t be all about restraint—give Great Preponderance’s momentum a release valve when the timing is right. Agree to a weekly decluttering review: clear away surplus anxiety and keep only the core goals.

relationship_name: Wind and Lake in Mutual Support
one_liner: One withstands heavy pressure, the other adapts to change; as partners, they get twice the result with half the effort.
analysis: Great Preponderance is like a deep pool bearing weight; the noble one stands independent and unafraid. Increase is like a spring breeze turning to rain, shifting toward whatever is good. When the two meet, it is a collision of steadiness and agility: Great Preponderance provides the pressure-resistant foundation, while Increase infuses the vitality to adjust—together they open new ground amid shifting circumstances. But take note: Great Preponderance's stubbornness may hinder Increase's flexible pivots, and Increase's frequent changes may unbalance Great Preponderance. The key is to accept change with an independent heart and to steady the foundation with the wisdom of increase, forming a symbiotic rhythm of firmness and flexibility.
resonance: ★ Bearing Pressure, Advancing Together: Great Preponderance's resilience gives Increase a stable backbone for bold advance, allowing them to face challenges without retreat.
★ Change and Mutual Growth: Increase's flexible adjustments help Great Preponderance dissolve rigidity, and together they grow through course corrections.
conflict: ◆ Stubbornness vs. Volatility: Great Preponderance's fixed views may resist Increase's quick reversals, causing them to fall out of step.
◆ Pressure and Lightness: Great Preponderance's heavy load may weigh down Increase's light rhythm; the tension needs balancing.
advice: Once a month, set a 'pressure-release day': the Great Preponderance partner openly shares current difficulties, the Increase partner proposes fine-tuned adjustments, and together they optimize their pace of action.

one_liner: One silently shoulders the load without a word; the other beats the drum and divvies up the spoils.
analysis: This pairing is all about handling 'overload' — but their methods are polar opposites. In Great Preponderance, lake water swamps the wood — silent, stubborn endurance under crushing weight, valuing independence and fearlessness, refusing to let go even as the roof beam bends. In Breakthrough, the lake water hangs high above the heavens — a decisive release after the reservoir is full, proclaimed in the royal court, cutting cleanly where cutting is needed and sharing out benefits where sharing is needed. Together, they complete the full loop of crisis response: Great Preponderance holds the line in the shadows and keeps the foundation steady; Breakthrough sets the rules in the open and clears the blockage. Without Great Preponderance's steadiness, Breakthrough's decisiveness can easily become reckless thrashing; without Breakthrough's boldness, Great Preponderance's forbearance will eventually fester into internal injury. Both are the same overflowing lake water, but one takes root inward while the other opens the sluice outward. Together, they can withstand the pressure and still break the game wide open.
resonance: ★ Shared Pressure Frequency: Both are at the breaking point of resource or emotional overload, and instinctively understand that urgent feeling of barely being able to hold it together.
★ Complementary Breakthrough: One guards the fort, the other opens the floodgates — when crisis hits, they can seamlessly switch between shouldering the load and clearing the field.
conflict: ◆ Quiet vs. Loud: Great Preponderance tends to digest pressure alone and hates showing off, while Breakthrough insists on making public declarations and setting rules — they can easily take each other as too withdrawn or too dramatic.

◆ Keep vs. Share: Great Preponderance believes good things should be kept as ballast, while Breakthrough argues for sharing it all out quickly to win hearts — arguments over distribution can get fierce.
advice: When trouble strikes, let Great Preponderance hold the bottom line and steady the ship first; then Breakthrough follows up by listing options and sharing openly. Don't let silence stew into a cold war, and don't let decisiveness harden into autocracy.

relationship_name: The Lone Ridgepole and the Gathering Crowd
one_liner: One dares to take on a heaven-collapsing burden alone; the other always wants to get a group together to head off the unexpected.
analysis: The upper trigram of both hexagrams is the Lake (Dui), so outwardly both radiate openness and fluidity — but underneath, their foundations couldn't be more different. Great Exceeding is "the lake submerging the wood": water spreads over the roots, and a ridgepole bears weight to its absolute limit. Its ethos is "stand alone without fear" — a solitary hero who takes on the crisis single-handedly, preferring to bend rather than break his integrity. Gathering Together is "the lake above the earth": water gathers into hollows. Its ethos is "maintain weapons and guard against the unforeseen" — a community-minded steward who prepares for rainy days, relying on solidarity and rules to keep things steady. When these two come together, the chemistry is remarkable: the impulsive forward thrust of "it furthers one to undertake something" can immediately ignite Gathering Together's collective action, while Gathering Together's vigilance gives that dangerously bowed ridgepole just the shock absorber it needs. But the trouble lies here, too: Great Exceeding thinks Gathering Together is too slow and too attached to ritual; Gathering Together thinks Great Exceeding is too much of a lone wolf and doesn't take team safety seriously. Fortunately, both hexagrams point to taking the initiative to break the deadlock. As long as they set their sights on the same goal — one leading the charge, one keeping the rear stable — they can turn a gamble into a brilliant victory.
resonance: ★ A shared urge to break through: both Judgements point directly to "it furthers one to undertake something." Facing a standstill, neither is willing to just burn time; both carry a deep, hard-edged resolve to take action and get results.

★ A composed lucidity under pressure: Great Exceeding sees through the glitter of the world with "retiring from the world without vexation," while Gathering Together guards against the unforeseen before it arrives. Both keep a keen nose for risk, even in high-stress or high-spirited moments.
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war between lone-wolf charge and team support: Great Exceeding is used to going in alone and shouldering everything; Gathering Together insists on process, consensus, and collective defense. One is fast, the other steady — they can easily wear each other down.

◆ The friction between minimalist breakthrough and elaborate ritual: Great Exceeding believes in doing extraordinary things in extraordinary times, unconcerned with small conventions; Gathering Together values the ceremony of "the great sacrifice brings good fortune." To Great Exceeding, that feels like a wasteful drain of energy.
advice: When the fight turns tough, divide the roles clearly: Great Exceeding sets the strategy and leads the assault, while Gathering Together builds the team and prepares contingency plans. Don't try to direct each other on how to execute.

one_liner: You crack the impasse, I build the staircase—together we mesh like gears.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is like floodwater surging over a dike, forcing you to straighten your spine in crisis. The Pushing Upward is like spring mud lifting tender shoots, teaching you to grow, inch by inch, along the lay of the land. Both rest on the same lower trigram, Xun (Wind), and at their core they share the penetrating power of softness conquering hardness. But the wind of the Great Preponderance is taut with the weight of the lake, while the wind of the Pushing Upward rides the land’s rising pulse. When the Great Preponderance’s courage to break through collides with the Pushing Upward’s patience to accumulate, a strange and wonderful relay unfolds: the first dares to bridge a cliff, the second compacts the earth beneath the arch. This combination doesn’t dread a bleak start—only a change of course midway. As long as the direction holds, even the steepest slope can be climbed in a rising spiral.
resonance: ★ Shared Wind, Shared Qi: Beneath it all, both carry the pliancy of Xun (Wind)—they don’t meet obstacles head-on, but use deft leverage to dissolve resistance.
★ Growing Upward Together: One dares to raise a beam over ruins, the other banks soil under the beam—both point toward upward breakthrough.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: The Great Preponderance is used to dismantling old arrangements with lightning speed, while the Pushing Upward favors slow cooking over a low flame—it’s easy for them to tug at each other’s pace.

◆ Strategy Clash: The Great Preponderance likes a single-point assault to crack the encirclement, while the Pushing Upward focuses on multiple roots to secure the base—their working paths often grind against each other.
advice: When stuck, let the Great Preponderance person tear open a breach, then have the Pushing Upward person lay down a cushion right behind—so you avoid losing ground after the breakthrough or freezing up during accumulation.

relationship_name: Full and Withered, Reflecting Each Other
one_liner: You're hauling an overloaded burden and toughing it out; I'm crouched over a dried-up well and refusing to give up. When two hardheads collide, nobody tries to make the other bow.
analysis: The Great Exceeding is the image of lake water rising over the wood — the ridgepole bends but refuses to break. The Oppression is the image of the lake leaking at the bottom — resources run dry, yet the will holds firm. Their upper trigrams are both Lake (Dui), so on the surface both like to project an easy-going, carefree air. But inside, one is suffocated by too much, the other exhausted by too little. When the two meet, the bold, go-for-broke energy of Great Exceeding can inject the breakthrough bloodlust into a person stuck in a deadlock; and the silent resilience of The Oppression — that determination to fulfill one's resolve even when fate is dire — reminds Great Exceeding not to just keep bearing the load, but to learn how to leave blank space and gather strength. This is not a light, casual partnership; it's two souls probing the edge of their limits, calibrating each other: one learns to release the flood, the other learns to dig a well, and together they transmute overload and scarcity into a shared bedrock of confidence.
resonance: ★ Never bending in extremity: both of you have a stubborn streak that refuses to accept fate. Even when the beam bends and the well goes dry, you won't make easy compromises.

★ Silent mutual understanding: on the surface, the Lake trigram loves to smile and chat, but actually both Great Exceeding and The Oppression are used to swallowing the heaviest pressure alone. Without a question, you both know exactly how the other is holding up.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms that never quite sync: Great Exceeding always wants to charge ahead and break the deadlock in one fierce push, while The Oppression is used to slowly simmering through scarcity. One thinks the other is dawdling; the other thinks the first is reckless.

◆ Mismatched expression: Great Exceeding likes to mask anxiety with grand stories, while The Oppression, having learned that words often fail, simply goes mute. During communications, one goes on a nonstop broadcast while the other just absorbs everything.
advice: Do regular water-level calibrations: Great Exceeding should willingly take some weight off and listen to the other vent; The Oppression should write down its choked-back needs as a clear list and say them out loud. Don't let stubborn endurance turn into mutual drain.

one_liner: You take the lead and shatter the impasse; I dig the deep well and hold the bottom line. Together, we're unshakable.
analysis: Both hexagrams are rooted in Xun wood below, so their foundation is that same supple, penetrating strength. Great Exceeding is lake water pressing down on wood — the load heavy enough to bend the house beam; it's about standing alone and fearless in a critical moment, daring to cross boundaries and take the weight. The Well, on the other hand, is water over wood, relying on "laboring the people and urging one another" — it doesn't go after a single dazzling moment, just a long steady stream that nourishes everyone. When these two meet, Great Exceeding's solitary courage and decisiveness inject the sharp will to break deadlocks into the Well's daily operations; the Well's depth and constancy, in turn, hold the balance when Great Exceeding's beam starts to strain. One leads the charge, the other handles the logistics. At first glance, one is fast, one is slow — but they share the same wind-and-wood root, and each understands the other's kindred instinct to sink roots deep while holding up the pressure from above.
resonance: ★ Same Root, Same Timing: With Xun wood underneath, both hexagrams know to first root themselves with flexibility, then face the heavy pressure or hidden currents above — so they naturally move at the same beat.

★ Complementary Roles — Breaking Through and Guarding the Source: Great Exceeding excels at tearing open an opening under high pressure; The Well is a master at storing water in the shadows to nourish life. One builds momentum, the other holds the safety net — a kindred understanding.
conflict: ◆ Lone Charge vs. Shared Nurture: Great Exceeding is used to silently carrying the entire load alone; The Well insists that everyone shares the burden and supports one another. These two ways of operating often fail to sync up.

◆ Bold Strides vs. Steady Steps: Great Exceeding pursues swift, boundary-crossing progress; The Well is devoted to the constant, even-keeled principle of 'no loss, no gain.' They often quarrel over how big a step to take.
advice: When differences come up, Great Exceeding, don't rush to ram through alone — first let the Well get the resources and people in order. And Well, don't always urge Great Exceeding to slow down; at critical moments, give it enough room to try and fail, with a way back.

relationship_name: Enduring the Weight, Meeting the Hour
one_liner: One endures crushing pressure without a whimper; the other watches for the right moment to flip the table. Together, they're the cure for every stale, stuck-in-the-rut pattern.
analysis: In the hexagram of Great Preponderance, lake water floods over the wood and the ridgepole bends, driving one to stand alone without fear and shoulder extraordinary weight. In Revolution, a hidden fire smolders beneath the lake; water and fire clash, forcing revolution — it stresses gaining trust at the appointed day, then reshuffling everything once the time ripens. Both hexagrams have Lake (Dui) on top, so they appear talkative and socially savvy on the surface, but inside one is silently bearing the load while the other is quietly stoking the fire. Great Preponderance's stubborn endurance gives Revolution the foundation to carry things; Revolution's adaptability shows Great Preponderance the way to break the deadlock. Together they can turn a burden on the verge of collapse into an imperative for change, curing stalemates and procrastination.
resonance: ★ Breakthrough kinship: Both know that extraordinary times call for extraordinary measures — one dares to carry the heavy load, the other dares to break the old rules.
★ Outward composure: With Lake above, both keep their cool under fire, never revealing fear or losing their footing in public.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythm: The Great Preponderance habitually endures first then looks for a way out, while Revolution insists on waiting for the appointed day — so one is eager and the other delays.

◆ Inner energy friction: The Great Preponderance's independence can turn into lone-wolf isolation, and if Revolution's change misses its timing, it may snap the beam the other is straining to hold up.
advice: When you hit a bottleneck, don't each plow ahead on your own: let the Great Preponderance side map out the limits and load-bearing capacity, and the Revolution side nail down the timing and build outward momentum. Set clear rules for when to act and who has your back before turning the game around.

one_liner: You break the deadlock, I tend the fire; wind-born flames, no blind bustle.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is like timber under strain—lake water may surge over it, yet it stands unbowed. The Cauldron is a vessel of burning fire, using the wind's force to forge a new order. Both share the lower trigram of Wind, giving them a supple, penetrating style of action—but their upper trigrams create different rhythms: the Great Preponderance dares to break convention under immense pressure, while the Cauldron seeks to establish a new pattern from stability. When they meet, the Great Preponderance's resilience under pressure supports the Cauldron's innovations, and the Cauldron's sense of direction keeps the Great Preponderance's breakthroughs from running wild. Like an old master and a new flame—one dares to dismantle old beams, the other excels at casting a new cauldron. Together they get things done; apart, their efforts scatter.
resonance: ★ Shared Momentum: both lower trigrams are Wind, so you act with the same flexible, penetrating energy—kindred in temperament, you naturally synchronize to advance the plan.
★ Resonance in Renewal: the Cauldron's discard-the-old, establish-the-new and the Great Preponderance's break-with-convention both dare to shatter old frameworks and carve out a fresh path.
conflict: ◆ Pressure Overload: the Great Preponderance's oppressive lake can destabilize the Cauldron's equilibrium, wearing thin each other's patience.
◆ Rhythmic Discord: the Cauldron needs time to settle into new rules, while the Great Preponderance's hurry to break through easily disrupts the strategy.
advice: Align your goals once a month: let the Great Preponderance pioneer through trial and error, let the Cauldron review and consolidate, and use the wind's momentum to weave breaking and building into a single rhythm.

relationship_name: The Perilous Beam and Startling Thunder
one_liner: One silently shoulders the whole mess, the other startles easily yet somehow always catches what would otherwise slip through.
analysis: Great Preponderance is the heavy structure of 'the lake submerging the wood' — a beam that bends under water pressure but refuses to break. Its core philosophy is toughing it out alone, standing independent and unafraid. Thunder, by contrast, is the sudden pulse of 'repeated thunder' — a shock that forces you awake, steadying the mind through fear and self-reflection. Bring these two together, and you get a collision between static pressure and dynamic jolt. Great Preponderance swallows all pressure silently, which tends to fester into inner injury. Thunder's sudden startle can instantly pierce that shell of forced endurance, making the other face hidden dangers head-on. Conversely, Great Preponderance's steady foundation gives Thunder's nervous energy an anchor, so that 'shock for a hundred miles' never degenerates into frantic thrashing. One holds the line under long, crushing weight; the other recalibrates fast in a sudden crisis. Together, they can carry things in calm times and hold the line when chaos hits.
resonance: ★ Fearless in the headwind: Great Preponderance's tough independence, paired with Thunder's composure that never drops the ritual spoon and chalice — both believe deep down that the more critical the moment, the less room there is for panic.

★ Holding the line at all costs: Great Preponderance's sense of duty in pressing forward meets Thunder's fearful self-examination. When it comes to fundamental issues of right and wrong, they never muddy the waters — they dare to push back, yet also know when to advance and when to yield.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Great Preponderance tends to bury its head and tough things out, reacting slowly; Thunder is hypersensitive to every rustle in the wind. One finds the other too sluggish, the other finds the first too alarmist.

◆ Emotional drain: Great Preponderance's independence can harden into a closed-off pretense; Thunder's fearful self-reflection can spiral into overthinking. When problems arise, each can easily feel the other just doesn't get it.
advice: When heavy pressure hits, Great Preponderance should trade silent endurance for active check-ins; Thunder should take three deep breaths before responding to any noise. Don't let misplaced vigilance wound the other's quiet sense of responsibility.

relationship_name: Crossing Boundaries, Knowing When to Stop
one_liner: One dares to flip the table and blaze a new path; the other holds the emergency brake with unwavering resolve.
analysis: The Great Preponderance is the image of the Lake overwhelming the Wood — an overloaded state, like a ridgepole bent nearly to breaking, knowing the risk yet choosing to press forward alone. Keeping Still, by contrast, is the Mountain rest upon Mountain — absolute stillness, valuing the wisdom of knowing when to stop and guarding one's position. When these two forces collide, it's a classic game of accelerator versus brake. The Great Preponderance's impulse to overturn the table can make Keeping Still feel out of control, while Keeping Still's insistence on boundaries often strikes the Great Preponderance as a stumbling block. Yet the Great Preponderance's sagging ridge precisely needs Keeping Still's grounding to keep from snapping; and Keeping Still's refusal to step out of place, without the Great Preponderance's push, would sink into stagnant water. When the two work together, it's bold hypothesis meeting careful verification — building a lighthouse in the eye of the storm that refuses to drift with the tide.
resonance: ★ Complementary dynamics of action and stillness: the Great Preponderance's fearless breakthroughs can activate Keeping Still's sluggish inertia, while Keeping Still's steady boundaries can catch the Great Preponderance before it spirals into recklessness.

★ Shared bottom line: the Great Preponderance's solitary courage in pressing forward needs Keeping Still's clear-headed awareness of its own place to calibrate direction and keep it from blind, head-on charging.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythms: the Great Preponderance is in a hurry to upend the old order and charge ahead, while Keeping Still insists on pausing to measure the safe distance over and over — each easily winds up tripping the other.

◆ Mutual energy drain: the Great Preponderance finds Keeping Still too conservative, a stumbling block; Keeping Still finds the Great Preponderance too reckless, a runaway horse — communication easily sparks gunpowder.
advice: When facing a major decision, let the Great Preponderance first list the worst-case risks and backup plans; then let Keeping Still draw the non-negotiable execution red lines and move forward according to those rules.

one_liner: One dares to bridge the rapids; the other tells you to wait for the sapling to grow strong on its own.
analysis: The Preponderance of the Great is the extreme pressure of the lake submerging the tree. Its judgment, 'It furthers one to undertake something,' carries the lone courage of standing independent and unafraid — it excels at charging through crises to break a deadlock. Development, by contrast, is the unhurried growth of a tree on the mountain; the image says, 'The superior person, dwelling in worthy virtue, improves the customs,' emphasizing gradual progress and patience with the current. When the two meet, it's a heavy foot on the accelerator meeting a steady chassis. The Preponderance of the Great supplies the sharp edge to break through stalemates; Development takes that edge and distills it into a foundation that can continue. Without Development as a safety net, The Preponderance of the Great tends to snap; without The Preponderance of the Great's breakthrough, Development tends to sink into tepidness. The chemistry lies in finding the balance between 'we have to make a big move' and 'we have to take it step by step' — the equilibrium of breaking through first, then building up.
resonance: ★ Same Source, Upward Urge: The Xun wood at the base of The Preponderance of the Great and the Xun wind of Development share the same origin — both know how to keep growing upward with resilience in turbulent times.

★ Charge and Hold, Complementary: The 'independent and fearless' boldness of The Preponderance of the Great tears open the gap, while Development's 'dwelling in virtue and improving customs' patience sews it closed — one breaks, one nurtures, a perfect loop.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: The Preponderance of the Great is used to 'undertaking with advantage' and charging straight ahead under pressure, but Development insists on 'the maiden's marriage brings good fortune' — it must follow the proper sequence. One fast, one slow, and they easily pull each other apart.

◆ Emotional Backlash: The suffocating weight of the lake over the tree can squeeze the calm of the tree on the mountain into anxiety — one finds the other too dawdling, the other finds the first too rash.
advice: In critical decisions, borrow the lone courage of The Preponderance of the Great to make the call, but when it comes to execution, follow Development's rhythm and break it into one small milestone per week. Never skip stages or pile on extra demands.

relationship_name: The Lone Beam and the Silken Thread
one_liner: You've sworn to hold up the whole sky; I'd rather drag you down into the warm grit of everyday life.
analysis: Great Preponderance is like a load-bearing beam: when the lake floods the wood, it only knows to bear up alone — independence and fearlessness are its native soil.
