The Judgement says, 'It furthers one to have somewhere to go,' meaning that once you identify a direction, you act like a doubly-wound spring, propelling each other forward without any thought of giving up. The Image emphasizes 'standing firm and not changing your direction,' and in you this manifests as an extraordinary regard for principles and commitments. But if the inner energy of Thunder and Wind is all directed at a single point, your days can easily become a repetitive copy machine, lacking the resilience to go with the flow. This is not a pairing for idle romance and moonlit reveries, but for building a nest, attracting the phoenix, and sharing the long nights together.
resonance: ★ Footsteps lock in perfect sync: You share an identical obsession with long-term planning, and even in daily life you naturally play by the same rhythm.
★ Roots grow ever deeper: Thunder's bold drive combined with Wind's penetrating power makes your principles and trust intertwine like the gnarled roots of an old tree.
conflict: ◆ Neither wants to turn first: Both cling to the bottom line of 'not changing direction,' so when disagreements arise, it's easy to slip into cold silence, lacking the softness to break the ice.
◆ Life lacks novelty: Double the stability can turn your days into assembly-line work, and over time you may feel bored, forgetting to leave some breathing room for the relationship.
advice: Set aside a half-day each week to break the routine — take a spur-of-the-moment different walk, or try something small neither of you has ever done. Loosen the tension in your tightly wound rhythm.

relationship_name: Hold the Constant, Know When to Retreat
one_liner: One roots deep, the other knows when to step back—together, they carry what must be carried and let go when it's time.
analysis: The Hexagram of Duration is like thunder and wind moving in tandem, devoted to the long game of standing firm without shifting course—once a path is chosen, it's braved through every storm. The Hexagram of Retreat is like the sky high above distant mountains, embodying the wisdom of leaving space when there is a mountain under heaven—when the winds shift, it knows how to bow out gracefully. When these two meet, they perfectly complete each other's rhythm of advance and retreat: Duration's thunder and wind can push Retreat out of its comfort zone to go deeper, while Retreat's vast heaven-and-earth perspective can apply the brakes just as Duration is about to spiral into tunnel vision. This isn't about one convincing the other—it's a mutual calibration between long-term commitment and boundary awareness. Duration teaches how to endure; Retreat teaches how to release. Together, they find the dynamic balance between stubborn persistence and knowing when to walk away.
resonance: ★ Long-termism's brake pad: The thunder-wind energy of Duration can make one plunge headlong into things, and Retreat's heaven-mountain perspective provides the sober clarity to cut losses before it's too late—keeping persistence from curdling into blind stubbornness.

★ The steady anchor in the open space: Retreat knows how to step back and protect itself, but it can easily come across as aloof or distant; Duration's unshakable steadiness gives that withdrawal a backbone and a principle, transforming a departure into a strategic relocation rather than an escape.
conflict: ◆ A tug-of-war between grit and cold war: Duration locks onto its chosen cause and refuses to let go, while Retreat defaults to a quiet, unspoken pull-back when things feel draining. One sees the other as pigheaded; the other sees the first as icy.

◆ The friction of mismatched rhythms: Duration craves the steady comfort of a slow-burning, ever-present companionship, whereas Retreat needs periodic stretches of solitude. Duration feels Retreat is hot-and-cold, and Retreat feels smothered by Duration's clinginess.
advice: Give Duration a clear stop-loss line and agree on a set return schedule for Retreat. Check in with each other regularly on how things are going—don't let silence replace honest conversation. Turn your shared rhythm of advancing and retreating into a living, workable understanding.

one_liner: One steadily builds momentum, the other storms ahead to break new ground—together they're a golden pairing of marathon and sprint.
analysis: The Heng hexagram is like a deep-rooted old tree, prized for the enduring steadiness of 'holding one's ground without changing course'; the Da Zhuang hexagram is like a thunderbolt splitting the sky, carrying the vigorous drive of 'treading not on what is improper.' Both share the Thunder image as their genetic core of action, yet their lower trigrams—Wind and Heaven—differentiate their rhythms: Heng weaves a resilient web through Wind's permeating power, while Da Zhuang releases breakthrough energy through Heaven's expansiveness. When Heng's 'steadfast rectitude' meets Da Zhuang's 'mighty advance,' a unique tension field forms—Heng gives Da Zhuang a compass that never veers off course, and Da Zhuang injects Heng with the thrust to break through the cocoon. But if they lack Kindred, Heng's caution may be seen by Da Zhuang as dawdling, while Da Zhuang's edge may be taken by Heng as recklessness; they must find a breathing rhythm between motion and stillness.
resonance: ★ Kinetic relay: Heng's enduring stored energy becomes Da Zhuang's confidence in breaking through, and Da Zhuang's explosive power feeds back into Heng's long-term goals.

★ Shared rules: both hexagrams value the path of 'rightness'—Heng builds its foundation on steadfastness, Da Zhuang draws its boundary at treading not on what is improper—so they share a natural consensus on bottom lines.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Heng is used to a slow, steady stream, while Da Zhuang favors quick strikes; friction easily arises over pace.
◆ Strategy divergence: Heng favors defensive deep-cultivation, Da Zhuang favors offensive pioneering; when allocating resources, they may each pull to their own extreme.
advice: Before Da Zhuang makes its move, run a risk sandbox through Heng's mindset; when Heng is consolidating, regularly bring in Da Zhuang-style breakthrough tests.

one_liner: You root and stand firm; I rise and shine. The longer we go, the better it gets.
analysis: Hexagram 32 (Duration) is like an old tree with deep roots—its essence is the resolve to 'stand firm and not change direction.' Hexagram 35 (Progress) is like the sun breaking through dawn—its drive is to 'illumine one's own bright virtue.' The beauty of this pairing lies in the meshing of 'stability' and 'advance.' Without Duration as the foundation, Progress's ascent can turn into a false blaze—fast to flare, fast to burn out. Without Progress's pull, Duration's perseverance can boil down to stagnant water—held steady but going nowhere. Thunder and wind clash with hidden power; fire and earth mirror each other with visible moves. In a relationship, it's like a long-distance run paired with a sprint's bugle call: one uses the inertia of daily rhythm to hold the bottom line, the other uses an ever-higher view to pry open new ground. Over time, Duration's resilience filters out Progress's restlessness, while Progress's light keeps injecting fresh life into Duration. This isn't simple complementarity—it's kneading 'endurance' and 'daring' into an upward spiral.
resonance: ★ Rooting and shooting share a rhythm: Duration's thunder and wind silently gather force underground; Progress's fire rises naturally above. One provides a sense of security, the other brings a sense of achievement.

★ Time reveals the real thing: Progress's 'three receptions in a day' needs Duration's 'it furthers one to have somewhere to go' as its foundation. Fast-paced recognition depends on slow, deep cultivation—together they create each other's shining moments.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms out of step can cause internal drain: Progress always wants to strike while the iron is hot and rush ahead, while Duration tends to follow a steady, step-by-step pace. One finds the other too slow, the other too hasty—it's easy to pull against each other.

◆ Sharp edge vs. steadfastness: Progress's 'illumining one's own bright virtue' likes to display achievements outward, while Duration's 'not changing direction' values quiet inner holding. High-profile self-promotion may touch the other's bottom-line principles.
advice: When facing major decisions, first clarify 'bottom lines' and 'rhythms': the Duration side holds firm to core principles without wavering; the Progress side plans phased sprint goals. Let Duration's steadiness hold Progress's urgency.

one_liner: You just keep your steps steady and don't go running off; I'll take care of dimming the lamp and lying low. Together, we're an ironclad team.
analysis: Heng (Duration) is Thunder over Wind, built on 'standing firm without changing direction'—once it locks onto a truth, it charges ahead, embracing long-term resilience. Mingyi (Darkening of the Light), by contrast, is Fire entering the Earth: light suppressed, teaching you to stay obscure yet bright in adversity, sheathing your edge to survive. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like a long-distance runner crossing paths with a night traveler. Heng's straight-ahead drive can easily smash against hidden reefs, while Mingyi's over-cautious retreat can dull your edge. But here's the wonder: Heng's constancy gives Mingyi's concealment its confidence—as long as the core doesn't crumble, a temporary dimming is just recharging. And Mingyi's steadfast endurance puts the brakes on Heng's forward rush, reminding it not to stumble blindly when visibility is zero. If the two can harmonize, they'll master the art of steadiness and concealment: not charging into rash glory, not playing turtle, but quietly sinking roots during the dark hours, waiting for the storm to pass and then breaking through the soil.
resonance: ★ Rooting in the Dark: Mingyi's restraint keeps Heng's persistence from becoming blind stubbornness, allowing it to quietly build strength in low periods.
★ Compass Guiding the Way: Heng's unwavering direction provides a spiritual anchor for Mingyi's dark periods—no matter how hard it gets, you won't lose your way.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Tempo: Heng wants to charge ahead, while Mingyi advises staying put—their action rhythms easily trip each other up.

◆ Clashing Edges: Heng's thunder likes frontal confrontation, while Mingyi's earth-fire nature prefers circumvention and concealment—the one hardness, the other hiddenness, can create internal friction.
advice: When the situation is dark, the Heng side should first set aside its impulse to press forward and let the Mingyi side scout the risks; the Mingyi side needs to break its concealment strategy into a concrete timeline, regularly aligning on bottom-line goals so the Heng side doesn't feel like it's treading water.

one_liner: You fix the course and don't look back; I'll turn a cold stove into a warm hearth.
analysis: Hexagram 32, Duration, supplies the skeleton through its principle of 'standing firm and not changing course'; Hexagram 37, The Family, supplies the flesh and blood through 'wind emerging from fire.' One is like a stabilizing sea-pillar — once the main line is clear, it advances with decisive energy; the other is like the family hearth — it prizes plain speech and steady action, keeping the small daily routines in order. The stirring of thunder and wind builds long-term momentum; wind and fire together simmer the warmth of human connection. When these two meet, they cover each other's blind spots: Duration can charge ahead and forget the temperature, while The Family hearth-warms that stubbornness with ordinary life; when The Family gets lost in chores, Duration's steady hand pulls everyone back to the main line. This is not a passionate fling; it's a long-term partnership of 'the big direction never wanders, and the small days never scatter.'
resonance: ★ The kindred 'constant' tempo: both sides value sustained effort — one holds the principle like a mountain, the other flows easily through daily life; their rhythms are natural allies.

★ A Complementary dance of action and stillness: Duration's thunder supplies the forward drive; The Family's wind-and-fire covers the warm-up — one outward, one inward, grounding the word 'steadiness' in real life.
conflict: ◆ Rigid principle hits soft human feeling: Duration's 'standing firm without changing course' can seem impersonal, and The Family, heavy on emotional communication, may feel the other is too stubborn to bend.

◆ Outward expansion pulls against inward home-keeping: Duration always wants 'it furthers one to have somewhere to go' and open new territory, while The Family cares more about its single acre of proper family order — so their tempos occasionally miss a step.
advice: After setting the key tone on big matters, don't keep revising it. On small matters, don't use long-term principles to grind against everyday life. Reserve a fixed time each week for pure conversation without goals, letting the warmth of wind and fire gradually melt the hard shell of thunder and wind.

relationship_name: Steadfast in the Right, Seeking the New
one_liner: One clings to the old rules, the other hunts for new paths—together they manage to get things done.
analysis: The Hexagram of Duration is like bedrock taking root; it speaks of a resolve that even thunder and wind cannot shake. The Hexagram of Opposition, by contrast, is like wildfire meeting water—born with the impulse to part ways. Yet oddly enough, Duration's 'standing firm without changing course' provides just the anchor Opposition needs to 'find common ground amid differences.' Without Duration's foundation, Opposition's search for unity in diversity can scatter like loose sand; without Opposition's breakthrough thinking, Duration's steadfastness can harden into rigidity. In real life, this pair often forms an ecology of 'new branches on an old tree': one deepens the roots, the other reaches the branches toward the unknown. The vibration of thunder and the leaping of fire seem mutually repellent, yet together they embody the wisdom of 'seeking stability in motion and holding to the constant amid change.'
resonance: ★ A Kindred of Long-Termists: both believe time will distill what is truly valuable—Duration tests it through persistence, Opposition filters it through difference.

★ A Resonance of Breakthrough Courage: Duration's forward drive of 'beneficial to have somewhere to go' and Opposition's flexible probing of 'small things bring good fortune' form a relay when venturing into new territory.
conflict: ◆ The Tug Between Principle and Flexibility: Duration treats rules as a lifeline, while Opposition often feels 'rules are dead, people are alive.'
◆ Friction from Mismatched Rhythms: Duration wants the patience to grind one sword for ten years; Opposition wants to quickly test, fail, and iterate—each may find the other too rigid or too flighty.
advice: Set aside half a day each month as 'exception time'—let Duration experience unconventional moves, and let Opposition practice deep, unhurried settling.

relationship_name: Hold the Course, Know When to Turn
one_liner: One person digs in and barrels ahead on a single truth; the other hits a snag and stops to take a good look at themselves. Put them together, and the message is: 'Don't rush blindly—steady your inner foundation before you move forward.'
analysis: Hexagram of Duration (Heng) speaks of 'standing firm without changing your ground'—thunder and wind in concert, all about locking your sights on a goal and grinding it down with staying power. Hexagram of Obstruction (Jian), by contrast, is 'mountain over water': when the path is blocked, it calls a halt and tells you to 'turn within and refine your character,' pulling that outward drive back into inner repair. Together, these are a 'doer' colliding with a 'reflector.' Duration can turn stubbornness into a virtue and mistake it for persistence; Obstruction, when blocked, tends to shrink into self-doubt. But Duration's 'unwavering' needs Obstruction's 'pause' to correct its aim, and Obstruction's inner work needs Duration's lasting power to take root. They can forge a rhythm of 'rest when you can't advance, then continue once rested'—turning dogged persistence into quiet strategy.
resonance: ★ Upholding the Right: Duration sets its direction and refuses to let go; Obstruction meets a rough patch and turns inward. At heart, both trust the honest road over any shortcut.

★ Action and stillness in balance: Duration supplies endless forward drive; Obstruction steps on the brakes at crucial moments to take stock. Together, the push and pull avoid both blind charging and procrastination.
conflict: ◆ Out-of-sync rhythms: Duration finds Obstruction's habit of stopping to reflect at every bump too laggard; Obstruction resents Duration's never-turn-back-until-you-hit-a-wall stubbornness, seeing it as just digging a deeper pit.

◆ Different emotional temperatures: Duration's thunder nature tends to leave problems to time and tough it out; Obstruction's water-on-mountain nature tends to swallow problems and digest them silently. In communication, one tends to erupt outward while the other freezes inward.
advice: Make a 'pause button' rule: for every three days Duration charges forward, set aside half a day to sit with Obstruction, review the books, and reflect together—turning internal wear-and-tear directly into a dashboard for the next course correction.

one_liner: One keeps the foundation steady, the other clears the cache with one click.
analysis: Duration is like bedrock, with wind and thunder following it; it values the steadiness of 'changing no direction' and long-term thinking. Deliverance is like spring thunder turning into rain, embodying the magnanimity of pardoning faults and the ability to break deadlocks. Both have Thunder as their upper trigram, so their drive and decisiveness are on the same frequency—but they push in completely different directions. Duration fears rigidity; Deliverance fears laxness. When together, Duration provides a stable framework and bottom line, keeping Deliverance's release from spiraling out of control; Deliverance is like a timely rain, washing away the inner friction and obsessions that Duration accumulates. When thunder cracks, it's not to shatter anyone, but to remind each other: stand firm where you must, and cleanly clear away what you need to let go. This pairing isn't maintained by sweet talk, but by the unspoken understanding of having each other's back and turning the page.
resonance: ★ Synchronized action: Both upper trigrams are Thunder, so they don't drag their feet when things come up—once they lock in a direction, they strike together, with highly consistent execution.

★ Complementary rhythm: Duration's long-term persistence provides a safety net for Deliverance, while Deliverance's flexible release lifts the psychological burden from Duration; they support each other without internal friction.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Duration is used to grinding along step by step, while Deliverance always wants to cut through knots for quick wins—they easily clash over whether to persist or cut losses.

◆ Emotional temperature difference: Duration's unwavering direction can come across as stubborn and rigid, while Deliverance's pardon-without-measure, if uncalibrated, can look like bottomless indulgence.
advice: When disagreements arise, first set a cooling-off period and a review day: Duration lists the issues without dredging up old grudges, Deliverance picks three things that can be let go right away and crosses them off, and the rest they tackle together.

one_liner: One wants to live at a steady rhythm; the other is always subtracting to make more space. The longer they're together, the more they see that what was cut away was never needed—what's left is the real bond.
analysis: Duration is like thunder and wind locked in struggle yet never ceasing to move—it speaks of the endurance that comes from standing firm and refusing to drift with the tide. Decrease is a lake at the foot of a mountain: water finds the lowest ground and slowly washes away the silt, teaching restraint and simplification. Together, they resemble a deep-rooted old tree and the pruning of its branches: Duration supplies the stable foundation, while Decrease cuts away the overgrowth and opens up air to breathe. Duration's 'it furthers one to have somewhere to go' needs Decrease's 'curbing anger and restraining desire' to keep it on course, or else it becomes stubborn inertia. And Decrease's 'two bowls are enough for the offering' needs Duration's steady resolve to hold the frame together—otherwise, reduce too much and the whole structure collapses. These two different hexagrams meet as one keeps and one cuts: it's not about dominance, but about seeing clearly which core is immovable and which baggage is there to be released.
resonance: ★ Leave Space and Put Down Roots: Duration's mountain-like stability pairs with Decrease's active simplifying to give each other exactly the room to grow—no jostling, no draining.
★ Restraint and Lasting Power: Decrease's discipline in desire helps Duration avoid mindless burnout, while Duration's persistence keeps Decrease's simplifying from being abandoned halfway.
conflict: ◆ Stubbornness Meets Decluttering: Duration tends to mistake habit for principle; Decrease starts cutting immediately and may hurt the security Duration values most.
◆ Off-Beat Rhythms: Duration wants steady progress, Decrease wants quick cuts through complexity—one fears change, the other fears delay, and everyday life easily becomes a fight over 'keep or toss.'
advice: When at an impasse, first set a bottom-line list: Duration will name three principles it will never compromise, and Decrease will name three old matters it can finally let go. Review and clear them out together on a regular basis.

one_liner: You hold the base steady and never veer off course; I know when to take the gains and upgrade. This pairing is a sure win for everyday life.
analysis: The Hexagram of Duration brings thunder and wind into mutual clash yet holds a fixed course — the point is to avoid restless maneuvering. The Hexagram of Increase lets wind and thunder surge, but changes in accord with the current — the aim is to upgrade. When these two come together, it's like fitting an elevator to an old house: Duration lays the foundation and raises the load-bearing walls, ensuring life never collapses; Increase handles demolishing the old, installing the new, and optimizing the flow, so days grow brighter and more spacious. Without Duration's steadiness, Increase's improvements easily become pointless churning; without Increase's flexibility, Duration's perseverance will eventually stew into a dead end. The upper and lower trigrams swap positions, exactly stitching persistence and iteration into a long-term algorithm for living — one provides security, the other novelty.
resonance: ★ Alignment of purpose: Both recognize the value of moving forward. Whether preserving gains or chasing change, the drive to advance is twisted into a single rope.

★ Complementary energy: Duration's thunder is in charge of setting the direction; Increase's wind gives the push. One supplies the courage, the other the thrust, so working together doesn't burn internal energy.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm: One is used to holding the line and sticking to the old path; the other always wants to fix faults and turn on a dime. Expect bickering over whether to change the rules.

◆ Different sense of security: Duration thinks frequent adjustments are pointless fuss; Increase thinks clinging to old rules is mired in nostalgia. Their definitions of stability are just on different wavelengths.
advice: When you hit a disagreement, first draw a bottom-line zone for Duration and leave an experimental plot for Increase. In big matters, let Duration set the direction; in small matters, let Increase fine-tune.

relationship_name: Guard the Constant, Decide the Change
one_liner: You sustain the days with a gentle, steady flow; I cut through the tangle with a sharp, quick blade.
analysis: Heng (Duration) is like an old tree with deep roots, devoted to the principle of "standing firm without changing direction," pouring energy into long-term persistence, with thunder and wind working together for stability. Guai (Breakthrough), on the other hand, is like a reservoir risen to the critical point — Lake over Heaven — and when it's time to clear the field, it never delays. When these two hexagrams come together, it's not about one dominating the other; it's a steady anchor meeting a sluice-gate knife. Heng's patient nature can let situations stagnate into calluses; Guai's impatience can cut through the congestion with one stroke. But if Guai simply charges ahead, it lacks Heng's stable foundation beneath it. Together, they're like a long-distance runner paired with a sprinter: in daily life, they build the groundwork at Heng's pace; when a bottleneck or mess appears, Guai acts decisively to clear the field. Both hexagram texts include "favorable to have somewhere to go," which shows that as long as this pairing doesn't consume itself in internal friction, its forward momentum is strong. The key is to blend Heng's principle of "not changing direction" with Guai's restraint of "not favorable to resort to arms" — don't let perseverance become stubbornness, and don't let decisiveness become recklessness.
resonance: ★ Long-term thinking meets the decisive type: Heng's steady, long-flowing stream provides the confidence for Guai's decisive moves, ensuring that every decision isn't made in a vacuum.
★ Floodgate-style clearing pairs with steady, sure steps: Guai's 'Lake over Heaven' outpouring can wash away the stale inertia that Heng has long accumulated, keeping the relationship fresh.
conflict: ◆ Rigid rule-following collides with cutting the Gordian knot: Heng fears change, Guai seeks breakthrough; when disagreements arise, one finds the other too stubborn, the other finds the one too impatient.

◆ Excessive decisiveness can damage the foundation: if Guai forgets the warning of 'not favorable to resort to force' and pushes change with hard-handed tactics, it will directly shake the stable base that Heng has painstakingly built.
advice: Set clear bottom lines for what must not change and red lines for what must change. Live at Heng's pace in ordinary times, but the moment a red line is crossed, switch immediately to Guai's quick-blade mode to clear the field, and never bring up old grudges afterward.

one_liner: You keep the steering wheel welded in place, and I'll pick up riders along the way — as long as the chassis is solid, this convoy can run for a lifetime.
analysis: The Hexagram of Duration is about 'standing firm without changing direction' — like a tree rooted in deep soil, it picks one path and follows it to the end, putting steadiness first. The Hexagram of Gathering Together, on the other hand, is 'the lake on the earth': water naturally flows to low ground, creating a magnetic field that draws people together, yet beneath the bustle lies the sober awareness to 'guard against the unforeseen.' When these two come together, it's one building the stage and the other putting on the show. Duration's steadfastness gives Gathering Together's assemblies the confidence that they won't fall apart, while Gathering Together's fluidity breaks through Duration's dull routines. The key is: Duration must not be too rigid — it needs to learn to make room for newcomers; Gathering Together must not only chase excitement — it has to understand that even the grandest gathering needs rules as a safety net. Combine long-term vision with short-term bursts of energy, and you have a golden partnership that can preserve the old and blaze new trails.
resonance: ★ Steady flow draws living water: Duration's persistent rhythm acts like a fixed riverbed, channeling the scattered resources Gathering Together brings into a sustainable, well-ordered system.
★ Gathering with safeguards: Gathering Together's vigilance against the unexpected perfectly compensates for Duration's potential path-dependency, building risk contingencies into long-term plans.
conflict: ◆ Rigid hold meets changing times: Duration runs on a set track, and when Gathering Together suddenly brings in new people or unforeseen developments, Duration can come across as rejecting and inflexible.
◆ Bustle drains energy: Gathering Together loves to constantly assemble and pool energy, but long-term high-frequency interaction will break the calm and solo recharging rhythm Duration needs.
advice: Set aside one day each month for a resource review. Log all the connections and opportunities Gathering Together brings, then break them down and feed them into Duration's long-term execution plan. Manage the bustle with systems, and keep the core mission alive with fresh input.

one_liner: You stay the course without wavering, I climb step by step — this pair is all about staying steady and reaching high.
analysis: Duration has upper Zhen (Thunder) and lower Xun (Wind) — thunder and wind clash, yet it holds the bottom line of 'standing firm without changing direction,' like an old tree rooted against the wind. Ascending has upper Kun (Earth) and lower Xun (Wind) — the earth's energy nourishes the young shoot, calling for the patience of 'accumulating small steps to reach great heights.' Both hexagrams share Xun (Wind) as their hidden card, showing they inherently reject quick gains and believe in the penetrating power of a steady stream. Duration's 'steadiness' gives Ascending a compass that never veers off course; Ascending's 'gentle advance' adds a buffer to Duration's unyielding straightness. This pair doesn't play the love-at-first-sight routine — they treat time as fertilizer: you establish the rules amid the storm, I thicken my growth rings in the soil. As days turn into years, Duration's persistence becomes the scaffolding for Ascending's climb, and Ascending's rapid growth gives back to Duration the conviction of 'no blame.' It's not about one transforming the other, but two survival wisdoms sprouting from the same root system — one keeps you from losing your way, the other reaches for what's above.
resonance: ★ Synced Rhythm: Both lower trigrams are Xun (Wind) — inherently believing that slow and steady wins the race, relying not on brute force but on gradual penetration.
★ Mutual Trust at the Root: One keeps promises and doesn't easily change course; the other knows how to adapt and take root without rushing — each can catch the other's steadiness.
conflict: ◆ Tug-of-War on Pace: Once Heng locks onto a certainty, it can get stuck in a rut; Sheng, after feeling around in the soil too long, may resent being rushed — when patience runs out, cold wars can set in.
◆ Misaligned Goals: Heng wants to preserve the present unchanged; Sheng wants to keep breaking upward. Over time, one may see the other as too stubborn, and the other may see the one as too rash.
advice: Once a quarter, review direction and progress together. The Heng side should stop leaning on old rules, and the Sheng side should share small milestones — replace emotional burnout with concrete progress.

one_liner: One charges ahead with a stubborn sense of purpose; the other quietly holds down the fort and feeds the fire. Together, they're the steadiest long-term duo around.
analysis: In the Duration hexagram, thunder moves and the wind follows, honoring the principle of 'establishing a direction and never changing it.' It relies on the supple toughness of the lower Xun wind to carve perseverance into the very bones. In the Well hexagram, water sits above wood, championing the saying 'towns may change, but the well never moves.' It, too, uses the penetrating power of Xun wood to draw living water up and nourish all. Together they are a classic case of same root, different fruits: at the base, both are pliant, stretchable winds quietly taking root; yet as they rise, they branch into thunder's decisiveness and water's nurturing grace. Duration supplies a strong sense of direction; the Well holds the warmth of everyday life. But thunder is quick and water is slow — one dreads dawdling, the other dreads rashness. They need to channel some of that 'tenacious go-getter' energy into the patience of 'tending the well and minding the rope,' or they'll simply burn out.
resonance: ★ Kindred Frequency in the Xun Wind: Their shared logic is supple and penetrating, so they instinctively understand each other's slow-burning warmth and lifelong constancy.
★ Complementary Motion and Stillness for the Long Haul: Thunder's pioneering force pairs with water's nourishing power — one expands the territory, the other secures the base.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Haste Pulls Against Slowness — The Duration hexagram's thunder urges constant motion, while the Well hexagram's water prefers a gentle, steady trickle. One may find the other too sluggish; the other, too reckless.

◆ Neglected Maintenance Can Undo Everything — The Well fears the careless broken jar, and Duration fears the rigid refusal to adapt. If they only charge forward and forget daily repair, the relationship can easily run dry.
advice: Every month, set aside one 'no-agenda talk.' Give some of Duration's focus to the Well's little maintenance tasks. When things get prickly, use the soft wind of the lower trigram to sidestep a direct collision — don't let principles choke the everyday.

one_liner: Same root, different frequencies: one grinds away for permanence, the other is all about upgrades; put them together and you get a slow fire brewing rich broth.
analysis: Both are rooted in Xun/Wind at the base, so they both instinctively understand going with the flow and infiltrating slowly. But above that, they part ways: the Heng/Duration hexagram carries Zhen/Thunder above, valuing an unchanging course — life should pass in order, and once committed to a path, never look back. The Ding/Cauldron hexagram carries Li/Fire above, valuing aligning one's position to fulfill destiny — always wanting to throw old materials into the pot and cook up new rules and new values. Put them together: one is like an old tree gripping its roots for stability, the other like boiling water on the stove craving change. Fortunately, wind and wood share a source — Heng's patience feeds Ding's blazing fire, and Ding's innovation adds flavor to Heng's stubbornness. Not a love-at-first-sight dry-wood-and-flame, but a relationship that becomes a slow simmer, ever richer as it brews.
resonance: ★ Same-frequency foundation: both share the Xun/Wind wisdom of going with the flow and infiltrating slowly; in communication, no need to push hard — a slight hint is enough for mutual understanding.
★ Complementary pacing: Heng's steadiness can hold Ding's restless experimentation, while Ding's creativity keeps injecting freshness into Heng's ordinary days.
conflict: ◆ The tug between keeping old ways and seeking change: Heng clings to the rule of the unchanging course and tends to see Ding's urge to overturn everything as reckless and unstable.
◆ Mismatched rhythm: Ding is eager to fulfill its destiny and see transformation immediately, while Heng is used to stretching the timeline, which easily makes Ding anxious.
advice: Heng should break long-term goals into small weekly tune-ups; Ding should consciously keep about 30% of old habits as a buffer when making changes, and use old bottles for new wine instead of tearing everything down.

one_liner: One keeps the gas pedal down, the other watches the road and brakes — this pair is the most dependable for a long haul.
analysis: The thunder-wind of Duration is a natural long-distance runner, fixated on a chosen direction with no looking back; the stacked mountains of Keeping Still, however, are an unshakable anchor, teaching precisely when to hold back and respect boundaries. When the two meet, it is not about one subduing the other but about installing an adjustment valve on each other's rhythm. Duration's 'standing firm and never changing direction' can easily become a stubborn full-speed charge, while Keeping Still's 'thinking without leaving one's position' pulls it back to the edges of reality. Conversely, Keeping Still's tranquility, lacking Duration's 'beneficial to have somewhere to go,' turns into stagnant water. The beauty of this relationship lies in movement that never oversteps and stillness that never hardens—like a long-distance runner equipped with a metronome. In daily life, one opens new ground while the other guards the line; the longer they travel together, the deeper their sense of reliability.
resonance: ★ Rhythmic interlock: Duration's sustained output, combined with Keeping Still's timely pauses, keeps long-term goals from derailing in blind haste.
★ Boundary consensus: Keeping Still's 'not stepping out of place' draws a safe zone for Duration's 'beneficial to have somewhere to go,' so both act with measure and never overstep.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched pace: Duration finds Keeping Still too slow and too eager to set limits; Keeping Still finds Duration too impulsive and unwilling to stop—leading to repeated tug-of-war over go versus stop.

◆ Energy divergence: the high-spirited thunder-wind meets the mountain's reserved nature—when things get lively, one is pouring out while the other goes silent, leaving communication as two parallel monologues.
advice: When disagreements arise, first set a fixed cycle of action and review, letting Duration move the progress forward while Keeping Still evaluates the limits, and let both impulse and caution be digested within that steady process.

one_liner: Once you set your direction, commit to it fully—but place each step firmly as you go.
analysis: In Duration, thunder and wind act together, standing firm without changing course—an anchor that keeps the inner core stable and the goal from drifting. In Development, wood grows on the mountain, dwelling in virtue and improving customs—like a spring silkworm spinning silk, moving with natural rhythm and advancing step by step. Together, they are like an old helmsman paired with a new sailor: one clings to the compass, terrified of veering off course; the other watches the water's ripples and rows slowly, never pulling up sprouts to force growth. Duration provides unshakable steadiness; Development provides adaptable rhythm. In the long run of life, this pair fears chaos, not slowness. Duration's composure can settle Development's fussy details; Development's patience can dissolve Duration's impatience. They don't compete on explosive power but wage a sustained war of endurance. Over time, the mountain tree naturally matures into timber, and thunder and wind take on their own grand presence.
resonance: ★ Rooting and branching: both trust the old wisdom that slow is fast—one uses steadiness to stabilize the foundation, the other uses patience to grow branches and leaves. The longer they go, the more kindred they become.
★ Shared destination: Duration holds to the big direction while Development takes steady small steps. Neither loves shortcuts; both believe the channel will form when the water arrives.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Duration rushes to lock down the framework for security, while Development insists on grinding through the details in sequence—each may find the other too rigid or too dragging.

◆ Disagreement on adaptability: Duration stays on one path without turning and tends to tough out new situations; Development, used to adjusting with the current, may feel the other doesn't understand going with the flow.
advice: Set a three-year direction, break it into quarterly tasks, and review progress only once a month. At all other times, don't rush each other—each moves at their own pace.

one_liner: It opens like a clap of thunder—one who wants to settle into a steady rhythm of life, and another who reads the cards as they go, probing the relationship's depth.
analysis: This pairing of hexagrams begins with a spring thunderclap overhead—both act with a can-do, impulse-driven energy. The foundation of Heng (The Persisting) is Xun, the Wind, which prizes the long, steady flow: it holds on to the green mountain without loosening its grip, turning life into an unshakable anchor. Gui Mei (The Marrying Maiden), by contrast, is grounded in Dui, the Lake, where emotions ripple easily across the surface, carrying a try-before-you-buy tentativeness. It knows relationships can't be forced; only by seeing the hidden pitfalls can they last. When these two come together, they're at first drawn to each other's decisive, thunderous boldness, but as time goes on they discover their rhythms are completely different. One is used to laying out a long road step by step; the other keeps tapping the brakes on any forward movement. Heng thinks Gui Mei is too anxious about gains and losses, while Gui Mei finds Heng too inflexible. Yet precisely this difference can patch each other's leaks: Heng's constancy can steady Gui Mei's emotional swings, and Gui Mei's clear-sightedness can remind Heng not to barrel into a dead end. With the same Thunder above and different foundations below, once they're polished and meshed, they become a partner pair that is steady yet alert.
resonance: ★ A perfect opening spark: Both are grounded in the Thunder hexagram; when opportunity arises, they dare to make the call first, never dragging their feet.

★ A safety-net understanding: Heng's 'standing firm without changing course' gives Gui Mei's 'knowing the pitfalls before seeing it through' a sense of security, turning cautious probing into grounded trust.
conflict: ◆ The fatigue of pulled rhythms: Heng tends to plan on long cycles, while Gui Mei is often swayed by momentary emotions—each easily sees the other as either too rigid or too flighty.
◆ A mismatch in risk perception: Heng sees persistence as victory, while Gui Mei stays alert to 'advancing into misfortune' and often misses good chances at critical junctures due to over-caution.
advice: Agree to a weekly 'cards-on-the-table check-in,' placing Gui Mei's intuitive warnings side by side with Heng's long-term plans. Focus only on solutions, never rehashing old grievances.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Duration and Abundance
one_liner: One lays the groundwork, the other shines; as they partner through life, the longer they're together, the brighter they glow.
analysis: The hexagram Duration (Heng) is formed by Thunder and Wind together; its Judgment says 'sublime success, no blame,' and the Image says 'standing firm without changing direction'—its core is enduring stability. The hexagram Abundance (Feng) has Thunder and Lightning both arriving; its Judgment says 'sublime success, it is fitting to be like the noonday sun,' and the Image says 'breaking lawsuits and applying punishments'—its core is abundance and decisiveness. Both have Thunder as the upper trigram, giving a shared drive and vibration. But the lower trigrams—Wind and Fire—differ in character: Wind brings penetration and gentleness, Fire brings brightness and attachment. Duration's persistence is like an old tree with deep roots; Abundance's fullness is like the fierce noonday sun. When they meet, Duration provides Abundance with a stable foundation so its burst of energy doesn't float unrealistically; Abundance injects highlights into Duration, so perseverance doesn't become dull. The chemistry lies in this: Duration's 'advantage in going forward' needs Abundance's 'fitting at midday' to ignite the climax, while Abundance's 'do not grieve' relies on Duration's 'no blame' to cover risks. In practice, this pairing is like a long-term project: Duration handles daily operations and patient accumulation, Abundance handles breakthrough moments and showcase opportunities—only by borrowing each other's strength can they succeed.
resonance: ★ Thunder Moving as One: With Thunder as the upper trigram for both, they act with drive and decisiveness, clicking instantly when opportunities arise without delay.
★ Wind and Fire Reflecting Each Other: Duration's gentle penetration can temper Abundance's impatience, while Abundance's bright direction illuminates the path of Duration's perseverance.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Rhythms: Duration stresses 'standing firm without changing direction' for long-term stability, while Abundance advocates 'fitting at midday' for quick results—one wants slow, the other fast, creating friction.

◆ Divergence of Energy: Wind-like Duration tends to disperse and penetrate, a long, steady stream; Fire-like Abundance tends to focus, burst, and dazzle instantly. In allocating resources, they may pull against each other.
advice: When setting annual goals, use Duration's steady, sure-footed approach; when breaking down quarterly sprint milestones, borrow Abundance's decisive strikes. Review and reconcile at the end of each month to keep their rhythm aligned.

one_liner: A steadying anchor paired with a wandering poet — one holds the line, the other roams far.
analysis: Duration (Heng) is like thunder and wind clashing yet returning to constancy, emphasizing deep roots and steadfastness; The Wanderer (Lü) is like mountain and fire roving, seeking vitality in flux. When they meet, it is a dialogue between anchor and sail: Duration's 'standing firm without shifting' gives the Wanderer a spiritual compass, while the Wanderer's 'clear-sighted caution in judgment' reminds Duration not to harden into dogmatism. The endurance of thunder and wind can absorb the Wanderer's restlessness, and the fluidity of mountain and fire can ignite the monotony of permanence — forming a cycle of 'overcoming movement with stillness, nurturing stillness with movement.' It suits scenarios calling for both long-term cultivation and flexible breakthroughs, like the pairing of strategic resolve and operational agility in a startup team.
resonance: ★ Steady progress: Duration's endurance underpins the Wanderer's explorations, and the Wanderer's adaptability keeps Duration from resting on its laurels.
★ Mutual balance of movement and stillness: thunder and wind store energy within, mountain and fire light the way without — together they create a sustainable rhythm of action.
conflict: ◆ Stasis vs. wandering: Duration dislikes frequent change, while the Wanderer resists uniformity, leading to tugs-of-war over pacing.
◆ Trust temperature gap: Duration values time-tested trust, while the Wanderer tends to cut losses early — their expectations of commitment are out of sync.
advice: Establish a 'flexible covenant': let Duration set the bottom-line rules, let the Wanderer explore paths within the framework, and spend three days each month reviewing and adjusting the boundaries.

one_liner: You're responsible for anchoring the big direction; I'm responsible for flexibly laying the trail. Teaming up is all about being both steady and agile.
analysis: The Hexagram of Duration (Heng) has thunder above and wind below; it emphasizes 'standing firm and not changing one's direction' — once the path is clear, proceed steadily. The Hexagram of the Gentle (Xun) has wind above and below; it focuses on 'entering with the wind' — soft in posture, many ways to move. Both share the same lower trigram of wind, so at the base they both understand how to advance with the current, and communication is almost effortless. But thunder above wants to set rules and endure; the twin winds want to slip through gaps and retune at any moment. It's like an old captain meeting an old sailor: one keeps his eyes locked on the compass and stays on course, the other adjusts the rigging to the wind. As long as Duration's persistence doesn't become stiffness, and Wind's gentleness doesn't become glibness, the two can blend long-term vision with flexible execution — their work will have both resilience and momentum.
resonance: ★ Core resonance: both know how to go with the flow; no lengthy explanations needed to communicate — one glance tells you how to borrow the wind's force.
★ Shared goal: both want to get things done; one anchors without veering off course, the other pushes the boat downstream — all strength pulled in the same direction.
conflict: ◆ Tempo mismatch: Duration insists on gripping the green mountain and never easing up, while the Gentle is used to turning with the wind — easy to get caught between persistence and flexibility.

◆ Rules clash: Duration wants the iron rule of standing firm without changing course; the Gentle prefers a flexible, 'repeat the order then act' approach. One finds the other too rigid, the other finds the first too flighty.
advice: When disagreements arise, the Duration partner gives the Gentle partner a three-day window for trial and error without meddling; the Gentle partner must deliver concrete results at key milestones. Trade flexibility for trust, and boundaries for space.

one_liner: You make our days a steady, enduring stream; I add the little joys to the mix.
analysis: The hexagram Duration is like an old tree with a deep root system; it values standing firm without shifting ground, committing to a path and not changing course lightly. The Joyous is like spring water just beginning to thaw, thriving on friendly exchange and nourishing the bond through conversation and emotional resonance. When the two come together, Duration's steady presence gives Joyous's exuberance a solid floor, so the happiness doesn't drift in the air. And Joyous's flexibility lets Duration's single-mindedness breathe, turning dry persistence into a warm daily rhythm. If Duration is too rigid, it may dismiss Joyous's spontaneity as childish; if Joyous is too flighty, Duration feels the ground shifting beneath it. The key is to blend unchanging principles with fluid emotions, so endurance doesn't become stubbornness, and liveliness doesn't turn into shallow excitement.
resonance: ★ Motion and stillness nurture each other: Duration's ceaseless thunder-wind supplies a stable rhythm, while Joyous's lake-water reflections breathe in freshness, giving the relationship both frame and flesh.

★ Aspirations speak as one: Joyous's gift for dialogue gives precise voice to Duration's steadfast purpose, while Duration's persistent action lends every hearty conversation the weight of real fulfillment.
conflict: ◆ Obstinacy vs. carelessness: once Duration locks on a direction, it's hard to turn; it tends to see Joyous's quick shifts as a lack of staying power and grows anxious about unreliability.
◆ Frivolity vs. dullness: Joyous seeks immediate emotional resonance; if Duration goes years burying itself in work without saying a word, Joyous feels the relationship become a stagnant pool.
advice: Set aside a half-day each week for aimless chats. Duration should lay its plans aside and simply share; Joyous should take the initiative to offer a specific word of affirmation at the key moments when Duration holds firm, turning emotional support into grounded reality.

one_liner: You keep us grounded, I keep us moving — this duo is built to last a lifetime.
analysis: The hexagram Duration is rock-solid, devoted to standing firm and never shifting its ground; thunder and wind clash yet move in step, all about deep feeling and stubborn persistence. The hexagram Dispersion is like flowing water — wind moving over water, dissolving what is blocked, a cure for rigid minds and stuck hearts. When these two meet, it is not a collision but the kindred understanding of an anchor and a sail. Duration provides the bedrock, so that Dispersion's flow never becomes a headless scramble; Dispersion provides the breathing hole, keeping Duration's resolve from hardening into brittle stone. In real life, this is the executor who tracks every milestone of a long-term project paired with the creative who loves to brainstorm breakthroughs. Duration fears change, Dispersion fears holding on; but together, they use Duration to establish the root and Dispersion to navigate transformation. Without Duration's steadiness, Dispersion's scattering is just chaotic thrashing; without Dispersion's clearing, Duration's persistence is just tunnel vision. Woven together, they can stir dead water into life, and carry living water far.
resonance: ★ Anchoring and Breakthrough: Duration's bottom-line thinking gives Dispersion's reshuffling a safe harbor, making every dispersal a step toward a stronger gathering.
★ Rooting and Ventilation: Thunder and wind's tenacious endurance paired with wind-over-water agility — one secures the big direction, the other blows away internal friction.
conflict: ◆ Stubbornness vs. Free-Spiritedness: Duration, once locked on a path, never looks back, and can find Dispersion too flighty; Dispersion wants to adapt and pivot, and finds Duration too rigid.

◆ Clinging vs. Letting Go: Duration wants to grip the status quo for safety, while Dispersion insists on cutting what must be cut and scattering what must be scattered; when rhythms are off, they can easily pull against each other.
advice: When disagreements arise, first have the Duration side set three non-negotiable bottom lines, then let the Dispersion side experiment freely within those lines — replace head-on persuasion with freedom inside a framework.

one_liner: If you want to go the distance, learn to grit your teeth when it's time to push through—and hit the brakes when it's time to stop.
analysis: Duration (Hexagram 32) carries thunder's decisiveness and wind's endurance: once it sets a course, it forges ahead through storm and calm—the essence of loyal constancy. Limitation (Hexagram 60), by contrast, borrows water's flow and the lake's boundaries, focusing on control and proportion. When these two energies merge, it's like a long-distance off-road vehicle equipped with a seasoned navigator. Duration supplies the stable, low-drama foundation; Limitation adjusts the tempo and draws the red lines at key moments. Without Duration's resilience, Limitation turns into capricious micro-managing; without Limitation's clarity, Duration becomes stubbornly banging against a wall. The Image reminds us: 'Galling limitation must not be persisted in,' a timely warning for Duration: constancy doesn't mean rigidity. Balance persistence with adaptability—that's how a relationship gains staying power.
resonance: ★ Same rhythm: Duration's staying power meets Limitation's sense of tempo. The two move at a calm, unhurried pace and can steadily bring long-term plans to life.
★ Balanced tension: Limitation's sense of proportion reins in Duration's forward drive, preventing reckless burnout and making every effort count.
conflict: ◆ Rules vs. resolve: Duration sticks to its principles and won't yield; Limitation loves to lay down rules. The two may pull against each other over when flexibility is needed.
◆ Suppressed friction: if Limitation turns moderation into over-restraint, Duration's long-term expectations will be dashed—holding it in too long only hurts the relationship.
advice: Set aside half a day each week as 'No Rules Day.' Put away the measuring stick of restraint and let Duration's resilience breathe naturally—don't let your sense of proportion harden into coldness.

one_liner: You keep to the old ways and steady steps; I give you all my heart—with each passing day, it becomes pure Kindred.
analysis: The Duration hexagram is about standing firm in an unchanging direction—like a stabilizing needle in the sea, once it sets a course, it sees it through to the end. The Inner Truth hexagram is a gentle breeze over the lake, focused on open-hearted sincerity that softens the rigid with the tender. When these two meet, it's as if living emotional water is poured into the cause of long-term commitment. Duration's steadiness gives Inner Truth's authenticity a sturdy chassis that never flips; Inner Truth's flexibility dissolves the stubborn rigidity that Duration can fall into. Thunder and wind are meant to move swiftly, but with Inner Truth's lake water supporting them, the pair becomes a slow-but-sure companionship that outlasts the hurried. One builds the frame, the other fills in the flesh; after years together, a single glance tells you whether the other needs stability or comfort.
resonance: ★ Steady in rhythm: Duration locks on a direction and holds firm; Inner Truth gives wholehearted cooperation. Once you two tune in, you can support each other and go far.
★ Melting principles with feeling: The breeze over the water catches the impatience of thunder and wind, gradually softening cold rules with empathy, without hurting the harmony.
conflict: ◆ Sticking to rules too rigidly: Duration's emphasis on an unchanging course can dismiss Inner Truth's flexible emotional needs as fussing, making it seem impersonal.
◆ Being led by emotions: When Inner Truth prioritizes the present feeling, it may adjust the rhythm too often, directly disrupting Duration's methodical long-term planning.
advice: When disagreements arise, first use Duration's logic to clarify the bottom line, then offer Inner Truth's empathy to give the other a way out—don't insist on who's right in the heat of the moment.

one_liner: One wants to run a marathon; the other insists you tie your shoelaces before you start. They bicker, but they're inseparable.
analysis: The hexagram Heng's 'standing firm without changing course' is a long-term mentality that picks a direction and follows it all the way—thunder and wind drive each other, and all the momentum lives in persistent forward motion. Xiao Guo, meanwhile, is the 'better to stay low than rise high' detail-obsessive: thunder pressed against the mountaintop, energy turned inward, devoted to over-preparation and self-restraint in small matters. Both carry the same impulsive thunder energy, but they land in completely different ways: Heng builds the skeleton and sets the tone; Xiao Guo works through the fine print and hits the brakes. Heng's stubbornness tends to overlook real-world friction; Xiao Guo's caution often seems narrow-minded. But together, they stitch long-term goals and short-term fault tolerance into a seamless whole. As long as they don't call each other too rigid or too timid, they're a rock-solid pair for getting life done.
resonance: ★ Shared fundamental drive: both carry the initial thunderous momentum—one nails down the big direction, the other thoroughly works out the small details, so they act with both long-term vision and concrete handles.
★ Similar instinct for avoiding risk: Heng seeks blameless steadiness; Xiao Guo seeks to stay low and hidden. When waves come, both instinctively tighten up defensively and protect their base first.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched pace: Heng clings to a position and refuses to look back, seeing the other as slow and procrastinating; Xiao Guo deliberates endlessly, afraid of overstepping, seeing the other as reckless. Communication easily degenerates into a dead loop of rushing progress versus obsessing over details.

◆ Conflicting standards for error tolerance: Heng values outcomes and endurance, thinking Xiao Guo wastes energy on trivialities; Xiao Guo values measure and restraint, thinking Heng's single-mindedness is blind confidence without flexibility.
advice: When they disagree, Heng should stop and listen to the hidden risks Xiao Guo points out; Xiao Guo should pick one or two small things and let Heng try them freely. Let the big direction set the tone and the small details be delegated, instead of wrestling with each other.

one_liner: One stretches the days into long, steady routine; the other finds leaks and patches them in times of peace.
analysis: The Duration (Heng) is thunder and wind spurring each other on — full of drive, yet seeking stability within motion. After Completion (Ji Ji) is water and fire working in harmony — but after success, the greatest fear is decline after the peak. Together, they are like a long-distance runner paired with a precision instrument inspector. Thunder's endurance lays a solid foundation for the relationship, while water's penetrating nature ferrets out flaws and nips problems in the bud. Yet the Duration's 'stand firm, change not' can easily harden into obstinate stubbornness, and After Completion's 'good beginning, chaotic end' anxiety can morph into daily nagging. If the Duration can leave room for adjustment and heed warnings, and After Completion can release its fixation on perfect closure, this pair can evolve from merely killing time into nurturing real roots. The worst case: one accusing the other of fussing over nothing, the other accusing them of rigidity, turning a lifelong partnership into a war of attrition.
resonance: ★ Kindred chassis-and-radar resonance: The Duration's bold advance needs After Completion's meticulous verification — one dares to move, the other watches the road; a Complementary fit, just right.

★ Long-distance running meets regular check-up: After Completion's prevention-mindedness gives the Duration's endurance battle scheduled maintenance, so its 'unshakable direction' never becomes blind slogging.
conflict: ◆ Friction between obsessive axis and nagging mouth: The Duration clings to its logic without swerving, while After Completion nags daily about latent risks; over time, one starts feeling pestered, the other exhausted.

◆ Tug-of-war between stability and anxiety: After Completion, fearing a chaotic end, always wants to brake early, but the Duration's inertia is too strong; forced intervention only throws both rhythms completely off.
advice: Agree to reserve half a day each month for a review-tea session: the Duration brings only ears to hear warnings, and After Completion offers contingency plans without pouring cold water — turning daily nagging into scheduled maintenance.

one_liner: One holds the ground steady; the other crosses the river by feeling the stones.
analysis: The Duration hexagram is the "pillar that steadies the sea" of thunder and wind following in tandem; it prizes planting one's feet and tilling ever deeper, day after day. The Before Completion hexagram, in contrast, is a "half-finished article" with fire and water refusing to meet, the whole board a snarl still to be unraveled. When these two energies collide, it is just like a marathon coach paired with a sprint finisher. Duration's "favorable to have somewhere to go" gives Before Completion's "little fox nearly across" the assurance it won't capsize, so the wet-tailed fox dares to keep wading onward. And Before Completion's "careful discernment of things and places" can put the brakes on Duration's "standing without changing direction", warning it not to drive one lane into a dead end. Thunder's decisiveness encounters fire's experiments, wind's osmosis collides with water's flux: one keeps the straight path, the other springs the surprise, kneading "stubborn perseverance" and "flexible adaptation" into a living strategy that can actually be executed.
resonance: ★ Steadying the Foundation: Duration's enduring resolve can firmly brace Before Completion's transitional anxiety, letting the unkempt mess find a place to settle.
★ Careful Discernment Lays the Course: Before Completion's cautious classification helps Duration adjust its direction amid long-term persistence, preventing it from doggedly dead-ending on habit.
conflict: ◆ Tug-of-War over Tempo: Duration resents Before Completion's constant upheavals and lack of staying power; Before Completion faults Duration's rigid thinking and failure to adapt to circumstances.

◆ Fire and Water Misaligned: Duration wants thunder and wind to carry through in one unbroken line, but Before Completion's fire and water turn their backs and resist blending; the mismatched rhythms easily wear down each other's patience.
advice: Before making a plan, first use Before Completion's "careful discernment" to take stock of the current situation, then use Duration's "standing without changing direction" to stretch the execution cycle. Each week, adjust only the tactical moves, never the core strategy.

one_liner: You get my unspoken words, I know when you pull back. We both love the blank spaces—and that's why we feel most secure.
analysis: When two Dun hexagrams meet, there is no aggressive probing, only an unspoken sense of boundaries. The image of 'the mountain under heaven' is layered, as if two silent mountain peaks gaze at each other from afar, each preserving the decorum of 'not angrily but with dignity.' Neither of you is good at using ardor to hijack a relationship; instead, you know how to actively create space to breathe amid the noise. The Judgment, 'small and correct furthers,' points to the underlying tone of this connection: not to pursue a dramatic bond, but to seek a steady, long-lasting peace. This kind of synchronized retreat filters out the drain of meaningless social interactions and establishes a trust that requires no words. But if both sides only defend and never advance, the connection can easily grow cold within politeness. True kindred means not always keeping distance, but knowing when to take a gentle step forward for the other.
resonance: ★ Kindred Blank Space: Both deeply understand the measure of 'not angrily but with dignity,' and can hold each other up without forced warmth.
★ Synchronized Advance and Retreat: When faced with turmoil, you instinctively choose to step back; a single glance tells you when to quietly exit.
conflict: ◆ Excessive Withdrawal: Both tend to retreat, and when key conflicts arise, neither is likely to break the ice, turning cold treatment into a real cold war.

◆ Overly Thick Boundaries: Each keeps the defense mechanism of distancing from petty people on full, which actually shuts out genuine feelings; over time, you become like strangers sharing an apartment.
advice: Agree to have one unguarded deep conversation each month, and take turns sharing a small vulnerable thing, turning the inertia of retreat into a rhythmic approach.

one_liner: Dodges the blade's edge, yet holds the stage.
analysis: The Retreat hexagram is like a mountain shadow in the clouds, teaching the wisdom of knowing when to yield and hold; Great Power resembles thunder from the ninth heaven, showing the courage to press forward. Their meeting is a dialogue between a deep pool and a plunging waterfall: Retreat's withdrawal is not cowardice—it gathers momentum for Great Power's eruption; Great Power's resolve is not recklessness—Retreat's lucidity teaches it how to measure give and take. When Retreat draws the line with 'dignity without hostility,' Great Power calibrates its course with 'no step beyond propriety,' forging a dynamic balance of retreat that guards the heart and advance that accomplishes the task.
resonance: ★ Stillness and motion in harmony: Retreat's concealment offers Great Power a strategic buffer, and Great Power's breakthrough creates a turning point for Retreat.
★ Shared principles: both value bottom-line thinking—Retreat protects its integrity through distance, Great Power disciplines force through ritual and law.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythms: Retreat's caution is easily misread as hesitation by Great Power, and Great Power's decisiveness may breach Retreat's protective net.
◆ Friction of bearing: Retreat's detachment can sting Great Power's frankness, while Great Power's pressure may trigger Retreat's over-defense.
advice: When facing a matter, first use Retreat thinking to observe the situation and draw clear boundaries; once the time is ripe, borrow Great Power's momentum to act decisively. Above all, avoid losing your principles while yielding or overstepping the rules while advancing.

one_liner: One slams the brakes and reads the wind; the other floors it and takes the high ground. As partners, they never drain each other with infighting.
analysis: The Retreat hexagram is like a clear breeze on a high mountain, urging a lucid withdrawal that is 'stern without hostility.' The Progress hexagram is like the morning sun breaking forth at dawn, pursuing an exalted advance that 'illumines virtue through itself.' These two energies seem to run in opposite directions, yet they secretly echo the rhythm of breathing. Retreat's withdrawal is meant to avoid futile consumption and clear a clean track for Progress's advance; Progress's light opens the way with real merits, so that Retreat's watchfulness does not sink into passive escapism. When Progress breaks through the impasse with high profile in front of the stage, Retreat filters out noise and draws red lines behind the scenes. If Progress's edge becomes too sharp and invites envy, Retreat's cool eye that 'keeps the petty man at a distance' is the safest breakwater. When the two meet, there is less blind internal competition and more ease in knowing when to advance and retreat—just like the 'striker and strategist' setup among trusted old partners.
resonance: ★ Rhythmic Complementarity: the Progress hexagram's breakthrough drive fills the gaps in the Retreat hexagram's contraction, so pullback never becomes standing still.
★ Shared Bottom Line: both are principled to the core—one stands tall through brightness, the other protects itself with distance—and neither has any use for empty show.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned Tempo: Progress wants immediate exposure and results, while Retreat feels the timing isn't ripe yet and keeps wanting to step back half a pace to watch.

◆ Communication Climate Gap: Progress likes to put everything on the table and talk it out; Retreat prefers to be certain internally without saying much—so each can see the other as too impatient or too cold.
advice: When the Progress side is pushing forward, don't pressure the Retreat side to take a stand right away; give a three-day buffer. Once the Retreat side spots the right moment, offering a proactive list of pitfalls works ten times better than silently observing.

one_liner: One knows when to step back, the other knows how to hide their light; together they're survival partners in complex situations.
analysis: Hexagram Dun (Retreat), Mountain over Heaven, advocates actively pulling back and drawing boundaries with 'firmness without hostility'; Hexagram Mingyi (Darkening of the Light), Earth over Fire, stresses sheathing one's brilliance in adversity and protecting the core by 'using darkness to stay bright'. Their interplay is a Kindred conspiracy about 'how to survive with dignity'. Dun provides a sense of space; Mingyi provides endurance. One extends outward to keep clear of foul air, the other turns inward to hide its light and outlast the dark night. They don't compete in high-profile attacks; instead they share a low-key survival wisdom: when it's time to retreat, don't cling; when it's time to hide, don't show off. In complex environments, they quickly sense risk and act as shields for each other. But if one wants a complete cut and the other chooses to hunker down in place, the misaligned pace can give rise to hidden reefs.
resonance: ★ Kindred reserved space: both know that silence is sometimes more powerful than argument, naturally giving each other breathing room as a buffer.
★ Bottom-line resonance: one actively stays away from draining sources, the other knows how to sheathe their edge to protect themselves; the logic of guarding the core is highly consistent.
conflict: ◆ Pace tug-of-war: Dun tends to break away cleanly and cut contact, while Mingyi is used to silently toughing it out in place; the rhythm of staying or leaving easily gets out of sync.
◆ Emotional temperature gap: Dun steps back for peace, but Mingyi swallows the grievance and toughs it out; if the cold treatment drags on, it can quietly breed internal friction.
advice: When under pressure, don't rush to cut contact or tough it out. Agree on a three-day cooling-off window, then decide together whether to make a graceful retreat or continue lying low.

one_liner: You take half a step back, I add a little more fuel to the fire—close without clinging, at just the right distance.
analysis: Dun (The Retreat) – 'a mountain under heaven' – prizes withdrawing without rancor, keeping a stern inner discipline, and stepping back from the clamor to hold one's spiritual ground. Jia Ren (The Family) – 'wind rises from fire' – requires speech with substance and conduct with constancy, turning everyday chores into order and warmth. When these two meet, it is a kindred interplay of 'leaving blank space' and 'filling in the colors.' The Retreat's nature runs to coolness and detachment, while the Family's wind and fire carry the scent of hearth and smoke. One keeps the noise of the world outside the courtyard; the other keeps the days inside spick-and-span. When Retreat longs to disappear, Family does not cling—it only quietly leaves the light on. When Family's rules turn rigid, Retreat's wisdom of stepping back reminds both sides to keep a lucid distance. With one stepping back and the other stepping forward, the sense of boundary is stewed into a sense of security.
resonance: ★ A sense of boundaries is a sense of security: Retreat knows proportion, Family honors rules, and neither oversteps—so being together feels steady and effortless.
★ Hearth-warmth heals coolness: The Family's steady words and deeds easily catch the Retreat's distancing tendency, turning solitude into tender companionship.
conflict: ◆ The tug between closing the door and knocking: Retreat habitually shuts the door to process things alone, while Family craves livelier communion—so concern can easily become intrusion.

◆ The rub between strict rules and free-spirited ease: Family seeks a steady tempo of word and deed, while Retreat tends to flexibly retreat when things come up—off-beat rhythms can breed silent frustration.
advice: Agree in advance on 'do-not-disturb windows' and 'family-sharing moments.' Replace emotional guesswork with explicit agreements, so both stepping back and drawing close have a clear basis.

one_liner: You don't force your way in, I don't force myself to fit; leaving a little space makes things most solid.
analysis: Retreat's nature is like a mountain holding up the sky—it carries a clear-eyed detachment, values being stern without being harsh, and draws interpersonal boundaries plainly. Opposition, on the other hand, is fire leaping upward and the lake flowing downward—naturally moving in opposite directions, yet it understands how to stay united in difference and find small agreements within divergence. When these two hexagrams come together, it's not sticky, clingy warmth but clear-eyed adult socializing. One instinctively steps back to leave a safe zone; the other doesn't chase after asking why the distance grew, but instead goes along with the differences and looks for intersections on its own track. Heaven's loftiness meets Fire's leaping without draining each other—it's like installing a buffer cushion in the relationship. After spending time together, you realize that this kind of non-in-your-face bond is the most durable, because both understand: respecting the other's retreat is the highest form of closeness.
resonance: ★ Kindred Boundary Awareness: Retreat naturally has a clear social distance, and Opposition's seeking common ground despite differences just catches that non-sticky rhythm—neither easily crosses the line to test.

★ The Real Test Is in Small Things: Opposition's focus on small matters being auspicious pairs with Retreat's pragmatic low-key style; the two of you can't be bothered with grand narratives, and instead build trust through everyday helping hands.
conflict: ◆ A Temperature Gap in Tempo: Retreat's nature is cool and restrained, preferring to stay still; Opposition's fiery side loves to probe outward and talk differences through—so they can easily misjudge each other as cold or overly serious.

◆ Retreat Meets Tug-and-Pull: In conflict, Retreat tends to withdraw and handle things coldly, while Opposition tends to spread out the differences and argue them through; the mismatched pace can let small issues drag into emotional knots.
advice: Agree on “don't ask why the other withdrew, but send a light signal regularly”—replace deep entanglement with sharing a song or a short greeting, letting the distance stay naturally fresh.

one_liner: Taking a step back isn't cowardice; it's waiting for the waters to recede and the mountain path to appear.
analysis: The Dun hexagram teaches one to withdraw in good time to avoid calamity; the Jian hexagram instructs facing obstacles directly to cultivate oneself. Both lower trigrams are Mountain, symbolizing that at their core, both people share a foundation of 'standing firm when danger approaches.' Dun's retreat is not escapism; it creates breathing room for Jian's assault on difficulties. Jian's hardship acts like a mirror, reflecting when Dun should pull back and when it should advance. Heaven is lofty and detached; Water is practical and penetrating. One surveys the situation from the clouds, the other wades through the mud. The Mountain foundation underneath steadies both: the one who retreats does not become passive, and the one who attacks does not act rashly. Together they form an implicit rhythm of 'concealing the blade in defense, breaking through through self-cultivation.'
resonance: ★ Shared Mountain Foundation: Both lower trigrams are Gen (Mountain). When danger arises, instinct is to plant one's feet firmly—no blind charges, no panicked retreats.
★ Water and Mountain complement each other: Jian's perils need Dun's yielding as a buffer; Dun's seclusion borrows Jian's moral cultivation to calibrate its direction.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Pace of Advance and Retreat: Dun advocates seizing the moment to pull out, while Jian emphasizes stubbornly breaking through. They tend to pull at odds over 'when to stop.'

◆ Different Vantage Points: Dun looks down on the big picture from above; Jian stays close to the ground figuring out details. When making decisions, they may find each other 'out of touch' or 'not clear-headed enough.'
advice: When hitting a bottleneck, the Dun side steps back half a step to define clear boundaries, then the Jian side steps forward half a step to break down the process. Replace all-or-nothing confrontation with a 'phased approach.'

one_liner: One is busy drawing clear boundaries; the other is a master at untangling life's stubborn knots.
analysis: The Retreat hexagram is like heaven covering a high mountain—its art lies in pulling back to preserve the field and marking clear boundaries. The Deliverance hexagram is like spring thunder shattering ice—its keynote is swift action that cuts through tangles and lets old grievances go. When these two meet, it is not a clash of forces but a relay between space and motion. Retreat's way of keeping petty people at a distance may look cold, yet it actually creates a buffer for Deliverance's forgiveness of faults and pardon of errors; without room to withdraw, thunder and rain would only brew a hurricane. Deliverance's timely intervention, in turn, dissolves the aloof deadlock that Retreat is prone to. It is like a messy situation: one person steps back and refuses to get caught in internal friction, while the other seizes the moment, striking while the iron is hot, and turns the page on old accounts. Heaven above stays still; thunder below breaks the deadlock. One handles the damage control, the other handles the reset—a profoundly clever crisis partnership.
resonance: ★ Space Breeds Clarity: The Retreat hexagram's active yielding clears room for the Deliverance hexagram to act, giving pent-up conflicts a place to land and dissolve.
