★ Discipline as a safety net: the Power of the Great's principled bottom line and Gathering Together's contingency planning combine, making cooperation both methodical and full of fallbacks.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: the Power of the Great wants a quick decisive battle, but Gathering Together insists on steady advances; the tug-of-war over progress breeds anxiety.
◆ Hard-soft friction: the Power of the Great's blunt directness may shatter Gathering Together's refined defenses; they need to soften the edges of their communication.
advice: Before acting, the Power of the Great should proactively sync its risk checklist with Gathering Together, and when Gathering Together makes plans, it should leave flexible room for the Power of the Great to adjust.

one_liner: One floors the gas to clear the way, the other digs deep to root down; as partners, they run the long haul without flipping over.
analysis: Great Strength's 'thunder above heaven' carries the momentum of breaking through; Pushing Upward's 'wood grows from the earth' is all about slow simmering. Put them together, and it's like a lightning bolt splitting frozen ground, then rain seeping through the cracks to nourish a sapling. Great Strength fears overreaching; Pushing Upward fears growing too slowly. But Great Strength's 'does not tread on what is improper' just puts the brakes on Pushing Upward's rash impulses, while Pushing Upward's 'accumulate the small to reach high and great' lays a cushion of soft landing for Great Strength's thunderbolt momentum. This relationship isn't a fleeting spark — it's a long-term game of 'break through first, then cultivate deeply.' Great Strength opens the road and splits the mountain; Pushing Upward takes the foundation and tamps it inch by inch. Together they move upward with steady, unshakable steps.
resonance: ★ Thunder splits the soil: Great Strength's ferocious force can instantly break a deadlock, giving Pushing Upward's slow growth room to drill upward.
★ Rules nurture the roots: Great Strength's 'does not tread on what is improper' just draws a safe boundary for Pushing Upward's 'accumulate small into great,' so the growth never goes off track.
conflict: ◆ The speed gap: Great Strength is used to thunder and lightning, while Pushing Upward goes with the current; when the impatient meet the methodical, both tend to fret over the other.
◆ Misaligned force: Great Strength's energy is too blunt, and it can easily shake loose the foundation Pushing Upward so carefully built — good intentions, bad outcomes.
advice: Before Great Strength makes a move, count three seconds to give Pushing Upward room to root; when Pushing Upward hits a snag, don't just tough it out — borrow Great Strength's momentum to break through.

relationship_name: The Power of the Great & Oppression: Mutual Tempering
one_liner: One runs at full battery and loves to charge ahead; the other stays in power-saving mode and stubbornly holds the line. Together they learn to win by staying steady.
analysis: Thunder moves across the sky in The Power of the Great; its force is imposing, but its greatest fear is overstepping the line — it must act within the rules. Oppression is a drained lake at the bottom; resources are spent, yet it tempers a fierce resolve to see its will through. When these two first meet, it's like a full-battery engine crashing into a powerless machine: the Great Power wants to break the deadlock with brute force, while Oppression simply endures in silence. But stay long enough and you'll understand: Oppression's aridity can restrain the Great Power's impulsiveness, forcing it to pull its thunderbolts back into the framework of 'no steps that violate propriety'; and the Great Power's ability to break through is exactly the torch handed to someone almost spent in a dead end. One teaches when to rein in; the other teaches when to give it everything. Energy is exchanged between movement and endurance, and hard against hard grinds out real gold.
resonance: ★ Thunder moves the spring: The Power of the Great's breakthrough momentum can split open the stagnant waters of Oppression, letting a dried-up environment flow again.
★ Oppression holds the anchor: Oppression's tenacious grip on its bottom line in desperate straits is exactly what tethers the Great Power's runaway horse.
conflict: ◆ Loquacity breeds error: The Power of the Great tends to make a loud noise, while Oppression knows that words are not believed; too much talk seems flippant and easily leads to mutual misunderstanding.
◆ Extreme hardness breaks: If the Power of the Great forces ahead regardless of the other's depleted state, Oppression's fragile foundation will be shattered, causing internal friction instead.
advice: Before the Power of the Great makes its move, it should ask whether the rule is worth breaking; when Oppression can no longer hold on, it shouldn't just endure in silence — instead, lay the gap open so the Great Power can fill it precisely.

one_liner: One charges ahead to clear the path, the other sinks deep to nurture the people; don't just rely on brute force — keep a well that slowly soaks the ground.
analysis: Great Strength is like thunder suspended in the sky, energy radiating outward and splitting all obstacles; yet its hexagram warns, 'Do not tread paths that are not proper,' reminding us that fierceness must be bridled. The Well, on the other hand, is a deep spring under wood, constant and silently nourishing, but it cautions, 'A broken jug brings misfortune,' telling us not to draw water too hastily. When these two meet, Thunder's explosive power can break any deadlock in an instant, while the Well's holding capacity keeps the foundation steady and prevents exhaustion. Great Strength borrows the Well's steadiness to learn restraint; the Well borrows Thunder's momentum to avoid becoming stagnant. As long as Great Strength does not cross the line and the Well does not seek credit prematurely, this relationship can stitch together the adventurous drive of expanding frontiers and the quiet confidence of a long, steady flow — creating a pattern of rooted expansion.
resonance: ★ Boundaries and Knowing When to Stop: Great Strength's 'do not tread improper paths' and the Well's 'broken jug brings misfortune' both emphasize a sense of limits — one holds back with rules, the other draws water with patience; both understand that overstepping always leads to a fall.

★ Action and Stillness Fill Each Other's Gaps: Thunder's burst can quickly break through and open a path, while the Well's constancy keeps the nourishment flowing. One leads the offense, the other handles the logistics — together they are a pair that can both strike and hold.
conflict: ◆ Clashing Tempos: Great Strength is used to swift, thunderous action and quick results; the Well believes in slow, careful work and letting things settle. One accuses the other of dragging, the other accuses the one of being rash — so their momentum tends to grind against each other.

◆ Clashing Values: Great Strength values visible, immediate victories; the Well values quiet, long-term nourishment. When 'I want outcomes' collides with 'you need to let the process steep,' they easily blame each other for not knowing how to manage things.
advice: Set an alternating rhythm of 'charge and replenish': after Great Strength concentrates its firepower on a breakthrough, always leave a set period for the Well to take stock of resources and tend to people's hearts. Do not run on continuous overdraft.

one_liner: One floors the gas and charges ahead; the other watches the stoplights and waits for the moment. Hit it right, and it's a breakthrough bomb.
analysis: Great Power is 'thunder in heaven' — an explosion of energy, yet it emphasizes 'no stepping where propriety forbids,' meaning this raw force must be harnessed by discipline, not let loose to charge blindly. The Revolution hexagram is 'fire in the lake' — water and fire clash, forcing transformation. Its core lies in 'winning trust when the time is ripe' and 'regulating calendars to clarify the seasons' — discerning the right moment, breaking the old, and establishing the new. When these two hexagrams come together, it's like a tamed lion meeting a precision scalpel. Great Power supplies the absolute momentum for breakthrough; Revolution calibrates the timing and precision of the cut. Without Great Power's ferocity, revolution becomes mere talk; without Revolution's sense of timing, Great Power's strength turns into reckless destruction. The two pull between 'upholding what is right' and 'seeking change,' finally achieving an uncanny balance of 'making revolution within the rules.' Energetically, thunder's directness and the lake's tolerance polish each other, forging pure brute force into a well-ordered power of breakthrough.
resonance: ★ Thunder in motion needs fire: Great Power's raw strength needs the Revolution hexagram's timing to ignite, otherwise it burns away in futile blind effort.
★ Lake water can contain strength: Revolution's inclusiveness and adaptability catch Great Power's momentum, turning destructive force into a driver for systemic upgrade.
conflict: ◆ Upholding propriety fears breakthrough: Great Power's boundary-conscious 'step only where rites allow' clashes with Revolution's impulse to 'break the old and establish the new,' causing repeated tug-of-war over whether to cross the line.

◆ Impetuous charging resents waiting: Great Power is naturally impatient and wants immediate results, while Revolution insists on the waiting period of 'gaining trust at the right time' — one finds the other too slow, the other too restless.
advice: When disagreement arises, set a timeline before acting: break Great Power's execution into Revolution's rhythm, using a series of small wins instead of one big overthrow.

one_liner: One cleaves through deadlocks, the other simmers a new brew—together, they break down only to build anew.
analysis: Da Zhuang (The Power of the Great) charges forward with thunderous might, holding the bottom line of 'never treading on what is improper.' Ding (The Cauldron) works like a slow, gentle fire, focusing on the deep settling of 'right position and confirmed mandate.' Thunder's raw force needs the alchemy of fire to stay in control, while fire's transformative renewal depends on thunder's momentum to break ground. When these two meet, the Power of the Great supplies the edge to cut through impasses, and the Cauldron takes charge of reshaping order—but thunder's impatience often clashes with the Cauldron's caution, and fire's patient endurance looks down on thunder's haste. The key is to turn the Power of the Great's steadfastness ('li zhen') into the Cauldron's foundation of 'primal good fortune' ('yuan ji'), allowing impulsive energy to settle into lasting innovation.
resonance: ★ Creation through destruction: the Power of the Great's momentum splits the old framework, and the Cauldron's furnace immediately casts a new structure.
★ Integrity sparks renewal: the bottom-line awareness of 'never treading on what is improper' and the calm resolve of 'right position, confirmed mandate' are a natural fit.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned rhythms: lightning-quick decisions from the Power of the Great leave the Cauldron's slow, meticulous craft struggling to keep up.
◆ Clash of standards: the Power of the Great wants to overturn the table and rewrite the rules, while the Cauldron insists on tending the fire by ancient methods.
advice: Before the Power of the Great strikes, have the Cauldron draw up the blueprints; as the Cauldron adds fuel, remember to leave an amplifier for the thunder.

one_liner: Both are rolling thunder — one brakes with rules, the other steadies the wheel with self-reflection. Put them together, and you've got the steadiest pair for a thunderstorm.
analysis: Da Zhuang (The Power of the Great) and Zhen (The Arousing) share the upper trigram Thunder, and both harbor explosive power not to be underestimated. Da Zhuang is 'thunder in the sky' — magnificent in momentum, yet it insists on 'refusing to tread where propriety forbids.' It's like a heavy truck at full throttle, knowing how to use rules to control its inertia. Zhen, by contrast, is 'thunder repeated' — a chain of booms — and its theme is 'fear and inner reflection.' It's more like a stabilizing anchor that can keep a wine glass steady in the middle of a thunderstorm. When the two meet, their outer energies easily resonate on the same frequency, and their drive hits full throttle. But Da Zhuang tends to overstep from sheer force, while Zhen habitually turns inward when startled. Their chemistry isn't about one overpowering the other; it's the complementary rhythm of 'outward thrust' and 'inward containment': Da Zhuang supplies the charging momentum to break deadlocks, and Zhen handles recalibrating the center of gravity in turmoil. As long as one doesn't act rashly and the other doesn't drain itself with self-rumination, they're a golden team that can shoulder heavy loads.
resonance: ★ Natural chemistry: Both are thunder-natured — when it's time to act, they move with a clean, no-nonsense drive, and communication needs almost no warm-up.

★ Kindred crisis response: Da Zhuang dares to charge ahead and clear the path, while Zhen excels at steadying the footing in sudden emergencies — in a pinch, they can swap driver and navigator seamlessly.
conflict: ◆ Rhythms can collide: Da Zhuang favors striking with the flow and pushing forward at all costs, while Zhen tends to startle first, then steady, and advance step by step. In the gap between fast and slow, they can easily trip each other up.

◆ Emotional outlets are mismatched: Da Zhuang digs in and resists head-on when blocked, while Zhen leans toward internal rumination under pressure. One finds the other too rigid; the other finds the one too restless.
advice: Set clear roles for action and stillness: Da Zhuang takes the outer frontier and expands territory; Zhen handles the inner work of risk assessment. When an issue arises, pause three minutes first — settle accounts after the thunder rolls.

one_liner: One steps on the gas while the other pulls the handbrake, but they both keep the steering wheel welded to the rules.
analysis: The thunder of Great Strength hangs over the heavens, its energy bursting outward with fierce aggression—yet it is held in check by the iron rule of 'never treading where propriety forbids.' Gen, meanwhile, piles mountain upon mountain, governing restraint and inner guard, drawing clear lines by 'keeping thoughts from straying beyond one's station.' These two hexagrams seem to be polar opposites—one all motion, the other all stillness—yet at their core, both are wrestling with a sense of measure. Without Gen as a ballast, Great Strength's brute force easily becomes a headless fly careening off the walls; without Great Strength to break the pattern, Gen's stillness can turn into a deadlock of spinning in place. Their chemical reaction is to pack explosive energy into a voltage stabilizer. Great Strength leads the charge, clearing the way; Gen surveys and sets the red lines. So long as they both hold to the common ground of knowing when to stop and abiding by the rules, they can forge a working rhythm that is round on the outside, square on the inside—an even, measured pace that knows when to give and when to hold.
resonance: ★ Boundary Consensus: Both place tremendous stock in rules and proportion—one uses ritual to curb impulses, the other uses role-awareness to steady the mind.

★ Complementary Dynamism: Great Strength's thunder energy can break through stalemates, while Gen's mountain nature supplies a steady foundation—working together, they act with ferocity and stability.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Disconnect: Great Strength finds Gen too slow and dull, muddling through tasks; Gen finds Great Strength too rash and impatient, risking overstepping and overturning.

◆ Temperamental Contrast: Great Strength likes to push straight ahead with head-on confrontation; Gen prefers to absorb in silence and let things cool down, which can leave Great Strength feeling splashed with cold water.
advice: Before Great Strength makes a move, let Gen first map out the action's red lines. When Gen is stuck at a bottleneck, borrow Great Strength's momentum to take the first step—don't just rely on thinking.

relationship_name: The Firm and the Steady, Aiding Each Other
one_liner: One wants to floor the gas pedal; the other insists on buckling up and driving slowly. They bicker, but neither can live without the other.
analysis: Great Strength is thunder above heaven—full battery, yet its Judgment cautions, 'do not tread on what is not proper,' reminding us that even the mightiest force must respect the limits. Development is wind brushing the mountain wood, emphasizing gradual progress and 'dwelling in virtuous goodness to improve customs,' all about steady, methodical steps. When these two hexagrams meet, it's like an impatient vanguard meeting a cautious strategist. Great Strength tears open the situation; Development cements the gains. Without Great Strength's drive, Development risks wallowing in lukewarm inertia; without Development's buffer, Great Strength's 'strength' easily becomes 'recklessness.' Energetically, the thunder's stir is absorbed by the mountain's weight, and the wind's infiltration teaches thunder's blunt force to bend around obstacles. In real life, this pairing doesn't fear a hard sprint; it fears losing steam mid-course. Keep the shared bottom line of 'steadfastness and the right' intact, and Great Strength's explosive power will climb Development's staircase and grow into a towering tree.
resonance: ★ Shared roots in integrity: Both hexagrams' Judgments say 'favorable to be steadfast,' showing that both people are principled at heart and don't play empty games, but Great Strength leads with toughness while Development roots with patience.

★ Mutual nourishment: Great Strength's thunderous energy provides the spring rain for Development's mountain woods to break through the soil, while Development's nurturing qi gives Great Strength lasting stamina, without inner friction.
conflict: ◆ Clashing rhythms: Great Strength finds Development's step-by-step approach too slow, wanting a quick win; Development finds Great Strength too rash, fearing that too large a stride will tear the roots.

◆ Boundary tug-of-war: Great Strength is used to pushing through by force, easily crossing the red line of 'do not tread on what is not proper'; Development stubbornly insists on procedures and propriety, appearing cold and unfeeling.
advice: Break big goals into quarterly milestones. Let Great Strength tackle the tough bones, and let Development build the stage and review. Set a fixed day each month to 'check in' and use progress bars instead of emotional tug-of-war.

relationship_name: Thunder Bond of Firm and Yielding
one_liner: One charges ahead, the other calculates carefully—thunder paired with raindrops can build a home.
analysis: The hexagram Great Strength depicts thunder over heaven, fierce and ascending, yet it heeds the rule 'Do not tread where propriety forbids'—like a powerhouse who acts on principle. The hexagram Returning Maiden shows thunder over the lake, tied to marriage yet its judgment warns 'to march is ominous,' and the Image teaches 'know the end and guard against decay'—like a meticulous planner always watching for pitfalls. The upper trigrams are both thunder, sharing the DNA of change and decisiveness, but the lower trigrams—Heaven and Lake—are one firm, one yielding, igniting a unique chemistry: Great Strength's momentum pushes Returning Maiden forward, while Returning Maiden's caution reins Great Strength back from veering off course. But Returning Maiden's dire warnings often make Great Strength feel hamstrung, and Great Strength's blunt directness leaves Returning Maiden uneasy. This is no naturally synchronized match, but a partnership that needs to tune into each other—Great Strength learning to pull its punches, Returning Maiden learning to turn worry into actionable plans. Over time, firmness and yielding harmonize, and things get done with stability.
resonance: ★ Acting with restraint: both Great Strength's 'do not tread where propriety forbids' and Returning Maiden's 'know the end and guard against decay' emphasize foreseeing consequences before acting and avoiding blind impulse.
★ Shared thunder: both upper trigrams are Thunder, sharing decisiveness and adaptability—when crisis hits, they respond with kindred understanding.
conflict: ◆ Drive meets the brakes: Great Strength's decisive moves are often interrupted by Returning Maiden's cautious warnings, slowing things down.
◆ Optimism collides with pessimism: Great Strength believes force can break through, while Returning Maiden habitually anticipates risks—everyday communication easily turns into arguments.
advice: Before deciding, Great Strength should pull Returning Maiden into making a risk checklist, and Returning Maiden shouldn't just cry 'ominous'—offer concrete steps to respond instead.

one_liner: One brings force within the rules, the other makes the call with brilliant insight. Together, they're a thunderously decisive, unbeatable duo.
analysis: Both The Power of the Great and Abundance are rooted in the decisiveness of Thunder, but they express it in completely different ways. The Power of the Great is 'Thunder in the heavens,' carrying the inner firmness of Qian (The Creative) — the principle that no matter how great the power, it must respect the rules. Abundance is 'Thunder and lightning arriving together,' grounded in the penetrating clarity of Li (The Clinging) — the quest to judge right and wrong with absolute lucidity at the peak moment. When the two meet, it's like a strictly principled operator joining forces with a hawk-eyed judge; their combined momentum goes straight to the max. The Power of the Great's steadiness can temper Abundance's impatience, while Abundance's transparency can give The Power of the Great's ferocity a clear direction. However, if both simply charge forward, they risk a head-on collision that exhausts them both. The key is to blend uprightness with decisive insight — then, at the critical moment, they can strike a battle that is both steady and precise.
resonance: ★ Swift and resolute, no lingering: Both carry a 'let's get it done' energy. When a mess appears, they never blame each other — they just roll up their sleeves and fix it.

★ Strong alignment in principles and vision: The Power of the Great holds the line on rules, Abundance insists on clear right and wrong. Together, they naturally repel those who play sly games and cut corners.
conflict: ◆ Tempo clashes can cause friction: The Power of the Great likes to build step by step, setting up the rules first, while Abundance wants to settle everything in one stroke at the height of the moment.
◆ Excessive intensity can backfire: Both exude dominant energy. When opinions differ, they tend to hold their ground and forget to give each other a graceful way out.
advice: Don't reveal your trump card too early. Let The Power of the Great set the framework first, then have Abundance fill in the detailed standards. Separate 'upholding rules' from 'pursuing efficiency' into two clear steps.

one_liner: One plays it steady and sets the rules, the other travels light and scouts new paths — together they're an expedition duo that never flips.
analysis: Great Strength is thunder over heaven: enormous power, yet it stresses 'no stepping beyond propriety' — knowing how to set limits when strong. The Wanderer is fire on the mountain: flames spread but never linger, valuing clear-sighted caution and no dawdling. When the two meet, it's like a heavily equipped engineer meeting a light, fast scout. Great Strength's unyielding drive needs the Wanderer's agility to break through dead ends, or it will keep slamming into rigid rules; the Wanderer's rootless drifting needs Great Strength's bottom line as a safety net, or it will lose its footing in unfamiliar territory. The thunder's authority gives fire its direction; the fire's brightness lights the thunder's road. This isn't about one overpowering the other — it's 'adventure with boundaries': Great Strength builds the skeleton, the Wanderer fills in the flesh, so together they can shoulder the hard stuff and adapt to anything.
resonance: ★ Kindred sense of limits and flexibility: Great Strength's 'no stepping beyond propriety' draws the safe zone, and the Wanderer's 'clear-sighted caution' moves flexibly within it — neither crossing the line nor getting stuck in it.

★ Matching frequency of efficiency and decisiveness: the Wanderer's crisp 'no lingering over lawsuits' hits Great Strength's resolute 'perseverance brings reward' — no inner friction, just decide and execute.
conflict: ◆ Restlessness from mismatched rhythms: Great Strength likes to go step-by-step, but the Wanderer is like a wildfire, ready to switch lanes at any moment — each finds the other too slow or too flighty.

◆ Tug-of-war between control and freedom: Great Strength naturally carries the commanding presence of an anchor that steadies the sea, always wanting to set rules and manage things, while the Wanderer is a traveler at heart and can't stand being boxed in.
advice: Set your non-negotiable hard boundaries in advance, give plenty of room for trial and error within those boundaries, and do a fixed weekly review of progress — don't let dead rules choke off a living path.

one_liner: You charge ahead with bold, sweeping strokes; I weave through the cracks and take care of the details.
analysis: Great Power is like thunder suspended in the sky—fierce and formidable, governed by the principle 'do not tread what is not proper.' It acts with bottom lines and drive, but can be too blunt and prone to head-on collisions. The Gentle is wind—soft and yielding, yet able to slip through every crack. 'Repeating orders and carrying on affairs' is about going with the current and penetrating layer by layer. When these two come together, they exactly make up for each other's shortcomings: the thunderclap of Great Power holds the room and sets the rules; the wind of The Gentle quietly carries those rules down to the smallest detail. Without Great Power's iron spine, The Gentle can drift into spineless smoothness; without The Gentle's flexibility, Great Power is all too likely to knock itself bloody against a wall. Working as a pair, they are like a heavy hammer fitted with a fine needle—able to split open a stalemate, yet also able to follow the grain and handle matters with watertight thoroughness. As long as Great Power listens to advice and The Gentle doesn't micromanage, this is a golden combination of 'hard execution + soft finesse.'
resonance: ★ Thunder opens the road, wind delivers the message: Great Power's decisiveness breaks deadlocks instantly, and The Gentle's penetrative reach carries orders into every corner—together they work with striking efficiency.

★ Righteousness and surprise, a double safeguard: Great Power clings to bottom lines without crossing them, while The Gentle flexibly finds shortcuts. One keeps the direction true, the other keeps methods flowing—action is both steady and alive.
conflict: ◆ The rigid find the yielding too slow: Great Power prizes clean-cut action, can't stand The Gentle's probing and roundabout ways, and easily sees the other as indecisive and a drag on the team.

◆ The yielding find the rigid too bossy: The Gentle goes with the current, resents Great Power's one-size-fits-all toughness, and feels it leaves no breathing room—communication can easily cross fire.
advice: When differences arise, Great Power shouldn't rush to make the final call; give The Gentle half a day to break apart and refine the plan. The Gentle, for its part, shouldn't just keep whispering from the sidelines—lay the pros, cons, and alternate routes openly on the table, and then move in sync.

relationship_name: Thunder and Lake in Mutual Aid
one_liner: One is swift and thunderous, the other gentle and beaming; their quarrels sound like drumbeats, their laughter like spring breeze.
analysis: Great Strength is like spring thunder splitting the sky, carrying an undeniable virile momentum and honoring the boundary of "treading not on what is improper." The Joyous, like two overlapping lakes, moistens all things with soft ripples and excels at the roundabout communication of "friends discussing and practicing." When thunder crashes into still water, the principled rigidity of the strong clings against the tolerant flexibility of the cheerful. The directness of Great Strength can make The Joyous feel suppressed, yet The Joyous's indirect soothing exactly cushions the rashness of Great Strength. This pairing shows its greatest power in career partnerships: Great Strength cleaves open the situation, The Joyous stitches relationships back together—like quenching hot iron, hardness and softness forge resilience in the collision.
resonance: ★ Strength meets gentleness: Great Strength's breakthrough drive injects momentum into The Joyous's social web, while The Joyous's lubricating tact keeps Great Strength's edge from wounding relationships.
★ Thunder and lake stir each other: Thunder's kinetic energy pushes the lake onward, and the lake's receptivity provides a spillway for thunder's violence.
conflict: ◆ Observance versus ease: Great Strength's devotion to rules can make The Joyous feel restrained, while The Joyous's flexibility looks like a lack of principles in Great Strength's eyes.
◆ Force collides with flexibility: Great Strength's direct spear-point style can scratch The Joyous's sensitive nerves, and The Joyous's circumlocution seems inefficient to Great Strength.
advice: Before opening your mouth, Great Strength should ask The Joyous, "How would you phrase this more fittingly?" And when Great Strength pressures, The Joyous shouldn't just nod—offer three alternatives outright.

one_liner: You build with rules as your load-bearing wall; I let human warmth sweep through like a corridor breeze. When we join forces, the hard and the soft both find their footing.
analysis: Great Strength is like a heavy truck running at full throttle yet equipped with its own brakes—full of explosive energy but strictly adhering to the rule of 'no stepping on impropriety.' Dispersion, by contrast, is like a cross-draft that skims across water, expert at stirring stagnant pools back to life and blowing away barriers, but also prone to scattering human heat past all limits. When these two come together, the firmness of Great Strength gives Dispersion's fluidity a load-bearing wall, keeping things from collapsing into loose sand; the tenderness of Dispersion lubricates Great Strength's rigidity, simmering cold regulations into a warm broth that gathers people's hearts. Great Strength builds the skeleton and sets the bottom line; Dispersion opens the channels and makes the connections. One fears overstepping, the other fears rigidity—a perfect Complementary system of outer rounds and inner squares.
resonance: ★ Scattering without chaos: Great Strength's bottom line of propriety is like an anchor that firmly holds the spreading sentiments and creativity of the Dispersion hexagram, turning diffusion into effective transmission.
★ Firm without breaking: Dispersion's soft permeability dissolves Great Strength's blunt edges, turning rigid rules into a consensus that everyone willingly follows.
conflict: ◆ Boundary friction: Great Strength has a purism about 'not treading on impropriety' and tends to find Dispersion's spontaneous, rule-breaking style undisciplined.

◆ Gathering and scattering at cross purposes: Dispersion breaks impasses with emotional resonance and flexible improvisation, while Great Strength insists on controlling the field with hard systems and clear boundaries—their rhythms misalign and drain each other.
advice: Before you collaborate, put the untouchable red lines in writing on paper. After that, hand over the execution details entirely to the other person's discretion—don't measure their wind with your ruler.

one_liner: You handle the full-throttle charge forward; I handle the steady braking that keeps us on track.
analysis: The Power of the Great is thunder over the heavens — raw, explosive energy. Yet the Judgment insists that even the strong must not tread on what is not proper; the mightiest force still needs rules. The Limiting is water over the lake — once the cup is full, it spills, so you build banks and sluices. The Image says, 'regulate the measures and deliberate on virtuous conduct' — it’s all about knowing the right measure. Put these two together and you have the perfect team of gas pedal and brake. Great Power supplies the momentum to break through; The Limiting acts like a precision navigation system. Without Great Power’s drive, restraint becomes a stagnant, bitter stagnation. Without The Limiting’s frame, Great Power turns into a reckless brute. Their meeting isn’t a cancellation — it’s wildness tamed into precise, explosive force. One dares to charge; the other manages the risk. Together, they get things done with both power and steadiness.
resonance: ★ Shared bottom line: both believe 'too much is as bad as too little.' Great Power respects the rites and never oversteps; The Limiting regulates measures and keeps proportion. Both operate with a clear sense of boundaries.
★ Aligned goals: Great Power seeks achievement, The Limiting seeks stability. Both want long-term, sustainable success — not a fleeting flash in the pan.
conflict: ◆ Tempo mismatch: Great Power is used to decisive, do-it-now action; The Limiting prefers repeated calculations and careful processes. When a fast mover meets a careful mover, each can easily think the other is too slow.

◆ Pull over flexibility: Great Power finds The Limiting’s rules too confining; The Limiting finds Great Power’s approach too wild and undisciplined. The free spirit clashes with the rule-follower, and they often argue over how loose or tight things should be.
advice: Before acting, Great Power should run a stress test with The Limiting. When The Limiting makes the rules, it should leave an emergency exit for Great Power. Turn restrictions into protection rather than roadblocks.

relationship_name: Strength and Sincerity, Hand in Hand
one_liner: You've got thunderous moves, I've got a genuine heart as our safety net—get us together and we won't tip over.
analysis: Great Power is thunder in the sky, overflowing with energy, but the hexagram's text stresses 'not treading on what is improper,' meaning this brute force must be bridled by rules. Inner Truth is wind over the lake, emphasizing 'sincerity reaching even to pigs and fish,' relying on heartfelt authenticity to transform others. When the two meet, it's a perfect complement of the firm and the gentle. Great Power provides the drive and execution to break through; Inner Truth injects empathy and a sense of proportion into that drive. Without Inner Truth's sincerity, Great Power can easily become a destroyer; without Great Power's vigor, Inner Truth's goodwill can easily degenerate into weakness. The chemistry of this pair is kneading 'hard rules' and 'soft hearts' together, so their actions have both the efficiency of swift and decisive action and retain a human touch.
resonance: ★ Thunder and Wind Propel Each Other: The thunderous momentum of Great Power needs the gentle breeze of Inner Truth to carry it; together, they let influence pierce through surfaces and reach straight to the heart.

★ Restraint That Transforms Others: Great Power's 'not treading impropriety' and Inner Truth's 'deliberating about judgments and postponing executions' are highly attuned in restraint and compassion; both understand leaving space and keeping proportion.
conflict: ◆ Firm Momentum Meets Gentle Deliberation: Accustomed to swift, decisive action, Great Power may find Inner Truth's endless weighing and empathy-driven hesitation maddening, and it can resort to stomping its feet in impatience, accusing the other of dawdling.
◆ Rules vs. Real Feeling: Great Power's rigid insistence on principle can make Inner Truth seem too soft and sentimental; Inner Truth sees Great Power as too cold and rigid, incapable of bending.
advice: When disagreements arise, Great Power should zip it for three seconds before rushing to a decision; Inner Truth should put its bottom-line on the table instead of leaning on sentiment. Then move forward on two tracks: set the rules and honor the human touch.

one_liner: One hits the gas, the other steers; only by working together do they avoid a rollover.
analysis: The Power of the Great is thunder in heaven—a boundary-breaking vanguard that holds the firm, upright line of 'not treading on paths that do not accord with propriety.' The Preponderance of the Small is thunder on the mountain—a fine-tuning specialist that embraces the wisdom of restraint found in 'expending with careful economy.' Both share thunder's kinetic energy, but the Power of the Great splits it upward, while the Preponderance of the Small lets it settle downward. In a startup team, the Power of the Great type dares to spend big to open markets; the Preponderance of the Small type keeps a hawk-like eye on cash flow to hedge risks. When the Great Power's 'perseverance furthers' meets the Small's 'fitting to be lowly', the two form a closed loop of offense and defense. As long as the Great Power doesn't dismiss the Small as hobbled by caution, and the Small doesn't resent the Great for recklessness, this pair can turn thunder's explosive energy into sustainable growth.
resonance: ★ Movement and stillness in balance: The Power of the Great's thunderous momentum and the Preponderance of the Small's mountainlike steadiness create a Complementary rhythm—one pushes boundaries, the other solidifies the base.

★ Proportion kept in common: The Power of the Great draws action red lines with propriety; the Preponderance of the Small sets spending thresholds with frugality—building a collaborative framework that never oversteps.
conflict: ◆ Timing gap in advance and retreat: The Power of the Great sees an opportunity and wants to push full throttle; the Preponderance of the Small habitually stress-tests first—their decision rhythms often misalign.

◆ Energy flow: The Power of the Great wants to concentrate resources on key targets; the Preponderance of the Small prefers to spread resources to keep ample buffer—resource allocation easily sparks disputes.
advice: Set aside a fixed half-day each week for an 'energy alignment meeting': the Power of the Great lists three nodes that must be attacked, the Preponderance of the Small provides three corresponding risk plans; after both sign off, each executes their part.

one_liner: One floors the accelerator and charges forward; the other keeps a hawk's eye on the dashboard to prevent overheating.
analysis: Great Strength is the explosive force of thunder moving across the sky; it stresses 'no steps that are not proper,' possessing raw drive but with a built-in brake of propriety. After Completion is the consummate state of water over fire; it knows well that 'the beginning is auspicious, but the end can be chaotic,' and excels at checking for omissions after success. When these two come together, it is like a pioneer expanding new territory meeting a steadfast defender ensconced in the central command tent. Great Strength is responsible for breaking open the situation and breaking the deadlock; After Completion is responsible for gathering things in and preventing decline after a peak. Thunder's ferocity needs water's cooling to bring down the heat; fire's embers need thunder's vibration to renew. Over time, Great Strength will learn to look two steps further before exerting itself, and After Completion, borrowing Great Strength's sharpness, can leap out of the comfort zone of over-defense. But if the rhythm is off, one finds the other overly timid, the other complains the first doesn't know when to advance or retreat, and they easily get consumed in the tug-of-war between charge and caution. The key is to apply Great Strength's breakthrough at the start and After Completion's caution at the finish.
resonance: ★ Thunder's movement needs boundaries: without After Completion's contingency plans as a safety net, Great Strength's explosive power can easily spiral out of control. After Completion's caution precisely can turn this charge into sustainable long-term progress.

★ Uphold integrity and guard against subtle ripples: Great Strength's 'no improper steps' and After Completion's 'preventing trouble before it arises' are both essentially reverence for boundaries. The two are naturally in tune in rejecting recklessness and maintaining proper measure.
conflict: ◆ The game of accelerator and brake: Great Strength is used to seizing momentum and advancing quickly, while After Completion always loves to repeatedly check for flaws. One fast, one slow — they can easily drag each other down.

◆ Divergent paths after completion: After Completion believes that once things are done, it should shift to stability and defense, but Great Strength feels the momentum is strong and should continue expanding. Disputes easily arise over whether to pull back or press the advantage.
advice: Set a red line for Great Strength's charges, and give After Completion a margin for tolerance: before any breakthrough, run through After Completion's risk plan; during stabilization, leave 20% room for Great Strength to experiment.

one_liner: One floors the gas, the other taps the brakes; together they can keep this ride steady.
analysis: Great Strength is spring thunder splitting the sky—headlong force that smashes impasses and clears the way. Before Completion is dark fire floating on water, hiding the restlessness of a timing not yet ripe. Thunder's momentum pushes things forward; Fire's discernment keeps pulling at the reins. The sense of propriety that refuses to tread on the improper meets the prudent heart that discerns and keeps its place—like an old smith swinging a hammer: Great Strength knocks out the sparks, Before Completion times the quench. When they strain against each other, they get stuck between 'charging too hard and rolling over' and 'overthinking and stalling out.' But fold Thunder's blast into Fire's slow burn, and they can brew a result both solid and luminous.
resonance: ★ Thunder and Fire in One Forge: Great Strength's momentum can ignite Before Completion's procrastination, and Before Completion's clarity can steer Great Strength clear of rash traps.
★ Propriety as the Guide: both insist on acting with measure—Great Strength keeps the rules and never oversteps, Before Completion discerns each thing and never moves blindly.
conflict: ◆ Speed and Slowness Repel: Great Strength finds Before Completion's dawdling a waste of time; Before Completion resents Great Strength's recklessness for ruining things.

◆ Bright and Shadowy Cross Swords: Great Strength craves the satisfaction of one swift slash through the tangle; Before Completion insists on waiting until the heat is just right for a flawless finish.
advice: When anything comes up, first have Great Strength draw up a three-step action plan, then hand it to Before Completion to pick out two risk contingencies; only act after both have signed off.

one_liner: Two clear-headed people meet, no need to sync watches, steps land on the same drumbeat.
analysis: When two 'Jin' (Progress) hexagrams meet, it's like twin suns rising over the horizon at once — no tentative probing, only resonance at the same frequency. The hexagram text's 'three audiences in a single day' becomes mutual applause in your relationship: you take a step forward, and the other instantly offers a foothold. Li fire governs clarity, Kun earth governs steadiness, and the double hexagram turns 'making one's virtue shine' into a duet: each reflects the other's brilliance, and even the rhythm of progress fits perfectly. But being in sync also means lacking a buffer; if two rising flames focus only on shining, they may overlook Kun earth's supporting role. True rapport isn't about who shines brighter, but about knowing when to quietly add a clod of earth under the other's too-quick steps, so the light lasts longer and the journey goes further.
resonance: ★ Morning Light Resonance: Both of you prefer putting goals in the open, no behind-the-scenes games, and your drive is naturally synchronized.
★ Mutual Support: Kun earth provides the foundation; both understand steady work, and when hitting a bottleneck, you naturally share the pressure without blaming each other.
conflict: ◆ Overexposed Halo: When Li fire stacks too intensely, you may fall into a contest of 'who's better,' which drains your energy instead.
◆ Missing Yin, Lacking Softness: All upward drive, but when something requires slowing down, settling, or compromising, patience runs thin.
advice: Set aside half a day each week as a 'no-rushing' buffer. Drink tea together, review your recent rhythm, cool down overheated ambitions, and bring the light back to everyday cultivation.

one_liner: By day, shine bright and deliver results; by night, sheathe your edge, stay safe, and refine your inner craft. Together, that's an all-weather strategy for life.
analysis: The Jin hexagram (Progress) is fire over the earth — the sun at dawn, all about open renown and the "three receptions in a day" energy pouring outward. The Ming Yi hexagram (Darkening of the Light) is fire under the earth — the sun sinking below the horizon, centered on "hiding the light to shine" and a quiet, inward-gathering power. These two inverse hexagrams are not opposites; they are the front and back of the same rhythm of life. Jin's "illuminating one's own bright virtue" needs Ming Yi's "persevering through hardship is favorable" as a safety net; otherwise, one-sided high visibility invites a fall. Ming Yi's hidden radiance needs Jin's enterprising spirit to break the impasse; otherwise, it collapses into internal friction. Together, they mirror the rhythm of a career or a life: when it's time to lead, burn like fire and light up the whole room; when it's time to lie low, cover your blade with earth. Knowing when to advance and when to retreat, when to show and when to conceal — that is the ultimate answer this pair of hexagrams offers.
resonance: ★ Day-Night Relay: Jin's sunrise momentum and Ming Yi's sunset posture connect seamlessly, representing a natural alternation between life's peak moments and periods of quiet consolidation, each letting the other take the spotlight.

★ Outward Radiance, Inward Stillness: Jin's flame rises to light the path ahead, while Ming Yi's flame descends to warm the roots — the two energy flows are Complementary, balancing expansion with consolidation.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned Rhythms: Jin is eager to press the advantage, while Ming Yi counsels holding the line — at key decision points, they can pull against each other between charging and lying low.

◆ Temperature Difference in Expression: Jin likes to lay achievements out in the sun for approval, while Ming Yi tends to swallow grievances silently — in communication, each may find the other too flashy or too brooding.
advice: In favorable times, adopt the Jin mindset — generously share your results and expand your network. As soon as the wind turns, switch to Ming Yi mode: sheathe your edge, focus on reflection, and don't try to save face during a downturn.

one_liner: You carve out new ground while I keep the home fires burning; one charges forward, one holds the fort—together, we can make it happen!
analysis: The Progress hexagram is like the sun breaking through dawn, carrying the enterprising energy of 'being received three times in a day' to expand outward. The Family hexagram is like a flame in the hearth, building the inner foundation with the disciplines of 'words have substance, conduct is constant.' When bright light meets family tradition, it's like moving the conference-room PowerPoint into the kitchen—the pioneering drive of Progress needs the Family's sense of order as its safety net, and the Family's instinct to preserve needs Progress's power to break open new paths. When the two collide, fire burns hotter with the wind at its back, but too harsh a wind scatters the sparks. The key is to transform the sharp edge of 'making one's bright virtue shine' into the enduring strength of 'keeping the household in right order.'
resonance: ★ Aligned goals: Progress's ambition and the Family's guardianship both point toward building—one charts the career map, one lays the foundation for life.
★ Mutually reinforcing energies: Fire's brightness depends on the wind's flow to spread warmth, just as career achievements need family support to keep radiating.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Progress's 'three receptions' tempo can break the Family's 'constancy' pace, like a frequent flyer who complains the household moves too slowly.
◆ Center of gravity shifts: Progress's outward pursuit of recognition can make the Family's inward order feel neglected, like a husband who is always out at business dinners.
advice: Reserve half a day each week for a 'hearthside meeting': when the Progress person shares outside news, the Family person responds with concrete life scenarios, turning broad goals into a family action list that can actually be put into practice.

one_liner: We both have the same sun in our eyes, but one of us rushes straight ahead while the other prefers to circle around and talk slowly.
analysis: Above you both hangs the same Li fire, and your eyes shine with the same clarity—but the ground beneath your feet is different: one of you stands on thick earth, the other on shallow marsh. The Progress hexagram is like the sun at dawn: once it sets its sights, it strides forward, favoring straightforward, aboveboard mutual gain. The Opposition hexagram, by contrast, is fire baking the lake surface: fire and water naturally run counter, and it has an inborn sense of how to keep measure within difference. You share clear values, but Progress always wants to pull the other person into its camp, while Opposition instinctively steps back half a step and prefers to test slowly. The beauty of this pairing is that Progress's drive can ignite Opposition's caution, while Opposition's reserved blank spaces can cool Progress's impulsiveness. As long as you don't force the other to synchronize immediately, this shared sun will illuminate two complementary paths.
resonance: ★ Synced clear-headedness: the upper trigram is Li fire in both hexagrams, so you both prefer to address matters openly and never resort to backroom maneuvering or mind-reading games.

★ A shared foundation of seeking common ground: you both value upright, aboveboard principles of conduct. Even when your routes differ, neither of you hides personal motives on the big-picture direction.
conflict: ◆ Rhythmic mismatch: Progress is used to striking while the iron is hot and forging ahead at full cry, while Opposition feels the differences are too great and needs to feel its way slowly—so one easily finds the other too slow, and the other too hasty.

◆ Divergence on togetherness vs. distance: Progress wants to huddle for warmth and level up together, but Opposition instinctively draws boundaries and guards its independence—so you can never quite agree on the right intimate distance.
advice: When disagreements arise, don't rush to pull the other person into your orbit. First arrange to do something harmless and easy together, let your shared firelight illuminate each other's pace, and then decide which way to go.

one_liner: You stride boldly ahead; I keep my head down to watch the path and keep us from stumbling. Together, we never veer off course.
analysis: Jin (Progress) is 'the sun rising over the earth'—like the noonday sun, charging ahead with a hunger for recognition. Jian (Obstruction) is 'water on a mountain'—like cold rain lashing a steep trail, a reminder to stop and reflect when blocked. Fire flares upward, water flows downward; when these two energies meet, one is eager to scatter its light everywhere, the other is used to sinking roots deep in the dark. Jin's drive tends to smash into Jian's obstacles, but Jian's 'turning back to cultivate virtue' puts the brakes on Jin's blind optimism; conversely, Jin's 'three receptions in broad daylight' can pull Jian out of the swamp of self-doubt. Their bond is not a simple contest of speed versus slowness, but the meshing of 'radiating outward' and 'storing up within.' Jin teaches Jian to stop staring at the mud underfoot; Jian teaches Jin to stop chasing clouds in the sky. One bright, one shaded; one advancing, one pausing—fitted together, they become a map that can cover a long road.
resonance: ★ Growing toward the sun meets a cold spring: Jin's self-illuminating virtue needs Jian's calm to settle the glitter, so its brilliance doesn't harden into a blinding display.

★ Braving danger never forgets the guiding star: in the lonely season of Jian's 'turning back to cultivate virtue,' it especially needs the outside recognition and warm support that Jin's 'three receptions in broad daylight' bring.
conflict: ◆ A hurried march trips over a stumbling stone: Jin finds that Jian always shrinks back, stews in self-doubt, and moves too slowly; Jian resents Jin for charging hard regardless of the terrain and overturning the cart.

◆ A warm cheek pressed against a cold ridge: Jin craves constant interaction and instant feedback; Jian likes to close the door and chew things over, disliking interruptions—so communication often runs hot and cold.
advice: Before making a proposal, the Jin side should first ask, 'Is the road steady right now?' When self-doubt creeps in, the Jian side should try answering, 'Let me turn on a light and give it a go.' Let the rhythm of charging and pausing be set by the actual situation, not by mood.

one_liner: You keep shining steadily; I'll clear the old ledger with one click.
analysis: The Progress hexagram is 'the sun rising above the earth' — like a sun slowly climbing, it seeks steady advancement and self-manifestation. 'Three receptions in a day' speaks of a hunger for recognition and upward motion. The Deliverance hexagram is 'thunder and rain arising' — all about cathartic release; its Image says 'pardons faults and forgives sins,' excelling at decisively breaking deadlocks and letting go of burdens. When these two energies collide, Progress's rising phase often accumulates inner friction from over-perfecting; Deliverance acts like a timely rain, resetting the stubborn obsession to zero. Progress provides clear direction and light; Deliverance clears emotional obstacles and historical baggage. One builds and reveals; the other cuts through and releases. As long as Progress doesn't mistake Deliverance's ease for carelessness, and Deliverance doesn't mistake Progress's earnestness for stubbornness, this relationship can find its most comfortable rhythm between steady ascent and timely letting go.
resonance: ★ Steady advancement meets breakthrough: Progress's upward climb often hits bottlenecks; Deliverance's decisive release can precisely clear the obstacles, leaving the path ahead unimpeded.

★ Travel light without inner friction: Deliverance's magnanimity in pardoning faults can catch the anxiety behind Progress's craving for recognition; together they shed their burdens and move forward.
conflict: ◆ Dogged perfectionism meets slashing decisiveness: Progress likes to go step by step and see things through; Deliverance tends to turn the page quickly — each may resent the other's pacing.

◆ Emotional detox meets repeated rumination: Deliverance believes in moving on after the storm; Progress is used to laying problems out in the sun and re-examining them — friction arises over whether old scores should be revisited.
advice: When you're stuck, Progress, don't rush to nitpick details — give Deliverance half an hour to clear the emotional cache. And Deliverance, build a platform for Progress to show its results — don't just close things off with a hasty 'forget it.'

one_liner: One throws all energy into chasing the spotlight; the other quietly retreats, simplifying and paring down. Together, they manage to live life to the fullest.
analysis: Jin (Progress) is the fire of dawn — it embodies the sun rising above the earth, three honors in a single day, with an outward hunger for expansion and expression. Sun (Decrease) is the still mountain — it advocates a lake at the mountain's foot, reining in anger and desire, habitually trimming inward and leaving space. Their meeting is not a head-on collision but a precise calibration of energy. Jin's fire easily flares into restlessness; Sun's restraint provides the cooling, turning the pursuit of fame and gain into grounded virtue. Sun's withdrawal, pushed too far, can sink into stark austerity; Jin's clear light falls on it, infusing that self-discipline with vitality and direction. Mountain receives light from fire; fire rises along the mountain's form. One pushes talent to center stage, the other prunes the branches backstage — between advance and retreat, they create their own sustainable way of shining.
resonance: ★ Same rhythm: both believe in deep accumulation before bursting forth; Jin's upward growth depends on Sun's downward rooting. Their long-term sense of purpose is remarkably aligned.
★ Complementary energy: Sun's simplicity can hold Jin's splendor, and Jin's drive can illuminate Sun's quiet practice; when the two work together, there is almost no inner friction.
conflict: ◆ Rhythmic mismatch: Jin favors striking while the iron is hot and moving fast, while Sun prefers repeated deliberation and cutting away redundancies; they easily get stuck on whether to push forward.
◆ Expressive gap: Jin craves being seen and applauded, while Sun feels plain tea and simple rice are enough. One finds the other too flashy; the other finds the one too bland.
advice: When a major decision arises, first have the Jin partner list three things they want to pursue, then have the Sun partner cross out two things that must be let go. Replace verbal tug-of-war with a written checklist, and together follow a rhythm of advancing three steps and retreating one.

one_liner: Wind pushes fire to flourish, fire lights the wind's way; as partners, they get double results for half the effort.
analysis: Jin (The Progressing) is like the first light of dawn, carrying an innate confidence to grow upward; Yi (Increase) is like a swift wind through the forest, skilled at borrowing momentum and tuning its frequency. The fire nature, open and upright, needs sustained exposure; the wind nature, nimble and adaptable, seeks dynamic optimization. When these two meet, Jin's 'illumining one's bright virtue' needs Yi's 'moving toward the good' to calibrate the direction, while Yi's 'crossing great rivers and pressing onward' depends on Jin's 'three receptions in a day' to provide a steady light source. It is like a mountaineer teaming up with a meteorologist—one lights the rock face to find footholds, the other monitors airflow in real time to adjust the rhythm. But they must guard against fire burning so fiercely that it dries up the wind's moisture, or wind scattering so widely that it breaks the fire's formation.
resonance: ★ Upward Resonance: Jin wants to grow by leaps, Yi wants to ride the wind—deep down, both believe 'forward is the only way.'
★ Interlocking Action: Jin's steady manifestation meets Yi's flexible iteration, slashing trial-and-error costs.
conflict: ◆ Rhythm Mismatch: Jin likes to wait until everything is fully exposed before hauling in the net, while Yi tends to seize every opening; they may find each other too slow or too hasty.
◆ Energy Tug-of-War: Fire seeks focused burning and fears dispersion; wind wants to flow in all directions and resents confinement—collaboration needs room to breathe.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for a 'focus session': Jin sets the main course with three priorities, Yi brings two fine-tuning plans for the flanks—don't let the wind drown the firelight.

relationship_name: Clarity and Decisiveness in Mutual Support
one_liner: You steadily gather the light, I decisively break through — together we're a steady, precise team of doers.
analysis: Jin rises like dawn breaking through soil, built on daily self-cultivation and deep accumulation — the Fire is gentle yet enduring. Guai is like the sky river bursting its banks, all about seizing the right moment to throw open the situation — the Lake gathers force and cuts sharp. When these two hexagrams meet, they complete the two poles of accomplishment: Jin's steady ascent gives Guai's decisiveness moral grounding and a resource base, keeping bold moves from becoming reckless. Guai's thunderous efficiency, in turn, cuts through Jin's tendency to shine without producing results. Fire warms, Lake moistens, Earth supports Heaven's momentum — one lays the road solid, the other kicks the door open, and energy flows from accumulation to release in one smooth arc.
resonance: ★ Complementary Rhythm: Jin's step-by-step progress builds the confidence for Guai's decisive strike, keeping boldness from becoming blind action.
★ Shared Values: Both value doing things openly and fairly — Jin earns recognition through virtue, Guai rallies people by openly bestowing rewards; the foundation is clean.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched Tempo: Jin prefers to polish details steadily over time, while Guai wants to clear obstacles in one sweep — one may find the other too slow, the other too rash.

◆ Friction in Expression: Jin's self-brightening virtue is introverted and cultivated, while Guai's proclamation before the court demands high-profile declaration — the sense of how much to show outwardly can spark disputes.
advice: Set clear roles and lock in the handoff points: Jin takes charge of early groundwork and nurturing momentum, Guai takes the lead on key decisions and breakthroughs. After setting the milestones, don't cross lines or push each other's timelines.

relationship_name: A Meeting of Light and Wind
one_liner: You shine steadily, I stir winds far and wide — when we come together, it's an instant hit.
analysis: The Jin hexagram (Progress) is like the rising sun: it values step-by-step advancement and making one's virtue visible, pursuing a clear and steady climb. The Gou hexagram (Coming to Meet) is like an unexpected long wind, carrying the breakthrough power of a strong woman and the penetrative reach that spreads influence in all directions — it excels at creating surprising connections. When these two meet, it's a collision of stability and change. Jin's radiant light needs Gou's long wind to be carried far, while Gou's drifting ways need Jin's deep virtue to stay anchored. But if Gou's wind blows too fiercely, it can scatter Jin's rhythm; if Jin is too rigid and conventional, it will miss the sudden opportunities Gou throws its way. The beauty of this relationship lies in the switch between paving the road and breaking new ground — the key is knowing who leads, who supports, and when to go with the flow.
resonance: ★ Borrowing Wind to Spread Fire: Gou's wide-reaching influence can quickly carry the virtue and achievements Jin has accumulated to all directions, letting the value of quiet dedication be seen by more people.
★ Encounter Gives Birth to Radiance: Jin's steadiness provides the grounding soil for Gou's unexpected encounters, allowing every chance meeting to settle into long-term resources.
conflict: ◆ Misaligned Rhythm: Jin is used to a step-by-step, steady approach, while Gou loves to seize the gaps and suddenly change the game — the two can end up pulling against each other's pace.
◆ Overbearing Gusts: If Gou's strong-willed nature isn't tempered, it can storm into Jin's otherwise clear path of advancement, causing loss of direction or unsteady foundations.
advice: When unexpected opportunities arise, spend three days writing those surprise variables into your existing plan before pushing forward — don't let high-frequency changes disrupt the steady rhythm you've built.

one_liner: You're the light out front, leading the way; I'm the one behind, amassing people and supplies.
analysis: The Hexagram Progress is like the sun rising over the earth; it seeks to break through stalemates, make a name, and rise quickly. The Hexagram Gathering Together is like water pooling in low places; it values resource integration and prevention of trouble. Both hexagrams stand on the same foundation of Kun earth, so at their core they both value solid grounding and practical work, but their directions of force are completely opposite: one expands outward to gain exposure, the other draws inward to seek stability. This combination is exactly like the 'trailblazer' and the 'chief steward' in a team. Progress's momentum can shatter Gathering's stale impasse, while Gathering's foresight can contain Progress's rash risks. Without Gathering's 'keeping weapons ready,' Progress's 'three receptions in a day' easily becomes a flash in the pan; without Progress's 'sun rising over the earth,' Gathering's convergence turns into stagnant water. If each recognizes the other's true capabilities, they can turn short-term hustle into a long-lasting enterprise.
resonance: ★ In step: beneath it all, both are built on Kun earth, so both value keeping their feet on the ground and avoiding empty talk — objectives stay rooted in what's real.
★ Complementary attack and defense: Progress clears new ground and delivers results; Gathering tallies resources and guards against risk. The one-two of advance and hold forms a complete circuit.
conflict: ◆ Off-beat tempo: Progress wants to strike while the iron is hot and push on; Gathering always wants to count resources and prepare fallbacks first. Each can easily see the other as too hasty or too lagging.

◆ Different thermostats: Progress is used to laying achievements out in the sunlight for approval; Gathering leans toward quietly pulling things together behind the scenes. At times one may find the other too flashy or too guarded.
advice: Set clear 'show-your-cards slots' and 'accounting days.' When Progress is sprinting, don't resent Gathering for checking the books too closely; once Gathering has done its prep, it must leave Progress a wide-enough window for visibility. Align the tempo with explicit milestones.

one_liner: You're eager to shine and grab the spotlight up front, while I'm content to put down roots and lay the groundwork behind the scenes. Working together, we actually make something of ourselves.
analysis: Jin ('Progress') is 'the bright rising over the earth' — it craves the instant recognition of 'three receptions in a single day.' Its fire nature is passionate, longing to display every talent in the sunlight. Sheng ('Pushing Upward') is 'wood growing within the earth' — it values building small into great, with an earthy steadiness that trusts only the slow work of one step at a time. When these two hexagrams meet, the initial impression is a mismatch of tempo, but underneath lies a hidden complementarity. Jin's radiance can point Sheng in the right direction and provide the opportunity to break through the soil; Sheng's depth can catch Jin's restlessness and turn its brief exposure into sustainable capital. It's like a high-profile launch event meeting long-term R&D: the former grabs attention, the latter delivers substance. As long as Jin doesn't find Sheng too slow, and Sheng doesn't find Jin too flighty, this pair can distill 'fame' into 'strength.'
resonance: ★ Shared Direction: Both believe in the path of upward growth — one uses light to guide the breakthrough, the other uses soil to support and store strength. They pull in the same direction without draining each other.
★ Mutual Enrichment: Jin's exposure lets Sheng's quiet cultivation be seen by the world; Sheng's patience stretches Jin's momentary heat into lasting reputation. Each completes the other.
conflict: ◆ Tempo Tug-of-War: Jin is used to the fast feedback of 'three receptions a day,' while Sheng believes in the slow cycle of 'small gains building to greatness.' When advancing work, they tend to rush each other or feel the other is dragging.

◆ Substance vs. Image Friction: Jin's fire nature leans toward outward display and immediate payoff; Sheng's earth nature focuses on inner reserves and a solid foundation. In cooperation, they often clash over 'polish first or refine first.'
advice: Agree on a 'weekly delivery + monthly announcement' rhythm: Sheng submits underlying progress at set milestones, and Jin distills the highlights for external syncing. Use a fixed cadence to align each other's haste and patience.

relationship_name: Reflecting Each Other's Rise and Fall
one_liner: You handle winning trophies in the sunshine; I handle grinding it out in the drought. Put us together and we've got life's ups and downs all figured out.
analysis: The hexagram of Progress (Jin) is like the sun blazing at dawn, carrying the auspicious aura of 'three audiences in one day.' Its energy expands outward, favoring going with the flow and dazzling brilliance. The hexagram of Oppression (Kun), by contrast, is the parched territory of 'a lake without water.' Its energy draws inward, centering on the silent persistence of 'words are not believed' and the solitary courage of 'staking one's life on one's purpose.' When these two meet, it is not about one changing the other, but about a Complementary rhythm in the cadence of life. Jin's brightness can instantly cut through Kun's stagnant fog, handing a ladder to those who have endured a bitter winter; Kun's deep submersion can brake Jin's ostentation, reminding those in luck not to be carried away by applause. When Fire and Lake meet, at first glance one seems scorching and the other barren, but actually Jin's 'fire' can dry up Kun's mud and Kun's 'lake floor' can hold back Jin's false heat. Together, one teaches how to win with dignity, and the other how to endure with grit, cooking life's peaks and valleys into a full philosophy of survival.
resonance: ★ A relay from fortune to adversity: Jin's 'three audiences in a day' gives Kun a breakthrough chance, while Kun's 'staking one's life on one's purpose' stores up long-term confidence for Jin.
★ Complementary flash and depth: The fire's radiance lights the road ahead; the lakebed's aridity squeezes out true skill. Together they complete both the outer face and the inner substance.
conflict: ◆ Out-of-sync rhythms: Jin is eager for results and applause; Kun is used to quietly enduring. Each thinks the other is at fault—one too laggardly, the other too flighty.
◆ Break in communication: Jin likes open expression and instant feedback, while Kun's 'words are not believed' carries a built-in wariness, so sincere words easily freeze into a cold war.
advice: When you disagree, Jin, don't rush to give advice or pep talks. First share a cup of tea with Kun and listen to their grievances. And Kun, don't just tough it out alone; lay out your bottom line and needs directly to Jin—don't make them guess.

one_liner: You just shine on stage; I'll quietly stay and keep your cup full.
analysis: The Hexagram Jin is like a rising sun breaking through the soil, carrying a blazing energy that pushes upward and longs to be seen. The Hexagram Jing is like an old well—it does not compete or grab, but relies on deep draw to provide endless nourishment. Fire nature rises, water nature moistens; when they meet, it is the mutual fulfillment of 'light' and 'source.' Jin's sharpness can easily drain its reserves in a wild rush; Jing's steadiness is just right to catch the impatience. If Jing stays buried in obscurity for too long, it needs Jin's brilliance to bring it into the spotlight, turning still water into living water. One is in charge of lighting up the stage, the other in charge of keeping supplies ready; in the alternation of light and shadow, both preserve momentum and retain the root.
resonance: ★ When the light-chaser meets the spring-keeper: Jin's upward drive can instantly light up Jing's silence, letting those who quietly work hard see that their efforts will eventually be recognized.
★ Supply line meets the charge: Jing's stable foundation perfectly catches Jin's need for expansion, ensuring every highlight is supported by living water.
conflict: ◆ Mismatched rhythm causes inner friction: Jin is used to quick battles and immediate rewards, while Jing values a slow, steady build of depth—one finds the other too slow, the other too hasty.

◆ Value orientation creates friction: Jin seeks fame and gain outward, while Jing cultivates the heart and nourishes the people inward; the former may see the latter as too conservative, the latter sees the former as too restless.
advice: Jin: don't always push the other with a progress bar; set aside half a day each week to hear Jing's underlying logic. Jing: don't just keep your head down storing water; regularly share your incremental results with Jin.

one_liner: You light the way forward, I break the old and usher in the new—together we keep leveling up and taking on every challenge.
analysis: Progress (Fire over Earth) rises like the sun breaking through the soil, shining from within as it steadily advances. Revolution (Lake over Fire) resembles water brought to a boil—it shatters old patterns and forges a new order. When the two meet, they create a dynamic loop: 'illumination guides revolution, revolution safeguards illumination.' Progress's gradual growth needs Revolution's power to clear away accumulated decay; Revolution's upheaval needs Progress's bright virtue to anchor its direction. The 'three gatherings in a day' of Fire over Earth and the 'trust at the appointed day' of Lake over Fire both speak to a shared philosophy of timing—one builds momentum through sustained radiance, the other turns decisively when the moment ripens. Fire and Lake excite rather than extinguish each other, becoming a blade of tempering: lake water soothes fire's ferocity, firelight illuminates the lake's hidden depths. So too does the reformer need idealism to light the way, and the doer need the courage to break old forms in order to protect the original vision.
resonance: ★ Both believe 'timing is destiny': Progress honors the steady accumulation of day and night; Revolution watches for the turning point of the appointed day—each knows how to move when the moment is right.

★ Both walk the path of breaking and building: Progress lays its foundation by making virtue luminous; Revolution opens new horizons by clarifying the seasons—each seeks breakthrough within continuity.
conflict: ◆ Different sense of rhythm: Progress favors careful, step-by-step increments; Revolution leans toward bold, all-or-nothing leaps. Expect friction over pacing.
◆ Clashing energy fields: the lake's water tries to cool the fire, only to be turned into steam—symbolizing how rational planning is often unsettled by revolutionary passion.
advice: Set aside a 'transparent review day' each month: use Progress's bright virtue to assess the gains and losses of change, and apply Revolution's calendrical thinking to recalibrate your next steps.

one_liner: One person brightens the spotlight on stage; the other keeps the heat steady behind the scenes — together, you both go viral and get the job done.
analysis: The Progress hexagram is the sun leaping over the horizon — open, bold, and step-by-step radiant, carrying its own spotlight wherever it goes. The Cauldron hexagram, by contrast, is wood feeding a slow fire, turning raw, tangled ingredients into a proper cauldron feast — it's all about steadying the base and condensing the essence. Both hexagrams share the Li (The Clinging) fire as the upper trigram, meaning the two of you have the same light in your eyes and always click instantly on the big picture. But Progress's momentum moves outward — it likes to strike while the iron is hot and bring home results. The Cauldron's nature pulls inward — it won't lift the lid until the heat is exactly right. This combo is like going into business together: Progress charges the market, grabs the spotlight, and pulls in resources; Cauldron builds the team, sets the rules, and lays the groundwork. The shared fire nature spares you from suspicion, but one of you is eager to bloom and bear fruit while the other insists on letting the broth simmer. You'll need to match each other's throttle and brake to turn the momentum of "three receptions in a day" into the legacy of "a firm position and a focused mandate."
resonance: ★ Same Frequency in Vision: You both carry the transparent heat of Li fire — no beating around the bush, and once you lock onto a big direction, you instantly align your targets.
★ Mutual Energy Nourishment: Progress's forward drive adds fuel to Cauldron's fire, while Cauldron's steadying power keeps Progress's brilliance from flaring into smoke.
conflict: ◆ Rhythmic Mismatch: Progress thinks Cauldron is too slow, always wanting to strike while the iron is hot; Cauldron thinks Progress is reckless, refusing to lift the lid before the heat is right.

◆ Foundational Disagreement: Progress is rooted in Kun (The Receptive) earth, seeking steady, measured expansion; Cauldron relies on Xun (The Gentle) wood, seeking flexible, adaptive reshaping — the underlying logic can easily clash.
advice: When a disagreement comes up, Progress shouldn't rush straight ahead, and Cauldron shouldn't cling to the rules. Instead, set up a "Heat & Quality Check" — Progress reports outward progress, Cauldron guards internal quality, and you sync on fixed milestones. Never just do your own thing.

relationship_name: Mutual Radiance of Light and Thunder
one_liner: One lights the way forward; the other slams a gavel to wake you up.
analysis: The Progress hexagram is like the rising sun at dawn—it values frank, enterprising openness, spreading its own brilliance without reserve before the world. The Arousing hexagram is like a sudden spring thunderclap—it focuses on reverence and self-reflection, using abrupt shocks to force people to bow their heads and examine themselves. Together, these energies are a pioneer paired with a risk-control officer. Progress's 'bright light rising over the earth' gives Arousing's actions clear coordinates, so the thunder never sounds in vain; Arousing's 'fear and self-reproof' becomes Progress's sobering agent, preventing brightness from turning into blind arrogance. Traveling by day, it’s easy to look only at the horizon—but Arousing's thunder explodes right by your ear, reminding you to hold the reins tight. This combination has no fear of upheaval; the more it enters a phase of breaking through and sprinting, the more it ignites a gutsy yet meticulous combat strength.
resonance: ★ Shared frequency of purpose: Progress's open enterprise gives Arousing's sudden actions a clear map, keeping the thunder from being louder than the rain.
★ Crisis forges composure: Arousing's reverence and self-reflection help Progress filter out restlessness, making the steady climb more solid.
conflict: ◆ Severe rhythm mismatch: Progress likes to advance step by step and show off achievements, while Arousing always loves to slam on the brakes to check for hidden hazards—easily throwing each other off balance.
