relationship_name: Movement and Sincerity in Mutual Support
one_liner: You drive the energy and set the vibe; I bring the heart and give us grounding.
analysis: The hexagram Yu (Enthusiasm) shows thunder bursting forth from the earth, governing movement in accordance with circumstances and expansive, joyful expression—favorable for enfeoffing princes and mustering armies, highlighting its outward, action-oriented drive. The hexagram Zhong Fu (Inner Truth) shows wind over the lake, governing utmost sincerity at the center and the transformative influence on all things—sincerity reaching even pigs and fish, accentuating its inward, trust-based nature. Their complementarity lies in the interlocking of movement and sincerity: if Yu's joy is not anchored by Zhong Fu's authenticity, it easily drifts into ostentatious indulgence; if Zhong Fu's quiet constancy is not propelled by Yu's thunderous momentum, it easily falls into empty talk and hesitation. Thunder and wind stir each other, sincerity steers joy, and joy enacts sincerity, forming a resilient dynamic of outward initiative and inward commitment—each fulfilling the other without overstepping the bounds.
resonance: ★ The explosive power of moving with the current
★ A spiritual covenant of trust reaching all things
conflict: ◆ The tug between uninhibited pleasure and careful restraint
◆ The rhythm gap between lightning-fast action and repeated verification
advice: Before acting, set clear rules and boundaries with sincerity; after letting loose, don't forget to review your emotional account. Use a clear sense of covenant to sustain the joy you share.

one_liner: You throw a party when things go well; I'm the one slamming the brakes on the details.
analysis: The Yu hexagram (Enthusiasm) shows Thunder bursting from the Earth, advocating 'favorable to enfeoff lords and raise armies'—moving with the times, with an open, joyful spirit. The Xiao Guo hexagram (Small Exceeding) shows Thunder atop the Mountain, and its Judgment clearly states: 'Not favorable to go upward, but downward; do small things, not great things.' Its Image stresses 'let your conduct be exceptionally humble and your spending exceptionally frugal.' Both share the dynamic impulse of Thunder, yet Yu uses the yielding nature of Earth (Kun) to radiate outward, pursuing grandeur and harmony, while Xiao Guo uses the stilling power of Mountain (Gen) to draw inward, focusing on fine-tuning and restraint. The tension is vivid: Yu's 'making music and exalting virtue' needs Xiao Guo's 'humility and frugality in due measure' as a safety net against drifting; Xiao Guo's 'not favorable to go upward' in turn needs Yu's 'moving with the times' to break the deadlock and lift the spirit. One releases, one contains—just like festive drumbeats meeting the ledgers backstage.
resonance: ★ Shared Thunder-like instinct for action
★ Keen sensitivity to the rhythm of the times
conflict: ◆ Grand momentum vs. detail control
◆ Singing with the current vs. pulling back against it
advice: When advancing major matters, let the Yu side set the tone and lead outward expansion, while the Xiao Guo side focuses on process risk control and resource conservation. Use the pragmatism of 'going downward' to support the ambition of 'raising armies.'

one_liner: Action opens new horizons, prudence preserves achievements; their complement ensures steady and lasting progress.
analysis: The hexagram Enthusiasm (Yu) shows thunder stirring above the earth; moving in accord with the season, it is favorable to appoint lords and dispatch armies — it signifies initiative and shared joy. After Completion (Ji Ji) shows water and fire mutually nourishing; affairs begin propitiously but end in disorder, so one must anticipate troubles and take precautions. The two complement each other: Enthusiasm's drive injects vitality into After Completion, while After Completion's prudence protects Enthusiasm from risk. The thunder's vigor and water's nourishment combine, making actions measured and accomplishment untroubled. Enthusiasm's delight needs the clear-headedness of After Completion for balance; After Completion's vigilance needs the agility of Enthusiasm for activation — forming a symbiotic relationship of dynamic equilibrium.
resonance: ★ Timely action brings joy
★ Anticipate danger to prevent chaos
conflict: ◆ Comfort breeds sloth
◆ Over-caution hinders action
advice: While celebrating, have contingency plans ready; before acting, weigh with caution; alternate motion and stillness.

one_liner: You ride the wind and waves to make a splash; I fill the gaps and hold the line.
analysis: In Enthusiasm, thunder bursts from the earth; the Image speaks of making music and honoring virtue, emphasizing the explosive power of moving in harmony with the moment. In Before Completion, fire hovers over water; the Image warns of careful discernment and settling in the right place, and the Judgment laments the little fox that wets its tail — focusing on caution while the work is still unfinished. Combined, Enthusiasm's thunder injects momentum into Before Completion's open-ended situation, while Before Completion's coolness sets limits to Enthusiasm's comfort. One moves, the other observes: Enthusiasm pushes forward with ardor, Before Completion recalibrates with clarity. The courage to lead an army is tempered by the wisdom to discern things, guarding against both blind charging and excessive hesitation, creating a unique complementary synergy where joy fuels action and prudence secures completion.
resonance: ★ Motion and stillness in balance, breaking deadlock together
★ Seize the momentum, position precisely
conflict: ◆ Rhythm mismatch: Enthusiasm wants quick celebration; Before Completion wants steady caution
◆ Energy pull: thunder's charge easily crosses lines; fire over water easily hesitates
advice: At the start of the partnership, let the Before Completion side outline the risk checklist and step milestones; then let the Enthusiasm side craft the incentive plan and take the lead. After each stage, review and recalibrate before celebrating.

one_liner: Only by syncing with your own rhythm can you dance a beautiful duet with the world.
analysis: The hexagram of Following, applied to the self, is like thunder hidden within a lake. The judgment — 'supreme success, perseverance furthers' — emphasizes that pure and correct following brings no blame. The Image's phrase 'goes to rest at nightfall' reveals the wisdom of self-regulation. The lake's gentle nature receives the thunder's stirring, creating a unique structure of outer compliance and inner firmness. When inner momentum (thunder) resonates with outer adaptability (lake), you avoid self-fragmentation and build an efficient, self-consistent system. The alchemy lies in using stillness to master movement, and yielding to nourish strength — through inner dialogue you align with the times, so that 'choosing the good and following it' becomes not blind conformity, but clear-sighted self-renewal.
resonance: ★ Inner and outer rhythms mesh naturally.
★ Knowing when to advance or withdraw without draining your energy.
conflict: ◆ Overactive thunder can shatter the lake's stillness.
◆ Excessive following loses the anchor of your true self.
advice: Each day, schedule a 'stillness-and-movement calibration' — ten minutes to log the balance between impulse and restraint, creating a personal decision buffer.

one_liner: Ride the current without blind submission; in the weaving of order and chaos, a kindred understanding is born.
analysis: The hexagram Following (Lake over Thunder) rests on gentle compliance with the hour; its Judgment, 'No blame,' underscores the wisdom of moving with circumstance. The hexagram Work on the Decayed (Mountain over Wind) stirs through the clash of forces, using firmness to clear away accumulated rot; its Image, 'Stimulate the people and cultivate virtue,' calls for the boldness of renewal. One is Lake, the other Mountain; one supple, one unyielding — yet both share the foundation of 'sublime success.' Following's 'withdraw at nightfall to rest' offers a rhythmic pause for Work on the Decayed's 'three days before and after,' while the latter's power to break through impasses opens fresh horizons for Following's pursuit of the good. Lake nourishes Mountain, Wind moves Thunder; in the endless cycle of yielding and rectifying, they create a dynamic, balanced symbiosis.
resonance: ★ The wisdom of knowing when to move with the tide
★ The moral passion for renewing what has grown stale
conflict: ◆ Taking things as they come vs. tearing down the old to build anew
◆ Guarding the present stability vs. risking a decisive breakthrough
advice: When facing change, first read the winds with Following's gentle flexibility; then act with Work on the Decayed's resolute precision. Be careful not to mindlessly follow or to forcibly overturn.

one_liner: One sets the stage and points the way; the other flows with the current and keeps in step—even their breathing falls into perfect sync.
analysis: The hexagram Approach (Lin), with Earth above the Lake, bestows the lofty inclusiveness and nurturing power of one who looks down from above; its Judgment warns of misfortune in the eighth month, reminding us to curb the urge to control. The hexagram Following (Sui), with Thunder within the Lake, carries the agility to yield to the times and the ease of retiring to rest at nightfall. Both share the joy of the Lake; the chemistry lies in Approach providing direction and Following receiving and transforming it with gentle flexibility. Approach's active output is perfectly absorbed by Following's talent for choosing the right path and going along, avoiding both coercion and blind obedience. Yet Following's desire for a blameless, steady course and Approach's sense of impending crisis can pull in different directions—so Approach must soften its sharp edges, and Following must stay alert, for the resonance of teaching and trusting to truly sing.
resonance: ★ In Tune with the Joyful Lake
★ Steering with the Current
conflict: ◆ Control versus Drift
◆ Out-of-Sync Sense of Crisis
advice: The guiding partner should regularly step down from the pedestal and listen to feedback; the following partner must proactively voice their views at key decision points—so neither one dominates excessively while the other vanishes into the background.

relationship_name: Wind and Lake in Mutual Radiance
one_liner: You move with the current, I quietly watch for changes—together we are a walking compass.
analysis: The hexagram Following, with Lake over Thunder, emphasizes adapting to the times and choosing what is good to act upon, like thunder hidden in the lake building its strength. The hexagram Contemplation, with Wind moving over the Earth, focuses on observing the people's condition and guiding them through teaching, like wind crossing the fields, moistening all without sound. Their resonance lies in both being rooted in alignment: Following aligns with the Way of Heaven through dynamic adjustment, while Contemplation grasps the human heart through still insight. When Following's agility meets Contemplation's depth, a cycle forms—'discerning the situation in movement, directing action in stillness.' The lake's receptive nourishment feeds the wind's spread, and thunder's awakening sharpens Contemplation's discernment, enabling the two to flow with change while recalibrating direction with clear eyes.
resonance: ★ In adaptability hides the power of transformation
★ In observation lies the wisdom of teaching
conflict: ◆ Thunder moving too fast loses its watchful awareness
◆ Wind drifting too slowly fails to respond to change
advice: Before acting, assess the times with the discerning eye of Contemplation; after deciding, advance with the supple ease of Following.

one_liner: The gentleness that moves with the current and the firmness that lays down ironclad rules perform a dance of order and adaptation amid thunder.
analysis: The Hexagram of Following (Sui) takes the image of Lake over Thunder, advocating adapting to the times and choosing the good to follow; its Judgement emphasizes that the way to remain blameless lies in flexible response. The Hexagram of Biting Through (Shihe) tempers Thunder's might with Fire, and its Image says clearly that clarifying punishments and enforcing laws is to rectify discipline. Both hexagrams share the lower trigram of Thunder, giving them the power to break deadlocks, yet their upper trigrams form a union of Lake and Fire: Lake water nourishes the field where thunder moves, keeping compliance from becoming blind obedience; Li fire forges the might of thunder, preventing punishment from turning into harsh cruelty. When the two meet, it is like the alternation of spring rain that nourishes and autumn frost that culls. In this dynamic balance, vitality is preserved while accumulated ills are cleared, forming a unique resonance field where gentleness guides firmness and firmness anchors gentleness.
resonance: ★ Same-Frequency Thunder · Power to Break Deadlock
★ Harmony of Hard and Soft · Order Takes Shape
conflict: ◆ Lake Water Quenches Fire · Adaptation Meets Resistance
◆ Li Fire Scorches the Lake · Rules Become Rigid
advice: When making decisions, use the gentleness of Sui to gather public opinion; when implementing, use the firmness of Shihe to draw red lines. At each monthly review, adjust the balance of hardness and softness in light of the hexagrams.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Following and Adorning
one_liner: One moves with the current, the other carves with care; within their contrast lies a quiet accord of motion and stillness.
analysis: The Following hexagram, with thunder in the lake, signifies adapting to the times and flexible change; the Adorning hexagram, with fire beneath the mountain, values ornamentation, restraint, and civil refinement. The two mirror lake and mountain — one gentle, one firm: Following accepts change with its fluid nature, while Adorning carves order with its still demeanor. In the judgments, Following's 'supreme success, persevering furthers' emphasizes the natural way, while Adorning's 'small benefit in going somewhere' warns that decoration must be measured. The images 'withdrawing to rest at nightfall' and 'illuminating governance without daring to settle judgments' create a tension — the former teaches one to rest in accord with the season, the latter advocates clarity in governance while cautioning against arbitrariness. In combination, Following's inclusiveness dissolves Adorning's rigidity, and Adorning's refinement lifts Following's scatteredness; yet too much following loses direction, and too much ornamentation becomes superficial. One must find balance between movement and stillness, nature and artifice.
resonance: ★ Keen sensitivity to the external environment
★ A shared core of seeking harmony and order
conflict: ◆ The clash between spontaneous adaptability and fixed standards
◆ The friction between natural expression and deliberate refinement
advice: In collaboration, use Following to set the overall direction and Adorning to fill in the details. Each month, do a 'nightfall review' to harmonize the rhythm, avoiding both drifting with the tide and over-embellishment.

one_liner: Build your foundation by following the flow; let deep accumulation achieve great things.
analysis: The Following hexagram (Lake over Thunder) stirs with yielding adaptability, moving in harmony with the timing of Heaven. The Splitting Apart hexagram (Mountain over Earth) relies on deep, quiet strength, making the firming of foundations its root. When these two meet, it is like flowing water upon a great rock: the flexible ingenuity of Following breathes vitality into Splitting Apart's period of decline, keeping it from rigidity; the generous stability of Splitting Apart gives Following a reliable anchor, keeping it from drifting with the current. The motion of Lake and Thunder requires the steadiness of Mountain and Earth to keep from dissolving; the guarding of Mountain and Earth benefits from the transformation of Lake and Thunder to keep from decaying. Thus they form a symbiotic cycle of dynamic equilibrium.
resonance: ★ Aligning with Heaven's timing
★ Strengthening the foundation
conflict: ◆ Seeking novelty through change
◆ Seeking security through conservatism
advice: Before acting, spend three days observing the trends of your environment, then seven days consolidating your core resources. When you adjust to circumstances, do not deviate from your fundamental goal.

one_liner: You let the current guide your direction; I put down roots and gather strength, biding my time. When we're in sync, it's the perfect time and place.
analysis: With Lake over Thunder, Sui (Following) urges going with the current and following the good—like water turning as the terrain shifts. With Earth over Thunder, Fu (Return) stirs beneath the surface, emphasizing the return of cycles and movement after stillness—like winter storing what spring will bring. These two natures, Lake and Earth, succeed each other: one is outwardly nimble and adaptive, the other inwardly keeps a rhythm of renewal. Sui’s timely withdrawal—'resting at dusk'—provides a buffer for Fu’s energy-storing cycle of 'return after seven days.' Fu’s 'thunder within the earth,' deeply accumulated and ready to burst, in turn grounds Sui’s fluidity. Together they create a dynamic balance: Sui melts obstacles with softness, Fu awakens vitality with stillness, completing an endlessly evolving spiral of energy.
resonance: ★ Follow the Current, Store Strength
★ Cyclic Symbiosis
conflict: ◆ Off-Beat Timing
◆ Divergent Directions
advice: Sui must preserve a settling period for Fu, and Fu should borrow Sui’s momentum to break new ground—create a phased plan where the two alternate in leading.

relationship_name: Thunder and Lake: A Shared Bond
one_liner: You move with the times, I stand in integrity; between movement and stillness lies a world of its own.
analysis: The Sui (Following) hexagram has thunder within the lake, responding to change with a gentle, yielding posture. The Wu Wang (Innocence) hexagram has thunder moving under heaven, acting with upright, steadfast virtue in accord with principle. Both share the thunder image, yet they manifest differently: lake water nourishes the vitality of thunder's motion, while the vault of heaven regulates the track of thunder's course. Both hexagram texts speak of 'yuan heng li zhen' (great prosperity and beneficial perseverance), but Sui values the flexible response of 'no blame,' while Wu Wang warns of holding the line against 'misfortune from improper action.' In the Image commentaries, 'retiring at night to rest' and 'responding to the seasons to nourish all things' echo each other as micro-level adaptation and macro-level order. The lake's inclusiveness and heaven's sense of order resonate through thunder's catalysis, complementing each other in times of upheaval, while the differing measures of 'following' and 'innocence' create a productive tension.
resonance: ★ Thunder in Unison: Both reveal the power of action through the thunder image
★ Lake and Heaven Support Each Other: Yielding nurture and upright order coexist
conflict: ◆ Following Can Lose Its Aim: Excessive adaptability may blur the boundaries of principles
◆ Uprightness Lacks Tact: Absolute sincerity may ignore contextual nuance
advice: For major decisions, first use the Sui hexagram's mindset to absorb the changing situation, then use the Wu Wang hexagram's standard to verify the legitimacy of your actions.

one_liner: One shifts with the tide, the other stands firm on solid ground — motion and stillness together work wonders.
analysis: Sui (The Following), with its Lake nature, governs fluid adaptability; Da Xu (The Taming Power of the Great), with its Mountain nature, governs deep accumulation. Sui's teaching, 'retire at dusk to rest and refresh,' calls for moving only after discerning the signs; Da Xu's dictum, 'learn much of the words and deeds of the past,' stresses building up strength before release. Lake and Thunder stir each other, and change arises; Mountain and Heaven pile up, and hidden power accrues. Together they form a tensile structure of 'outer motion, inner stillness': Sui's flexibility provides a weathervane for Da Xu's preparations, while Da Xu's depth acts as ballast, keeping Sui's shifts from capsizing. The hexagram texts 'No blame' and 'Favorable to cross the great river' echo each other, revealing that only by riding the current without blind conformity, and by storing virtue without rigid adherence, can one truly accomplish things amid change.
resonance: ★ Sharpness in sensing the trend and seizing the moment
★ Patience in accumulating virtue and nurturing talent
conflict: ◆ Immediate adaptability vs. long-term preparation
◆ Shifting goals vs. rigidly fixed paths
advice: When facing major decisions, the Sui party should test the waters and gather feedback, while the Da Xu party simultaneously builds its reserves. Once the winds are clear, join forces and advance together.

one_liner: One flows with the times, the other cultivates the self; pairing action with stillness means you never wear each other out.
analysis: The hexagram Sui (Following) — Lake over Thunder — stirs with the impulse to yield to the times and advance or retreat with measure (Yuan Heng Li Zhen: supreme success, favorable constancy). The hexagram Yi (Nourishment) — Mountain over Thunder — emphasizes inner cultivation of the roots, careful speech, and moderate eating (Zhen Ji: perseverance brings good fortune). The Lake is fluid and changeable; the Mountain is steady and still. With Thunder as their link, they form a dynamic balance: Following's flexible responsiveness gives Nourishment's self-cultivation a practical arena, while Nourishment's restraint and stillness set boundaries for Following's spontaneity. In the hexagram images, Thunder moves under the Lake and hides under the Mountain — just as outward action and inwardly stored energy complement each other, together building a symbiosis of "following the current without losing one's root, and nurturing stillness without becoming stuck in form."
resonance: ★ The rhythm of action and stillness generating each other
★ The cycle of yielding and inner nourishment
conflict: ◆ Following the tide can lose the self vs. holding fast can become rigid
◆ The different pace of Lake-motion and Mountain-stillness
advice: Those embodying Following should ask the Nourishment person for input before acting; those embodying Nourishment should step out of their comfort zone from time to time to join in practice.

one_liner: One glides with the current, the other poles against it—practicing Tai Chi push-hands in the same lake.
analysis: The Following hexagram shows Lake over Thunder, yielding to the rhythm of heaven; the Preponderance of the Great shows Lake overwhelming Wind and Wood, breaking convention with firm resolve. Both share the Lake-Water nature yet stand at opposite poles of motion and stillness: Following's wisdom of 'withdrawing to rest at dusk' holds the subtlety of yielding, while Preponderance of the Great's 'standing alone without fear' reveals the courage to break through. Their common Lake-Water essence makes them resonate naturally in crisis, but Thunder's hidden latency and Wind's penetrating quality create a divergence in the rhythm of action. When Following's 'choose good and follow it' meets Preponderance of the Great's 'bent beam pressing onward,' it becomes like the cooperation of water carrying a boat and wind filling the sails—requiring the Lake's inclusiveness to harmonize the polarities of firmness and yielding.
resonance: ★ Shared Lake, Common Source: both cultivate resilience through water's virtue
★ Mutual Generation of Hidden and Manifest: Thunder gathers power in stillness while Wind passes without a trace—a complement across time and space
conflict: ◆ Contest of Direction: the tug-of-war between yielding to the times and defying the tide in decisive action
◆ Load-Bearing Difference: a rhythm mismatch between periods of restful recharge and periods of standing alone under pressure
advice: Establish a 'tidal decision method': on the new moon and full moon each month, alternate who takes the lead—Following governs the phase of adaptive adjustment, Preponderance of the Great governs the phase of hard breakthrough.

relationship_name: Lake and Abyss in Mutual Aid
one_liner: You go with the current while I break the waves; stillness and motion interweave into a scene of their own.
analysis: The hexagram Following (Sui) pairs Lake over Thunder, advocating going with the times and resting when appropriate; Kan (The Abysmal) is double water and stacked perils, stressing perseverance to weather crises and teaching to secure the root. When these two meet, they create a unique field of 'supple motion assisting each other': Following's agility dissolves Abysmal's stagnation, while Abysmal's tenacity anchors Following's drift. The Lake-Thunder 'resting at dusk' and the Abyss-Water 'practicing constancy' form a complementary rhythm across time—like the cooperation of tide and undercurrent, keeping Following from being swept along, and preventing Abysmal from freezing in peril.
resonance: ★ Dynamic balance between going with the flow and breaking through
★ Natural affinity between restorative and disciplined cycles
conflict: ◆ Spontaneous adaptability meets stubborn persistence
◆ Rhythm mismatch between carpe diem and long-term discipline
advice: Establish a 'three-question mechanism': before acting, ask about timing (Following), then risk (The Abysmal), then sustainability—use both hexagrams' perspectives to cross-check decisions.

one_liner: You follow the tide, I carry the lamp; one gentle, one luminous, lighting the path ahead.
analysis: The Following hexagram shows thunder hidden in the lake, yielding softly to the time; the Clinging hexagram shows fire stacked upon fire, illuminating all quarters with bright light. Lake water nourishes all things and knows how to change; fire burns bright and steady, giving direction. When the two meet, they form a dynamic balance: the Following's choice of the good and its obedience requires the Clinging's clear discernment as guide; the Clinging's power to shine in all directions relies on the Following's receptive, adaptable support. In the Judgments, 'Supreme success, perseverance furthers' and 'Perseverance furthers, success' echo each other, revealing the dialectic of adapting and remaining steadfast. The Images—'withdraw into rest at nightfall' and 'continue the brightness to illuminate the four quarters'—complement each other, holding the wisdom that stillness and motion give rise to each other in a shared life. Lake and fire support each other instead of clashing; they become nourishment—like night sailors finding a lighthouse, or a boat catching a long wind.
resonance: ★ Flexibility meets clarity; going with the flow without losing your way
★ Thunder rouses, radiance follows; every action finds its home
conflict: ◆ Lake water easily overflows its banks; fire easily scorches across boundaries
◆ Following without focus dissolves momentum; forceful brightness crushes gentleness and drains vitality
advice: Each month, set three shared core goals. The Following role flexibly adapts the execution path; the Clinging role focuses on calibrating direction without crossing the line.

relationship_name: The Lake's Sensing, the Following Response
one_liner: Flow with the current and respond; heart-resonance blossoms in silence.
analysis: The hexagram Sui (Following), Lake over Thunder, stirs and interplays, emphasizing harmony with the times and choosing what is good. The hexagram Xian (Influence), Lake over Mountain, contains and reflects, valuing an open heart that senses and connects. Both share the nature of the Lake, yet one moves and one is still: Sui breaks through with thunder's motion, Xian embraces change with mountain's stillness. Both hexagram texts speak of 'Heng' (success) and 'Li Zhen' (perseverance furthers), revealing that these two naturally align in upholding the right path. The Image words, 'Going to rest at twilight' and 'emptiness receives others,' interweave to create a symbiotic pattern of 'following outwardly, sensing inwardly.' Thunder in motion needs the mountain's stability to channel its force; the Lake's moisture needs thunder's spark to bring forth its life. Together they find dynamic balance in the rhythm of advance and retreat.
resonance: ★ Sync with the Flow
★ Mutual Reflection in Openness
conflict: ◆ Overly Impetuous Momentum
◆ Stillness That Lags in Response
advice: Before acting, pause for three breaths to quietly observe your partner's aura; replace instant reactions with a 'pause-then-respond' rhythm.

relationship_name: Mutual Sustenance of Adaptation and Constancy
one_liner: You shift, I stay grounded—in perfect step, never weary.
analysis: The Sui (Following) hexagram, with the fluid nature of the Lake, advocates yielding to the times and choosing the good before acting. The Heng (Duration) hexagram, with the firm dynamic nature of Thunder, emphasizes establishing a foundation and never wavering from one's resolve. Their union creates a dynamic equilibrium: Sui's flexible adjustments provide an environmental buffer for Heng, while Heng's enduring steadiness anchors Sui's direction. The interaction of Lake and Thunder is like spring rain nourishing all things; the stirring of Wind and Thunder is like new shoots breaking through the soil—achieving a symbiotic rhythm between change and permanence.
resonance: ★ A symbiotic rhythm where action and stillness complement each other
★ Goal-oriented coordination of inner and outer forces
conflict: ◆ Anxiety triggered by differing rhythms
◆ The tug-of-war between holding principles and remaining flexible
advice: Designate a fixed review day each month. Use Heng's framework to trace and sort through Sui's paths of adaptation.

relationship_name: Go with the Flow, Know When to Retreat
one_liner: You know the ease of going with the flow, I know the clarity of knowing when to step back. Even our 'lying flat' has a sense of rhythm.
analysis: The Following hexagram, with 'thunder within the lake,' belongs to Lake. Its Judgement speaks of 'great success through perseverance,' and the Image advises 'retiring at dusk to rest,' advocating yielding to the times and balancing movement with stillness. The Retreat hexagram, with 'mountain under heaven,' belongs to Heaven. Its Judgement speaks of 'small perseverance brings good fortune,' and the Image emphasizes 'keeping away from inferior people, not with severity but with dignity,' focusing on reading the times and withdrawing proactively. One governs smooth following, the other governs retreat; yet they resonate strongly on 'knowing when to stop and keeping to the hour.' The softness of the Lake nourishes the loftiness of Heaven; the firmness of Heaven clarifies the Lake's direction. When Following's choice of the good meets Retreat's dignified distance, both understand how to leave room amid noise and advance by retreating—forming a resonant field that consumes nothing yet runs deep.
resonance: ★ The kindred rhythm of retiring at dusk
★ The clear-headed awareness of keeping one's distance and guarding boundaries
conflict: ◆ Following along can blur personal boundaries
◆ Retreating can come across as cold and aloof
advice: Agree to set aside half a day each week as a personal offline period. The Following hexagram takes charge of sorting through outside information and sharing it gently; the Retreat hexagram responds with clear, unemotional feedback. Replace over-adjusting with a rhythmic give-and-take.

one_liner: The supple pairs with the strong; advance and retreat follow a clear pattern.
analysis: Following (Sui) has thunder within the lake, advocating going with the flow and choosing what is good; The Power of the Great (Da Zhuang) has thunder in the heavens, emphasizing firm correctness and refraining from what is not proper. The two, one lake and one thunder, form a dynamic complement: Following’s resilience can soften the sharp edge of the Great Power’s strength, while Great Power’s steadfastness can anchor Following’s flexible direction. In the judgments, Following’s “no blame” presupposes discernment, and Great Power’s “favorable to be steadfast” requires restraint as its baseline. United, they are like water bearing thunder—Following supplies adaptability, Great Power supplies momentum, allowing one to read changing circumstances without losing principled boundaries.
resonance: ★ The rhythmic resonance of going with the flow and storing energy
★ The shared frequency of upholding principle and responding to change
conflict: ◆ Following’s tendency to compromise may be seen by the Great Power as lacking conviction
◆ The Great Power’s rigid principles may stifle Following’s flexibility
advice: When making decisions, first use Following’s mindset to gather diverse information, then use the Great Power’s standards to set action boundaries, avoiding excessive accommodation or recklessness

relationship_name: Mutual Aid of Lake and Fire
one_liner: You move forward on the light I lend; I pave the way with the current’s flow — in motion and in stillness, all becomes a scene.
analysis: The Following hexagram (Lake over Thunder) holds the two elements in mutual embrace; its theme is gentle compliance and timely adaptation, like lake water receiving the thunder’s movement and gathering momentum. The Progress hexagram (Fire over Earth) shines through mutual illumination; its theme is bright advancement and radiant virtue, like the morning sun breaking the earth’s surface and ascending. By nature, Lake moistens and Fire illuminates; in principle, the Follower knows when to stop and the Progressor knows when to advance—thus forming a cycle of “nourishing clarity through compliance, and guiding compliance through clarity.” The Following hexagram’s “resting at nightfall” provides the restorative foundation for the Progress hexagram’s “three audiences by day”; the Progress hexagram’s “brightening his own bright virtue” lights the path for the Following hexagram’s “choosing the good and following it.” Water and fire are fundamentally antagonistic, yet in this configuration the lake does not extinguish the fire but instead evaporates into clouds, and the fire does not boil the lake but instead warms it into a spring. This is the noble person’s way in the world: knowing when to advance and when to retreat, holding fast to the center and the right, yielding to the times while preserving the original heart.
resonance: ★ Follow the tide and gather strength; do not strive to be first, yet you will come to a good end.
★ Break the darkness with the light of Progress; without hiding your edge, you shine of your own accord.
conflict: ◆ The Follower risks sinking into passive waiting; the Progressor often appears hasty and overreaching.
◆ The Lake’s nature is soft and slow, needing time to settle; the Fire’s nature is fierce and hot, demanding swift results.
advice: On every new moon and full moon, sit together and plan the rhythm of action: three days ahead, the Following person lists the “opportunities for yielding,” while the Progressing person marks the “nodes for breakthrough.” Let the lunar calendar anchor your timing, harmonizing the frequency of motion and stillness.

relationship_name: Mutual Aid of Dark and Light
one_liner: Flowing water moves with the current, colliding with a dark fire that hides its edge within the earth.
analysis: In the Hexagram of Following, Lake over Thunder evokes the nimble art of yielding to the times; in the Darkening of the Light, Earth over Fire quietly speaks of the endurance that comes from sheathing one's brilliance. The fluid tolerance of the Lake and the calm bearing of the Earth form a dynamic balance: the 'supreme success, furthering through perseverance' of Following is held in check by the 'perseverance furthers in hardship' of Darkening. The former teaches us to read the signs and act on what is good; the latter reminds us to keep our core intact and hide our light in adversity. The two Image texts—'withdrawing at dusk to rest' and 'using darkness to make things clear'—point to a shared wisdom: knowing how to shift between openness and concealment. And yet, Lake-Thunder's active responsiveness and Earth-Fire's patient withdrawal are apt to fall out of step when it comes to action.
resonance: ★ Both value inner discipline and steadfastness.
★ Both counsel the wisdom of moving with the times while keeping one's edge concealed.
conflict: ◆ Following seeks change vs. Darkening of the Light guards stillness.
◆ Darkening's forbearance can easily be misread by Following as passivity.
advice: In smooth times, let Following draw on Darkening's steadiness to curb impulsiveness; in hard times, let Darkening learn Following's flexibility to break a stalemate.

one_liner: Sailing with the wind outside, keeping the family lamp burning within—the true test lies in the dance of motion and stillness.
analysis: The Following hexagram, Lake over Thunder, embodies the art of adapting to the times—lake water shifts as thunder moves. The Family hexagram, Wind over Fire, takes the constancy of the household as the foundation of life—a gentle breeze flowing forth from the flame. Together they create a tension between change and constancy: Following teaches us to read the moment and choose what is good, while Family stresses consistency in word and deed and holding fast to what is right. When external circumstances are turbulent, Following's flexibility can break a path forward, and Family's steadiness can anchor core values. Yet yielding too much risks losing your roots, and clinging too rigidly to family rules risks rigidity. The two must serve as mirrors for each other in dynamic balance.
resonance: ★ Motion and stillness give rise to each other
★ Order within and without
conflict: ◆ The tug-of-war between adapting and abiding
◆ The clash of outward expression and inward restraint
advice: When adapting to external changes, let family principles be your decision-making baseline, and practice enduring values through flexible means.

relationship_name: Mutual Completion of Following and Divergence
one_liner: You know how to ride the wave and lay the groundwork; I dare to plant my own flag. Together, our partnership’s signature move is winning without a head-on clash.
analysis: The Hexagram of Following’s ‘sublime success, perseverance furthers’ and ‘retreating at dusk to rest’ reveal the gentle compliance of the Lake nature—knowing how to read the times, advancing and retreating with measure. The Hexagram of Opposition’s ‘small things bring good fortune’ and ‘together yet different’ show the bright intensity of the Fire nature—valuing clear boundaries, harmonizing without uniformity. When these two meet, the Lake’s inclusiveness can dissolve the Fire’s restlessness, and the Fire’s clarity can illuminate the Lake’s drifting with the current. Following gives Opposition a buffer and an opening, so that ‘contrariness’ never becomes a split; Opposition gives Following resolve and independent viewpoint, so that ‘going along with the crowd’ never loses its way. This complementarity is a precise meshing of movement and stillness, union and separation—finding rapport within difference, and guarding the inner self while adapting.
resonance: ★ The relaxed ease of sensing the moment and riding the flow
★ The lucid clarity of harmony without sameness
conflict: ◆ Too much go-with-the-flow can blur your bottom line
◆ Boundaries too rigid can leave the air cold
advice: When disagreements arise, let the Following partner gracefully build a staircase, while the Opposition partner clearly states their bottom line. Agree on ‘seek common ground on small matters, let each shine in their own way on big ones’—and replace emotional exhaustion with regular check-ins.

relationship_name: A Symbiosis of Marsh and Water
one_liner: You ride the currents; I temper my spirit in the wind. Together, our rhythm is the key to breaking through.
analysis: In Following, Lake over Thunder urges compliance with the times and choosing the good, as pliant and welcoming as a marsh. In Obstruction, Water over Mountain warns of danger and calls for turning inward, refining virtue to break through, like a frozen spring that still holds the pulse of life. One is a lake, the other water—same family, yet currents run differently: Following dissolves resistance by flowing; Obstruction concentrates power by settling. When Following's adaptability meets Obstruction's deep stillness, they form a complementary whole of 'outer compliance, inner cultivation.' Following helps Obstruction avoid rigid stands; Obstruction gives Following a moral compass. Between movement and steadfastness, they find dynamic equilibrium—as if marsh soothes mountain bones and water quickens thunder's voice.
resonance: ★ The balance of going with the flow and cultivating the heart
★ The complement of flexibility and resolve
conflict: ◆ Over-adaptation loses direction
◆ Over-steadfastness loses flexibility
advice: In any endeavor, first gauge the direction of events with a Following mindset, then turn inward with an Obstruction attitude to recalibrate your strategy—neither drifting nor hardening.

one_liner: One weaves with the current, the other breaks through to open the floodgates. Together they untangle a thousand knots; apart, each spins in circles.
analysis: The Following hexagram, with its Lake nature, holds the spirit of gentle acceptance, following the wisdom of 'withdrawing at dusk to seek rest and refreshment.' The Deliverance hexagram, with its Thunder nature, moves to cut through stagnation, using the momentum of 'thunder and rain arising' to sweep away old pitfalls. Together they form a chemical reaction of 'quiet accumulation giving way to dynamic release': the Following hexagram's inclusiveness gives the Deliverance hexagram breathing room, while the Deliverance hexagram's decisiveness infuses the Following hexagram with the power to break through. Yet when Lake and Thunder clash, if Following yields too much it dulls the edge of action, and if Deliverance rushes too fast it disrupts the rhythm of flow. Balance must be found between the leniency that 'forgives faults and pardons offenses' and the timeliness of 'early good fortune.'
resonance: ★ Energy conversion: the soft stores power, the hard releases it
★ Resonance between the ripening of timing and the breakthrough moment
conflict: ◆ The tug between a slow, yielding pace and the demand for swift resolution
◆ Friction between merciful leniency and thunderous action
advice: Before major decisions, spend three days observing with the mindset of Following, then spend three days crafting a breakthrough plan in the mode of Deliverance.

relationship_name: Mutual Aid of Flow and Rest
one_liner: You know the harmony of going with the flow; I know the measure of knowing when to stop — together we make a lasting relationship free of inner friction.
analysis: The Sui (Following) hexagram, Lake above Thunder, advocates resting in darkness and retiring at nightfall, in harmony with the seasons and choosing only the good. The Sun (Decrease) hexagram, Mountain above Lake below, emphasizes curbing anger, restraining desire, and offering with two simple baskets — focusing on reducing excess and cultivating inward. With Lake water as their common medium, one is outwardly yielding and adaptive, the other inwardly restrained and disciplined. Their unique chemistry: Sui's fluidity dissolves Sun's rigidity, while Sun's focus anchors Sui's drift. When Sui learns to leave open spaces within 'sublime success and furthering perseverance,' and Sun learns to relax within sincerity and constancy, the two can build a deep complementarity without inner friction, moving freely between advance and retreat, tension and ease.
resonance: ★ Shared origin in Lake water — both value inner cultivation and sincerity.
★ Rhythmic movement and stillness — together holding a shared sense of measure in advance and retreat.
conflict: ◆ The Following hexagram tends to overcompromise; Decrease finds it lacking in principles.
◆ The Decrease hexagram is overly restrained; Following feels it oppressive and dull.
advice: Set aside half a day each week for spontaneous, unplanned time and half a day for decluttering and quiet reflection, so your rhythms naturally interlock in ebb and flow.

relationship_name: Mutual Growth of Following and Increase
one_liner: You understand the value of going with the flow and gathering strength; I dare to ride the wind and break new ground. Together, we're a winning combination.
analysis: The Following hexagram has Lake above and Thunder below; its Judgment emphasizes 'Success through perseverance', and its Image points to the wisdom of yielding to the time and choosing what is good in order to gather strength. The Increase hexagram has Wind above and Thunder below; its Judgment highlights the power to act that can cross great rivers, and its Image advocates the enterprising spirit of moving toward the good when one sees it. Lake's inclusiveness provides a stable foundation for Wind's diffusion, while Wind's fluidity activates Lake's latent potential. They share Thunder's dynamism but diverge in their upper and lower trigrams: Following uses softness to master hardness, dissolving resistance; Increase uses sharpness to break deadlocks and open new opportunities. When Following's timely assessment meets Increase's proactive augmentation, they form a cycle of 'quiet accumulation and dynamic release'—the former avoids the depletion of recklessness, the latter compensates for the limits of conservatism, achieving an upward spiral of resources and opportunities in dynamic balance.
resonance: ★ Resonance between yielding and gathering strength and breaking through with initiative
★ Synergy between choosing the good to follow and moving toward the good when seen
conflict: ◆ Lake's steady rhythm vs Wind's seeking quick results
◆ Avoiding blame and staying safe vs braving risks and exploring new ground
advice: The Following side should proactively issue a trend observation report each month; the Increase side should break down large goals into adjustable milestones. Together, establish a dual-track mechanism of 'assessing the situation, then augmenting and executing'.

relationship_name: The Confluence of Yielding and Resolve
one_liner: One paves the way by going with the flow; the other dares to cleave mountains and open a road. Together they get twice the results with half the effort.
analysis: The Following hexagram shows thunder within the lake, responding to the times with gentle compliance and emphasizing the choice to follow what is good. The Breakthrough hexagram shows the lake risen to heaven, acting with firm decisiveness and courage, advocating the bestowal of benefits upon those below. Both share the nature of the lake, yet one is subtle and the other overt. The Following's image of 'withdrawing to rest at nightfall' provides strategic flexibility, while the Breakthrough's caution against 'rushing to arms' imparts boldness to action. The chemistry lies in how the Following's accommodating buffer can dissolve the Breakthrough's sharp edge, while the Breakthrough's decisiveness can push the Following's intentions into concrete reality. Like lake water that surges into power when stirred by thunder, or rises and turns to rain when meeting heaven, the two form a unique collaborative pattern of 'gentleness guiding, firmness advancing.'
resonance: ★ The supportive embrace of kindred waters
★ The complementary rhythm of following the flow and breaking through impasses
conflict: ◆ Compliance risks losing your own viewpoint vs. decisiveness risks seeming dictatorial
◆ Differences in the rhythm of seizing the right moment
advice: For major matters, deliberate jointly and apply the Breakthrough's clear judgment; for minor matters, act with the Following's flexibility. Use gentleness to temper strength and avoid forcing.

one_liner: You move with the current; I arrive on the wind. Our harmony springs from timing, not contrivance.
analysis: The Sui hexagram (Following) is lake-natured—soft and pliant, with Thunder as its mover—and it stresses adapting to the times and choosing what is right to follow. The Gou hexagram (Coming to Meet) is heaven-natured—lofty and far-reaching, with Wind that slips into every opening—and it symbolizes the chance of an unexpected encounter. One belongs to the lake, the other to the sky, creating a resonance between 'gathering force in the lowlands' and 'deploying influence from the heights.' Sui's 'great beginnings, smooth progress, benefit, and constancy' must borrow the reach of Gou's 'issuing commands throughout the four quarters' to amplify its impact; conversely, Gou's warning against 'the woman grown too strong' is tempered by Sui's cautious discernment, balancing impulsiveness. In the images, lake and thunder clash to generate change, while heaven and wind intermingle to build momentum. When the two meet, Sui's inclusiveness dissolves Gou's abruptness, and Gou's keen perception stirs Sui out of its stagnation—forming a unique cycle: 'ride the flow to greet opportunity, use the encounter to open new ground.'
resonance: ★ Soft adaptability draws in sudden opportunities
★ The alternation of stillness and motion catalyzes fresh beginnings
conflict: ◆ Sui's pursuit of stability may miss the fleeting window that Gou opens
◆ Gou's forceful entry can disrupt Sui's rhythmic balance
advice: When Gou presents an unexpected opportunity, Sui should apply the wisdom of 'retiring at dusk to rest'—pause before deciding, and use a three-day observation period to test the opportunity's authenticity before acting.

relationship_name: The Divergent Paths of Following and Gathering
one_liner: One rides the timely currents of heaven; the other builds dikes against undercurrents.
analysis: The upper trigrams both belong to Lake (Joyous), but the lower trigrams—Thunder and Earth—forge the core contrast. In Sui (Following), 'thunder is within the lake'; thunder stirs beneath the lake, and the Judgment speaks of 'supreme success, favorable through constancy,' while the Image advises 'retiring at nightfall to rest.' The hexagram is about adapting to circumstances with flexibility and blamelessness. In Cui (Gathering Together), 'the lake rises above the earth'; water gathers into a deep pool, and the Image warns 'to remove weapons and guard against the unexpected.' It emphasizes rallying people together and staying vigilant in times of peace. Both share the Lake's joyful receptivity, but Sui responds to change through movement, detouring around obstacles, while Cui stores strength through stillness, preparing against danger. The chemistry lies in this: Sui's free-spirited ease often looks like carelessness to Cui, and Cui's caution often feels tense to Sui. Yet if they merge, Sui can dissolve Cui's pent-up frustration, and Cui can anchor Sui's drifting—creating a dynamic tension of movement and stillness.
resonance: ★ Both share the Lake's joy and are skilled at gathering people
★ Both value going with the current, favorable to see the great person
conflict: ◆ Sui's flexible adaptation vs Cui's strict defense
◆ Resting at dusk and following the season vs Guarding against the unforeseen
advice: In collaboration, clarify the division of labor: let Sui (Following) handle external adaptation and breakthrough, while Cui (Gathering Together) manages internal coordination and risk control; set a fixed monthly meeting day to align goals with ritual, preventing Sui's carefree energy from draining Cui's focus.

one_liner: You move with the moment, I root and grow, and together we ascend in rhythm.
analysis: The Following hexagram (Lake over Thunder) draws its strength from mutual support, receiving Heaven's timing with pliant compliance. Pushing Upward (Earth over Wind) nurtures through reciprocal fostering, growing by bearing all things with deep virtue. Both share the foundation of 'sublime success' (yuan heng), but Following emphasizes shifting cleverly toward what is good, while Pushing Upward values steady, step-by-step accumulation. When the Lake's waters meet the Earth's wind—as spring thunder turns to rain that nourishes the trees—the Following's agility calibrates the course of Pushing Upward's ascent, while Pushing Upward's stability anchors the values that keep the Following's flow from drifting. However, the Lake's nature may easily become superficial in its compliance, and the Earth's nature may fall into a conservative rut of deep plowing. Take care lest a mismatch in tempo exhaust you with either 'following without advancing' or 'ascending without direction.'
resonance: ★ Riding the momentum to store energy: the Following's wisdom of choosing what is good optimizes the path for Pushing Upward's steady accumulation.
★ Balancing motion and stillness: the adaptability of Lake/Thunder and the steadfastness of Earth/Wind create a growth metronome.
conflict: ◆ Tempo friction: the Following's quick pivots can easily become misaligned with Pushing Upward's incremental pace.
◆ Goal tension: the Lake's adaptable fluidity can dilute the Earth's focused resolve for deep cultivation.
advice: Each month, hold a 'Flow Review Day' to recalibrate Pushing Upward's stage goals using the Following's flexible thinking, turning spontaneous adjustments into stepwise growth.

relationship_name: The Mutual Aid of Following and Oppression
one_liner: Flow with change but hold your lines; even in deadlock, vitality stirs.
analysis: Following, with thunder within the lake, stresses the flexibility of adapting to the times; Oppression, with the lake's water run dry, highlights the resilience of holding fast to one's inner core in adversity. Though both share the lake's encompassing nature, they present a dialectic of movement and stillness: Following's 'choosing the good and following it' offers a path to break the deadlock for Oppression, while Oppression's 'staking one's life to fulfill one's aim' anchors the coordinates of value for Following. Thunder moving beneath the lake stirs transformative energy; the waterless lake forces deeper potential to emerge, creating a symbiotic structure of 'round outside, square inside.' Yet it must be noted that Following's excessive adaptability may dilute Oppression's decisiveness, while Oppression's solitary steadfastness may hinder Following's flow. The key is to find a balance between flexibility and persistence.
resonance: ★ Both share the lake's encompassing nature, valuing the resonance between circumstance and resolve.
★ Following's thunder can break the impasse of Oppression; Oppression's firm will can steady the course of Following.
conflict: ◆ In resource allocation, Following's drive for change and Oppression's hold-fast stance can create friction.
◆ As for tempo of action, Following's quickness and Oppression's heavy slowness need coordinated adjustment.
advice: Each month, together draw up a 'change and hold' list: let Following lead on three flexible-response strategies, and Oppression lock in two core bottom lines, using the wisdom of thunder to channel the waterless bind.

relationship_name: The Lake and the Well, Mutual Sustenance
one_liner: You choose your path by following the current; I nurture from deep springs. Together, we become living water that flows forever.
analysis: The Following hexagram (Thunder over Lake) drives action in accord with the times, while the Well hexagram (Water over Wind) nourishes through constancy. The fluidity of the Lake and the stability of the Well form a natural complement: the Following hexagram is like ripples on water, adept at seizing moments and adjusting direction; the Well hexagram is like an underground spring, quietly accumulating resources and sustaining the root. Their union mirrors the dialectical unity described in the Image texts: 'retire to rest when day darkens' and 'encourage the people to mutual aid.' The adaptive wisdom of the Following resolves the rigidity of the Well's constancy, while the deep substance of the Well tempers the risk of superficial drift in the Following. Together they build a symbiotic system of 'motion within stillness, constancy within change.'
resonance: ★ Agility in moving with the current
★ Sustained nourishing power
conflict: ◆ The rhythm gap between flexibility and constancy
◆ Dominance over resource allocation
advice: Establish a 'tidal collaboration' mechanism: when the Following hexagram blazes new trails, reserve a third of resources for the Well hexagram to settle and store; before the Well hexagram dispenses its nourishment, let the Following hexagram assess the timing and fitness.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Following and Revolution
one_liner: Move with the times, break the old pattern, and find new life.
analysis: Following (Hexagram 17) has thunder within the lake, accepting Heaven's timing with gentle compliance; its Judgment, 'supreme success, furthering through perseverance,' stresses holding firm while waiting for the right moment. Revolution (Hexagram 49) has fire within the lake, shattering stale arrangements with fierce decisiveness; its Image, 'set the calendar and clarify the seasons,' proclaims the will to destroy the old and establish the new. Both share the Lake body yet hide a difference: in Following, still water veils thunder — retreating to advance, storing energy; in Revolution, boiling water feeds flame — breaking to create, catalyzing transformation. When they come together, Following's habit of 'turning toward dusk to rest and refresh' cushions Revolution's drastic reforms, while Revolution's 'in one's own day there is trust' drives momentum into Following's conservative stance. Lake water merges, thunder and fire quicken each other, producing a dynamic balance of 'staying true without stiffness, seeking change without reckless action' — exactly what the Commentary calls 'those who adapt and transform are those who move with the times.'
resonance: ★ Go with the flow, build momentum
★ Break the old, welcome the new
conflict: ◆ Blind obedience erodes your own voice
◆ Radical overhauls undermine the foundations
advice: Build a window for revolutionary change inside Following's flexibility. Review your situation every month, and let small experiments replace grand upheavals.

relationship_name: Ride the Current, Found the Cauldron
one_liner: You go with the flow and avoid needless struggle; I spark the flame and build something new.
analysis: Ze Lei Sui (Lake over Thunder: Following) is about yielding and following. The soft lake water moves while thunder hides within, emphasizing the adaptive and contracting nature of 'going to rest in the dark of evening'. Huo Feng Ding (Fire over Wind: The Cauldron) is about renewal. Wood feeds fire, emphasizing the transformative and stabilizing nature of 'correcting the position and fixing one's fate'. The two form a striking contrast: Following is like water—flexible and accommodating; The Cauldron is like fire—steadfast and reshaping. The 'sublime success, perseverance' of Following lies in following others without blame; The Cauldron's 'supreme fortune and smooth passage' lies in breaking the old pattern and founding the new. The chemistry between them is 'nourish The Cauldron with Following, and guide Following with The Cauldron' — Following's soft tolerance cushions The Cauldron's drastic transformation, while The Cauldron's clear direction prevents Following from drifting into mindless conformity. One yielding, one firm, they strike a dynamic balance between going with the flow and making it happen.
resonance: ★ The penetrating wisdom of yielding to Heaven's rhythm
★ The enterprising spirit of grasping the right moment
conflict: ◆ Taking life as it comes vs. Calling the shots
◆ Flexible compromise vs. Stubbornly fighting tooth and nail
advice: For major matters, the Cauldron should make the decisions and set the rules; for minor matters, the Following should improvise and adapt. The Cauldron must leave the Following time to rest and recharge at dusk, while the Following must hold the line on principle and avoid over-conceding.

one_liner: You split the chaos and astonish the crowd; I ride the current and catch you.
analysis: Zhen is pure thunder; its Judgment 'startles a hundred miles but does not drop the sacrificial ladle' speaks of breaking through impasses and awakening. Sui is lake over thunder; its Image says 'thunder in the midst of the lake: at dusk, retire and rest' speaks of yielding and embracing. The two share the thunder nature: Zhen's thunderbolt is the inner drive for Sui, and Sui's gentle lake is the buffer for Zhen. Zhen ignites action with 'fear and self-examination'; Sui softens the landing with 'choosing the good and following it.' The thunder entering the lake does not clash outright, but turns into a long, lingering echo. This is the precise meshing of movement and stillness: Zhen supplies the sharp edge to break through, Sui supplies the flexible recovery to settle things after — together they build a resonant field of 'moving with restraint, yielding without blindness.'
resonance: ★ The action resonance of a thunderbolt breaking through the deadlock
★ The embracing resonance of lake water going with the flow
conflict: ◆ The rhythm mismatch between ceaseless thunder and resting at dusk
◆ The boundary test between upright self-discipline and blind compliance
advice: When disagreements arise, the Zhen side first clarifies its bottom line without pressure; the Sui side proactively proposes a flexible transition plan, and establish a regular review mechanism that alternates between motion and stillness, so the thunder's explosive force is precisely transformed into the lake's nourishing power.

relationship_name: Mutual Accord of Movement and Stillness
one_liner: Flow with the current, find peace in knowing when to stop; between action and stillness lies a kindred understanding.
analysis: The Hexagram Sui (Following) has Thunder within the Lake, responding to the times with gentle compliance. Its Judgement, 'Supreme success, perseverance furthers,' highlights the unblocked course of moving with the situation. The Hexagram Gen (Keeping Still) is Mountain upon Mountain, guarding its own position through stillness. Its Image, 'The superior man does not allow his thoughts to go beyond his situation,' emphasizes the wisdom of knowing when to stop. The flowing waters of the Lake and the stable mass of the Mountain create a tension in their natures, yet they resonate because they share the baseline of 'no blame': Sui's flexible discernment infuses Gen's quiet constancy with vitality, while Gen's defined boundaries and cessation of delusion anchor Sui's course. Like thunder hidden in the Lake, gathering force to break forth, and a Mountain standing firm while nurturing life, the interplay of movement and stillness achieves a delicate balance between 'retiring to rest at nightfall' and 'entering the courtyard without seeing anyone,' transforming conflict into generative power.
resonance: ★ The 'No Blame' Consensus
★ Flow with the Times, Know When to Stop
conflict: ◆ The Tug Between Movement and Stillness
◆ The Delicate Balance of Advance and Retreat
advice: Observe the current before you act, and adapt; when deciding, hold your position and know when to stop. Let stillness master motion, and motion break deadlock, drawing clear lines between advance and retreat.

relationship_name: Following the Flow, Ascending Step by Step
one_liner: One switches with the flow without burning out; the other grinds to the end, slowly enduring. As a pair, they stay right on track.
analysis: The Sui hexagram belongs to the lake, with thunder within the lake. Its text says 'supreme success; perseverance brings good fortune,' and centers on the flowing art of 'going to rest and repose at nightfall.' Water is fluid and agile, moving when it meets an opening. The Jian hexagram belongs to the wind, with wind over the mountain. Its text says 'the maiden is given in marriage; good fortune,' and embodies the step-by-step process of 'a tree growing on the mountain.' The wind is penetrating and values deep, long-term roots. The two are in sharp contrast: one fast, one slow; one lively, one steady. Sui's agility can break through Jian's rigidity and prevent it from exhausting itself in stubborn persistence; Jian's steadiness can anchor Sui's drift and keep it from being swept away by the current. This pairing is like flowing water circling a green mountain — knowing when to advance and when to retreat, understanding deep cultivation, and finding a dynamic balance between change and constancy.
resonance: ★ The ease of going with the flow
★ The sureness of step-by-step persistence
conflict: ◆ Rhythm clash: one quits while ahead, the other moves at a leisurely pace
◆ Strategy split: flexible trial-and-error versus one step, one mark
advice: The Following partner should curb the urge to frequently change course during the Development partner's deep-dive period, and the Development partner should leave room for flexibility for the Following partner at key junctures. Together, they agree to keep the big direction fixed and make quick small adjustments.

relationship_name: Mutual Aid of Thunder and Lake
one_liner: Flow with the times without blind conformity; know when to stop without overreaching—a steady win for the pair.
analysis: In the Following hexagram, Lake lies below and Thunder above. Yielding in softness, it bears the movement of the strong, and the judgment 'Supreme success, perseverance furthers' reveals the wisdom of following the time and staying free of blame. The Marrying Maiden hexagram places Thunder above and Lake below—force presses down on the soft lake, and the warning 'Undertakings bring misfortune' cautions against reckless advance. Though the two are opposites in nature—Thunder and Lake reversed—they form a dynamic complement: the dormant wisdom of Following, 'retiring at dusk to rest,' tempers the impatience of Marrying Maiden, which 'knows the end and foresees decay'; while Marrying Maiden's decisiveness can activate Following's tendency to drift. Both Image commentaries carry the core message of 'knowing the time'—one hides its edge and waits for the moment, the other plans before acting. Hardness and softness interweave into a symbiotic rhythm of measured advance and retreat.
resonance: ★ Softness bearing the strong turns danger into safety
★ The breathing cadence of knowing the moment and knowing the limit
conflict: ◆ Thunder's urgency can break the pattern vs Lake's sluggishness loses the lead
◆ Yield to shifting currents vs Cling to a fixed end—the tug-of-war
advice: When deciding, first let Following test the wind and adjust the rhythm; then let Marrying Maiden fix the bottom line and manage risk. Each month, co-cultivate an 'advance and retreat checklist' to recalibrate your pace.

one_liner: Move with the times, and shine together in shared brilliance.
analysis: The hexagram Sui (Following) — Lake over Thunder — stresses moving with the pulse of heaven and choosing what is good to follow; Feng (Abundance) — Thunder over Fire — blazes with expansive radiance and sharp discernment. When these two meet, the Lake's soft, moist grace tempers the fierce heat of Thunder-Fire, creating a resonant field in which movement holds stillness and clarity embraces tolerance. Sui's wisdom of 'retiring to rest at nightfall' complements Feng's resolve to 'render judgments and enforce penalties,' striking a dynamic balance amid change. Yet thunder-fire can easily sear lake-water: watch that Feng's force does not dominate Sui's yielding nature, or that Sui's excessive concession does not blunt Feng's decisive clarity.
resonance: ★ Kindred Resonance in Going with the Tide
★ The Mutual Support of Decisiveness and Tolerance
conflict: ◆ The Misalignment of Fast and Slow Rhythms
◆ Friction Along the Edge of Clarity and Obscurity
advice: Each month, set a 'Day of Quiet Observation' to review your rhythm together, letting the Lake's softness buffer the Thunder-Fire's impetuous rush.

relationship_name: Lake and Fire in Mutual Support
one_liner: One knows when to go with the flow and take it easy; the other holds the lantern and scouts the way. Their blend of action and stillness never loses its footing.
analysis: The Following hexagram has the Lake's tolerant nature, like a water surface bearing thunder, and it teaches us to yield to the right moment and choose what is good to follow. The Wanderer hexagram has Fire's discerning nature, like a torch burning on a mountain, and it reminds us that traveling far requires careful judgment. The Lake governs gentle movement while Fire governs firm clarity; together they form a complementary structure of inner flexibility and outer caution. Following's elasticity dissolves the traveler's tension, and the Wanderer's alertness anchors the follower's ease. In the hexagram images, Lake-and-Thunder conceal a spark of vitality, while Mountain-and-Fire signal a need for vigilance—just as water carries a boat and fire lights the night path. In a changing environment, this pair can adjust direction fluidly while keeping a clear bottom line, creating a dynamic, balanced symbiosis.
resonance: ★ A kindred accord between following the current and perceiving the finest details
★ Resonance between inner composure and outer prudence
conflict: ◆ Going with the flow may meet fiery impatience; caution may look like hesitation
◆ Flexible adaptability is easily held in check by over-cautiousness
advice: When making decisions, first use the Following hexagram to sense the environmental winds, then use the Wanderer hexagram to draw safe boundaries. Each month, revisit the hexagram images to recalibrate your collaborative rhythm.

one_liner: You follow Heaven's timing and choose what is good; I move with the wind's momentum. Our harmony isn't forced—it comes from kindred understanding.
analysis: The Sui hexagram (Following) shows thunder within the lake, adapting to the times with a gentle, yielding posture, emphasizing the importance of seizing the right moment and choosing what is good. The Xun hexagram (The Gentle) features wind following wind, advancing its will through penetration, highlighting action that is gentle yet firm. Together, the lake's water nourishes the wind's momentum, while the wind helps the lake flow, creating a complementary cycle of 'waiting for the right time' and 'moving forward proactively.' Sui's 'great success and no blame' requires Xun's 'small efforts bring progress' to activate; Xun's 'carrying out orders' also needs Sui's 'resting at dusk' to balance the pace. This relationship is not about strong dominance, but naturally accomplishes things through resonance with the prevailing current.
resonance: ★ Riding the Current in Sync
★ Choosing the Good and Advancing Together
conflict: ◆ Differences in Rhythm
◆ The Pull Between Initiative and Going with the Flow
advice: Sui should clearly state its bottom line at key moments; Xun should leave room for flexibility before acting. Replace forceful pushing with the gentle touch of wind brushing the lake's surface.

relationship_name: The Symbiosis of Following and Joy
one_liner: One goes with the flow, the other opens hearts; stillness and motion weave into a wordless rapport.
analysis: The hexagram Following (Sui) is Lake embracing Thunder, emphasizing the supple wisdom of reading the moment; its Judgment's 'Supreme success, furthering through perseverance' conceals the way of dynamic equilibrium. The hexagram The Joyous (Dui) is twin Lakes stacked, where 'Lake upon Lake' signals emotional resonance, and the Image's 'friends join in discussion and practice' highlights the formative power of speech. Both share the element of Lake, yet their character is vastly different: Following is like a hidden undercurrent surging forward by retreating; The Joyous is like bright ripples spreading, drawing people in through delight. When the strategic flexibility of Following meets the open warmth of Joy, a symbiotic field emerges where gentleness dissolves rigidity and words move hearts. But excessive following can dilute the sincerity of Joy's expression, and endless discussion can disturb the quiet rhythm of Following's accumulation.
resonance: ★ The fluid grace of following the current with joy
★ The illuminating interplay of speech and action
conflict: ◆ Following the current may erode one's own agency
◆ Joyful words often remain on the surface
advice: Keep Following's calm observation for key decisions, and bring out Joy's empathy in daily interactions; do not let compromise replace sincere dialogue.

relationship_name: Wind and Lake: Following the Ripples
one_liner: You know the relaxed art of going with the flow; I know the kindred spirit of gathering after scattering. We click without effort.
analysis: The Following hexagram is of the Lake, and its Image—'Thunder in the Lake'—speaks of yielding to the times and going to rest with the dusk. The Dispersion hexagram is of the Wind, and its Image—'Wind over Water'—speaks of dissolving stale patterns and drawing hearts together in a common center. When they meet, the Lake's soft, moist nature can carry the Wind without pushing back, and the Wind's quick, animated spirit can stir ripples across the Lake. Following's steady devotion to 'choosing what is good and holding to it' gives Dispersion a gentle anchor against chaos; Dispersion's courage to 'cross the great river' shakes Following out of habits and prevents it from blindly following others. One is still, one is moving; together they reach a deep resonance between compliance and refashioning.
resonance: ★ A rhythmic sense of moving with the flow
★ A centripetal force that regathers after scattering
conflict: ◆ Following can sink into passive waiting, while Dispersion is too eager to break loose
◆ A wind too fierce disturbs the lake's peace; thunder too frequent breeds inner friction
advice: Regularly set shared goals as spiritual anchors: let Following flexibly adjust the rhythm, let Dispersion reach outward, and keep a boundary that honors the stillness and motion of the alternating cadence.

relationship_name: The Balance of Following and Limitation
one_liner: You drift with the waves, I build dikes against floods; together we create a landscape, apart we invite disaster.
analysis: Following's hexagram is like thunder in a lake, advocating going with the flow and adapting flexibly; its judgment "yuan heng li zhen" signifies unimpeded success. Limitation's hexagram is like water stored above a lake, emphasizing institutional restraint and knowing when to stop, with the warning "bitter restraint cannot endure." Together they form a dynamic balance: Following's flexibility needs Limitation's framework to prevent dissipation, while Limitation's rigor needs Following's adaptability to avoid rigidity. When the waters of the lake clash, the wisdom of going with the times and the rationality of measured restraint collide; they may work in concert when goals align, or create friction due to differing rhythms. The key lies in embracing the middle way: "follow without being indulgent, restrain without being harsh."
resonance: ★ The agility of going with the flow
★ The clarity of measured restraint
conflict: ◆ Impulsively breaking the rules
◆ Rigidity suppressing vitality
advice: Set flexible boundaries before taking spontaneous actions, and leave room for adaptation within disciplined plans.

relationship_name: Mutual Support of Sincerity and Following
one_liner: You go with the flow, I anchor with sincerity; rapport naturally grows.
analysis: The Sui hexagram (Following) — Lake over Thunder — moves in accord with circumstances; Zhong Fu (Inner Truth) — Wind over Lake — stirs with a core of sincerity. The Lake is soft and moist, able to hold Thunder's movement; Wind is formless, able to carry trust far. When the two meet, the adaptability of Following needs the steadfastness of Inner Truth as its foundation, or it becomes mere opportunism; the constancy of Inner Truth needs the flexibility of Following as its wings, or it turns into stubbornness. In the hexagram images, 'Lake' is the common carrier; the interplay of Thunder and Wind creates a dynamic balance. Following dissolves the solemnity of Zhong Fu's 'deliberating over cases and delaying executions' with the wisdom of 'retiring at dusk to rest'; Zhong Fu nourishes Following's agility of 'choosing the good and following it' with the purity of 'trust reaching pigs and fish.' Together they form a symbiotic state of outer adaptability and inner integrity.
resonance: ★ Lake embraces wind and thunder; sincerity and following feed each other.
★ Motion holds stillness; trust set, momentum forms.
conflict: ◆ Following the trend without restraint makes sincerity superficial; guarding sincerity rigidly makes opportunity stall.
◆ Sudden wind stirs the lake's calm; thunder's rumbling upsets the balance of trust.
advice: When facing a choice, first use the sincerity of Inner Truth to fix your core principles, then use the wisdom of Following to find the path of action. At the end of each month, review the balance between 'keeping sincerity' and 'adapting to change' like reconciling accounts.

one_liner: You understand the ease of going with the flow; I'm good at the steadiness of keeping my head down. When we're in sync, it's 'just right' — not overcompetitive, not anxious.
analysis: The 'Following' hexagram teaches going home to rest at nightfall—yielding to the seasons and pacing oneself with ease. The 'Preponderance of the Small' hexagram advises against ascending, in favor of staying low—emphasizing caution, humility, and moderation. Both hexagrams contain the Thunder trigram: one hides its power beneath a Lake, the other sends a warning from a Mountain, forming a resonance of outer compliance and inner vigilance. The Lake nature of Following brings fluidity and tolerance; the Mountain nature of Preponderance of the Small supplies boundary and foundation. When the grand success of the great picture meets the grounded practicality of small actions, the two can deeply align in their rhythm of living: not blindly chasing peaks, but sinking their efforts into details; understanding when to advance and when to retreat; dissolving anxiety with flexibility; and securing their bottom line with prudence.
resonance: ★ Flowing with the current, knowing when to stop — in sync on tension and release
★ Staying low and cultivating details — resonance in the small stuff
conflict: ◆ Casual compromise can blur boundaries
◆ Overcaution and perfectionism can drain energy
advice: When you're stuck, let the 'Following' partner suggest pausing to let emotions cool, then the 'Preponderance of the Small' partner lists three concrete small tasks — replace grand debates with specific micro-actions.

one_liner: One knows how to break through by riding the current, the other excels at finding and filling the gaps. Together, they're rock-solid.
analysis: Following's image, Lake over Thunder, stirs things into motion, advocating going with the flow and choosing what is good. After Completion's image, Water over Fire, blends water and fire, emphasizing the need to guard against danger after success.
